A direct flight from Hyderabad (Rajiv Gandhi International Airport) to Colombo (Bandaranaike International Airport) takes approximately 1 hour 55 minutes . Connecting flights via Bengaluru, Chennai, or Kochi take about 4–6 hours total.

Places to Visit in Sri Lanka
Here are the top destinations covered in our Sri Lanka vacation packages from Hyderabad :

Ravana Falls and Ravana Cave are just 2 km from Ella, famous from the Ramayana. According to the Ramayana tradition, this cave is associated with the period when Sita was held captive in Lanka. The waterfall cascades through a lush valley and you can swim in the cool water at the base.
Tip: Fog is common until 10 AM — arrive after that for clearer views.

Sigiriya, also called Lion Rock, is a 200-metre-high ancient rock fortress — UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built as King Kashyapa's palace in the 5th century, it is now one of Sri Lanka's most visited archaeological sites. Climb to the top for the Lion Gate, colourful frescoes, and views across the surrounding jungle.
Tip: Start your climb before 7 AM to avoid crowds and midday heat.

Dambulla Cave Temple is more than 2,000 years old, dating from the 1st century BCE when King Valagamba took refuge here — five caves filled with Buddha statues, ancient paintings, and stone carvings. From the hilltop, you get wide views of the surrounding rice fields.
Tip: Dress modestly and remove shoes before entering.

Bentota is one of Sri Lanka's most popular beach resort towns. The beach is calm and safe, with golden sand and clear water. Water sports including snorkelling, scuba diving, and deep sea fishing are available.
Tip: Carry sunscreen and a hat — the sun on Sri Lanka's west coast is strong.

A UNESCO World Heritage Site on Sri Lanka's southwest coast. Built by the Portuguese in the 1500s and later expanded by the Dutch — one of the best-preserved colonial forts in Asia. Inside: charming cafes, boutique shops, a lighthouse, a Dutch Reformed Church, and sea-facing rampart walks.

Sri Lanka's cultural capital, home to the Temple of the Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa) — one of the most sacred Buddhist temples in the world. Set in the central highlands surrounded by tea plantations. The Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is 40 km away — ideal for families.

Sri Lanka's commercial capital — usually the first or last stop on any Sri Lanka trip from Hyderabad . Key stops: Gangaramaya Temple , Galle Face Green (sunset walk), Pettah Market (spices, goods, local energy), and the Lotus Tower — South Asia's tallest self-supported structure at ~350 metres, with an observation deck and revolving restaurant.

Sri Lanka's hill station at 1,868 metres. Surrounded by tea estates — visit a working tea factory and taste freshly made Ceylon tea. Horton Plains National Park (32 km away) has the famous World's End cliff and Baker's Falls.

Mirissa is one of Sri Lanka's most popular beaches on the south coast, about 150 km from Colombo. It's the main departure point for blue whale and dolphin watching boat tours (November–April). The beach itself is a curved bay with calm water, palm trees, and good seafood restaurants. Mirissa is also a popular surfing spot from March to October.

Yala National Park in southeastern Sri Lanka is one of the most visited national parks in Asia, and has one of the highest densities of leopards in the world . The park also has elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles, and over 200 bird species. Jeep safaris are the standard way to explore. Best visited between February and July when wildlife concentrations are highest and water levels are low.

Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's northeast coast is known for its natural harbour — one of the finest in the world — and its beautiful beaches. Nilaveli Beach and Uppuveli Beach are among the cleanest beaches in Sri Lanka. Pigeon Island National Park, just offshore, has excellent snorkelling with reef sharks and coral. The Koneswaram Temple on Swami Rock, overlooking the sea, is one of Sri Lanka's five ancient Shiva temples. Best visited April–September.

Ella is a small hill town in Sri Lanka's Uva Province, popular for its views, short hikes, and relaxed atmosphere. The Nine Arch Bridge — a colonial-era stone railway viaduct — is one of Sri Lanka's most photographed landmarks. Little Adam's Peak (easy 2-hour hike) and Ella Rock (4-hour hike) both offer views across the tea valleys. Ravana Falls and Ravana Cave are 2 km from Ella town.

Direct flights from Hyderabad to Colombo take approximately 1 hour 55 minutes . Connecting flights via Bangkok, Chennai, or Singapore take 4–6 hours total. IndiGo and SriLankan Airlines both operate direct services.

blocks.text: Q1. Which airlines have direct flights from Hyderabad to Sri Lanka?

Ans: IndiGo (~6 flights/week) and SriLankan Airlines (~5 flights/week) operate nonstop flights from Hyderabad to Colombo. Flight time: ~1 hour 55 minutes. Air India has connecting services only. Check current schedules on airline websites before booking.
Q2. What currency is used in Sri Lanka?
Ans: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). Exchange USD, Euros, or Indian Rupees at banks or airport counters. Carry LKR cash for local markets and smaller towns.
Q3. How many days are enough to see Sri Lanka from Hyderabad?
Ans: 7–10 days covers Sri Lanka comfortably. 4–5 days works for a focused trip (Colombo, Kandy, Nuwara Eliya). 8 days is ideal for the Ramayana circuit or a full island loop.
Q4. Do Indians need a visa for Sri Lanka in 2026?

Ans: No visa or ETA required for Indians in 2026. Enter with a valid passport and return air ticket. 30-day stay, double-entry permitted. ETA at eta.gov.lk is optional but saves queue time. (Source: Sri Lanka High Commission India, Feb 2026)
Q5. What is the best time to visit Sri Lanka from Hyderabad?

Ans: December to March for west/south coast beaches (Bentota, Mirissa, Galle). April to September for the east coast (Trincomalee, Arugam Bay). Cultural sites and hill stations (Kandy, Nuwara Eliya) are accessible year-round.
Q6. What is the Sri Lanka tour cost from Hyderabad?
Ans: Ground packages start from ₹24,900 per person (4 days, no flights). A 7–8 day package costs ₹36,900–₹45,000. Return flights add ₹12,000–₹25,000. No visa or ETA fees for Indians in 2026.
Q7. Is the Sri Lanka Ramayana tour worth it for Hyderabad pilgrims?

Ans: Yes — the 8-day Sri Lanka Ramayana Tour from Hyderabad (₹28,900) is very popular with Hindu devotees. It covers Ravana Cave, Sita Amman Temple (Ashok Vatika), Divurumpola, Munneswaram Temple, and Anuradhapura. For pilgrims from Hyderabad, this combines devotion with a complete Sri Lanka experience.
Q8. Is Sri Lanka good for a honeymoon?

Ans: Yes. Our Sri Lanka honeymoon package from Hyderabad (7 days, ₹38,500) includes Colombo, Kandy hills, and Bentota beach resort. Beach resorts at Mirissa and Passikudah also offer private pool options. Sri Lanka's mix of beaches, wildlife, hills, and heritage makes it a varied and private honeymoon destination.
Q9. What are the best wildlife experiences in Sri Lanka?

Ans: Yala National Park for leopards (highest density in Asia), sloth bears, and elephants. Udawalawe National Park for large elephant herds including calves — best year-round. Mirissa for blue whale and dolphin boat tours (November–April). Pigeon Island, Trincomalee for reef sharks and coral snorkelling.
Q10. Can I use Indian Rupees in Sri Lanka?

Ans: Some authorised exchange counters at Colombo airport accept Indian Rupees for conversion to LKR. However, Indian Rupees are not accepted as payment currency in Sri Lanka's shops, restaurants, or taxis. Exchange to LKR at the airport or authorised bank counters on arrival.
Q11. What should I buy in Sri Lanka?

Ans: Ceylon tea (buy from plantation shops in Nuwara Eliya for best prices), cinnamon and spices, gemstones from certified shops, batik fabric, and traditional wooden masks. Pettah Market in Colombo is good for bulk spice purchases.
Q12. How far is Sri Lanka from Hyderabad?

Ans: Hyderabad to Colombo by direct flight is approximately 1 hour 55 minutes — making Sri Lanka one of the closest international destinations from Hyderabad. The aerial distance is approximately 2,000 km. With a connecting flight the total journey can be 4–6 hours.
Q13. What is the Sri Lanka Ramayana package itinerary?
Ans: 8 days: Anuradhapura → Trincomalee → Kandy (Temple of Tooth) → Sita Amman Temple, Nuwara Eliya → Ravana Cave, Ella → Kataragama → Divurumpola → Colombo departure.
Q14. Is Sri Lanka a good family destination from Hyderabad?

Ans: Yes. Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, Sigiriya, Kandy cultural show, whale watching, and Colombo city tours all work well for families. Short 2-hour flight and no visa requirement make it very practical.
Q15. What is the best Sri Lanka package for first-time visitors?
Ans: The 8-day Sri Lanka Group Tour (₹36,900) covering Colombo → Sigiriya → Kandy → Nuwara Eliya → Ella → Galle is ideal — covers culture, wildlife, hills, and beach in one trip.

With this package, you'll get a chance to visit four of the most sacred destinations- Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri. You can participate in various rituals held at these sacred sites and offer prayers to the deities. We have designed this package thoughtfully to cater to the diverse needs of NRIs looking to have a sacred connection with their roots. We offer a customized Char Dham yatra for NRI travel package that includes sightseeing, accommodation, meals, transportation and other amenities.

Experience a harmonious blend of devotion, culture, and tradition as you visit the revered Char Dham sites by booking our package. Our Char Dham NRI tour packages come with guided tours that are led by experts who try their best to enhance your experience. They share cultural insights and historical context that enrich your pilgrimage. Whether you want to explore your ancestral roots or are returning to your homeland, our packages provide a once-in-a-lifetime chance to deepen your connection with the rich heritage of India.
Why Choose a Char Dham Yatra for NRI Tour Package?

If you are an NRI for that matter, even planning a holy trip in India can be a hard time as most NRIs have less time to plan their trip and yes new roads, booking etc. The solution to all of these problems is the special Char Dham Yatra for NRI Package which provides a fixed plan with expert assistance.

3. Helpful Guides Trained guides help NRIs with temple rules, local habits, and travel timing.
4. Fast VIP Darshan When possible, quick temple entry is arranged to save your time standing in long lines.
5. Well Planned Travel Routes The Char Dham Yatra itinerary for NRIs is made carefully to avoid feeling tired and to help your body adapt to high mountains.
6. Safe and Secure Travel Good cars, expert drivers, and daily help make the trip very safe.
This mix of holy feelings and easy travel makes the NRI Char Dham Yatra package the best choice for people living abroad.
Best Time for Char Dham Yatra
The holy temples open every year around April or May and close in October or early November, depending on the weather.

items: May - June: Very nice weather and it is the best time for the holy trip.
July - August: Rainy season and travel can be hard due to heavy rain.
September - October: Clear sky, less rush, and nice travel weather.

blocks.text: Most NRIs like to come in May, June, or September when the roads and weather are very nice.

items: Your Char Dham tour will start from Delhi, the heart of India.
As you arrive at Indira Gandhi International Airport Delhi our representative will greet you and welcome you with open arms.
After picking you up from the airport our representative will transfer you to your pre-reserved hotel where you will have an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 2 : Delhi - Haridwar - Drive: Time: 06 – 07 hrs.- 220 km

items: Wake up early in the morning and relish a tasty breakfast.
Post breakfast, you will check out from your hotel and embark on a pleasant drive to Haridwar.
You'll reach Haridwar by the evening and check in to your pre-booked hotel. After relaxing for some time, you will head to Har Ki Pauri, a sacred ghat in Haridwar.
You'll attend the Ganga Aarti at the ghat. After that, you'll return to your hotel and have a soothing sleep in your room.

blocks.text: Day 3 : Haridwar – Barkot - Time: 06 – 07 hrs.- Drive: 177 km

items: Savour a delicious breakfast in the morning at your hotel, and then you'll embark on a picturesque drive to Barkot.
On the way you will stop by Kempty Fall, a cascading waterfall surrounded by mountains and lush green forests.
Continue your journey to Barkot and then check in to your camp and have a mouth-watering dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your camp.

blocks.text: Day 4 : Barkot – Yamunotri – Barkot - Trek: 05 km- Drive: 45 km + 45 km

items: Today you will wake up early in the morning and relish a tasty breakfast. After breakfast, you will embark on a scenic drive to Jankichatti, i.e, the starting point of the trek to Yamunotri Dham.
You can trek or take a pony/doli to reach Yamunotri Dham . Once you have arrived at Yamunotri Dham, you will buy Prasadam from local shops.
Once you have reached the temple premises, you will take a holy dip in the holy water. After the bath, you will head to the main temple to seek blessings from Mata Yamuna.
Later you'll trek down towards Jankichatti. From Jankichatti you'll drive back to Barkot for dinner. Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 5 : Barkot – Uttarkashi - Drive: Time: 03 – 04 hrs.- 81 km

items: Have a tasty breakfast in the morning and then embark on a scenic drive to Uttarkashi. After arriving in Uttarkashi, you will visit Hanuman Temple and Vishwanath Temple.
Hanuman Temple is dedicated to Lord Hanuman and it is believed that carrying the mountain Sanjivani to Lanka Lord Hanuman rested at this spot.
Vishwanath Temple was constructed by Queen Khaneti Devi over an ancient altar that dates back to the era of Mahabharata.
Later you'll drive around 5 km. To reach your pre-booked resort.
You will check in to your luxurious resort for dinner. Post dinner you will have an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 6 : Uttarkashi – Gangotri – Uttarkashi - Drive: Time: 06 hrs-92 km one side

items: Wake up early in the morning and head to Gangotri Dham . During the sacred yatra, you will take a halt at Gangnani and take a dip in the hot water spring.
You will then continue your drive to Gangotri via Harsil.
Once you have arrived at Gangotri Dham, you'll perform pooja at the river Bhagirathi's bank and seek Goddess Ganga's blessings.
After pooja, you will head to the main temple and have Mata Ganga's darshan. Post darshan you will head back to Uttarkashi.

blocks.text: Day 7 : Uttarkashi - Guptkashi Time: 07 – 08 hrs.- Drive: 198 km

items: Have breakfast early in the morning. After breakfast, you'll embark on a scenic drive to Gupatkashi.
On the way, you'll pass by Tehri Dam, which is known to be the highest dam in India.
Once you have reached Guptkashi, you will check in to your pre-reserved resort for dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 8 : Guptkashi – Kedarnath - Trek: 19 kms- Drive: 45 kms.

items: Wake up early in the morning and then embark on a drive to Sonprayag.
Once you have arrived at Sonprayag, you will take a local jeep that will drop you at Gaurikund (2 km).
From Gaurikund, you will begin your trek to Kedarnath. After arriving at Kedarnath/ you'll check in to the guest house.
Relax for some time and then you'll get ready to visit Kedarnath Temple to attend the evening Aarti.
Post Aarti you will return to your guest house and have an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 9 : Kedarnath – Rudraparyag - Trek: 18 kms- Drive: 75 kms

items: Today you'll wake up early in the morning and get ready to visit Kedarnath temple to attend the morning Aarti.
After the Aarti and darshan of Lord Kedar, you'll head back to your guest house and have a yummy breakfast.
Post breakfast you will pack your bags and embark on an 18 km long trek back to Gaurikund.
Drive to Rudraprayag from the road head. After arriving at Rudraprayag you will check in to your hotel and have a mouth-watering dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 10 : Rudraprayag – Badrinath Time: 06 – 07 hrs.- Drive:157 kms

items: Have a lip-smacking breakfast in the morning and then embark on a picturesque drive to Badrinath, which is situated on the Alaknanda River banks.
After arriving in Badrinath, you will check in to your hotel. Relax and unwind for some time, and then in the evening you'll head to Badrinath temple.
After the darshan of Lord Badri, you will head back to your hotel and have a mouth-watering dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 11 : Badrinath – Rishikesh - Drive: 295 kms.- Time: 10 – 11 hrs.

items: Have a yummy breakfast in the morning and then drive to Rishikesh via Devprayag.
You will stop by Devprayag to see the confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda Rivers from which the river Ganga formed.
You will then continue your journey to Rishikesh, admiring the scenic views.
Once you have arrived at Rishikesh, you will check in to your pre-booked hotel and have a tasty dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 12 : Rishikesh - Delhi Drive 6 Hrs/232 Kms

items: Post breakfast you will complete the check-out formalities and drive back to Delhi.
Once you have reached Delhi you'll check in to your pre-booked hotel and have an overnight stay.
Relish a yummy breakfast in the morning and then pack your bags and check out from your pre-reserved hotel.
You'll be transferred to the airport or railway station from where you'll head to your hometown.

blocks.text: Mahavatar Babaji Cave Tour Package, Dunagiri
Learn about the historical prominence of Mahavatar Babaji's Cave with our 2-night 3-day package from Delhi. See More

Mahavatar Babaji's Cave is believed to be the site where the immortal Babaji got the teachings related to Kriya Yoga from Lahiri Mahasaya in 1861 (as stated in the Autobiography of a Yogi that has been written by Paramahansa Yogananda).

The cave is situated at around 2600 meters above sea level. It is considered to be an embodiment of profound spiritual energy and peace. You can meditate and practice yoga amidst the breathtaking backdrop of the Himalayas at this place. Many Kriya Yogi devotees believe that Jesus and Mahavatar Babaji are one.

A moderately challenging trek through lush green forests takes you to this hallowed destination. For an average person, the trek to the cave takes around one hour. On the way, you can also visit Dunagiri Mata Temple and explore Dwarahat Town. Join us on the expedition to Mahavatar Babaji's Cave for a transformative experience filled with spiritual growth and peace.
Kriya Yoga is a spiritual practice involving breath control, meditation and discipline to connect with divine energy. It became famous through Paramahansa Yogananda’s book autobiography of a Yogi.

items: Breath Control - It is the practice of controlling the life energy (prana) using special breathing techniques that keeps the mind calm and energizes the body.
Meditation - It helps you to focus better and is beneficial for self-peace to connect with the divine.
Inner Peace - It helps to purify the mind and body that bring higher consciousness.

blocks.text: Activities to Do in Mahavatar Babaji Cave
There are several things to do in Mahavatar Babaji Cave that devotees perform while visiting the cave-

items: Meditation and Yoga - Many visitors practice yoga or meditation in the peaceful cave to relax their mind and achieve inner peace. People can easily focus in this relaxed environment and feel more balanced.

Trekking - Some visitors enjoy trekking to reach the cave, as it gives them a chance to connect with nature and enjoy peaceful surroundings. Trekking also gives a feeling of adventure that helps visitors to experience the spiritual vibes of the place.

Photography - Many tourists love to take pictures of the cave and its beautiful surroundings, which include green landscapes, scenic views, unique flora and fauna. Visitors can also enjoy capturing photos of wildlife.

Bird watching - You can see several bird species around Mahavatar Babaji Cave that makes it a perfect spot to enjoy birdwatching. There are many colorful Himalayan birds like thrushes, woodpeckers and sometimes rare species in that area.

blocks.text: Places to Explore near Babaji Cave
There are best places to visit near Mahavatar Babaji Cave that tourists must explore-

items: Dwarahat Temple - This ancient temple is famous for its beauty and historical importance, and it is located in the Dwarahat region. This temple is around 1,000 years old and dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Therefore, it attracts many visitors.

Pandukholi - This calm place is known for its natural beauty and ancient caves. It is also a perfect spot for meditation and stress relief. It is believed that the Pandavas stayed here during their 14 years of exile.
Chaukhutia - It is a small village known for its beautiful views and its close to spiritual sites. This village is surrounded by wonderful hills and forests. Nature lovers must visit this place.

Dunagiri Temple - This temple is surrounded by dense forests and stunning mountains. It is believed that Goddess Durga mediated here. Many people believe that visiting this temple brings good fortune and removes obstacles in life.

Ranikhet - It is one of the wonderful hill station often called ‘Queen of Kumaon’. Visitors can see the beautiful view of Himalayan peaks from Ranikhet, especially Nanda Devi and Trishul. This destination is also known for its pleasant weather that makes it a great spot to visit.

blocks.text: How to Reach Mahavatar Babaji Cave

items: The nearest airport is Pantnagar Airport (about 125 km from Dwarahat).
Travelers can take a taxi from the airport to Dwarahat
The cave is located near Dwarahat in Almora, visitors can reach Dwarahat by taxi or bus from Almora or Haldwani.
From Delhi or Nainital, go by road to Almora and take a taxi or other local transport to reach Dwarahat.
The closest railway station to Dwarahat is Kathgodam (around 108 km).
From Kathgodam, take a taxi to Dwarahat and continue to the cave.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Mahavatar Babaji Cave

items: The best time to visit Mahavatar Babaji cave is from April to June and September to November, because the weather is pleasant at this time and the paths are clear.
The trekking routes are easier to follow during these months.
Avoid visiting during the monsoon season.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. How long is the trek to Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. You will have to undertake a 3 km long trek to reach Mahavatar Babaji's Cave. Depending on your pace you won’t take more than an hour to reach the cave via trekking. The trail is well-paved with stones and you’ll encounter breathtaking scenery during the trekking expedition.
Q2. What is the relevance of Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. Mahavatar Babaji Cave is the place where Lahiri Mahasaya is known to have spent a previous incarnation. Lahiri Mahasaya received Kriya Yoga initiation here from Babaji, and then he started spreading it out worldwide. You can meditate in the cave and practice yoga. The cave is surrounded by Himalayas offering you an unadulterated view of breathtaking sceneries
Q3. What is the best time to visit Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. Mid-February to mid-June (summer and spring seasons) are considered the best to visit Mahavatar Babaji's Cave. This period offers clear blue skies, pleasant weather, and cool and comfortable temperatures for a spiritual expedition. The awe-inspiring scenic views enhance the overall travel experience.
Q4. How can you reach Mahavatar Babaji's Cave from Delhi?

Ans. From New Delhi, you can embark on a scenic drive to Ranikhet lasting around 10 to 11 hours. From Ranikhet, you can drive towards the cave via Kukuchina Village and Dwarahat. Once you have arrived at the road’s tail end you will undertake a 3-kilometer long trek to the cave.
Q5. What can you do at Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. At Mahavatar Babaji's Cave, you can meditate and practice yoga. You can also absorb the cave’s positive energy and appreciate the beauty of the surroundings. If you have time you can explore the places near this cave.

blocks.text: Apart from being known as the land of palaces and maharajas, Rajasthan is also one of the prime romantic destinations. With the atmosphere enveloped in colorful beauty and surreal landscapes, Rajasthan can be your next favorite exotic destination for you and your better half. Explore the many vibrant faces of Rajasthan with My Quick Trippers’s, 6 days and 5 nights romantic tour of Rajasthan.

You will be transferred to your allotted hotel upon your arrival in Jaipur. Later you will be taken on a brief sightseeing tour of the city like – Hawa Mahal (palace of winds) – one of the most prominent landmarks of the city, representing the fine craftsmanship of the city; you will also be taken to Jantar Mantar – which is one of the most well preserved observatories in the subcontinent.
You will finally be taken back to your hotel for an overnight stay.

Post breakfast, you will be taken on a brief excursion of Amber Fort palace – which is a classic sign of romance, and perched atop a large platform from where you can take a breathtaking view of the Jaipur city; Nahargarh fort will be your next destination which is located all along the Aravali ranges. Next stop for you will be the holy Laxmi Narayan temple – a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Laxmi and Lord Vishnu.
Later in the evening, you will be made to visit the teeming colorful marketplaces of Jaipur.
You can shop for locally made souvenirs like – traditional blue pottery, camel leather products, lac bangles, silk quilts, Jaipur handicrafts, bandhej and many more.
You also have the freedom to try out some delectable cuisines like – dal baati churma, laal maas, the iconic Rajasthani thali, Kachori and a whole plethora of others.

You will be driven to Pushkar in the morning after breakfast, which is located at a distance of 2 hours and 40 mines. Upon arriving at Pushkar you will be immediately checked in to your hotel for staying the night. After freshening up you will be taken to Brahma Mandir – one of the few temples that is dedicated to Lord Brahma. It is a common belief that the Lord had personally chosen Pushkar as the temple site making it extremely pious. You will then proceed towards the sacred Pushkar Lake – which is surrounded by 52 bathing ghats and a dip here is believed to cleanse all your sins and skin related diseases.
After spending a memorable day in one of the most fascinating destinations in India, you will then be made to head back to your hotel.

Early in the morning, you will be made to head for Udaipur, which is located at a distance of 5 hours and 10 mines. Upon arriving at this beautifully enchanting town you will be made to check in to your hotel for a night stay.

Your sightseeing tour of Udaipur will commence in the morning starting with a visit to the famous city Palace museum – a beautifully created palace complex, which has served as the resident place for numerous ruling dynasties. Jagdish Mandir will be your next destination, which is situated just outside the royal city palace and is dedicated to Lord Jagannath and is one of the major tourist attractions in Udaipur. Saheliyon ki bari will be your next destination, a beautiful garden complete with numerous fountains, lotus pools and elephant statues made of marble. You will then be taken to bhartiya lok kala mandir which is a folk art museum.
After a day of exploration and fun you will be guided back to your hotel for staying the night.
After the completion of your breakfast, you will be transferred to the airport or railway station from where you will depart towards Delhi and onto your desired location.

blocks.text: Q1. Is Rajasthan Suitable For A Honeymoon?

Ans. However, if you are celebrating your honeymoon during the winter and want to experience some royalty as a couple, there is no better place to go than Rajasthan. Rajasthan, one of India's most romantic honeymoon destinations, has many charming places offering a variety of romantic things to do, attractions to visit, and places to stay.
Q2. When Is The Best Time To Go On A Honeymoon In Rajasthan?

Ans. Other than winter, the monsoon season is the best time to visit Rajasthan. The honeymoon months of July to September (Monsoon) are ideal, when the arid and barren landscape transforms into a lush green haven.
Q3. What Is Rajasthan's Distinguishing Feature?

Ans. The ruins of the Indus Valley civilisation at Kalibangan and Balathal, the Dilwara Temples, a Jain pilgrimage site at Rajasthan's only hill station, Mount Abu, in the ancient Aravalli mountain range and eastern Rajasthan, and the Keoladeo National Park of Bharatpur, a World Heritage Site, are among its major attractions.
Q4. What Are Rajasthani Eating Habits?

Ans. Rajasthani cuisine is influenced by the state's rich heritage and arid climate. Their cuisine is distinguished by the scarcity of fresh fruits and vegetables. Beans, lentils, gramme flour, corn, barley, millet, bajra, bread, and dairy products are all common ingredients (esp. Ghee).
Q5. What Is The Name Of Rajasthani Clothing?

Ans. Rajasthani women traditionally wear Ghagra, Choli (also known as Kanchli or Kurti), and Odhni. The Ghagra is a full-length, embroidered and pleated skirt available in a wide range of colours, prints, and fabrics such as silk, cotton, georgette, and crêpe.

blocks.text: Plan a trip to Guwahati, the largest city in Assam! Also known as a gateway to the Northeast, this place’s beauty will make you fall in love with it at first glance. See More

With this 2 Nights and 3 Days Guwahati temple tour package with Meghalaya , you get to visit all the important sightseeing places – whether it’s the popular limestone caves, ancient temples with deep-rooted Tantric significance, or the simply picturesque lakes that impress you in a heartbeat – you’re bound to go on a trip of your dreams. Book My Quick Trippers’s package to avail all the tour-related amenities – from accommodation to meals to transport services.

To tell you more about this tour plan, the package covers most of the popular temples and sites of Guwahati to make your trip worthwhile. We have also selected comfortable stays that provide delicious meals. With our service, you also get to avail the service of guided tours that will offer you historical insights into every temple you visit. In a nutshell, it is a short trip created for working professionals or people who prefer not to compromise on their work commitments. Book the package to Guwahati & Meghalaya now and enjoy the most affordable prices in the industry.

blocks.text: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati – Sightseeing in Shillong (100 km /3 hrs)

items: Welcome to Assam! Upon your arrival at Guwahati Airport/Railway station, our tour representative will greet you with a warm welcome. From here on, you’ll be transferred to Shillong .

Along the way, we’ll make a stop at the magnificent Umiam Lake (Barapani Lake), which is also the largest artificial lake in Meghalaya. Surrounded by pine-covered hills, it makes for an excellent photo-op. Also, do not forget to capture the shimmering waters of the lake during the sunset. The views are just simply another world!
Once you arrive at Shillong, check into your pre-booked hotel. Freshen up!

If time permits, we’ll set out on a mini sightseeing tour in the cool mountain air of the city. Visit the local markets, such as Police Bazaar, for shopping of handicrafts. Also, try authentic Khasi cuisine like Jadoh (rice with meat).
Return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: DAY 2 - Elephant Falls - Sightseeing in Cherrapunji - Transfer to Guwahati (100 km/3 hrs)

items: Savour some delicious breakfast in the morning.
After that, we'll take you on a tour of Elephant Falls . This three-tiered cascading waterfall makes for an excellent photograph. Stand at the bottom tier if you want to capture the best views.

Later, we’ll transfer you to Cherrapunji, the most rainy place in the world (a 60 km drive; 2 hours driving time). Also known as the "Scotland of the East", it's famous for its unique natural wonders. You’ll go sightseeing at: Seven Sisters Falls: Watch the gushing water as it falls down from seven streams side by side. Mawsmai Cave: This cave is popular for its narrow passages and stunning limestone formations. You’re advised to carry a flashlight inside the cave for better views. Thangkharang Park: Overlooking the Bangladesh plains, you get to enjoy the most beautiful panoramic views of the valley here. Don’t forget to take your camera up there!
After your sightseeing tour is over, we’ll drive you back to Guwahati for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: DAY 3 – Temple tour in Guwahati and Departure

items: Get up early in the morning, as today you're up for a full-day tour of Guwahati city!

We’ll start our day early, around 4 AM, and will visit the holy Kamakhya Temple at Nilachal Hill. This is one of the revered 51 Shakti Peethas , and we recommend getting a VIP pass, which costs around INR 500 per person. This will help you skip long queues.
Also, explore nearby temples dedicated to Maa Tara, Maa Kali, Maa Chhinnamasta, Maa Bhuvaneshwari, Maa Bagalamukhi, Maa Bandurga, and Dhumapati , which are all located within walking distance.
Now take a ferry to Peacock Island on the Brahmaputra to the Umananda Temple . Photo op moments galore! This island is also home to the endangered Golden Langur. You’ll be lucky if you spot one!
Have breakfast, and after that, we’ll take you on a half-day excursion in Shillong.
This concludes your trip with us. Now, you’ll be dropped off at the railway station or airport, as per your choice. Hope you have made great memories on this tour!

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is the best time to explore Guwahati?
Ans. The best time to visit Guwahati is from October to April when the weather is nice for sightseeing.
Q2. How far is Guwahati from the airport?
Ans. Guwahati is 25 kilometres from Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, and it takes about 45 minutes to reach.
Q3. Is the Brahmaputra River Cruise included in the package?
Ans. Yes, the package includes an evening cruise ride on the Brahmaputra river.
Q4. Apart from tourist attractions, what is famous in Guwahati?
Ans. Assam is famous for its silk Sarees, tea and handicrafts using bamboo. You can explore and shop these items from Fancy Bazar and the Handicraft market.
Q5. Is it safe to travel solo in Guwahati?
Ans. Yes, Guwahati is a safe place for solo travellers. However, you must stay alert and take care of your belongings.
Q6. Can we take photographs inside Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. You can take photos of the temple complex. However, capturing pictures of the temple sanctum is prohibited. You can capture the outside of the temple architecture though, which is really beautiful.
Q7. How far is Shillong from Guwahati?

Ans. Shillong is located about 100 km from Guwahati. If you get on NH6, you can easily cover this distance in under 3 hours. The journey is quite scenic, and many people make a stop at the beautiful Umiam Lake along the way.
Q8. What kind of clothes should I pack for this tour?

Ans. As the weather in Shillong is quite cool, you’re advised to bring some light woollen clothes with you, along with jackets. We also recommend carrying rain gear and comfortable walking shoes with you. Also, you should have modest clothes on you if you're planning to visit temples.
Q9. What are the local food specialities to try in Shillong?

Ans. While visiting Shillong, we recommend trying the local, authentic cuisine. You must try Jadoh (red rice with pork), Dohneiiong (pork with black sesame), and Tungrymbai (fermented soybeans), as these are some of the most popular dishes there. Also, you can easily avail of vegetarian options as well.

rows: On this first day of the Varanasi tour, you'll be taken to the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat . Don't forget to take snaps of the gorgeous views. Wander around and soak in the aura of Varanasi!

Varanasi and Sarnath Pilgrimage Tour from Bangalore are often clubbed together. Take a short trip outside of Varanasi and go to Sarnath (10 km drive). This is the very place where Lord Buddha gave his very first sermon. You can see here Dhamek Stupa and the Archaeological Museum .

blocks.text: Top Places to Visit in Varanasi
Here are some places that must be a part of your Varanasi Trip Package from Bangalore:

Kashi Vishwanath Darshan is one of the top things to do when you come here. This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is also one of the 12 Jyotirlingas. No wonder it's called the spiritual centrepiece of Varanasi!

If you want to experience the true blue Ganga Aarti Varanasi experience, then come to this Ghat in the evening. The event takes place here every day, and a sacred atmosphere is created, lit with bright lamps and sacred chants.

If you want to experience the peace and serenity of Varanasi, then come to this Ghat. You'll often find people doing yoga and meditation here, especially in the early morning. The Assi Ghat sunrise boat ride is a must-try experience in this city.

It's one of the main cremation Ghats of Varanasi. More than just a cremation ground, it symbolises the recurring life and death cycle in Hinduism. You'll feel the powerful spiritual aura of this place when you're here.

Sarnath is located just 10 km from Varanasi and must be added to your Bangalore to Varanasi itinerary. This is a very important place for Buddhists. Plus, you can visit the Ashokan Pillar here which is also a UNESCO heritage site.
Come here to see the rich heritage of the yesteryear era. You'll find here royal artifacts, ancient weaponry, and even vintage cars! Do taka pictures of its marvellous architecture.

Best Time to Visit Varanasi from Bangalore

The best time to visit Varanasi is hands down in the winter season ( October to March ). This period here is quite nice and pleasant, letting you do your temple tours and sightseeing in peace and pleasure. The temperature in this window swings between 10°C and 25°C. The other great thing about this period is that you can attend the festival here, like Diwali, Maha Shivratri, Holi, etc., if you come at the right time.
Also, we advise against booking your trip in summer (April - June) and monsoon (July - September) as they are very hot and humid, respectively.

items: If you're going to temples, always remove your shoes before entering the shrines.
If you want to hire a guide for an enriched experience, make sure you always hire a licensed one.
If you're visiting temple, or attending any religious ceremonies, always wear modest clothes. Traditional attire are your best bet.
Manikarnika Ghat is a cremation Ghat, therefore, avoid taking photographs there.
Visit Assi Ghat in the morning and try yoga there.
Always pre-book your Karnataka to Varanasi Pilgrimage Package in advance in order to avoid last-minute rush.
If you're buying from a local vendor, always carry cash, as they may not always accept credit cards.

blocks.text: With direct flights from Chennai to Colombo taking less than two hours, Sri Lanka is one of the most accessible international destinations for travellers from Tamil Nadu. A Sri Lanka trip from Chennai costs less than most domestic hill station holidays — and gives you beaches, UNESCO heritage sites, hill country, and wildlife all in one.

Sri Lanka is a dream destination for anyone looking for adventure, beautiful scenery, or a cultural tour. To enjoy a hassle-free trip to this southern island, book our Sri Lanka Tour Packages from Chennai! With this tour plan, you get accommodation, meals, and dedicated transport. Also, our packages are fully customizable, allowing you to go on a trip tailored exactly to your preferences! Contact us now to know more!

Also known as the pearl of the South Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka has a lot to offer its tourists. Whether it's the golden-sand beaches, revered temples, or the full-fledged UNESCO World Heritage sites, there's everything for everyone — from nature lovers to history buffs! And while you're here, don't miss out on the wildlife safaris and the ever-so vibrant markets, which are a great spot for souvenir shopping. Book the Sri Lanka Sigiriya Kandy Ella tour now to explore the best of the best in Sri Lanka!
Best Time to Visit Sri Lanka from Chennai

The best time to visit Sri Lanka from South India falls in two main windows. If you're visiting the west coast of the island, the window from December to March is the perfect time. And if you're travelling to the East Coast, come here in April–September.
In the December–March window, you can enjoy Colombo, Kandy, Bentota, and Galle. In the April–September window, you can explore Trincomalee, Arugam Bay, and Batticaloa.

Colombo as a city can be visited year-round — its markets, food scene, and urban attractions are not dependent on coastal weather. If your Sri Lanka holiday package from Chennai focuses on sightseeing and culture rather than beaches, November to April is a reliable window for a 4-day, 5-day, or 6-day package.
What's Included in Sri Lanka Trip Package From Chennai?
Here's what you get with our tour plans:

items: Transfers in a private AC vehicle
Driver allowance, parking fees, and fuel charges
Pick up and drop off service
Extensive sightseeing in the city and trips to cultural sites

blocks.text: Sri Lanka Tour Itinerary from Chennai
Here's how your Sri Lanka trip, in general, looks like:

rows: Arrive in Colombo. Have a nice little tour of the place. Enjoy the nightlife of the bustling city of Colombo.
Enjoy the scenic drive to Kandy itself! Once you're there, visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic and indulge in other sightseeing.
Head into Sri Lanka's hill country. Explore lush tea plantations, colonial-era bungalows, and waterfalls around Nuwara Eliya — the 'Little England' of Sri Lanka.
Spend a leisure day at Bentota Beach.
Enjoy the Sri Lanka cultural heritage tour! Take a trip to the UNESCO site that is the Galle Fort, and get charmed by its architecture.
On the departure day, engage in some souvenir shopping in the morning and have some relaxation before catching your flight back home.

blocks.text: How to Reach Sri Lanka from Chennai?
There are primarily two ways to reach Sri Lanka from Chennai:

By Air: You can book a direct flight from Chennai (MAA) to Bandaranaike International Airport, Colombo (CMB). The flight duration is under two hours. IndiGo, SriLankan Airlines, and Air India operate on this route. Most of our Sri Lanka tour packages from Chennai with flight include the return airfare — contact us for current flight-inclusive pricing.

By Sea (Ferry): The Nagapattinam–Kankesanthurai ferry service resumed in August 2024 after a 41-year gap. The 'Sivaganga' ferry departs Nagapattinam at 7 AM and arrives at Kankesanthurai port in Jaffna by around 11 AM — approximately 3.5 hours covering 60 nautical miles. One-way fare: ₹5,000 (general class) or ₹7,500 (premium class). Book at indsri.com. Note: Nagapattinam is about 300 km from Chennai and the ferry arrives in Jaffna (northern Sri Lanka), not Colombo. Ferry schedules are subject to weather conditions and operational changes — always verify sailing dates before planning your journey.
Airlines operating: IndiGo, SriLankan Airlines, and Air India operate direct flights on the Chennai (MAA) – Colombo (CMB) route.
Flight duration: Under 2 hours (approximately 1 hour 45 minutes for direct flights).
Average economy fare: ₹7,500–₹15,000 one way depending on season, airline, and how far in advance you book. Prices are lower between May and October (shoulder season).
Airport: Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB), Colombo. Located approximately 35 km north of Colombo city — transfer to your hotel takes 45 minutes to 1.5 hours depending on traffic.
Tip: Book flights at least 3–4 weeks in advance for Pongal, summer holidays, and December peak season — fares on the Chennai–Colombo route spike during these periods.
Good news for Indian travellers in 2026 — Sri Lanka has waived the ETA fee for Indian nationals from 25 May 2026. Here's what you need to know:

ETA (Electronic Travel Authorisation): Mandatory for all Indian visitors. Apply online at eta.gov.lk before your trip. The application is free of charge as of 25 May 2026 — no fee, no embassy visit needed.
Validity: 30 days from date of first arrival. Double entry permitted within the 30-day window.
Passport requirement: Valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. Carry a printed copy of your ETA approval to speed up immigration.
Extensions: You can extend your stay up to 270 days by applying at the Department of Immigration in Colombo. Extension fees apply.
Visa on arrival: Available at Bandaranaike Airport, but applying online before travel is strongly recommended to avoid queues.
Top Attractions Covered in Sri Lanka Holiday Package
Here are some of the most frequent places in the island country:
Colombo: Come here and have a taste of a true-blue cosmopolitan city! Treat yourself to world-class casinos and a vibrant nightlife!
Kandy: Next, take a bite of culture and visit the famous Temple of the Tooth Relic. The botanical gardens here are another top attraction. A must-visit for any Chennai to Sri Lanka holiday!
Nuwara Eliya: The cool weather and the lush green tea plantations here will remind you of being in Britain — and that's why it's belovedly called 'Little England', and rightly so!
Sigiriya: Come here and see the marvel that this UNESCO World Heritage rock fortress is.

Bentota & Mirissa: These are two of the most frequented honeymoon places in Sri Lanka . Enjoy sun-kissed beaches and whale watching. You can also indulge in water sports such as diving, surfing, and more!
Galle: Appreciate the colonial architecture here and the famous Galle Fort itself! This iconic site should be a part of any Sri Lanka Tour Package from Chennai!
Ella: Visit here to relish the calming scenic train rides.
Sri Lanka Ramayana Trail — For Hindu Pilgrims from Chennai

For pilgrims and devotees from Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka carries a special significance — as the Lanka of King Ravana from the Valmiki Ramayana. The Ramayana Trail in Sri Lanka connects over 20 sites tied to events from the epic, and many of them are within easy reach of the standard Colombo–Kandy–Nuwara Eliya circuit.

Sita Amman Temple (Sita Eliya): Near Nuwara Eliya, this temple is built on the site where Sita Mata is believed to have been held captive by Ravana. Hanuman's footprints can be seen on a rock face near the temple stream.
Ashoka Vatika / Hakgala Botanical Garden: The garden near Nuwara Eliya identified as the Ashoka Vatika of the Ramayana — where Ravana kept Sita captive. Home to over 10,000 plant species.

Divurumpola Temple (Welimada): Believed to be the exact site of Sita's Agni Pariksha — where she walked through fire to prove her purity. Locals still come here to take oaths, continuing the ancient tradition.
Ravana Cave (Ella): A cave near Ella town believed to have been used by Ravana to keep Sita. About 2 km from Ella town — a short drive and walk.
Munneswaram Temple (Chilaw): Where Lord Rama is said to have prayed to Lord Shiva after defeating Ravana. One of the five ancient Ishwarams of Sri Lanka.

We offer a dedicated Sri Lanka Ramayana Tour Package from Chennai (7 Nights / 8 Days starting from INR 36,900) covering these and more Ramayana-connected sites across the island. Contact us for details.
Sri Lanka Holiday Package Price from Chennai

The cost of Sri Lanka tour from Chennai starts from INR 24,900 and goes up to INR 58,500, which is also inclusive of Sri Lanka mythological heritage tour from India. Our tour plans are extensively customizable and include your hotel bills, food charges, visa assistance, and local transfer.

Practical Travel Information for Sri Lanka

Currency: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). As of 2026, roughly 1 INR ≈ 4.1–4.3 LKR. Carry Indian Rupees or USD for exchange — exchange counters are available at Colombo airport and in major cities. ATMs (Visa/Mastercard) work well in Colombo, Kandy, and other tourist areas.

Can Indians use UPI in Sri Lanka? Not widely. UPI is not yet accepted at most Sri Lankan merchants. Carry cash (LKR) or use an international Visa/Mastercard debit or credit card. Some larger hotels in Colombo accept INR, but do not count on it.

Mobile network & SIM: Dialog and Mobitel are the two main networks with the best coverage across the island. A local SIM (with data) costs around LKR 500–1,000 (approximately ₹120–250) and is available at the airport on arrival. eSIM options via Airalo and similar providers also work for Sri Lanka.
Time zone: Sri Lanka Standard Time (SLST) is UTC+5:30 — same as Indian Standard Time (IST). No time adjustment needed.
Power plugs: Sri Lanka uses Type D and Type G sockets (the same Type D used across India). Your Indian plugs will work in most hotels without an adaptor.

Language: Sinhala and Tamil are both official languages. English is widely spoken in tourist areas, hotels, and restaurants. Tamil speakers from Chennai will find communication comfortable in many parts of northern and eastern Sri Lanka.
Is Sri Lanka Safe for Indian Tourists?

Yes, Sri Lanka is a safe and popular destination for Indian tourists. The country has been welcoming a rising number of Indian visitors — India is currently the top source market for Sri Lanka tourism in 2026. Here are a few standard safety guidelines:

items: Tourist areas including Colombo, Kandy, Galle, Nuwara Eliya, and Sigiriya are generally safe for solo travellers, families, and couples.
Avoid isolated beaches after dark — stick to well-lit, populated beach areas in the evenings.
Use licensed taxis or app-based cabs (PickMe and Uber both operate in Sri Lanka). Agree on a fare before getting into non-metered tuk-tuks.
Follow local temple regulations — remove footwear, cover shoulders and knees, and do not pose with your back to Buddha statues for photos.
Keep a copy of your passport and ETA approval in your email or phone — local authorities may ask for ID at some heritage sites.
Sri Lanka's healthcare in Colombo and major cities is reasonably good. Carry basic medicines, especially if travelling with children or seniors.

blocks.text: Essential Tips for Sri Lanka Trip
Here are some travel tips that you might find useful:

items: Although cards are accepted at all modern restaurants and hotels, it's still a good practice to carry cash in Sri Lanka's home currency — the Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR).
Respect the local customs in Sri Lanka. Be respectful to Buddha idols and images, which are quite common across the island.
Book your Sri Lanka vacation packages from Chennai according to the region you want to visit in the country.
Mosquitoes can give you trouble. Carry mosquito repellents and mosquito nets with you to protect yourself from insect bites.
Do try the Sri Lankan delicacies: Kottu Roti, Egg Hoppers, Gotu Kola Sambol, Wambatu Moju, Lamprais, Ambul Thiyal, and Polos.
Do not drink tap water while you're in the country. Always carry packaged drinking water with you.
From 25 May 2026, ETA is completely free for Indian nationals. Apply at eta.gov.lk before your trip. Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months from your travel date.

blocks.text: Why Book Sri Lanka Tour from Chennai with My Quick Trippers?

Our packages are meticulously crafted by travel experts who have years of experience in the industry, especially for international tours. From the luxury Sri Lanka honeymoon tours to affordable Sri Lanka group tour from India, we provide it all! With us, you get pre-arranged vehicles, best hotel deals, and tailor-made itineraries, in addition to 24x7 customer support and fully professional services. Q1. What are the visa requirements for Indians traveling to Sri Lanka?

Indians travelling to Sri Lanka need an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorisation) — apply online at eta.gov.lk. From 25 May 2026, the ETA is completely free for Indian nationals. The application is still mandatory, but the fee has been waived. The ETA is valid for 30 days with double entry. Carry your passport (valid for 6+ months) and a printed ETA approval for smoother immigration.
Q2. Which is the cheapest month to visit Sri Lanka?

The cheapest months to travel to Sri Lanka are the shoulder seasons. If you are looking for a budget plan or even an affordable Sri Lanka romantic tour under ₹39,999, then visit in the window of May to October.
Q3. What is the cost of the ferry from Nagapattinam to Sri Lanka?

The Nagapattinam–Kankesanthurai ferry (Sivaganga) runs from Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu to Kankesanthurai port in Jaffna, Sri Lanka. One-way fare: ₹5,000 (general class) or ₹7,500 (premium class). The journey takes approximately 3.5 hours covering 60 nautical miles. Departs Nagapattinam at 7 AM, arrives Kankesanthurai at ~11 AM. Book at indsri.com. Note: Nagapattinam is ~300 km from Chennai and the ferry arrives in Jaffna, not Colombo. Schedules are subject to weather — verify before booking.
Q4. How much is the ticket price from Chennai to Sri Lanka?

Economy class airfare from Chennai to Colombo is around INR 7,500 upwards and business class approximately INR 22,500 and above. Fares vary by season — they are lower in May–September and higher around Pongal, summer holidays, and December. IndiGo, SriLankan Airlines, and Air India operate the Chennai (MAA)–Colombo (CMB) route. Contact us for round-trip Sri Lanka holiday packages from Chennai with flight.
Q5. How many hours does it take to reach from Chennai to Sri Lanka?

By air, it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours from Chennai to Colombo. If you're travelling by ferry from Nagapattinam, the crossing to Kankesanthurai (Jaffna) takes approximately 3.5 hours — departs 7 AM, arrives ~11 AM.
Q6. How long is a Sri Lanka trip from Chennai?

A 4 to 7 day trip is usually sufficient to explore major cities, hills, and beaches. A 4-day Sri Lanka package from Chennai covers Colombo and Kandy. A 5-day or 6-day package adds Nuwara Eliya and Bentota. For the full experience including Galle, Ella, and Sigiriya, a 7-day Sri Lanka holiday from Chennai works best.
Q7. Is Sri Lanka a good honeymoon destination?

Yes, Sri Lanka is a great honeymoon destination and is one of the most romantic places near India. You can enjoy a fun beach day at Bentota, enjoy the nightlife in Colombo and have candlelight dinners at its posh restaurants. The island country is ideal for couples!
Q8. Is Sri Lanka safe for Indian tourists?

Yes, Sri Lanka is safe for Indian tourists and is currently one of the most visited international destinations for travellers from South India. Tourist areas are well-policed, hotels are accustomed to Indian guests, and Tamil is spoken in many parts of the north and east. Stick to licensed cabs, follow temple dress codes, and carry a copy of your ETA and passport for site visits.
Q9. What kind of food can I expect on Sri Lanka holiday from Chennai?

Sri Lanka offers you everything from South Indian specialities to seafood to even international cuisine. There are also a lot of restaurants here that serve Indian food, especially in the tourist hotspots.
Q10. Can I customize Sri Lanka travel package from Chennai?

Yes, My Quick Trippers offers you customizable Sri Lanka packages, where you can adjust the length of your trip, pick the hotel of your choice, and even opt for add-on experiences like safari and boat rides!
Q11. Is Sri Lanka expensive for Indian tourists?

Sri Lanka is one of the more affordable international destinations for Indians. A mid-range 5-day Sri Lanka trip from Chennai — including flights, hotel, meals, and transfers — can be done comfortably for ₹35,000–₹55,000 per person. Budget travellers can do it for less; luxury packages go higher. The Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR) is weaker than INR, so your money goes further on food, tuk-tuks, and local shopping.
Q12. Which currency should I carry for Sri Lanka?

Carry Indian Rupees and exchange them to Sri Lankan Rupees (LKR) at the airport or authorised exchange counters in Colombo. As of 2026, roughly 1 INR ≈ 4.1–4.3 LKR. You can also carry USD for exchange — it is widely accepted. ATMs (Visa/Mastercard) work in most cities. UPI is not widely accepted at Sri Lankan merchants yet.
Q13. Can Indians use UPI in Sri Lanka?

Not widely. UPI is not yet accepted at most shops, restaurants, or hotels in Sri Lanka. Use a Visa or Mastercard-enabled debit or credit card for card payments, and carry local LKR cash for smaller purchases and tuk-tuks. Some large hotels in Colombo accept INR, but it is safer not to rely on this.
Q14. Do Indians need travel insurance for Sri Lanka?

Travel insurance is not mandatory for Sri Lanka but it is strongly recommended — especially for medical coverage, trip cancellation, and lost baggage. Medical care in Colombo is reasonably good but costs can be high for foreigners without insurance. Look for a policy that covers emergency medical evacuation. blocks.text: Chardham Yatra Packages 2026 are designed for devotees seeking blessings at Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath in Uttarakhand . These itineraries include the required services to complete this soulful journey safely and securely.

Char Dham Yatra is one of the most sacred pilgrimages in Hinduism and is best undertaken in May, June, September, and October. Every year, millions of pilgrims, not only from India but also from foreign countries, undertake this sacred Himalayan pilgrimage. Moreover, this spiritual voyage requires careful planning due to high altitudes, changing weather, and limited seasonal accessibility.

Starting Points: Delhi, Haridwar, Rishikesh, Dehradun

Chardham Yatra 2026 Registration — How to Register

Registration for Char Dham Yatra 2026 is mandatory for all pilgrims — without a valid Yatra registration number, you cannot book helicopter tickets or get VIP Darshan passes. Register well in advance to avoid last-minute complications.

items: Create an account using your mobile number and email ID.
Enter details of all pilgrims in your group — name, age, ID type, ID number.
Upload a scanned copy of your government-issued photo ID.
Select your planned travel dates and preferred starting point.
Submit and receive your Yatra Registration Number and QR Code via email and SMS.
Keep the QR code handy — it is checked at helipads, temple entry gates, and registration counters.

items: Foreign nationals must register with their passport details.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit on Chardham Tour
Besides the four main shrines, the pilgrimage opens a gateway to visit other nearby places as well.

rows: Yamunotri Temple Surya Kund Divya Shila
Main shrine dedicated to Goddess Yamuna. Boiling hot spring used to prepare Prasad; believed to have healing properties. Sacred stone pilgrims must worship before entering the temple.
Gangotri Temple Bhagirath Shila Tapovan Gaumukh

Main temple where Ganga is believed to have first descended; built of white granite. Rock where King Bhagirath meditated to bring Ganga to Earth. Picturesque meadow with snow-capped peaks; ideal for nature lovers. Glacier source of the Ganga River; popular trekking site.
Kedarnath Temple Adi Shankaracharya Samadhi Gaurikund Rudra Cave

Ancient Shiva temple built by the Pandavas, revived by Adi Shankaracharya. Final resting place of Adi Shankaracharya. Starting point of the Kedarnath trek; where Goddess Parvati meditated. Meditation cave; gained fame after PM Modi's 2019 visit.
Badrinath Temple Tapt Kund Mana Village Charan Paduka Joshimath

Main shrine of Lord Vishnu; self-manifested black stone idol. Sacred hot spring for pre-Darshan purification. Last village of India before Tibet border — must visit, often missed. Boulder bearing Lord Vishnu's footprints; panoramic valley views. Winter seat of Lord Badrinath; skiing, trekking, and spiritual significance.

blocks.text: How Tough Is the Journey to Char Dham?
Char Dham pilgrimage is mentally invigorating yet physically tiresome. It involves lengthy road journeys, rough geography, high altitude, and erratic weather in the upper Himalayan areas.
5-6 km walk from Jankichatti, steep in places. Pony, Palki, and Pitthu services available.

16-17 km uphill walk from Gaurikund, 8-12 hours, oxygen scarcity at the summit. Helicopter, pony, palki, and Kandi services available for those who cannot trek.
Road accessible, minimal walking. Challenge is low temperatures and thin air at high altitude.

blocks.text: Medical Advisory for Senior Citizens and Health-Restricted Pilgrims

Completing the Char Dham Yatra is a deeply personal and spiritual aspiration — and helicopter packages make it possible for pilgrims who may not be able to manage the physical demands of road travel and trekking. However, even the helicopter Yatra involves some exposure to high altitude. Here is what you need to know:

items: Heart patients with controlled conditions: Safe for helicopter Yatra in most cases. Mandatory requirement: written fitness certificate from your cardiologist before departure.
Emergency oxygen: Available on all our helicopter flights and at our ground support stations.
Altitude: Kedarnath helipad is at 3,583 m. Even with helicopter travel, some mild breathlessness is normal at this altitude for unacclimatised individuals.
Patients with uncontrolled blood pressure or recent surgery (within 6 months): Consult your doctor before booking — your safety is our priority.
Diabetic pilgrims: Carry insulin and all medications. Our hotel kitchens can accommodate dietary requirements — inform us at booking.
Pulse oximeters: Recommended for all pilgrims above 60 — carry one to monitor oxygen saturation at altitude.
Our ground coordinators are trained in basic first aid and altitude sickness management. They accompany every senior group throughout the journey.
Walk slowly and do not panic.
Hydrate continuously with water and ORS.
Do not smoke or drink alcohol.
Take 20-30 minute rest breaks on the Kedarnath trek.
Carry doctor-recommended medication and portable oxygen.
Dress in layers to handle changing temperatures.

blocks.text: Helicopter Slot Availability and Priority Rules

Of the four shrines, Kedarnath is the only one directly reachable by helicopter. A flight from Sersi, Phata, or Guptkashi to Kedarnath is about 7-10 minutes — ideal for senior citizens, families with young children, and pilgrims with health or time restrictions.

Helicopter tickets to Kedarnath are scarce — especially in peak season (May-June). All official bookings are handled through the IRCTC portal only, released in small batches. Tickets sell in minutes. No third-party or offline bookings allowed. Book as early as possible.

blocks.text: Helpful Tips for Char Dham Yatra 2026

items: Register early — complete Yatra registration at registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in before booking anything else.
Book hotels and transport in advance — peak season (May-June) accommodations fill up 2-3 months early.
Get a medical check-up — especially if you are above 55 or have any chronic condition.
Buy travel insurance — covers weather delays, medical evacuation, and trip cancellation.
Pack layers — temperatures at Kedarnath and Badrinath drop sharply at night even in summer.
Carry valid photo ID (Aadhaar/Passport) for all group members.
Warm jacket, thermal wear, and gloves — essential even in May-June.
Waterproof rain jacket — mountain weather is unpredictable.
Comfortable trekking shoes with good grip.
Personal medications — altitude sickness tablets (Diamox), blood pressure, diabetes medications.
Pulse oximeter — highly recommended for pilgrims above 60.
Portable oxygen can — available at medical stores in Haridwar and Rishikesh.
Sunscreen, sunglasses, and lip balm — UV intensity is high at altitude.
Dry snacks, ORS sachets, and a refillable water bottle.
Start each day's drive or trek early — mountain roads get congested by mid-morning.
Do not rush Darshan — plan at least 2-3 hours per temple for a calm experience.
ATMs are unreliable at high altitudes — carry sufficient cash from Haridwar or Rishikesh.
Mobile network coverage is weak at many points — download offline maps before departure.
Eat light at high altitude — heavy meals can cause discomfort and nausea.
Respect local customs — dress modestly and observe temple etiquette.
Do not litter — these are sacred and ecologically sensitive areas.
Opt for helicopter packages — eliminates trekking and significantly reduces physical strain.
Inform your coordinator about any health condition at the time of booking.
Request ground-floor hotel rooms to avoid stair climbing at altitude.
Carry a copy of all prescriptions and a one-page medical summary with emergency contacts.

Q1: What is Char Dham Yatra?
Ans: It is a sacred Hindu Himalayan pilgrimage covering Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath.
Q2: Are there any helicopter services to cover the entire trip?
Ans: Yes, to cover all Char Dhams, avail heli service from Dehradun.
Q3: Which tour operators provide the best services for Chardham Yatra packages?
Ans: My Quick Trippers, Chardham Tour, Atlas Travel, Chardham Hotels, and Udan Aviation
Q4: What is the opening date for Chardham sites for 2026?
Q5: Which helicopter agents are trustworthy for the Chardham Yatra by helicopter?
Ans: Pawan Hans, Udan Aviation, YatrabyHelicopter, Mr. Pilot, Heritage Aviation, Global Connect Aviation.
Q6: Is online registration for Chardham compulsory?
Ans: Yes, as it helps track your identity and promotes safety and security.
Q7: Is the Chardham Yatra by helicopter safe for families with senior citizens?
Ans: Yes, if the booking is done through DGCA-approved operators and passengers pass the medical fitness check, then there is nothing to worry about.
Q8: What type of accommodation can we get during this soulful journey?
Ans: It ranges from standard to premium depending on location and package type.
Q9: Can the Char Dham Yatra itinerary be customized?
Ans: Yes, itinerary customization depends on travel dates, group size, and preferred travel mode.
Q10: How much does 4 Dham Yatra cost?
Ans: It would cost you between ₹24,000–₹45,000 by road for 9–12 days and ₹2.2–2.35 lakhs by helicopter for 2–5 days, depending on the package and inclusions.
Q11: Is a pre-Char Dham Yatra medical check-up compulsory?
Ans: It is not a compulsory medical check-up, but it is highly encouraged for older citizens and travelers with prior health issues.
Q12: Is it possible to do the Char Dham Yatra in stages and not in a single trip?
Ans: Char Dham Yatra can indeed be done over several visits in phases.
Q13: Do Char Dham Yatra have ATM/digital payment facilities?
Ans: In the remote location, there are no ATM and digital payment options.
Q14: What is the weather unpredictability of Char Dham Yatra?
Ans: The weather conditions of the Char Dham can change in a few hours based on the climatic conditions in the high Himalayan weather, particularly in the afternoon.
Q15: Does the Char Dham route have coverage of network connectivity?
Ans: Most of the Char Dham areas have inconsistent mobile network connectivity.
Q16: Can oxygen cylinders be easily found at Char Dham Yatra?
Ans: Oxygen cylinders can be purchased at large halts and medical camps.
Q17: Can I postpone the trip mid-journey because of some health or weather problems?
Ans: Yes, the trip can be delayed or rearranged on the way due to health reasons or weather inconveniences, under the conditions of availability and local norms.
Q18: Is the travel insurance useful in the Char Dham Yatra?
Ans: Yes, because it will cover any medical emergency, trip interruption, or weather cancellation.
Q19: Are night stays near the temples comfortable for pilgrims?
Ans: Yes, they are, but do check the locality before booking.
Q20: How important is it to start physical fitness training for this soulful yatra?
Ans: Physical activity practice sessions can assist the traveler to deal better with trekking and high altitude conditions.
Q21: What is included in the Chardham Yatra package?

Ans: Our all-inclusive packages include accommodation (standard or deluxe hotels), daily breakfast and dinner, AC/non-AC vehicle transfers, VIP Darshan passes at all four temples, helicopter tickets (in selected packages), airport/railway station transfers, all permit and entry charges, and basic medical support. GST, personal expenses, pony/palki charges, and travel insurance are excluded.
Q22: How many days does Chardham Yatra take?
Ans: By road: 9-12 days. By helicopter: 2-5 days. Our standard helicopter package covers 5 Nights and 6 Days, visiting all four Dhams.
Q23: Is the advance payment refundable?

Ans: Yes, as per our cancellation policy. In case of weather cancellations or natural events beyond control, alternate travel dates are offered. For full details, please refer to our Terms and Conditions page.
Q24: What special arrangements are there for senior citizens?

Ans: We provide wheelchair assistance at helipads and major transit points, priority helicopter boarding, VIP Darshan passes to avoid long queues, senior-friendly ground-floor hotel rooms, a dedicated on-ground coordinator throughout the journey, and emergency oxygen support where required.
Q25: What documents are required for Chardham Yatra?

Ans: All pilgrims must carry a valid government-issued photo ID (Aadhaar Card, Passport, or Voter ID). A Chardham Yatra Registration Number from the official Uttarakhand government portal (registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in) is mandatory. Foreign nationals must carry their passport at all times.
Q26: Can heart patients do Chardham Yatra by helicopter?

Ans: Yes, in most cases - provided the patient has a written fitness certificate from their cardiologist before travel. Emergency oxygen is available on all our helicopter flights. Passengers with severe or uncontrolled cardiac conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure, or major surgery within the last 6 months must consult their doctor before booking.
Q27: Are helicopter tickets booked through IRCTC or through you?

Ans: The Kedarnath helicopter shuttle tickets (for the trek bypass) are booked through the IRCTC Heli Yatra portal (heliyatra.irctc.co.in). For full Chardham helicopter tour packages - including accommodation, ground transfers, and VIP Darshan at all four Dhams - book directly with us and we handle all arrangements.
Q28: What is the best time to book Chardham Yatra packages?

Ans: For May-June peak season: book 2-3 months in advance. For September-October post-monsoon season: 4-6 weeks advance booking is usually sufficient. Helicopter slots on IRCTC fill up within minutes of release - book as early as possible.
Q29: What is the price difference between road and helicopter Chardham Yatra?

Ans: Road Chardham Yatra starts from approximately Rs.84,000 per couple for a budget 10-day package. Helicopter Chardham Yatra starts from approximately Rs.2,20,000 per person for a 6-day package. The helicopter option saves 5-6 days, eliminates all trekking, and is ideal for senior citizens, NRIs, and time-constrained pilgrims.

blocks.text: One of the most famous multi-day Honeymoon Tour in the Himachal. Mesmerizing Shimla & Adventure in Manali: explore Himachali cultures. Create Lifelong memories. We all go on many trips in a lifetime, but honeymoon is something special, always. Honeymoon is the most important trip of one’s life. It is the first journey of you two being together giving your lives a new start. It is meant to be more than perfect, as these memorable days of your lives ain’t going to return ever. In short, you plan it, we execute it. With our 10 days / 9 nights tour you have the most enticing and valuable offers for all the newlyweds. Bloom your love amidst the most fascinating & exquisite locations of Himachal the wonderland.
Day 1 : Delhi – Shimla (330 kms / Approx.9 Hrs)
You are greeted by My Quick Trippers representative and transfer you to Shimla, where on arrival, you will check into your hotel. The rest of the evening is at leisure, Overnight stay at Shimla.
Day 2 : In Shimla – Day Excursion to Kufri (20 kms / Approx. 1 hrs)

Morning proceed for the sightseeing of Shimla covering Kalbadevi Temple, Jakhu Temple, Hanuman Temple or stop for a while at the beautiful stained-glass-windows of Christ Church, which was built in the 1850 ‘s.

Afternoon excursion to Kufri a 30 Minutes’ drive from Shimla, an exotica of nature as a place surrounded by dense forest and snow caped mountains amidst virgin peaks and natures flora and fauna where one can completely relax and tune oneself for natural beauty, Evening free to enjoy the scenic beauty of Kufri. Fagu, Indira Gandhi Holiday Home and enjoy horse riding in the apple orchids. Return to the Hotel Rest of the day is free to explore various scenic sights or visit mall road and shopping, Night stay at Hotel.
Morning drive to Manali. Enroute visit Kullu valley, Beas River, Dashehra maidan etc. Evening free, Night stay in Manali.

The Kullu- is spread in the entire Kullu Valley which is lavishly gifted with superb scenic wealth. Kullu also known as ‘Valley of Gods’ has numerous temples. Kullu valley offers a scenic charm of peaceful wooded glades and rivers through the rocks. The Dussehra of Kullu is world famous. The ancient Hindus regarded Kullu as the farthest limit of human habitation ‘Kulantapitha’ and its original name finds mention in the epics, The Ramayana and Mahabharat as well as the Vishnu Purana. Kullu, which is located on the bank of river Beas is the Central point of this tourist complex. Running North to South, the main river valley is only 80 km. long and 2 km. at its broadest, yet a fairly wide area is open to the visitors to enjoy the spectacle of variegated mountain scenery. The deodar-fringed grassy Maidan, Dhalpur, is a stage for many colorful fairs.

Today morning, proceed on a day excursion to the Rohtang pass. If roads to Rohtang pass are closed, then visit snow point where ponies/horses can be hired directly, later visit Solang Valley where Himachal’s best ski slopes can be found( here you can enjoy paragliding, horse-riding, scooter riding etc. on direct payment basis). The rest of the day is free to explore this scenic town, Overnight stay at Hotel.

Today we will progress to Dharamsala. The plan for the day is to shop in the bazaar for Tibetan handicrafts. Here you can full your bags with exquisite Tibetan handicrafts, Tibetan carpets, garments and other trinkets. Stay overnight at hotel in Dharamsala.

Morning, after breakfast visit a quaint little town, Mcleodganj. Also known as “Little Tibet” Mcleodganj is the place of residence of Dalai Lama. Later transfer to Dalhousie. Overnight stay at Dalhousie.
Day 7 : In Dalhousie – Excursion to Khajjiar (23 kms/approx.1hrs)

In morning, drive to Khajjiar (commonly called as mini-Swiss of Himachal), a picturesque spot set amidst a backdrop of dense pines, deodars and lush green meadows. Khajjiar is exquisitely nestled down in the foothills of the imposing Dhauladhar ranges of the western Himalayas providing a panoramic and breathtaking view to the visitors. Khajjiar is part of the notified Kalatop – Khajjiar sanctuary. And later proceed to Chamba. Stands on the right bank of the river Ravi, It is well known for its splendid architecture and as the base for numerous excursions. Night stay at hotel.
After breakfast visit Dalhousie local, later drive to Amritsar. Evening you can become a part of Wagah Border. Overnight stay at Amritsar.

After Breakfast, Start your city tour with the blessings of Golden Temple-the most important Sikh shrine also known as Harmandir Sahib and Durbar Sahib. Then visit Jallianwala Bagh- the place that reminds every Indian of the brutal and heartless massacre by British general Dyer. Later Transfer to Chandigarh. Overnight at Chandigarh-Hotel.

Morning Visit Chandigarh Local like Sukhna Lake, Rock garden, later transfers to Delhi to catch your train for boarding onward journey. Thanks you for your patronage and looks forward to serving you again in the near future.

blocks.text: Q1. What Should I Pack For My Trip To Himachal?

Ans. Wearing woollens in Himachal Pradesh is one of the most crucial travel advice for the region because it can become chilly up in the mountains of Northern India. In addition to thick tee shirts and bottoms, one may decide to wear a variety of coats, sweaters, scarves, and woollen socks.
Q2. What Makes Himachal Such A Stunning Place?
Ans. The beautiful splendour of Himachal Pradesh is well-known for its spectacular snow-capped mountains, lush green forests, and gushing rivers and streams.
Q3. Where Is Himachal’s Heart Located?
Ans. Heart of Himachal Pradesh: Sundernagar.
Q4. Which Location In Himachal Pradesh Is Dubbed “Queen Of Hills”?

Ans. In essence, it turned into a second home for the British, who established it as their summer capital. Shimla was then appropriately dubbed the “Queen of Hills” for its location on a crescent-shaped series of seven hill.
Q5. Which Region Of Himachal Attracts The Most Tourists?
Ans. The most popular vacation spots in Himachal Pradesh are Shimla, Manali, and Dharamshala.
