blocks.text: Special Group Tour Package for Karnataka

Southern India is truly a treat for every traveler since it is dotted with numerous holy shrines, sculptures that are intricately created and natural beauty which is incomparable. My Quick Trippers presents you with the Karnataka special group tour package planning for 10 days and 9 nights where you will be immersed in the true spirit of southern India.
Once you arrive in Bangalore you will be made to proceed towards your hotel after which a brief sightseeing tour of the city will commence.

You will be taken to Cubbon Park, which is a lush green park and pans over a massive area of 300 acres. A wonderful site for nature lovers and peace seekers this place is considered to be the lungs of Bangalore.

You will then be made to proceed towards Lalbagh botanical gardens which houses India’s largest tropical plants collection and also has a lake, making it the perfect place for families to spend some quality time.

You will then be taken to Bangalore Palace, which was built in the year 1878 using intricate designer architectural form and the massive ground in front of the palace is used for holding public events.
Before heading back to your hotel you will be made to visit the famous and holy ISKCON temple.
Day 2 : Bangalore – Shravanabelagola – Hassan – Belur – Halebidu – Hassan

Early in the morning, your 3-hour journey towards Shravanabelagola will commence which is an extremely important Jain pilgrimage center and showcases the peak of architectural brilliance. Here you will be made to visit the famous Gommateshwara Bahubali which is the main attraction. It is also the place of death for Chandragupta Maurya after he became a monk and took up an ascetic way of life.

After paying your respects here you will be driven to Hassan, which is at a distance of just an hour from here and had served as the seat for Hoysala Empire. The entire district is dotted with numerous ancient important temples. After getting checked in to your hotel you will be driven to Belur, which is also at a mere distance of an hour from Hassan.
In Belur you will be made to visit the Chennakeshava Temple complex which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and highly revered among the South Indian population.

From Belur you will proceed towards Halebidu, which is located at a distance of half an hour and had served as the capital for the Hoysala Empire during the 12th century. Here you will be made to visit Kedareshwara and Hoysaleswara Temple. After this holy temple tour, you will be made to drive back to Hassan where you will be spending your night, since there are no hotels or accommodation places available in Belur or Halebidu.

Your morning will commence after breakfast where you will be made to proceed towards the sacred 400-year-old, Sri Nimishamba (an incarnation of goddess Parvati) temple and is at a distance of 2km from Srirangapatna by the banks of River Cauvery.
Entry Fees: free entry for all

Your next location will be the famous UNESCO world heritage site of Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple, which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and houses a large towering Rajagopuram which rises up to a height of 237 feet. The holy temple is located on the confluence point of River Cauvery and Kollidam on an island.
Temple Timings: 9 am to 12 pm; 1:15 pm to 6 pm; 6:45 pm to 9 pm
*during festival seasons the darshan timings are prone to change.

You will then be taken to witness some of the major attractions in Mysore starting with a visit to the Chamundeshwari Temple, which is located atop Chamundi hills and at a distance of 13 km from Mysore. In order to reach the temple you will be required to climb 1,008 stairs and halfway across you will encounter the statue of Nandi the bull which is the vehicle of Lord Shiva. This site is not only a prime pilgrimage destination but it also rewards the visitors with a breathtaking panoramic view of the Mysore city lying below.
Temple Timings: 7:30 am to 2 pm; 3:30 pm to 6 pm.

Your next stop at Mysore will be the 14th-century magnificent palace of Mysore. This palace is the 2nd most visited tourist attraction in India. The entire palace is adorned with beautiful and intricate artworks, majestic domes and gateways and designer carvings and engravings making it a must visit site.
Finally, you will be headed back to your hotel.
Early in the morning, post breakfast, you will be made to proceed towards the magical city of Coorg which is at a distance of 2 hours and 45 mines.

En route you will be made to visit Talakaveri, which is considered to be the birth place of River Cauvery. One can take holy dip in the water within the temple premises which was constructed to mark the sacred place.

You will then finally proceed towards one of the most pleasant hill stations in India, Coorg. Here, before checking in, you will be made to visit the famous Abbey falls, where the cascading water plunges down from a massive height of 70 feet. There are 200 steps that lead downwards towards the base of the falls from its main entrance.
Your next holy stop will be at one of the most prominent Hindu temple for Lord Shiva, Omkareshwara temple. This ancient temple is situated in the town of Madikeri amongst a fish-filled pond.
Temple Timings: 6:30 am to 12:30 pm; 12:30 pm to 3:30 pm; 3:30 pm to 8:30 pm
You will then be headed back to your allotted hotel in Coorg.
Day 5 : Coorg – Kukke (73 km) – Dharmasthala (60 km) – Kalasa (90 km) – Hornadu (6 km)

Early in the morning, you will be driven to Kukke Subramanya Temple, which is dedicated to the lord of serpents, Subramanya. It is situated on the lush green slopes of Western Ghats amongst the dense green forest and by the bank of River Kumaradhara.

After Darshan, you will be taken to Dharmasthala, where you will be made to visit the sacred, massive 57 feet Gommateshwara statue (one of the tallest standing statues in the world), which is a monolithic structure and is dedicated to Jain god Bahubali.
Timings: Open at all hours for visitation.
Entry Fees: free entry for all

Your next and final pious location for the day will be at Kalasa, Kalaseshwara Temple, which is a small Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and offers a magnificent view of the surrounding hills due to its location atop a hill.
Temple Timings: 7:30 am to 1 pm; 3:30 pm to 8:30 pm
You will finally head towards Hornadu where you will be checked in to your hotel.
Day 6 : Hornadu – Sringeri (42 km) – Kateel (92 km) – Mangalore (18 km)
You will be taken for an early morning darshan at Annapoorneshwari Temple, which is located on the bank of River Bhadra among the lush greenery of Western Ghats and is dedicated to goddess Parvati.
Temple Timings: 6:30 am to 9 am; 11 am to 2 pm; 7 pm to 9:30 pm

After the holy Darshan, you will be driven to Sringeri which is an ideal spot for every nature lover or photography enthusiast. Here you will savour the refreshing surrounding nature at Agumbe Ghat. After spending some quality time here, you will finally be headed to Mangalore.
En route you will be made to stop at Kateel for darshan at the famous Kateel Durga Mandir popularly known as Shri Durgaparameshwari Temple which is located by the River Nandini.
Upon arrival at Mangalore you will be straightaway headed to your allotted hotel in Mangalore after which you will enjoy the pleasant and relaxing sunset by the beach.
If time permits you will be taken to Mangala Devi Temple, a 9th century temple which is dedicated to the Hindu goddess Shakti.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 1 pm; 4 pm to 8:30 pm

Early in the morning, before breakfast, you will be made to proceed towards Kudupu Sri Anantha Padmanabha Temple, which is located at a distance of 10 km from the main city of Mangalore and is dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
It is vital for you to make reservations for the darshan before heading to the temple.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 12:30 pm; 5 pm to 8:30 pm
After the puja rituals you will be made to head back to your hotel where you will have your breakfast before proceeding towards Udupi.

At Udupi you will be made to visit Sri Krishna Matha mandir, which is a famous Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Krishna and Dvaita Matha. You will then be made to visit Anantheshwara Temple which is known for being over 1,000 years old and is located really close to Krishna Matha Temple.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 8 pm (it does not close for afternoon)
Make sure you wear appropriate clothing while visiting the temple since it is extremely important.

You will finally be made to head towards Murdeshwar, en route you will be made to visit Anegudde (30 km), which is home to one of the most famous Lord Ganesha temple, Sri Vinayaka Devasthana and one of the seven ‘Mukti Sthalas’ in Karnataka.

You will then proceed towards Mookambika (before reaching Murdeshwar) in Kollur, and the temple is dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi or also known as Mookambika Devi. Dating back to 800 AD this temple is amidst a pleasant and green location.

Finally, after reaching Murdeshwar you will be made to check in to your hotel before heading out for a holy visit at one of the main attractions here which is the world’s second-tallest Lord Shiva statue (123 feet).
You will then be headed towards Murudeshwara Temple which sits atop Kanduka hill and surrounded by Arabian Sea on three sides, it is also adorned with intricate carvings all over.
Temple Timings: 3 am to 1 pm; 3 pm to 8 pm
In the evening you will be taken for spending some peaceful and relaxing time by the Murdeshwar beach, before heading back to your hotel.
Day 8 : Murdeshwar – Idagunji – Gokarna – Goa (240 km)
Your morning journey towards Goa will commence while stopping en route at Idagunji and Gokarna.

At Idagunji you will be made to visit the famous Ganpati temple, and it sees numerous visitors on an everyday basis. It is also located by the holy banks of River Sharavathi and was built in 4th-5th century CE.
Temple Timings: 6 am to 1 pm; 3 pm and 8:30 pm

You will then proceed towards Gokarna, an important pilgrimage centers in Karnataka where you will be made to visit Mahabaleshwar temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple here is known for housing one of the original lingams in India making it a prime pilgrimage destination for Hindu devotees.
After darshan, you will be driven towards India’s party destination, Goa.
Upon arriving here you will be checked in to your hotel after which you will be free to watch the glorious setting sun while relaxing by the beach.

After breakfast in the morning, you will be taken for a sightseeing tour of South Goa which will start off with a visit to some of the most pristine beaches like, Miramar beach, Colva beach and Dona Paula beach. You will then be taken to one of the most regal and pious old churches at old Goa, Bom Jesus Basilica.
Old Goa is also home to Mangeshi temple (built in 1560), and is one of the largest and most frequently visited temples in Goa.

Finally, you will be made to go on a cruise on River Mandovi, which comprises of Goan dance, singing and music performances accompanied by delicious traditional Goan cuisines and is one of the prime things to do in Goa.

After breakfast, early in the morning, you will be made to proceed towards the UNESCO world heritage site of Hampi which is a group of monuments. Spread over an area of 4,100 hectares, the Hampi ruins are set by the banks of Tungabhadra River and the ruins here date back to 14the century.
Your journey will finally conclude here after being transferred to Hosapete Junction Railway Station.

Ans. Karnataka, located in the midst of the Western Ghats, the Deccan Plateau, and the Kannad Coast, is home to a variety of forests, beaches, waterfalls, coffee plantations, lakes, and other natural wonders. The state also has historically significant monuments and structures that draw visitors from all over the world.
Q2. When Is The Best Time To Visit Karnataka?

Ans. The best time to visit Karnataka and South India is from October to April. Because of the state's location in South India, the climate in Karnataka is generally mild throughout the year. Winters in Karnataka are mild, summers are hot and humid, and monsoon season arrives early.

item.name: Munnar Alleppey Tour Package – 4 Days – 3 Nights

blocks.text: The Munnar Alleppey Tour Package offers a perfect blend of hill station charm and serene backwaters over four days.

Your journey begins with a scenic drive from Cochin to Munnar, a picturesque hill station known for its lush tea plantations, wildlife sanctuaries, and cool climate. After settling into your hotel, you can relax and enjoy the natural beauty of Munnar before embarking on a sightseeing tour the next day. Explore the stunning Rajamalai National Park, the picturesque Mattupetty, and the scenic Top Station, known for its vast tea plantations and breathtaking views.

On Day 3, you'll travel to the tranquil town of Alleppey, famous for its backwaters, houseboats, and picturesque landscapes. After a relaxing evening on a houseboat or in a hotel, enjoy a delicious breakfast before heading back to Cochin on Day 4 for your departure. This 4-day, 3-night tour ensures a memorable experience, combining Munnar's natural beauty with the serenity of Alleppey’s backwaters, leaving you with lasting memories of Kerala's finest landscapes.

On arrival at Ernakulam Railway Station/Cochin Airport you will be welcomed by our representative and he will take you transfer to Munnar (Approx 155KMs/ 5hrs). Munnar means “The three rivers” which are situated at the confluence of three mountain streams Nallathanni, Muthirapuzha (Kannimalayar), and Kundala. Munnar is an attractive hill station full of natural resources located at an altitude of 6000 ft from sea level; this hill station is the part of Idukki district. The temperature stays here between the range of 5 °C to 25 °C in winter, and 15 °C to 25 °C in summer. There are several hot plantations of tea, cardamom, coffee, and other spices, dark forests & wildlife sanctuaries.

At arrival to Munnar just check in to your hotel, Welcome drink would be offered after you get fresh at the comfort of your room. Rest of the time enjoy leisure at the hotel, you can enjoy the scenic beauty of Munnar also. Stay overnight at the hotel in Munnar.
Post breakfast, get ready to experience an amazing local sightseeing of Munnar, which includes the visit to Rajamalai National Park, Mattupetty, and Top Station.

Rajamalai National Park- this national park is also known by the name of Eravikulam National Park, it is situated in Idukki, which is the bordering district of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. You can see some of the rare animal species can be found here- you may see Elephant, Nilgiri Marten, Nilgiri Langur, small-clawed otter and a rare tiger or leopard and the Nilgiri wood pigeon etc.
Mattupetty- It is approx 15 KMs away from Munnar, this is an extremely picturesque hill station.

Top Station– is placed at the approx distance of 40KMS from Munnar, and a well-known spot for the highest tea plantation in India. Later on arrive back and check in to the hotel. Overnight stay at the hotel.

Just finish your breakfast, we’ll take you to Alleppey (190 KMs / 5 Hrs). Alleppey is a scenic and popular town for its marvellous backwaters, it will attract you by its natural appeal. Alleppey is also known for its Boat races, Beaches, Houseboats, Marine Products and Coir Industry. In evening return back to your hotel/houseboat and check in to relax overnight.

In the morning time enjoy your breakfast at hotel/ houseboat. Later check out from the houseboat/hotel and we’ll take you towards the Cochin airport (90 KMs /2 hrs) / Ernakulam Railway Station (60KMs/1 Hr 15Min Approx) for your onward journey. We hope that you’ve enjoyed your tour and wish to arrange your next tour soon.

How to Reach Varanasi from Mumbai
Because Mumbai and Varanasi are far from each other, there are no direct buses between the two cities. The best options for travel are by train or by flight.

You can reach Varanasi from Mumbai by flight easily. You can fly directly from Mumbai (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport - BOM) to Varanasi (Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport - VNS).
Traveling to Varanasi from Mumbai is easy with options like IndiGo, Air India, Akasa Air, Air India Express, and SpiceJet. These flights take only 2 to 2.5 hours.
A train journey from Mumbai to Varanasi usually takes 25 to 31 hours. Trains like LTT Jaynagar Express, Mahanagari Express, LTT Banaras Express, and Kamayani Express run on this route.
Trains leave from Mumbai stations like Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT), CSMT, Bandra Terminus, and Dadar. In Varanasi they stop at Varanasi Junction (BSB) or DD Upadhyaya Junction.

blocks.text: FAQs for South India Temple Package
Q1. What Distinguishes The South Indian Temple?

Ans. The South Indian temple is essentially composed of a square-chambered sanctuary topped by a superstructure, tower, or spire and an attached pillared porch or hall (maapa, or maapam), surrounded by a peristyle of cells within a rectangular court.
Q2. Which Of The Following Is The Oldest Temple In South India?

Ans. The magnificent Siva temple of Thanjavur, built by Raja Raja I in 1009, and the Brihadisvara Temple of Gangaikonda Cholapuram, completed around 1030, are both fitting memorials to the two Chola emperors' material and military achievements.
Q3. In South India, Which City Is Also Known As The City Of Temples?

Ans. Although Kanchipuram is popularly known as the "City of a Thousand Temples," there is no prescribed circuit and no comprehensive temple listing or map to guide visitors. Rather, the thousands of pilgrims who visit the city every day are usually only familiar with the five most famous temples.
Q4. What Is South Indian Temple Food?

Ans. Temple food is always sattvic, which means it contains no meat, fish, onion, or garlic and is typically composed of grains, vegetables, fruits, and dairy products. "The food offered in South Indian temples is almost always cooked at the temple, unlike in North India, where you can offer store-bought food,"
Q5. What Is The South Indian Food Culture Like?

Ans. South Indian food dishes are generally lighter and revolve around a rice-based diet, as opposed to wheat-based North Indian food. Many of the world's most coveted ingredients, such as curry leaves, peppercorns, tamarind, coconut, and chilies, are grown in South India.

The Varanasi trip is not just an outing, it's a journey, a spiritual awakening! Once you get here, you immediately get surrounded by its sacred aura, embellished only by the sacred chants by the Ghats, the soft murmurs of the flowing Ganga River, and the ringing bells in the temples! If you seek divine blessing or want to explore the rich heritage of the country nestled in this holy city, then this tour is for you!

To go on a smooth and comfortable trip, book our Bangalore to Varanasi trip, where we'll take care of all your travel logistics ranging from meals to accommodation to flight. If you have any doubts, then feel free to give us a call!
Q1. What is the best time to see Ganga Aarti in Varanasi?
Ans. The Ganga Aarti in Varanasi starts at 6.30 pm every evening. It's advised that you reach here an hour earlier in order to secure a good viewing spot.
Q2. What is the fastest way to reach Varanasi from Bangalore?

Ans. The fastest way to reach Varanasi from Bangalore is by taking a flight from Kempegowda International Airport (BLR) to Varanasi Airport (VNS). The flights will take around 2.5 hours and will conveniently take you to the holy city of Varanasi.
Q3. How many days are enough for a Varanasi trip?

Ans. Usually, 4 to 5 days are ideal to cover Varanasi trip. In this span, you can easily cover the major attractions like Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Ghats, and more at a comfortable pace, without feeling rushed.
Q4. Are there direct trains from Bangalore to Varanasi?
Ans. Yes, there are direct trains available from Bangalore to Varanasi. Trains like Sanghamitra Express and Bagmati Express run regularly on this route.
Q5. What should I wear in Varanasi?

Ans. Varanasi is a holy city and is known for its spiritual legacy. Therefore, it's best if you wear modest clothes that cover your knees and legs. Don't wear revealing clothes here as this is a very sacred place. Traditional attire works best in this city.

blocks.text: Q1. Is Vietnam safe for Indian travellers?

Ans. Vietnam is generally considered safe for tourists. Use Grab for transport, stay in well-reviewed hotels, and carry document copies. Women travelling solo are comfortable in major tourist cities. Exercise standard caution as you would in any new country.
Q2. Do Indians need a visa for Vietnam in 2026?

Ans. Yes. Apply for an e-visa at evisa.gov.vn — valid for 90 days, costs USD 25 (single) or USD 50 (multiple entry). Processing takes 3–5 working days. Exception: Phu Quoc Island entry gives 30 days visa-free for Indians staying on the island.
Q3. What is the flight time from Mumbai to Vietnam?

Ans. Direct flights (when available) take approximately 5–6 hours. Connecting flights via Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, or Singapore take 7–10 hours total. VietJet and Vietnam Airlines operate select direct services — check current availability before booking.
Q4. What is the best time to visit Vietnam from Mumbai?

Ans. October to March is best overall. November–February has the clearest weather nationwide. September–October and April–May offer good conditions at lower prices. July–August is the cheapest but wettest.
Q5. How much does a Vietnam tour package from Mumbai cost?

Ans. Ground packages (no flights) start from ₹65,000 per person for 6–7 days. Standard packages with return flights run ₹80,000–₹95,000. Luxury packages from ₹1,10,000. Honeymoon packages ₹90,000–₹1,20,000. E-visa (USD 25–50) is additional.
Q6. What currency is used in Vietnam?

Ans. Vietnamese Dong (VND). USD is accepted at larger hotels but at worse rates. Exchange at airport banks. Carry VND cash for markets and smaller towns — cards are not always accepted outside cities.

Ans. With planning, yes. Buddhist vegetarian restaurants (com chay) are common. Indian restaurants operate in HCMC, Hanoi, and Da Nang. Halong Bay cruises can arrange vegetarian meals with advance notice. Carry snacks for rural days.
Q8. What are the must-see places on a Vietnam tour from Mumbai?
Ans. Halong Bay, Hoi An Ancient Town, Ho Chi Minh City (Cu Chi Tunnels, Ben Thanh Market), Hanoi Old Quarter, Da Nang (Golden Bridge, Ba Na Hills). Most 7–8 day packages cover all five.
Q9. How many days are ideal for a first Vietnam trip?
Ans. 7–8 days covers the main highlights comfortably. 5–6 days works for 2–3 destinations only. 9–10 days allows adding Hue, Sapa, or Phu Quoc. We recommend at least 7 days for a first visit.
Q10. Is there Indian food available in Vietnam?
Ans. Yes — Indian restaurants in HCMC (Tandoor), Hanoi (Mumtaz), and Da Nang (Namaste Vietnam). Most Halong Bay cruises and tour packages can arrange Indian or vegetarian meals with advance request.
Q11. What is the best Vietnam package for a honeymoon from Mumbai?

Ans. Our Vietnam honeymoon package from Mumbai (7–9 days, ₹90,000–₹1,20,000) combines Hoi An boutique stay, Halong Bay cruise (private cabin), and a beach resort in Da Nang or Phu Quoc. Romantic room setup and candlelight dinner included on request.
Q12. Is Vietnam a good destination for families with children?

Ans. Yes. Ba Na Hills (Fantasy Park, cable car), water puppet shows, Halong Bay boat rides, and Cu Chi Tunnels are all family-friendly. Our Vietnam family packages from Mumbai are paced to avoid rushing and include child-friendly hotels.
Q13. What SIM card should I use in Vietnam?
Ans. Buy a Viettel or Vinaphone tourist SIM at the airport on arrival — costs under ₹1,000 and provides data for the full trip. Both networks have good coverage across major cities and tourist areas.
Q14. How do I pay for things in Vietnam?

Ans. Carry Vietnamese Dong (VND) for markets, street food, and small towns. Cards are accepted at hotels and malls in major cities. Grab app payments work with international cards. UPI is not currently accepted in Vietnam.
Q15. What is the Tet festival and should I travel during it?

Ans. Tet (17 Feb 2026, Year of the Horse) is Vietnam's biggest festival — flower markets, fireworks, and family celebrations. Worth experiencing, but book everything 6–8 weeks ahead. Many shops close 3–5 days around Feb 16–19. Domestic flights and trains sell out completely.

Originally developed during the British Raj as a summer getaway destination to achieve some relief from the scorching heat of the plains, the town has now fully blossomed into a tourism hub. And rightly so! It is one of those rare places in India that offer you all kinds of activities, ranging from hiking trails to going on trekking expeditions to enjoying scenic road trips. Try boating or sample the delicious local cuisine, you're sure to create some irreplaceable memories here! blocks.text: The best time to visit Nainital depends on the activities that you're interested in doing here.

Many tourists pick the summers (March - June) to come here. In this window, you can bask in its pleasant weather and enjoy sightseeing at ease. Also, boating is another star attraction of this period.

Another great time to come here is the wintertime (October - February) . The snow blankets the whole region, creating a winter paradise for the travellers. Enjoy snowfall and other snow-related sports such as snowboarding.

You can also come here in the monsoon season (July - September) . Enjoy the lush greenery that the region is blessed with during this period. Moreover, there are fewer crowds, letting you enjoy your tour in peace.
Nainital, therefore, can be visited at any time. That's one of the best things about this hill station - you're welcome throughout the year!
Here are some ways by which you can reach the picturesque hill station of Nainital:

items: By Air: The nearest airport to Nainital is Pantnagar Airport, located about 70 km from the hill station. From the airport, you can easily hire a taxi to reach this beautiful town.

By Train: Nainital tour by train is another great option! Kathgodam Railway Station is the nearest railhead (about 34 km away) and is well-connected to major cities like Delhi, Dehradun, Lucknow, etc.

By Road : Nainital is very well-connected by roads. You can either drive to reach there yourself, or you can visit by the regular buses that run from major cities, like Delhi, Dehradun, etc. Also, the Delhi to Nainital Trip by car is another popular option among tourists.

Top Places to Visit in Nainital
Here are some places that must be on your Nainital tour itinerary:

rows: Consider it the heart of Nainital! Famous for boating, it's a quintessential part of any Nainital Lake Tour!

It's the perfect place to take in the panoramic views of the mighty Himalayas! The ropeway ride up 'till here is just the cherry on the top.
It's a nice site to indulge in horse riding and some downtime picnics. Also, it's a great spot for couple selfies! A must addition to any Nainital Honeymoon Package!

blocks.text: Here are some must-try activities for your trip:

items: The calm waters and the surrounding green hills of the Naini Lake will put you right in a state of relaxation. The best thing about it is that you can indulge in boating here throughout the day! Also, both paddle boats and rowboats are available here.

This is one of the most exciting things about your Nainital Sightseeing Tour! Simply take a cable car from Mallital to Snow View Point and allow yourself to get spoiled by the rich Himalayan valley views!
Mall Road is definitely a go-to as it's a perfect place to grab a snack or go full-blown souvenir shopping. While you're there, do look for wooden handicrafts and woollen wear.
Tibet Market is another popular market that you can visit to buy goods. It's a great place to purchase Tibetan artefacts and even jewellery.

The picturesque Nainital also offers tourists a chance to dip their toes into adventurous activities. You can enjoy here anything from horse riding (speciality of Tiffin Top) to paragliding. You can also choose our Nainital Adventure Tour Packages to have an adrenaline-pumping trip!

While Nainital is all about sightseeing and adventure, it's also about taking a laidback approach and going for simple walks. You'd love taking leisure walks on what is known as the 'Thandi Sadak'. Soak in the pleasant cold as the rustling pine trees and chirping birds make up the background music!
While in Nainital, do try the local dishes like Aloo Ke Gutke, Ras Bhaat, Kumaoni Raita, Bhat ke Dubke and Bal Mithai.

Q1. How many days are enough for Nainital?
Ans. Usually, three to five days are enough to explore the hill station in depth. In this span, you can easily cover all the major sightseeing destinations in the town.
Nainital is a small hill station that has a definite set of sightseeing places. These places and experiences take no more than 5 days for a leisure holiday, along with proper sightseeing.
Q2. How can I spend 3 days in Nainital?

Ans. You can cover a lot in 3 days in Nainital: Day 1 - visit Nainital Lake, Naini Devi Temple and Nainital Zoo. Day 2 - visit the eco cave garden, shop at Mall Road and take a fun ropeway ride. Day 3 - if leaving Nainital by evening, then after check out in the morning, you can go to Kilbury Bird Sanctuary or Tiffin Top, which will take around half a day to cover and explore.
Q3. How can I plan a trip to Nainital?

Ans. The first step is to see if you are going during the right month. Summertime means inflated prices of everything, while wintertime means fewer tourists and lower rates. Next, you need to check out the various rooms and accommodations depending on your budget. There are lots of varieties available, so you can choose as per your liking. Getting around is another important factor. There are rickshaws available to take you around. To further explore, you can even book a taxi service here.

Q5. What should I buy from Nainital?
Ans. You can buy souvenirs in Nainital like wooden artefacts, hand-woven shawls, woollen textiles, trinkets, handicraft items, and so much more.
Q6. How can I travel locally in Nainital?

Ans. Nainital has developed into a full-on tourist hub. There are rickshaws available if you want to get around the market area. There are also taxis and shared autos available. There are local buses that connect the nearby villages to Nainital. You can even rent a bike or a car if you like.
Q7. Is it safe to travel from Delhi to Nainital at night?

Ans. Travelling from Delhi to Nainital is generally considered safe. The route through NH 9 is well-maintained. However, once you get near Nainital, be wary of the hilly stretches. Hiring a professional driver is a good idea as well.
Q8. Which is better: Mussoorie or Nainital?

Ans. Both Mussoorie and Nainital are beautiful hill stations. However, they offer different experiences to the tourists. If you want to enjoy boating or lakes, then pick Nainital. And if you want to soak in the colonial charm or take short hikes, then Mussoorie is a better option for that.
Q9. What is Nainital famous for?

Ans. Nainital is mainly famous for Naini Lake, Naini Temple, Tiffin Top, Kilbury Bird Sanctuary, and shopping marketplaces. It has also gained popularity for being the gateway to several other places like Mukteshwar, Binsar, Pangot, Bhimtal, and Almora.
Q10. What is the best time to visit Nainital?

Ans. The months of March to June mark the best time to come, especially if you want to get some refreshing mountain air in summer. If you wish to avoid the tourists, then going there during the autumn-winter months of October to February is fine too.
Q11. How is the road from Delhi to Nainital?

Ans. The roads are very well built & maintained, and even more roads are being constructed. There are two main ways you can reach Nainital from Delhi: one is via Kashipur and Kaladhungi, while the other is via Haldwani. How to Reach Ujjain from Rajkot?

The best time to visit Ujjain is from October to March . You'll find the weather at this time to be really pleasant and cool. This is perfect for all your temple tours and nearby sightseeing. The temperature swings between 10°C and 25°C, making for a delightful trip.

mainEntity.name: What Is Attractive About Bali?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is raw beauty all over and around Bali. The island boasts a myriad of impressive volcanoes, crystalline beaches, world-class diving, diverse nightlife, iconic ricefields, and and gorgeous waterfalls. Hiking on the island, as well as the nearby Lombok and Java islands, is breathtaking.

mainEntity.name: Where Are The Best Beaches In Bali?

acceptedAnswer.text: The majority of Bali's best beaches are in the south, near Kuta, Jimbaran, and the Bukit Peninsula. Some of these are also extremely busy (particularly the coast from Kuta to Seminyak). If you take a taxi, you can easily find some beautiful stretches of sand with few other tourists.

mainEntity.name: Why Is Bali Such A Popular Romantic Destination?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bali's stunning landscapes, romantic beaches, picturesque islands, and sunsets make it ideal for post-wedding photography. blocks.text: Bali is a dream destination for couples looking for a romantic honeymoon. This 4-day Bali honeymoon tour package is specially designed for couples who want a mix of romance, relaxation, and a little adventure on their honeymoon.

Imagine waking up in a private villa surrounded by palm trees, stunning views, hearing soft ocean waves, and having a floating breakfast just for the two of you. Well, that’s what Bali can bring to the table for couples looking for a memorable romantic honeymoon trip.
From exploring lush green rice terraces to enjoying beachside cafes, from watching stunning sunsets to exploring the key attractions…Bali is full of surprises waiting for you.

items: Check in with a Warm Welcome: Enjoy welcome drinks, a cozy ambience, and a romantic honeymoon room setup.

blocks.text: Day 2 : Visit to Tanjung Benoa Beach

Start your morning with a comfortable, delicious breakfast at your hotel. After breakfast, meet your driver, who will take you to explore one of the most exciting destinations of your Bali honeymoon trip.
Tanjung Benoa Beach – Bali's Watersports Hub

Witness the stunning views of the Indian Ocean, sandy beaches, crystal clear water, and water sports activities. It is the perfect place for couples to have a mix of fun, excitement, and playful moments together.

Day 3 : Uluwatu Sightseeing & Kecak Fire Dance Show

Day 3 of this honeymoon package is full of culture, cliffs, sunsets, and unforgettable moments in Bali. So, start your day with a delicious breakfast at the hotel. Next, you'll head to South Bali to visit some of the most iconic destinations.
This is one of Bali's most iconic cultural landmarks. This place is a mix of culture, tradition, nature, and some breathtaking views.

items: The massive Garuda Wisnu Kencana statue is considered one of the tallest statues in the world.
Beautiful Gardens and Pathways - Perfect for clicking couple's photographs
Watch Cultural Performances, Balinese Music & Artistic Displays
Walk through famous areas like Lotus Pond, Wisnu Plaza, etc.

blocks.text: After spending some time exploring the cultural park, you will head to the next destination.
2. Visit Uluwatu Temple - The Sunset Point
Ready to experience some breathtaking views from the mountain cliff, and a spiritual experience? Your next stop is the iconic Uluwatu Temple.

items: The temple is situated on a 70-meter-high cliff, which offers some stunning views. You can enjoy the beautiful sunset from the top.
Visit the temple to explore the unique Balinese culture and history

blocks.text: The temple is open for visitors from 7 AM to 7 PM. You have to pay an entry fee of IDR 50,000.
As soon as the sun sets you can attend Bali's famous and most iconic dance performances... the Kecak Fire Dance.

blocks.text: The name Pachmarhi is said to have originated from the Hindi words Panch (“five”) and Marhi (“caves”). Tradition holds that during their thirteen years of exile, the five Pandava brothers of the Mahabharatha era built these caverns. The lofty position of the caverns makes them an excellent vantage point. One of the most famous tourist attractions in India is the isolated hill village of Pachmarhi, which is entirely covered in stunning flora. Pachmarhi does add a new flavour to this Central Indian curry, and the state is widely recognised for its rich heritage, historical sites, and lush forest. The Pachmarhi 3 days / 2 nights tour will take you on a short yet exciting journey.

The My Quick Trippers representative will receive you at Pachmarhi and take you to the hotel for check-in and rest. You can come out later in the day to stroll around the town and shop from the local market. Overnight stay will take place in the Pachmarhi hotel.

On day 2 post breakfast you will drive to the various tourist spots in Pachmarhi all through the day. Your day will start with ‘Jata Shankar’ visit which is a ‘sacred cave’ situated under lose boulders displaying nature’s unique architecture. Move on to ‘Christ Church’ which crucially reminds of the colonial rule here. The architecture of the church reminds you of the European style of architecture especially with the altar and walls brought from that region. You can take a break and get back to your hotel to take lunch. Post lunch you will be taken to other sites of tourist attraction in Pachmarhi. Go to the Bee Falls to get closer to nature and then move on to the ‘Vaniki Sangrahalya’ (Bison Lodge) followed by the ‘Bal Udayan (Children’s park). To get a scenic view of the sunset visit the ‘Noka Vihar’ and take a boat ride in the Pachmarhi Lake here. Proceed to Dhoopgarh which is the ‘highest peak’ in the Pachmarhi region. Return to your hotel for night stay.

Day 3 is the final day and after a filling breakfast, you will check out of the hotel. The My Quick Trippers representative will assist you safely to the point from where you will return home with unforgettable memories.

item.name: Sri Lanka Tour Packages from Chennai with Flight

blocks.text: With direct flights from Chennai to Colombo taking less than two hours, Sri Lanka is one of the most accessible international destinations for travellers from Tamil Nadu. A Sri Lanka trip from Chennai costs less than most domestic hill station holidays — and gives you beaches, UNESCO heritage sites, hill country, and wildlife all in one.

Sri Lanka is a dream destination for anyone looking for adventure, beautiful scenery, or a cultural tour. To enjoy a hassle-free trip to this southern island, book our Sri Lanka Tour Packages from Chennai! With this tour plan, you get accommodation, meals, and dedicated transport. Also, our packages are fully customizable, allowing you to go on a trip tailored exactly to your preferences! Contact us now to know more!

Also known as the pearl of the South Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka has a lot to offer its tourists. Whether it's the golden-sand beaches, revered temples, or the full-fledged UNESCO World Heritage sites, there's everything for everyone — from nature lovers to history buffs! And while you're here, don't miss out on the wildlife safaris and the ever-so vibrant markets, which are a great spot for souvenir shopping. Book the Sri Lanka Sigiriya Kandy Ella tour now to explore the best of the best in Sri Lanka!
Best Time to Visit Sri Lanka from Chennai

The best time to visit Sri Lanka from South India falls in two main windows. If you're visiting the west coast of the island, the window from December to March is the perfect time. And if you're travelling to the East Coast, come here in April–September.
In the December–March window, you can enjoy Colombo, Kandy, Bentota, and Galle. In the April–September window, you can explore Trincomalee, Arugam Bay, and Batticaloa.

Colombo as a city can be visited year-round — its markets, food scene, and urban attractions are not dependent on coastal weather. If your Sri Lanka holiday package from Chennai focuses on sightseeing and culture rather than beaches, November to April is a reliable window for a 4-day, 5-day, or 6-day package.

Here's what you get with our tour plans:

items: Transfers in a private AC vehicle

blocks.text: Sri Lanka Tour Itinerary from Chennai
Here's how your Sri Lanka trip, in general, looks like:

rows: Arrive in Colombo. Have a nice little tour of the place. Enjoy the nightlife of the bustling city of Colombo.
Enjoy the scenic drive to Kandy itself! Once you're there, visit the Temple of the Tooth Relic and indulge in other sightseeing.
Head into Sri Lanka's hill country. Explore lush tea plantations, colonial-era bungalows, and waterfalls around Nuwara Eliya — the 'Little England' of Sri Lanka.
Spend a leisure day at Bentota Beach.
Enjoy the Sri Lanka cultural heritage tour! Take a trip to the UNESCO site that is the Galle Fort, and get charmed by its architecture.
On the departure day, engage in some souvenir shopping in the morning and have some relaxation before catching your flight back home.

blocks.text: How to Reach Sri Lanka from Chennai?
There are primarily two ways to reach Sri Lanka from Chennai:

By Air: You can book a direct flight from Chennai (MAA) to Bandaranaike International Airport, Colombo (CMB). The flight duration is under two hours. IndiGo, SriLankan Airlines, and Air India operate on this route. Most of our Sri Lanka tour packages from Chennai with flight include the return airfare — contact us for current flight-inclusive pricing.

By Sea (Ferry): The Nagapattinam–Kankesanthurai ferry service resumed in August 2024 after a 41-year gap. The 'Sivaganga' ferry departs Nagapattinam at 7 AM and arrives at Kankesanthurai port in Jaffna by around 11 AM — approximately 3.5 hours covering 60 nautical miles. One-way fare: ₹5,000 (general class) or ₹7,500 (premium class). Book at indsri.com. Note: Nagapattinam is about 300 km from Chennai and the ferry arrives in Jaffna (northern Sri Lanka), not Colombo. Ferry schedules are subject to weather conditions and operational changes — always verify sailing dates before planning your journey.
Airlines operating: IndiGo, SriLankan Airlines, and Air India operate direct flights on the Chennai (MAA) – Colombo (CMB) route.
Flight duration: Under 2 hours (approximately 1 hour 45 minutes for direct flights).
Average economy fare: ₹7,500–₹15,000 one way depending on season, airline, and how far in advance you book. Prices are lower between May and October (shoulder season).
Airport: Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB), Colombo. Located approximately 35 km north of Colombo city — transfer to your hotel takes 45 minutes to 1.5 hours depending on traffic.
Tip: Book flights at least 3–4 weeks in advance for Pongal, summer holidays, and December peak season — fares on the Chennai–Colombo route spike during these periods.
Good news for Indian travellers in 2026 — Sri Lanka has waived the ETA fee for Indian nationals from 25 May 2026. Here's what you need to know:

ETA (Electronic Travel Authorisation): Mandatory for all Indian visitors. Apply online at eta.gov.lk before your trip. The application is free of charge as of 25 May 2026 — no fee, no embassy visit needed.
Validity: 30 days from date of first arrival. Double entry permitted within the 30-day window.
Passport requirement: Valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. Carry a printed copy of your ETA approval to speed up immigration.
Extensions: You can extend your stay up to 270 days by applying at the Department of Immigration in Colombo. Extension fees apply.
Visa on arrival: Available at Bandaranaike Airport, but applying online before travel is strongly recommended to avoid queues.
Top Attractions Covered in Sri Lanka Holiday Package
Here are some of the most frequent places in the island country:
Colombo: Come here and have a taste of a true-blue cosmopolitan city! Treat yourself to world-class casinos and a vibrant nightlife!
Kandy: Next, take a bite of culture and visit the famous Temple of the Tooth Relic. The botanical gardens here are another top attraction. A must-visit for any Chennai to Sri Lanka holiday!
Nuwara Eliya: The cool weather and the lush green tea plantations here will remind you of being in Britain — and that's why it's belovedly called 'Little England', and rightly so!
Sigiriya: Come here and see the marvel that this UNESCO World Heritage rock fortress is.

Bentota & Mirissa: These are two of the most frequented honeymoon places in Sri Lanka . Enjoy sun-kissed beaches and whale watching. You can also indulge in water sports such as diving, surfing, and more!
Galle: Appreciate the colonial architecture here and the famous Galle Fort itself! This iconic site should be a part of any Sri Lanka Tour Package from Chennai!
Ella: Visit here to relish the calming scenic train rides.
Sri Lanka Ramayana Trail — For Hindu Pilgrims from Chennai

For pilgrims and devotees from Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka carries a special significance — as the Lanka of King Ravana from the Valmiki Ramayana. The Ramayana Trail in Sri Lanka connects over 20 sites tied to events from the epic, and many of them are within easy reach of the standard Colombo–Kandy–Nuwara Eliya circuit.

Sita Amman Temple (Sita Eliya): Near Nuwara Eliya, this temple is built on the site where Sita Mata is believed to have been held captive by Ravana. Hanuman's footprints can be seen on a rock face near the temple stream.
Ashoka Vatika / Hakgala Botanical Garden: The garden near Nuwara Eliya identified as the Ashoka Vatika of the Ramayana — where Ravana kept Sita captive. Home to over 10,000 plant species.

Divurumpola Temple (Welimada): Believed to be the exact site of Sita's Agni Pariksha — where she walked through fire to prove her purity. Locals still come here to take oaths, continuing the ancient tradition.
Ravana Cave (Ella): A cave near Ella town believed to have been used by Ravana to keep Sita. About 2 km from Ella town — a short drive and walk.
Munneswaram Temple (Chilaw): Where Lord Rama is said to have prayed to Lord Shiva after defeating Ravana. One of the five ancient Ishwarams of Sri Lanka.

We offer a dedicated Sri Lanka Ramayana Tour Package from Chennai (7 Nights / 8 Days starting from INR 36,900) covering these and more Ramayana-connected sites across the island. Contact us for details.
Sri Lanka Holiday Package Price from Chennai

The cost of Sri Lanka tour from Chennai starts from INR 24,900 and goes up to INR 58,500, which is also inclusive of Sri Lanka mythological heritage tour from India. Our tour plans are extensively customizable and include your hotel bills, food charges, visa assistance, and local transfer.

Prices are indicative and may vary depending on travel dates, hotel category, flight availability, and seasonal demand. Contact us for current pricing and availability.
Practical Travel Information for Sri Lanka

Currency: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). As of 2026, roughly 1 INR ≈ 4.1–4.3 LKR. Carry Indian Rupees or USD for exchange — exchange counters are available at Colombo airport and in major cities. ATMs (Visa/Mastercard) work well in Colombo, Kandy, and other tourist areas.

Can Indians use UPI in Sri Lanka? Not widely. UPI is not yet accepted at most Sri Lankan merchants. Carry cash (LKR) or use an international Visa/Mastercard debit or credit card. Some larger hotels in Colombo accept INR, but do not count on it.

Mobile network & SIM: Dialog and Mobitel are the two main networks with the best coverage across the island. A local SIM (with data) costs around LKR 500–1,000 (approximately ₹120–250) and is available at the airport on arrival. eSIM options via Airalo and similar providers also work for Sri Lanka.
Time zone: Sri Lanka Standard Time (SLST) is UTC+5:30 — same as Indian Standard Time (IST). No time adjustment needed.
Power plugs: Sri Lanka uses Type D and Type G sockets (the same Type D used across India). Your Indian plugs will work in most hotels without an adaptor.

Language: Sinhala and Tamil are both official languages. English is widely spoken in tourist areas, hotels, and restaurants. Tamil speakers from Chennai will find communication comfortable in many parts of northern and eastern Sri Lanka.
Is Sri Lanka Safe for Indian Tourists?

Yes, Sri Lanka is a safe and popular destination for Indian tourists. The country has been welcoming a rising number of Indian visitors — India is currently the top source market for Sri Lanka tourism in 2026. Here are a few standard safety guidelines:

items: Tourist areas including Colombo, Kandy, Galle, Nuwara Eliya, and Sigiriya are generally safe for solo travellers, families, and couples.
Avoid isolated beaches after dark — stick to well-lit, populated beach areas in the evenings.
Use licensed taxis or app-based cabs (PickMe and Uber both operate in Sri Lanka). Agree on a fare before getting into non-metered tuk-tuks.
Follow local temple regulations — remove footwear, cover shoulders and knees, and do not pose with your back to Buddha statues for photos.
Keep a copy of your passport and ETA approval in your email or phone — local authorities may ask for ID at some heritage sites.
Sri Lanka's healthcare in Colombo and major cities is reasonably good. Carry basic medicines, especially if travelling with children or seniors.

blocks.text: Essential Tips for Sri Lanka Trip
Here are some travel tips that you might find useful:

items: Although cards are accepted at all modern restaurants and hotels, it's still a good practice to carry cash in Sri Lanka's home currency — the Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR).
Respect the local customs in Sri Lanka. Be respectful to Buddha idols and images, which are quite common across the island.
Book your Sri Lanka vacation packages from Chennai according to the region you want to visit in the country.
Mosquitoes can give you trouble. Carry mosquito repellents and mosquito nets with you to protect yourself from insect bites.
Do try the Sri Lankan delicacies: Kottu Roti, Egg Hoppers, Gotu Kola Sambol, Wambatu Moju, Lamprais, Ambul Thiyal, and Polos.
Do not drink tap water while you're in the country. Always carry packaged drinking water with you.
From 25 May 2026, ETA is completely free for Indian nationals. Apply at eta.gov.lk before your trip. Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months from your travel date.

Q1. What are the visa requirements for Indians traveling to Sri Lanka?

Indians travelling to Sri Lanka need an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorisation) — apply online at eta.gov.lk. From 25 May 2026, the ETA is completely free for Indian nationals. The application is still mandatory, but the fee has been waived. The ETA is valid for 30 days with double entry. Carry your passport (valid for 6+ months) and a printed ETA approval for smoother immigration.
Q2. Which is the cheapest month to visit Sri Lanka?

The cheapest months to travel to Sri Lanka are the shoulder seasons. If you are looking for a budget plan or even an affordable Sri Lanka romantic tour under ₹39,999, then visit in the window of May to October.
Q3. What is the cost of the ferry from Nagapattinam to Sri Lanka?

The Nagapattinam–Kankesanthurai ferry (Sivaganga) runs from Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu to Kankesanthurai port in Jaffna, Sri Lanka. One-way fare: ₹5,000 (general class) or ₹7,500 (premium class). The journey takes approximately 3.5 hours covering 60 nautical miles. Departs Nagapattinam at 7 AM, arrives Kankesanthurai at ~11 AM. Book at indsri.com. Note: Nagapattinam is ~300 km from Chennai and the ferry arrives in Jaffna, not Colombo. Schedules are subject to weather — verify before booking.
Q4. How much is the ticket price from Chennai to Sri Lanka?

Economy class airfare from Chennai to Colombo is around INR 7,500 upwards and business class approximately INR 22,500 and above. Fares vary by season — they are lower in May–September and higher around Pongal, summer holidays, and December. IndiGo, SriLankan Airlines, and Air India operate the Chennai (MAA)–Colombo (CMB) route. Contact us for round-trip Sri Lanka holiday packages from Chennai with flight.
Q5. How many hours does it take to reach from Chennai to Sri Lanka?

By air, it takes about 1.5 to 2 hours from Chennai to Colombo. If you're travelling by ferry from Nagapattinam, the crossing to Kankesanthurai (Jaffna) takes approximately 3.5 hours — departs 7 AM, arrives ~11 AM.
Q6. How long is a Sri Lanka trip from Chennai?

A 4 to 7 day trip is usually sufficient to explore major cities, hills, and beaches. A 4-day Sri Lanka package from Chennai covers Colombo and Kandy. A 5-day or 6-day package adds Nuwara Eliya and Bentota. For the full experience including Galle, Ella, and Sigiriya, a 7-day Sri Lanka holiday from Chennai works best.
Q7. Is Sri Lanka a good honeymoon destination?

Yes, Sri Lanka is a great honeymoon destination and is one of the most romantic places near India. You can enjoy a fun beach day at Bentota, enjoy the nightlife in Colombo and have candlelight dinners at its posh restaurants. The island country is ideal for couples!
Q8. Is Sri Lanka safe for Indian tourists?

Yes, Sri Lanka is safe for Indian tourists and is currently one of the most visited international destinations for travellers from South India. Tourist areas are well-policed, hotels are accustomed to Indian guests, and Tamil is spoken in many parts of the north and east. Stick to licensed cabs, follow temple dress codes, and carry a copy of your ETA and passport for site visits.
Q9. What kind of food can I expect on Sri Lanka holiday from Chennai?

Sri Lanka offers you everything from South Indian specialities to seafood to even international cuisine. There are also a lot of restaurants here that serve Indian food, especially in the tourist hotspots.
Q10. Can I customize Sri Lanka travel package from Chennai?

Yes, My Quick Trippers offers you customizable Sri Lanka packages, where you can adjust the length of your trip, pick the hotel of your choice, and even opt for add-on experiences like safari and boat rides!
Q11. Is Sri Lanka expensive for Indian tourists?

Sri Lanka is one of the more affordable international destinations for Indians. A mid-range 5-day Sri Lanka trip from Chennai — including flights, hotel, meals, and transfers — can be done comfortably for ₹35,000–₹55,000 per person. Budget travellers can do it for less; luxury packages go higher. The Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR) is weaker than INR, so your money goes further on food, tuk-tuks, and local shopping.
Q12. Which currency should I carry for Sri Lanka?

Carry Indian Rupees and exchange them to Sri Lankan Rupees (LKR) at the airport or authorised exchange counters in Colombo. As of 2026, roughly 1 INR ≈ 4.1–4.3 LKR. You can also carry USD for exchange — it is widely accepted. ATMs (Visa/Mastercard) work in most cities. UPI is not widely accepted at Sri Lankan merchants yet.
Q13. Can Indians use UPI in Sri Lanka?

Not widely. UPI is not yet accepted at most shops, restaurants, or hotels in Sri Lanka. Use a Visa or Mastercard-enabled debit or credit card for card payments, and carry local LKR cash for smaller purchases and tuk-tuks. Some large hotels in Colombo accept INR, but it is safer not to rely on this.
Q14. Do Indians need travel insurance for Sri Lanka?

Travel insurance is not mandatory for Sri Lanka but it is strongly recommended — especially for medical coverage, trip cancellation, and lost baggage. Medical care in Colombo is reasonably good but costs can be high for foreigners without insurance. Look for a policy that covers emergency medical evacuation. With comfortable accommodations and a relaxed pace, the tour allows ample time for sightseeing and leisure. Whether enjoying the serene beaches or exploring historical sites, this package provides a memorable way to experience the beauty and culture of the Andaman Islands at an affordable price.
Day 1 : Pick up from Port Blair Airport– Sightseeing

Get a warm welcome at Port Blair Airport by our representative, and take a drive for the hotel. Welcome drink on check in to the hotel. After relaxing some time you will start the tremendous tour to Corbyns Cove Beach, one of the most picturesque, Enjoy coconut palm fringed beach which is located at just 7 KMs away from Port Blair city, Visit Cellular Jail-an auspicious place for all liberty loving persons. You can also see the history of the heroic freedom fight which is brought alive in a moving Light & Sound Show at the Cellular Jail. In evening come back to hotel, enjoy your night meal and stay overnight in Port Blair.

Take a departure in early morning by inter-island ferry to Neil Island (Approx 90 Minutes- 45 KMs), an island with clear turquoise sea and white sand beaches. On reaching just check in to your hotel, enjoy your breakfast later on visit Sitapur viewpoint, Bharatpur Beach- this is one of the most attractive beaches in Andaman. You can also enjoy a ride in a glass bottomed boat to see under water corals and marine life (Optional – extra cost). Late in afternoon visit to the Laxmanpur Beach II to view the natural coral bridge and also go to Laxmanpur Beach I to see the sunset. You can use your evening at leisure or exploring by self. Enjoy your dinner and overnight stay at hotel in Neil Island.

After breakfast take the transfer to Neil Island, take the inter-island ferry to Havelock Island (Approx 2 Hrs, 55 KMs). Enjoy your afternoon at Beach Number 7 which is also known as Radha Nagar Beach. Return back to your hotel at late evening, Enjoy your night meal & overnight stay at hotel in Havelock.
Enjoy your breakfast, later you can go on an optional trip to Elephant Beach (for Extra cost), or you may use it as leisure time or explore your own interest. Stay overnight at hotel in Havelock.
Day 5 : Havelock Island – Port Blair (Approx 57 kms by sea – 3Hrs)

After breakfast, check out from the hotel and head to Kalapathar Beach for a visit. Later, proceed to the Havelock jetty to board your return ferry to Port Blair. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel. Enjoy an overnight stay in Port Blair.

After breakfast get ready to see stunning sightseeing tours of North Bay Island followed by Ross Island, The island presently houses the ruins of old buildings like Chief Commissioner’s House, Church, Bakery, Government House, Press, Cemetery, Swimming Pool, etc. and all in decrepit condition. Later on you can enjoy a Harbour Cruise which includes a trip to tiny, serene, beautiful island called “VIPER ISLAND” where you can see the Gallows’s sight. At evening come back to your hotel. Enjoy your dinner & overnight stay in Port Blair.

After breakfast take a drive to Port Blair airport for your onward scheduled journey. We hope that you had a memorable tour around Andaman- Nicobar, also we wish to see you soon for your next journey. Have a safe & enjoy full journey ahead.

blocks.text: Popularly known as “Queen of Hills”, Darjeeling is one of the most eminent holiday destinations of almost every travel enthusiast. The breathtaking views of the mountains, picturesque surroundings, beautiful monasteries, and panoramic landscapes take Darjeeling tourism a notch higher.
This gorgeous hill station is blessed with steep mountain ridges bestowed with lush green tea plantations and offers you mesmerizing views of the sunrise from snow-peaked mountains.

Gangtok, the capital city of Sikkim, leaves every traveler awestruck and spellbound with its impeccable spiritual aura and tremendous scenic vista. The city boasts of various exciting tourist places where travelers from far around the country visit and feel immensely astonished with the views of Kanchenjunga, the third highest mountain peak in the world. It happens to be one of the best places to start your newly married life with positivity and love.

On this 5 nights and 6 days long Darjeeling honeymoon package you will be provided with enough time and opportunity to witness the glory and charm of these cities and can enjoy some really amazing and romantic moments with your family and friends. On this honeymoon trip, My Quick Trippers will provide you great services and facilities that include transportation, food, a cozy and comfy stay, and many more.

Arrive in New Jalpaiguri and Bagdogra to a warm welcome by our tour guide who then escorts you to the coach that will take you to your hotel. Relax a bit and as the sun starts dipping, set out to explore The Mall and sample the local cuisine.

Rise early at around 3 AM and set out in the cool air of pre-dawn to Tiger Hill and wait with bated breath for the Sun to rise over the Kanchenjunga. This sight alone is worth the trip and both of you will remember it forever. Return via Batasia Loop where you can see the railway line spiraling around before vanishing into a tunnel. Take in the Ghoom Monastery later in the day and then you can, on your own, visit the Japanese Temple and Peace Pagoda or wander out of town to stroll along the waterfalls. Lovers love riding on the toy train and this is something you should not miss.

After breakfast, the group sets out on an excursion that will take you to the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, the Dhirdham Temple, and the Zoological Gardens. There is a brief interlude as you take a ride on the ropeway after which we visit Lebong Race Course, Gombu Rock, Happy valley tea estate, and the Peace Pagoda. Return to your room for the night.

Enjoy a Bengali breakfast in the crisp morning air and board the coach for the 100 km drive to Gangtok across scenic, winding mountain roads. The half-day trip to Gangtok includes a visit to Hanuman Tok, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Tashi View Point with its wonderful view of the Himalayas, Rumtek Monastery, and Ganesh Tok. Stay in the picturesque Buddhist environment of Gangtok for the night.

Enjoy a Tibetan breakfast and then we take you to Tsomgo Lake in East Sikkim. The trip includes a visit to Baba Harbhajan Temple and the forbidden Nathula Pass located at a height of 4310 meters that was once a part of the Silk Route.

On this last and final day, you have a sumptuous breakfast and board the coach for the return drive to New Jalpaiguri/Bagdogra over a distance of 110 km that in itself is a beautiful journey that lovers enjoy. When you arrive the tour guide assists you with onward travel and bids you a fond farewell.

A. The entire budget of the trip depends on the number of days. On an average it can cost anywhere from 30,000 rupees to 55,000 rupees/-, transportation and stays included.
Q. Which Are Some Of The Best Honeymoon Hotels In Darjeeling?

A. There are several hotels in Darjeeling catering to newly married couples and people on their honeymoon. Some of these are: Sinclairs Hotel, Mayfair Darjeeling, Ging Tea House, Cedar Inn, Summit Hermon Hotel and spa etc.
Q. Are There Any Darjeeling Tour Packages Under 10,000 Rupees/-?

A. Yes. There are many different types of Darjeeling tour packages available. You can even make a trip on your own. But be prepared to eat basic food, stay in underwhelming places and cut down on the number of holidays.
Q. Which Is The Best Time To Visit Darjeeling?
A. April to June are the most pleasant months to visit Darjeeling.
Q. Is Darjeeling Safe To Visit?
A. Yes. Darjeeling is one of the safest tourist spots in India and can be visited freely anytime of the year.

blocks.text: Kerala is Nature at its best, a land blessed with ample amount of lush tropical vegetation, mountains, rivers, lakes, waterfalls and golden beaches. This is the perfect mix for the romantically inclined to discover love and let it bloom like the orchids for which the State is so well known. Whether you are going off as a couple on a honeymoon or on your anniversary, My Quick Trippers romantic Kerala tour gives you a lovely experience of being together in the lap of nature. A typical 5 nights 6 days romantic Kerala tour itinerary would go like this:

Welcome to Kochi by our My Quick Trippers tour guide who escorts you to your hotel room where you freshen up. Then, you set out to explore Kochi starting with the Fort followed by the Bolgatty Palace, a trip to the seashore to see how fishermen still use the Chinese style fishing nets, to Mattancherry Palace and the Jewish Synagogue. You will also visit Marine Drive and the Pareekshith Thampuran Museum during the day.

Have a cosy Kerala breakfast together and get ready for the 150 km drive to Munnar, the loveliest hill resort of Kerala. The drive takes you across splendidly breathtaking scenery made up of water bodies, waterfalls, lush green rice fields and a rolling countryside that exudes the warmth of nature and its people. Arrive at Munnar, the queen of Kerala hill resorts, and check into your hotel. From your room, you can see miles of undulating slopes covered by tea plantations. Freshen up and set out to explore the winding lanes of Munnar in the evening. Munnar is at the confluence of three rivers and has colonial overtones as you will find.

Enjoy local steaming hot breakfast and thus fortified set out to explore the beauties of Munnar. During the course of the day, you will visit the Eravikulam National Park, Rajamalai National Park, Kundala Lake, Echo Point and Mattupetty Dam. Starting at Mattupetty you enjoy a morning boat ride that puts you in a nice, romantic mood for the rest of the day. A walk through Eravikulam gives you glimpses of the Nilgiri Thar, an endangered species of goat along with a view of orchids, birds and other fauna. In the afternoon we stop at a tea plantation, watch workers picking leaves that are then processed. Sample tea and buy a pack to remember Munnar. Return to your room and if you are in the mood, visit Chinnakanal waterfalls, a lovely spot or go to Top Station.

Rise early, breakfast on hot Kerala delicacies and board the coach for the 120 km drive to Thekkady and the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary. Here you check into your hotel, freshen up and set off for Periyar where you go boating on the Lake, one of the best ways to view the innumerable birds, elephants, tigers, leopards and amphibian life. The view is wonderful and acts as a catalyst for romance. This boat trip done we take you to neighboring spice plantations where you can buy choicest spices to take back home.

Bite into delicious steaming hot Kerala style breakfast and get ready to travel to Athirapally, one of the most charming waterfalls in Kerala and a popular picnic spot. The falls are about 80 feet high, surrounded by lush tropical vegetation. Just sit, watch the water cascade and let love bloom inside you. You might want to splash about in the gurgling waters and walk the trails. Later, you return to Athirapally where you enjoy a lovely night in a picturesque resort.

You are treated to a sumptuous breakfast and then check out to go on to Kochi, at a distance of 80 km. This is where the romantic tour of Kerala ends but your journey of love does not. You promise to return to Kerala on a My Quick Trippers Kerala tour very soon. Try it in the monsoon!

blocks.text: Q. Why Is Kerala Ideal For A Honeymoon?
Ans. If you leave the hills to the north, "God's Own Country" Kerala, with its beaches, backwaters, Ayurveda, hills, and natural splendor, is one of the best places to visit in India for a honeymoon.
Q. When Is The Best Time To Visit Kerala For A Honeymoon?

Ans. The months of October to March are considered tourist season, and the months of December 20 to January 15 are considered peak tourist season. As the rains have subsided and the summer heat has passed, October to March is the best time to visit Kerala for a honeymoon.
Q. What Should I Wear On A Kerala Trip?

Ans. Carry dark coloured clothes because you don't want your white or light coloured clothes to get dirty from the rain and slush, especially when visiting tourist attractions in Alleppey. When visiting Kerala during the summer, light cotton or linen clothing is recommended.
Q. What Distinguishes Kerala From Other States?

Ans. Because of its unique geography, Kerala benefits greatly from the south-west monsoon. It has a pleasant climate throughout the year. We might as well leave the extreme weather to other states. It should have been a "must see" destination for ages, with 44 rivers and the mighty Western Ghats.
Q. Which City Is Known As Kerala's Heart?
Ans. Thrissur, Kerala's "cultural capital," is located in the heart of the state and is a hub of festivals and traditions.

This 18th-century fort is located right across the Ganga River. There's also a museum here where you can see royal costumes from the yesteryear as well as the weapons used at the time! In addition, there are also vintage cars on display here.

mainEntity.name: How do I reach Kedarnath from Mumbai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fly Mumbai to Dehradun (2–3.5 hours), road transfer to Guptkashi (~7–8 hours), local taxi to Gaurikund, then trek 16 km or take helicopter to Kedarnath.

mainEntity.name: What are the Kedarnath darshan timings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Morning: 4:00 AM to 12:00 noon. Evening aarti: 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM. The 4:00 AM opening darshan is considered most auspicious.

mainEntity.name: Is Kedarnath Yatra registration mandatory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — compulsory for all pilgrims. Register free at registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in. Each person registers individually.

mainEntity.name: What is the history of Kedarnath Temple?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Pandavas built the original shrine post-Kurukshetra war. The current stone structure dates from the 8th century CE. The 2013 floods destroyed the surrounding valley but left the temple untouched.

mainEntity.name: How long is the trek from Gaurikund to Kedarnath?

acceptedAnswer.text: 16 km one way — 5–8 hours ascending, 4–6 hours descending depending on fitness.

blocks.text: For devotees of Lord Shiva, the Kedarnath Yatra package from Mumbai is one of the most sacred journeys a person can undertake. The temple sits at 3,583 metres in the Garhwal Himalayas — 16 km beyond the last motorable road, accessible only by trek or helicopter.

Mumbai is at sea level. The altitude difference is 3,583 metres. Planning this journey independently — flights, mountain taxis, Kedarnath accommodation, Yatra Registration, trek logistics — takes weeks and still leaves most pilgrims uncertain about what they will face on the ground.

At My Quick Trippers, we have been managing Kedarnath Yatra packages for 17 years. Every transport detail, hotel booking, and on-ground arrangement is handled. You arrive at the Kedarnath temple with energy left for the purpose of the journey.
What Is a Kedarnath Yatra Package from Mumbai?

A Kedarnath Yatra package from Mumbai is an all-inclusive pilgrimage tour covering travel from Mumbai to Kedarnath temple and back. It includes flights or train coordination, all mountain ground transport, hotel stays, vegetarian meals, Yatra Registration assistance, and a dedicated tour manager. Standard packages run 7 to 9 days . Prices start from approximately ₹25,000 per person for group packages and go up to ₹85,000+ for helicopter packages.

Kedarnath is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga temples of Lord Shiva - the most sacred form of Shiva worship in Hinduism. It forms a key part of both the Char Dham Yatra and the Panch Kedar pilgrimage circuit.

The temple origin traces to the Mahabharata. After the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas sought Lord Shiva's forgiveness for killing their kin. Shiva, unwilling to give them audience, took the form of a bull and disappeared into the earth at this spot. When Bhima caught the bull, only the hump remained above ground - that hump is the Shivalinga worshipped at Kedarnath today.
The 2013 floods that devastated the surrounding valley left the temple itself untouched. For millions of Shiva devotees, this is not coincidence.

blocks.text: Route Guide for Kedarnath Yatra from Mumbai

By Flight (Recommended): Mumbai to Dehradun (Jolly Grant Airport) - approximately 2 hours direct, or 3-3.5 hours via Delhi. From Jolly Grant, road transfer to Guptkashi - approximately 220 km, 7-8 hours.
By Train: Mumbai CSMT or LTT to Haridwar - approximately 18-22 hours. Book 60-90 days in advance during Yatra season.
Complete Route: Mumbai → Dehradun/Haridwar → Rishikesh → Devprayag → Rudraprayag → Guptkashi → Sonprayag → Gaurikund → Trek 16 km or Helicopter → Kedarnath Temple, 3,583 metres
Day-by-Day Itinerary - Standard 9-Day Package from Mumbai

rows: Flight or overnight train, arrive and check in
Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri, rest, overnight
Mountain drive via Devprayag, Rudraprayag (~8 hrs)
Acclimatisation - Kashi Vishwanath Temple visit, rest
Early start, trek or helicopter, darshan, overnight near temple
Early morning darshan (4:00 AM), Bhairavnath Temple, return trek/helicopter to Guptkashi
Triveni Ghat Aarti, rest before departure

blocks.text: Why Day 4 acclimatisation at Guptkashi matters: Mumbai is at sea level. Kedarnath is at 3,583 metres. The acclimatisation day at Guptkashi (1,319 metres) gives your body a gradual altitude adjustment - this directly reduces Altitude Mountain Sickness risk on the trek day.

Why the Day 5 overnight near Kedarnath is worth booking: The 4:00 AM darshan - before the day crowds arrive - is the most spiritually significant part of the entire Kedarnath experience. Day-trip pilgrims from Guptkashi miss this entirely.
Best Time for Kedarnath Yatra from Mumbai

rows: Heavy rain, frequent landslides, helicopter disruptions
Crisp air, lower crowds, clear views

blocks.text: For Mumbai pilgrims, September and early October are ideal - stable weather and a more peaceful darshan experience than the May-June peak.
The trek is 16 km one way, gaining 1,400 metres in altitude. Most pilgrims take 5-8 hours ascending, 4-6 hours descending.

The first 4 km out of Gaurikund are the steepest - stone-stepped, continuous climb. The trail then opens into the Mandakini river valley. The final stretch to the temple is steep again. Medical aid posts are stationed at regular intervals.

rows: Carries your bag so you walk lighter

blocks.text: Book at official counters at Gaurikund only - our tour manager takes you directly to the right counter.

Not booking flights with the package. Mumbai-Dehradun fares during Yatra season rise steeply close to travel dates. Pilgrims who book the package first and "sort flights later" often pay ₹4,000-₹8,000 more per ticket.

Assuming Mumbai weather prepares you for Kedarnath. Mumbai is at sea level and humid. Kedarnath nights in May drop to 0-5°C. Most Mumbai pilgrims arrive with one light jacket - completely inadequate for 3,583 metres.

Skipping the acclimatisation day. A direct Haridwar-to-Kedarnath push in one day is the most common reason for AMS on this route. Our itinerary builds a rest day at Guptkashi for this reason - do not ask us to remove it.

Booking helicopter tickets from unofficial sources. IRCTC helicopter tickets are sold only at heliyatra.irctc.co.in. Any agent or WhatsApp contact offering these tickets is running a fraud without exception.

Comparing total package price without checking inclusions. A ₹18,000 "Kedarnath package from Mumbai" that excludes accommodation, meals, and return transport is not cheaper than a ₹38,000 all-inclusive package. Always get a written line-by-line breakdown before paying advance.

Start the Gaurikund trek by 5:00-5:30 AM. Reaching Kedarnath by 9:00-10:00 AM means attending the morning puja, darshan in smaller crowds, and having the afternoon to explore Bhairavnath Temple and the surrounding area before the afternoon cloud buildup.

Carry a pulse oximeter from Mumbai. A small device (₹800-₹1,200) that monitors blood oxygen at altitude. At 3,583 metres, normal resting SpO2 drops to 88-93% for most people. Knowing your number helps you decide whether to rest or continue.
Break in your trekking shoes 2-3 weeks before travel. New shoes on a 16 km mountain trek cause blisters that can genuinely ruin the journey. Wear the shoes daily for 2 weeks before the trip.
Book a ground-floor room if travelling with parents above 65. Mountain hotels have no lifts. After a long trek day, walking up 3 flights of stairs at altitude is exhausting - even for fit pilgrims.

Attend the Sandhya Aarti at 7:30 PM on arrival evening. Most pilgrims who stay overnight focus on the morning darshan and miss the evening aarti. Both are worth attending - the Sandhya Aarti at dusk with the temple lit up against snow peaks is unlike anything else.
