About Kainchi Dham and Neem Karoli Baba

Kainchi Dham is a serene Ashram known for its spiritual significance. The Ashram was established by Neem Karoli Baba , who was also known as Maharaj ji in the 1960s. Located near Nainital , Uttarakhand , it is believed to have performed many miracles in the lives of devotees. Celebrities like Steve Jobs , Mark Zuckerberg , Virat Kohli etc have visited the place due to its high popularity.

The moment you step in the Kainchi Dham Ashram, you are sure to experience an unmatched divine atmosphere that’s going to fill you with immense peace. The Ashram is dedicated to Lord Hanuman and also houses the Samadhi of Neem Karoli Baba. It can be a great place to unplug from the hassle of big cities and engage in meditation here.

Daily rituals, Pooja, spiritual practices like collective meditation are performed in the ashram. The Ashram also organizes a grand feast (Bhandara) on June 15th every year. One must experience the energy of the serene and peaceful environment of this place at least once in their lives.
Why Choose Kainchi Dham Tour Package?

Choose the right package for Neem Karoli Baba Dham Darshan to witness the spiritual essence along with the beauty of Nainital’s hills. Here’s some of the benefits of choosing My Quick Trippers’s package:

items: Transportation: We provide a comfortable travel option starting from your pick up point in Delhi to Kainchi Dham via a shared transport or private vehicle.
Accommodation: We provide the most comfortable hotels in and around Nainital to make your stay even better.
Sightseeing: You can go around and explore the nearby attractions of Nainital.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Kainchi Dham from Delhi

The best time to visit Kainchi Dham Ashram is between March and June (summer) or September to November (autumn), as the weather stays pleasant during these months, which helps enhance your overall tour experience.

In the peak season, that is summers, the ashram draws a large number of people from every corner of the world. And, therefore, it can sometimes get very crowded. Therefore, we suggest the autumn window, if you prefer fewer crowds.
There are many places to visit near Kainchi Dham that travellers must visit-

Naini Lake, also called Nainital Lake, is the main place to visit and a popular spot near Kainchi Dham. It is surrounded by seven beautiful hills and attracts travelers from all over the world. Many tourists come here, so it's known as one of the most visited lakes in India.

The name “Nainital” comes from two words- “Naina” means eye, and “Tal” means lake. In Hindu mythology, when Sati jumped into the fire, her eyes fell here, and the lake formed at this spot. Because of this, the lake is very special to many people. The boat ride is a relaxing and gives a unique experience that visitors shouldn’t miss. The views from the boat are wonderful for taking photos. A must-addition to the your Kainchi Dham Yatra package!

items: Entry Fee- There is no entry fee to visit Naini Lake. However, if you want to enjoy the boat ride, a small ticket fee is charged.

blocks.text: Bhowali is a peaceful town in Kumaon, located 1704 meters above sea level. This place is well known for growing great fruits like apples, peaches, strawberries, plums, and apricots that are sent to many places. The views in Bhowali are beautiful, and many travelers come here for camping, trekking, and enjoying nature. The place is peaceful and nice, so it’s good to visit anytime. You can often see animals like jackals, kakkar, Himalayan eagles, and pheasants here.

Neem Karoli Baba Ashram is a special place that many people visit for spiritual peace. It’s close to Kainchi Dham and is built in memory of the great saint Neem Karoli Baba. The ashram has a calm and positive atmosphere. It’s a nice place to relax and learn. People also take part in prayers and satsangs every day.

Pangot is a small and beautiful village approximately 28 km away from Kainchi Dham. It’s well known for its forests and a variety of birds. When you reach Pangot, it’s like entering a peaceful mountain village, away from all the city noise. If you enjoy birdwatching, you’ll love this place because more than 300 bird species can be seen nearby. Birds like woodpeckers, thrushes, and sometimes even eagles can be seen here. If you're looking for peace or enjoy spending time in nature, Pangot is a wonderful place to visit. If you're on a Kainchi Dham trip, do come here as it’s a refreshing visit.

The town of Bhimtal is named after Bhima, one of the well-known Pandava brothers in the Mahabharata. It is famous for its beautiful lake. People love it for its wonderful surroundings, and it is located at 1,370 metres above sea level. In the middle of Bhimtal Lake, there’s a small island with a big aquarium. Earlier, this aquarium was a restaurant. This lake is surrounded by natural beauty, has lovely views, and is well connected by road. It’s a good place to visit in any season.
How to Reach Kainchi Dham from Delhi?

Road trip from Delhi to Kainchi Dham takes around 6 to 7 hours and is the easiest way to reach there. You can either drive yourself or take a taxi. You can also travel from Delhi to Haldwani by bus or train, and then take a taxi from Haldwani to Kainchi Dham.

If you’re travelling by train, Kathgodam is the nearest station. Trains like the Ranikhet Express or Uttar Sampark Kranti Express take about 6 hours from Delhi to Kathgodam. From there, Kainchi Dham is 43 km away. You can easily find taxis or shared cabs outside the station. Road to Kainchi Dham is good and has lovely views of hills and forests.

If you want to travel by flight, the nearest airport to Kainchi Dham is Pantnagar Airport, around 70 km away. It is a small airport with limited flights. From there, you can take a taxi or a local bus to reach Kainchi Dham.
Here's what you should bring for a Kainchi Dham Darshan:

items: Medical Needs: Remember to carry motion sickness tablets (only if your doctor says it’s okay), some vomit bags, lemon candies, a small towel, and water to help you stay comfortable and fresh during the trip.
Comfortable Shoes: Choose comfortable shoes or sandals with a good grip so you can walk easily in the hills.
Power Bank / Portable Charger: Electricity may not always work well in the hills, so bring a power bank to keep your phone charged.
Snacks with High Energy: Carry energy bars, nuts, or dry fruits with you because shops can be far away, and these snacks will keep you active during walks or temple visits.

blocks.text: Travel Tips for Kainchi Dham Tour

items: Don’t go on Crowded Days: On June 15th, there’s a Bhandara, and thousands of devotees come. It’s better to skip that day unless you’re okay with big crowds.
Avoid Plastic and Keep the Area Clean: Try to keep the place clean. Don’t use plastic bags or bottles, and always throw trash in the dustbin.
Carry Some Cash: You’ll find only a few ATMs around, and they don’t always work. Many shops won’t take a card or UPI, so make sure you have some cash with you.

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrive Delhi – Drive to Kainchi Dham (330 km / 7 hours)

items: Welcome to Delhi! Once you arrive at Delhi airport or railway station, you will receive a warm welcome from our tour representative.

Now, begin a scenic drive among the Himalayan foothills to Kainchi Dham . This spiritual Ashram is located amidst lush green valleys near Bhowali. Also, this ashram is world famous, and celebrities like Apple founder Steve Jobs and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg have visited this place!
Once you get there, check into your pre-booked hotel. Have some rest if you feel like!

In the evening, get ready to visit the Kainchi Dham Temple . Soak in the utterly calm vibe of this ashram. Take some time out to meditate in its serene surroundings. You can also attend the evening prayers here!
Your night stay will be in the Kainchi Dham.

blocks.text: Day 2: Morning at Kainchi Dham – Sightseeing in Nainital (20-25 km / 1.5 hours)

items: Have the perfect start to your day with meditation in the peaceful atmosphere of the Ashram. Take this time to ponder over the humanitarian teachings of the Neem Karoli Baba.
After that, have breakfast. Now, you can explore the ashram complex and learn more about Baba’s teachings of love, service, and devotion. Also, visit the sacred banyan tree!

After your Kainchi Dham visit, you can go on exploring the nearby sightseeing places, such as Bhumiadhar Temple . Dedicated to Goddess Shakti, it’s famous for its calm energy and less crowded atmosphere.
Later, you’ll be taken on a sightseeing tour of the ever-so-beautiful Nainital . Explore Naini Lake and the Naina Devi Temple here, which is also one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.
Now, go on a trip to a trio of scenic lakes – Bhimtal, Sattal, and Naukuchiatal . You can spot migratory birds here. You can also just sit here in its pure serene vibes!

The last trip of the day will be made to the most famous market of Nainital, that is Mall Road . Explore the myriad of shops here, selling everything from handicrafts to delicious food. We recommend trying the local Kumaoni dishes such as Bhatt ki Churkani and the spicy Aloo ke Gutke!
End the day by going to your hotel in Nainital and getting a restful night of sleep.
Have a delicious breakfast in the morning.
Afterwards, depart from Nainital towards Delhi, as your tour concludes today. Don't forget to capture the beautiful sunrise views over the hills as you leave Nainital!
Our driver will drop you off at the Delhi airport or railway station, as per your preference. Hope you have a fantastic trip!

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. Why is Kainchi Dham so popular?

Ans. It is a spiritual ashram located in Uttarakhand. It was established by Neem Karoli Baba, who was a spiritual guru. The ashram is believed to have performed many miracles and transformed the lives of many devotees.
Q2. How to reach Kainchi Dham?
Ans. It is located 20 km away from Nainital. The nearest Airport is Pantnagar airport, and the nearest railway station is Kathgodam.
Q3. Are meals included in the package?
Ans. Vegetarian meals are included in the package at the hotel and are served as Prasad at Kainchi Dham.
Q4. Is there any dress code to visit the Ashram?
Ans. There is no strict dress code, however, it is recommended to dress modestly, considering the spiritual nature of the ashram.
Q5. What activities are available at Kainchi Dham Ashram?
Ans. There are a variety of activities available at the Ashram. You can engage here in meditation, Satsang, Yoga sessions, Temple Rituals and even Seva.
Q6. How far is Kainchi Dham from Delhi?
Ans. Kainchi Dham is located about 330 km from Delhi. This 7–8-hour drive is quite scenic as you pass through the Himalayan foothills and forests.
Q7. When is the best time to visit Kainchi Dham?

Ans. The best time to visit Kainchi Dham is from March to June in summer. This window offers you quite pleasant weather where you can comfortably indulge in sightseeing and other things. Another great period to come down here is in the autumn season, that is, from September to November. The skies are clear in this season, and you get to enjoy fewer crowds.
Q8. Is photography allowed inside Kainchi Dham?
Ans. The Kainchi Dham is quite sacred, and therefore, to maintain its sanctity, the photography inside the ashram is restricted. However, you can capture the pics from outside!
Q9. Do I need prior permission to visit Kainchi Dham Ashram?
Ans. If you're visiting for a single day, you don’t need to obtain any prior permission. However, if you wish to stay inside the Ashram, special permission is required from the management staff.
Q10. Are there any accommodation facilities near Kainchi Dham?

Ans. Yes, Kainchi Dham has so many guesthouses and small hotels nearby it that you can easily stay near the Ashram. With our package, you get to enjoy staying in a comfortable accommodation, which will be booked by us on your behalf.

It is said that for every Hindu devotee, the Darshan of Lord Kedarnath is a must. Blessed are the people who get a chance to undertake the challenging journey to Baba Kedar once in a lifetime. Our Kedarnath Yatra Tour packages can fulfill your auspicious dream of landing at the sacred abode of Baba Kedar.

Our Kedarnath itineraries are crafted according to your preferences and are suitable for all age groups whether family, solo traveller or senior citizen. So, don't miss the amazing chance to see the highest Lord Shiva Jyotirlinga temple . Book our Kedarnath Travel Packages which will take care of A to Z of your travel in the tricky hilly areas.

Every package below includes AC vehicle, trained hill driver, driver allowance, tolls, parking, fuel, GST, hotel, and VIP Darshan coordination. Helicopter shuttle fares (IRCTC) and Char Dham registration are separate.

What most people don't realize: the price difference between a ₹18,500 group package and a ₹22,500 private package is roughly ₹800 per day. For a family with elderly parents or young children, that ₹1000/day gap buys you a private vehicle, flexible timing, and the ability to stop whenever needed. Worth it.
Group Tour vs Private Tour - Which Kedarnath Package Is Right for You?

From practical experience: solo pilgrims under 45 with flexible schedules do great on group packages. Families with anyone above 60 — always go private. The extra cost is minor. The difference in comfort and pace is significant.
Kedarnath Helicopter Package - Prices and How It Works
Helicopter Yatra is not a luxury — for senior citizens, it is often the safest option. The 16 km trek from Gaurikund is completely bypassed. You land 500 metres from the temple.

IRCTC is the only authorised platform for shuttle tickets. No agent or portal can sell IRCTC shuttle tickets. Booking opens mid-April 2026 for pre-monsoon; mid-June for September–October dates. Slots for Phata and Guptkashi sell out within hours on opening day — have your URN ready before 6 PM.
Fraud warning: Agents on WhatsApp, Instagram, and travel apps 'sell' Kedarnath helicopter tickets every season. Many are fake. Report to cybercrime.gov.in. Only use heliyatra.irctc.co.in.
Kedarnath Yatra Registration - Mandatory QR Pass
Every single pilgrim must register before visiting Kedarnath. No registration = no entry at Sonprayag. Registration is free.

items: Go to registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in — or WhatsApp 'Yatra' to 8394833833
Enter pilgrim details + Aadhaar / Passport number
Download QR-coded e-pass — carry digital + printed copy

blocks.text: One mistake many people make: they arrive at Sonprayag checkpoint without completing this registration, assuming it can be done on the spot. It cannot. The process takes 5 minutes online — do it 2–3 days before your departure. My Quick Trippers assists all clients with this at no charge.

Contact My Quick Trippers at +91-8171158569 or myquicktrippers.com with your travel dates, group size, and city of departure.

On travel day: My Quick Trippers driver picks you up. From that point, everything — Sonprayag arrival timing, Gaurikund departure, trek pace, Darshan slot — is coordinated.

blocks.text: If you are planning this seriously: book at least 60 days in advance for May–June dates. September–October packages can be booked 30 days out. What happens if you delay? In peak 2025 season, Phata and Guptkashi IRCTC slots sold in 90 minutes. Hotels near the base helipads were fully booked by March. Starting late means paying more and getting less.

Perfect weather for trekking. Snow still visible on peaks. But Sonprayag sees 8,000–10,000 pilgrims daily in this window. Book 60–90 days ahead. Budget at least 90 minutes for Sonprayag queue. Arrive early.

This is where experienced Kedarnath yatris go. Post-monsoon skies are clear, queues are short, Darshan is peaceful. Nights drop to -5°C — carry serious woollens. Helicopter slots are easier to get. First-time visitors: choose this window.
Helicopter suspended. NH-58 landslides close the route regularly. The trek becomes dangerously slippery. No responsible operator recommends this window. Skip it.
Sonprayag is where every pilgrim's real journey begins — and where most itineraries fall apart if not planned correctly.

items: Sonprayag is the last point for private vehicles. From here, a government-authorised shuttle (Mahindra Bolero, ₹50 fixed) covers 5 km to Gaurikund.
In peak May–June, Sonprayag parking fills by 6:30–7 AM. My Quick Trippers drivers know this — our standard departure from base hotels is 3:30–4 AM.
At Gaurikund (1,981 m), take a dip in Gauri Kund hot spring before the trek. Customary, sacred, and practically useful — warm water eases the muscles before the 16 km climb.
Trek milestones: Gaurikund → Jungle Chatti (4 km, toughest) → Bheembali (6 km, rest point) → Rambara (9 km) → Lincholi (13 km, altitude felt here) → Kedarnath (16 km).
Average trek time: 6–8 hours upward. Return: 4–5 hours. Plan minimum 2 days — one to ascend, one for darshan and descent.
Pony: ₹3,000–₹5,000 round trip. Palki: ₹8,000–₹12,000. Helicopter shuttle: IRCTC booking.

blocks.text: What a Real Kedarnath Package Day Looks Like

4:00 AM. Your My Quick Trippers driver is outside the hotel, engine running. You leave Guptkashi while the rest of the town sleeps. The road to Sonprayag is clear at this hour — 35 minutes, no traffic.

5:15 AM. You are at Sonprayag. The parking lot has maybe 20 vehicles. You board the government shuttle to Gaurikund in 8 minutes. Others who arrive at 8 AM will wait 90 minutes for this same shuttle. That is the only difference — departure time.

6:00 AM. Trek begins at Gaurikund. The first 4 km to Jungle Chatti is steep. Your My Quick Trippers guide sets a slow, deliberate pace. No rushing. At Bheembali (6 km), a tea stall. Sit for 10 minutes. Eat something.

By 11:30 AM, you reach Kedarnath. Your VIP Darshan coupon — arranged in advance — takes you to the priority entry. General queue at this time is 3 hours long. You complete Darshan in 40 minutes. The Jyotirlinga up close, the chanting, the high-altitude stillness. That moment is why this Yatra exists.

From practical experience, the single factor that separates a smooth Kedarnath Yatra from a chaotic one is not money — it is departure time from the base hotel. Leave by 4 AM. Everything else follows.

Common Mistakes Pilgrims Make on Kedarnath Tour

items: Skipping Char Dham registration until arrival. Entry denied at Sonprayag without QR e-pass. Takes 5 minutes online — do it 2–3 days before departure, not on the road.
Leaving the base hotel after 7 AM. Sonprayag parking fills by 6:30–7 AM in May–June. Late arrival means 2+ hours wasted before the trek even begins.
Booking helicopter tickets through WhatsApp agents. Every season, pilgrims pay ₹5,000–₹15,000 to agents for IRCTC tickets that either don't exist or are revoked. Use heliyatra.irctc.co.in only.
Not carrying printed documents. Mobile network fails between Sonprayag and Kedarnath. If your phone dies at the checkpoint, a printed Char Dham e-pass and ID copy saves you.
Wearing wrong footwear. Sandals and sneakers on the Kedarnath trek cause ankle injuries on the rocky path, especially on the descent. Trekking shoes or grip-soled boots only.

Rushing at altitude. Pilgrims who push pace above Lincholi (13 km mark) are the ones who end up with AMS symptoms — headache, nausea — and can't complete darshan. Walk slower than you think you need to.

Booking only for themselves, not accounting for delays. If your return train from Haridwar is on Day 4 and your trek Day is Day 3, a single weather delay or landslide destroys the plan. Always keep a buffer day.

blocks.text: Pro Tips for Kedarnath Tour Package

For road Yatra: reach Gaurikund by 6–6:30 AM. This gives you 5–6 hours of trek time before the afternoon cloud buildup and crowd peak at the temple.
September 15 – October 10 is the sweet spot — post-monsoon clarity, 60–70% fewer pilgrims than May, and IRCTC helicopter slots that are actually bookable without a 6 PM alarm.
Carry ₹3,000–₹5,000 in cash. UPI fails above Sonprayag. ATMs at Gaurikund run dry in peak season. Your entire on-ground spending — shuttle, tea stalls, emergency — depends on physical cash.

Senior citizens: get the medical fitness certificate before departure. Without it, Char Dham registration cannot be completed for 60+ pilgrims. Your doctor signs it — takes 10 minutes.

blocks.text: Kedarnath is the highest Jyotirlinga in India. At 11,755 ft, the air is significantly thinner. Helicopter pilgrims ascend from 1,319 m to 3,583 m in under 15 minutes — zero acclimatisation time.

items: AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness): Headache, nausea, dizziness within 2–4 hours of arrival. Rest and hydrate. Descend if it worsens.
HAPE (High Altitude Pulmonary Edema): Fluid in lungs. Persistent cough, chest tightness, breathlessness at rest. Medical emergency — immediate descent needed.
HACE (High Altitude Cerebral Edema): Brain swelling. Severe headache, disorientation, loss of balance. Requires immediate evacuation.
Walk slowly. Take breaks every 30 minutes above 2,500 m. Never rush.
Heart / BP / COPD conditions: medical fitness certificate mandatory. Declare at registration.
Pregnant women (6+ weeks): not permitted on the high-altitude route.

blocks.text: Kedarnath and the Panch Kedar — The Complete Circuit
Kedarnath is the first of the five Panch Kedar shrines. Each represents a part of Lord Shiva's divine bull form that appeared across the Garhwal Himalayas.

After the Kurukshetra war, the Pandavas sought Lord Shiva's forgiveness for the bloodshed. Shiva, unwilling to grant them absolution easily, took the form of a bull and fled to the Himalayas. At Kedarnath, Bhima recognized the bull and grabbed it — but the bull disappeared into the ground, leaving only his hump above the surface.

The hump became the Kedarnath Jyotirlinga. Other parts of the bull are said to have emerged at four other locations — together forming the Panch Kedar . The temple, originally built by the Pandavas and restored by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century, has stood at 3,583 m for over 1,200 years.

blocks.text: Pleasant Pilgrimage Tour to The Revered Shirdi

The town of Shirdi is situated 300km away from Mumbai. It lies right in the middle of Maharashtra’s ‘sugar cane belt’. It happens to be the most visited pilgrimage site immediately after Tirupati which lies in Andhra Pradesh.

This is owing to the fact that this place belongs to Sai Baba, a revered religious and spiritual guide who is also considered God’s incarnation and worshipped with devotion and fervour. People belonging to various faiths and ‘walks of life’ meet here at Shirdi to worship their favourite ‘Sai Baba’ in reverence and awe. They get inspiration from the teachings of Sai Baba. They gather at Shirdi to pay their homage to this divine human being. Every year several thousand pilgrims visit this place to gain spiritual blessings from Shirdi Sai Baba, making it one the most important tourist destinations in India.

My Quick Trippers offers an exclusive tour package to Shirdi Sai Baba that will take you through Shani Shingnapur and Nashik. The pilgrimage tour packages organized by this well-reputed online travel agency are aimed at allowing you to smoothly enjoy the trip and at making your spiritual advances the way you prefer to. All provisions related to the pilgrimage including the stay and the shrines for visit, are selected in order of high demand of visitors for the location. With professional assistance, this online company ensures that your Shirdi trip is a religiously blissful one without any bumps on the way. And for the convenience of the customers My Quick Trippers also provides customization of the tour packages to meet the budget requirements of the customers.
Day 1 : Shirdi Arrival and Shani Shingnapur Visit:

You will be picked up by My Quick Trippers representative from Kopargaon /Nagarsol/Manmad railway station and taken safely to Shirdi where you will check into a hotel booked for you. After freshening up you will visit the ‘Shirdi Temple’ for ‘darshan’. This place is flocked with devotees who need to travel 296km from the city of Mumbai to visit this Temple that is built over Sai Baba’s Samadhi. Both the Hindu and Muslim communities deeply revere this place and make it point to visit this blessed place. After your ‘darshan’ is over you will take a launch to reach Shani Shingnapur, a tiny Maharashtra village famous for the ‘Shani Temple’ located here. Inside the shrine is a ‘black rock’ 5.5ft in height which signifies the presence of the Hindu deity, Lord Shiva. The village too is popular because none of the houses here has a ‘door’ and surprisingly no report of robbery has been registered here. The residents of this village believe that anyone who tries to steal will be heavily punished by Lord Shiva. Return to Shirdi to spend the night.
Day 2 : Shirdi to Nashik (140km/ 3 hours) and Back

On day 2 after a filling breakfast you will go one to visit the ‘Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple’ and then move on to the ‘Kalaram Temple’, the ‘Muktidham’, the ‘Seetha Guha’, the ‘Panchavati Goraram Temple’, the ‘Kapaleswar Temple’, the ‘Godavari Ghat’ and the ‘Chandramouleshwara Mandir’ after which you will return to Shirdi. While ‘Muktidham’ is a popular located on Nashik road where Hindu deities are worshipped, ‘Panchvati’ is another significant pilgrimage centre where Lord Ram is supposed to have dwelt with brother Laxman and wife Sita. The ‘Godavari Ghat’ houses the ‘Godavari Temple’ that was constructed by Gopikabai, mother of ‘Elder Madhavrao Peshwa’ in the year 1760. This temple remains open strictly while the ‘Kumbh Mela’ is on. As you cover all these places, you will keep coming closer to Nashik which again has mythological prominence with Lord Ram spending his exile (final four months) in Tapovan, next to Nashik. Important tourist spots along the periphery of Nahsik are inclusive of the ‘Dudhsagar Falls’, the ‘Gangapur Dam’, the ‘Pandavleni Caves’, the ‘Museum of Numismatics’, the ‘Nandur Madhyameshwar Bird Sanctuary” and the ‘Anjaneri Parvat’. The wine exported from Nashik is world-famous. After visiting the vineyards you will be taken back to Shirdi for spending the night.
Day 3 : Departing Shirdi and End of Tour

On the final day, you can visit the ‘Shirdi Temple’ one final time and return to the hotel for breakfast after which you will be safely transported to Kopargaon/ Nagarsol/ Manmad railway station to get back home with spiritual awakening and lots of blessings.

About Kamakhya Temple - The Supreme Shakti Peeth of India

Kamakhya Temple stands apart from every other temple in India. Perched atop Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam, it is the most powerful of the 51 Shakti Peethas - and the only Yoni Peetha, where the creative energy of Goddess Sati is believed to reside.

According to the Kalika Purana, when Goddess Sati self-immolated at Daksha's Yagna after her father insulted Lord Shiva, a grief-stricken Shiva carried her body through the universe. Lord Vishnu used his Sudarshana Chakra to divide Sati's remains into 51 parts. The Yoni fell here, on these very hills.

What strikes every first-time visitor: there is no idol inside the main sanctum. Devotees descend into a small, dark cave and offer prayers at a natural fissure in the rock - always moist from an underground spring. No statue, no image. Just the raw, living energy of the Goddess.

The temple's architecture follows the Nilachala style - a beehive-shaped dome surrounded by smaller shrines, different from anything in North or South India. The complex houses the full Dasa Mahavidya - ten great forms of the Divine Mother - each with its own temple on the hill.
Ambubachi Mela - Kamakhya's Most Sacred Annual Event

Every June (22nd-25th), Kamakhya Temple closes its doors for three days. This is Ambubachi - the annual period when Goddess Kamakhya is believed to undergo her menstrual cycle. The natural spring inside the temple is said to run red during these days.

When the temple reopens (from 26 June), the Ambubachi Mela begins and runs till 3 July. Lakhs of devotees, sadhus, and Tantric practitioners gather from across India. It is one of the largest spiritual congregations in Northeast India. If you plan to attend, book your Kamakhya tour package at least 3-4 months in advance - hotels fill fast.

Practical tip: Arrive before 8:00 AM on weekdays for shorter queues. Weekends and Hindu festival days are significantly busier. Purchase the VIP Darshan Pass (₹501/-) at the temple counter to avoid the general queue.
Best Time to Visit Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati

From practical experience: October to February is the sweet spot. The weather is pleasant, Darshan queues are manageable, and the Brahmaputra looks its most picturesque. Most families, senior pilgrims, and solo travelers prefer this window.
How to Reach Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati

The nearest airport is Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (LGBI), Guwahati - approximately 14 km from Kamakhya Temple. Direct flights connect Guwahati to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Pune. Our package includes airport pickup.

Two railway stations serve the temple: Guwahati Railway Station (main, ~10 km from temple) and Kamakhya Railway Station (~2 km from temple, closer option). Major trains include Rajdhani Express, Brahmaputra Mail, and Saraighat Express from Delhi and Kolkata. Our package includes station pickup.

Guwahati is connected via National Highway 27. State buses, private taxis, and app-based cabs are easily available from the city. The temple hill is about 8 km from Guwahati city centre - roughly 25 minutes by road. Note: the final stretch up Nilachal Hill is by road or on foot (~200 steps).

blocks.text: Practical Tips for Visiting Kamakhya Temple

items: Reach early - Arrive before 8:00 AM on weekdays. The morning Darshan is calmer, the air is cooler, and the experience is far more personal.
Buy the VIP Pass - ₹501/- per person, purchased at the temple counter. Saves 2–4 hours in the general queue on busy days.
Carry cash - ATMs are at the temple base but can be crowded. Keep ₹500–700 in cash for the pass, Prasad, flowers, and small donations.
Wear appropriate clothes - Modest clothing — avoid shorts and sleeveless tops inside the temple. Sandals are easier than laced shoes.
Photography rule - Photography inside the main sanctum (the cave chamber) is strictly prohibited. Outer courtyard is fine.
Combine with Navagraha - Navagraha Temple is a 15-minute drive from Kamakhya. Very few tour operators include it — we do, on Day 2.
Ambubachi planning - Book 3–4 months in advance if visiting during Ambubachi Mela (late June). Hotels at Guwahati book up quickly.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is included in the Kamakhya Temple tour package?

Ans. The package includes 1-night hotel accommodation (double sharing), daily breakfast, a private AC vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing, pickup and drop from Guwahati Airport/Railway Station, and all applicable taxes. Excludes VIP darshan pass, ferry/ropeway charges, personal expenses, and airfare/train tickets.
Q2. How many days are needed for the Kamakhya Temple tour?

Ans. Our standard package is 2 days / 1 night, which is sufficient to cover Kamakhya Darshan and all major Guwahati spiritual sites. If you plan to add Kaziranga National Park or Shillong, extend to 4–6 days.
Q3. What is the Kamakhya Temple tour package cost per person?
Ans. Standard package starts at ₹5,650 per person (double sharing, currently at 15% discount from ₹6,500). Deluxe and Luxury options are available on request. Use coupon WELCOME500 for extra savings.
Q4. When is the best time to visit Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. October to February is ideal — weather is pleasant (12°C–24°C), queues are manageable, and the Brahmaputra looks its most scenic. The Ambubachi Mela in late June is the most spiritually powerful time but requires advance booking due to massive crowds.
Q5. What is Ambubachi Mela and when does it happen?

Ans. Ambubachi Mela celebrates the annual menstrual cycle of Goddess Kamakhya. The temple closes from 22–25 June every year, then reopens with a grand Mela running from 26 June to 3 July. Lakhs of devotees attend. Book your Kamakhya Yatra package at least 3–4 months early if you plan to attend.
Q6. Is a VIP Darshan pass available at Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. Yes. The VIP Darshan Pass costs ₹501/- per person and is purchased directly at the temple counter. It allows faster entry and is strongly recommended on weekends, festivals, and peak season (October–February). This charge is NOT included in the tour package price.
Q7. What temples are covered besides Kamakhya in the 2-day package?

Ans. The itinerary covers all major Dasa Mahavidya temples on Nilachal Hill (Dhumavati, Tripureswari, Maa Tara, Maa Kali, Chhinnamasta, Bagalamukhi, Bhuvaneshwari, Banadurga), Umananda Temple on Peacock Island, Navagraha Temple, and a Brahmaputra sunset cruise (optional, direct payment).
Q8. Is Kamakhya Temple accessible for elderly or differently-abled visitors?

Ans. There are approximately 200 steps to the temple, but a road also goes up to Nilachal Hill by car. Elderly pilgrims can be driven to the temple entrance and walk only a short final stretch. Our driver and guide assist accordingly.
Q9. Can I arrange a special puja at Kamakhya Temple through this package?

Ans. Yes. Inform us at least 1 day before your tour date and we will coordinate with the temple priests to arrange special puja or ritual as per your requirements. Additional costs for puja materials and priest fees apply and are paid directly.
Q10. What is the pickup and meet-up process?

Ans. Our representative will be waiting outside the exit gate of Guwahati Airport or Railway Station, holding a placard with your name. Driver and cab details are shared 1 day prior to tour start. Pickups can also be arranged from your hotel or residence in Guwahati.
Q11. Is this tour available for solo travelers?
Ans. Absolutely. Solo traveler packages are available. Pricing differs from twin-share rates — contact us directly for a solo quote. We also run group departure tours that solo travelers can join.
Q12. Can I customize the tour or add more destinations?

Ans. Yes. We offer extended Northeast India packages combining Kamakhya with Kaziranga National Park (one-horned rhinoceros, UNESCO World Heritage Site), Shillong, Cherrapunji, Majuli Island, and Manas National Park. Contact our team for a customized itinerary and pricing.

Places to Visit in Sri Lanka
Here are the top destinations covered in our Sri Lanka vacation packages from Hyderabad :

Ravana Falls and Ravana Cave are just 2 km from Ella, famous from the Ramayana. According to the Ramayana tradition, this cave is associated with the period when Sita was held captive in Lanka. The waterfall cascades through a lush valley and you can swim in the cool water at the base.
Tip: Fog is common until 10 AM — arrive after that for clearer views.

Sigiriya, also called Lion Rock, is a 200-metre-high ancient rock fortress — UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built as King Kashyapa's palace in the 5th century, it is now one of Sri Lanka's most visited archaeological sites. Climb to the top for the Lion Gate, colourful frescoes, and views across the surrounding jungle.
Tip: Start your climb before 7 AM to avoid crowds and midday heat.

Dambulla Cave Temple is more than 2,000 years old, dating from the 1st century BCE when King Valagamba took refuge here — five caves filled with Buddha statues, ancient paintings, and stone carvings. From the hilltop, you get wide views of the surrounding rice fields.
Tip: Dress modestly and remove shoes before entering.

Bentota is one of Sri Lanka's most popular beach resort towns. The beach is calm and safe, with golden sand and clear water. Water sports including snorkelling, scuba diving, and deep sea fishing are available.
Tip: Carry sunscreen and a hat — the sun on Sri Lanka's west coast is strong.

A UNESCO World Heritage Site on Sri Lanka's southwest coast. Built by the Portuguese in the 1500s and later expanded by the Dutch — one of the best-preserved colonial forts in Asia. Inside: charming cafes, boutique shops, a lighthouse, a Dutch Reformed Church, and sea-facing rampart walks.

Sri Lanka's cultural capital, home to the Temple of the Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa) — one of the most sacred Buddhist temples in the world. Set in the central highlands surrounded by tea plantations. The Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage is 40 km away — ideal for families.

Sri Lanka's commercial capital — usually the first or last stop on any Sri Lanka trip from Hyderabad . Key stops: Gangaramaya Temple , Galle Face Green (sunset walk), Pettah Market (spices, goods, local energy), and the Lotus Tower — South Asia's tallest self-supported structure at ~350 metres, with an observation deck and revolving restaurant.

Sri Lanka's hill station at 1,868 metres. Surrounded by tea estates — visit a working tea factory and taste freshly made Ceylon tea. Horton Plains National Park (32 km away) has the famous World's End cliff and Baker's Falls.

Mirissa is one of Sri Lanka's most popular beaches on the south coast, about 150 km from Colombo. It's the main departure point for blue whale and dolphin watching boat tours (November–April). The beach itself is a curved bay with calm water, palm trees, and good seafood restaurants. Mirissa is also a popular surfing spot from March to October.

Yala National Park in southeastern Sri Lanka is one of the most visited national parks in Asia, and has one of the highest densities of leopards in the world . The park also has elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles, and over 200 bird species. Jeep safaris are the standard way to explore. Best visited between February and July when wildlife concentrations are highest and water levels are low.

Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's northeast coast is known for its natural harbour — one of the finest in the world — and its beautiful beaches. Nilaveli Beach and Uppuveli Beach are among the cleanest beaches in Sri Lanka. Pigeon Island National Park, just offshore, has excellent snorkelling with reef sharks and coral. The Koneswaram Temple on Swami Rock, overlooking the sea, is one of Sri Lanka's five ancient Shiva temples. Best visited April–September.

Ella is a small hill town in Sri Lanka's Uva Province, popular for its views, short hikes, and relaxed atmosphere. The Nine Arch Bridge — a colonial-era stone railway viaduct — is one of Sri Lanka's most photographed landmarks. Little Adam's Peak (easy 2-hour hike) and Ella Rock (4-hour hike) both offer views across the tea valleys. Ravana Falls and Ravana Cave are 2 km from Ella town.

Direct flights from Hyderabad to Colombo take approximately 1 hour 55 minutes . Connecting flights via Bangkok, Chennai, or Singapore take 4–6 hours total. IndiGo and SriLankan Airlines both operate direct services.

December to March for west and south coast beaches (Bentota, Mirissa, Galle). April to September for the east coast (Trincomalee, Arugam Bay). Cultural sites and hill stations are accessible year-round.

blocks.text: Q1. Which airlines have direct flights from Hyderabad to Sri Lanka?

Ans: IndiGo (~6 flights/week) and SriLankan Airlines (~5 flights/week) operate nonstop flights from Hyderabad to Colombo. Flight time: ~1 hour 55 minutes. Air India has connecting services only. Check current schedules on airline websites before booking.
Q2. What currency is used in Sri Lanka?
Ans: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). Exchange USD, Euros, or Indian Rupees at banks or airport counters. Carry LKR cash for local markets and smaller towns.
Q3. How many days are enough to see Sri Lanka from Hyderabad?
Ans: 7–10 days covers Sri Lanka comfortably. 4–5 days works for a focused trip (Colombo, Kandy, Nuwara Eliya). 8 days is ideal for the Ramayana circuit or a full island loop.
Q4. Do Indians need a visa for Sri Lanka in 2026?

Ans: No visa or ETA required for Indians in 2026. Enter with a valid passport and return air ticket. 30-day stay, double-entry permitted. ETA at eta.gov.lk is optional but saves queue time. (Source: Sri Lanka High Commission India, Feb 2026)
Q5. What is the best time to visit Sri Lanka from Hyderabad?

Ans: December to March for west/south coast beaches (Bentota, Mirissa, Galle). April to September for the east coast (Trincomalee, Arugam Bay). Cultural sites and hill stations (Kandy, Nuwara Eliya) are accessible year-round.
Q6. What is the Sri Lanka tour cost from Hyderabad?
Ans: Ground packages start from ₹24,900 per person (4 days, no flights). A 7–8 day package costs ₹36,900–₹45,000. Return flights add ₹12,000–₹25,000. No visa or ETA fees for Indians in 2026.
Q7. Is the Sri Lanka Ramayana tour worth it for Hyderabad pilgrims?

Ans: Yes — the 8-day Sri Lanka Ramayana Tour from Hyderabad (₹28,900) is very popular with Hindu devotees. It covers Ravana Cave, Sita Amman Temple (Ashok Vatika), Divurumpola, Munneswaram Temple, and Anuradhapura. For pilgrims from Hyderabad, this combines devotion with a complete Sri Lanka experience.
Q8. Is Sri Lanka good for a honeymoon?

Ans: Yes. Our Sri Lanka honeymoon package from Hyderabad (7 days, ₹38,500) includes Colombo, Kandy hills, and Bentota beach resort. Beach resorts at Mirissa and Passikudah also offer private pool options. Sri Lanka's mix of beaches, wildlife, hills, and heritage makes it a varied and private honeymoon destination.
Q9. What are the best wildlife experiences in Sri Lanka?

Ans: Yala National Park for leopards (highest density in Asia), sloth bears, and elephants. Udawalawe National Park for large elephant herds including calves — best year-round. Mirissa for blue whale and dolphin boat tours (November–April). Pigeon Island, Trincomalee for reef sharks and coral snorkelling.
Q10. Can I use Indian Rupees in Sri Lanka?

Ans: Some authorised exchange counters at Colombo airport accept Indian Rupees for conversion to LKR. However, Indian Rupees are not accepted as payment currency in Sri Lanka's shops, restaurants, or taxis. Exchange to LKR at the airport or authorised bank counters on arrival.
Q11. What should I buy in Sri Lanka?

Ans: Ceylon tea (buy from plantation shops in Nuwara Eliya for best prices), cinnamon and spices, gemstones from certified shops, batik fabric, and traditional wooden masks. Pettah Market in Colombo is good for bulk spice purchases.
Q12. How far is Sri Lanka from Hyderabad?

Ans: Hyderabad to Colombo by direct flight is approximately 1 hour 55 minutes — making Sri Lanka one of the closest international destinations from Hyderabad. The aerial distance is approximately 2,000 km. With a connecting flight the total journey can be 4–6 hours.
Q13. What is the Sri Lanka Ramayana package itinerary?
Ans: 8 days: Anuradhapura → Trincomalee → Kandy (Temple of Tooth) → Sita Amman Temple, Nuwara Eliya → Ravana Cave, Ella → Kataragama → Divurumpola → Colombo departure.
Q14. Is Sri Lanka a good family destination from Hyderabad?

Ans: Yes. Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, Sigiriya, Kandy cultural show, whale watching, and Colombo city tours all work well for families. Short 2-hour flight and no visa requirement make it very practical.
Q15. What is the best Sri Lanka package for first-time visitors?
Ans: The 8-day Sri Lanka Group Tour (₹36,900) covering Colombo → Sigiriya → Kandy → Nuwara Eliya → Ella → Galle is ideal — covers culture, wildlife, hills, and beach in one trip.

blocks.text: What to Carry for Do Dham Yatra

rows: Thermal inners, fleece jacket, windproof shell, warm socks, gloves, woollen cap. Even in May/June, nights near Kedarnath (3,583 m) drop to near zero.
Waterproof trekking boots for Kedarnath and Yamunotri treks. Sandals/sneakers are not suitable for the 18 km and 6 km uphill paths.
Compact poncho, waterproof jacket. Mountain weather changes without warning.
SPF 50+ sunscreen, UV sunglasses. UV radiation at 3,000+ m is significantly higher than at sea level.
Paracetamol, AMS tablets (Diamox - consult doctor), ORS sachets, antacids, cold medicine, basic first aid. Buy before leaving home.
Printed Yatra Pass (mandatory), Aadhaar/Passport, helicopter confirmation if applicable. Keep in waterproof pouch.
Minimum Rs. 3,000 cash - digital payments unreliable on mountain routes, especially near Gaurikund and Badrinath.
Flowers, chandan, kumkum, akshat, coconut, prasad. Pujari services available at all temples.

blocks.text: Book Your Divine Do Dham Yatra Now

A journey to Kedarnath & Badrinath or Gangotri & Yamunotri is not just about visiting temples - it's an opportunity to reconnect with your spiritual self. Let us plan every tour detail for you while you immerse in devotion and natural beauty!
Call us now at +91-8171158569 or send an inquiry to know more about travel solutions, fixed departures, and early booking offers!
Q1. How many days are required for Do Dham Yatra?
Usually, 4 to 6 days are sufficient for road travel. The exact duration depends on the route and travel mode. Helicopter packages can complete the Yatra in 1-4 days.
Q2. Can I cover Kedarnath without trekking?
Yes, you can skip the trek entirely and opt for helicopter service from Phata, Sirsi, or Guptkashi helipads. Pony and Palki (palanquin) services are also available from Gaurikund.
Q3. Are Do Dham helicopter tours safe for senior citizens?

Yes, the helicopter journey is designed keeping elderly pilgrims in mind. It eliminates the 18 km Kedarnath trek and long mountain road travel. Senior citizens with heart conditions, high BP, or respiratory issues must get a doctor's clearance before booking. Medical certificate is required at the time of registration for those above 60.
Q4. Can I customize my Do Dham Yatra package?
Yes, full customization is available - from the city you start, to the duration, stopovers, hotel category, and mode of travel. Contact us for a tailored quote.
Q5. Are medical services available on the route?

Yes, first-aid kits, oxygen support, and contact with nearby hospitals are available. SDRF (State Disaster Response Force) posts are staffed on the Kedarnath trek route. Helicopter evacuation can be arranged in emergencies by informing any checkpoint staff.
Q6. Is Yatra registration mandatory for Do Dham in 2026?

Yes - registration is compulsory for all four temples. Register at registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in before travelling. You'll receive a Yatra Pass that must be printed and carried. Checkpoints at Sonprayag (Kedarnath route) and on the Badrinath highway verify it. Arriving without a pass means you'll be turned back.
Q7. What is the best Do Dham combination - Kedarnath-Badrinath or Gangotri-Yamunotri?

Both combinations are spiritually complete in their own right. Kedarnath-Badrinath is more popular - it covers a Jyotirlinga (Shiva) and a Divya Desam (Vishnu). Gangotri-Yamunotri is less crowded, involves less physical strain (no 18 km trek), and is ideal for those who want a peaceful yatra focused on the river goddess temples.
Q8. What is the Do Dham Yatra cost by helicopter in 2026?

Same-day Kedarnath-Badrinath helicopter packages start at approximately INR 1,20,000-1,35,000 per person. Multi-day helicopter packages (3-4 days) range from INR 1,30,000 to 1,45,000. Prices include helicopter flights, VIP Darshan, meals, and transfers. Contact us for the most current 2026 pricing.
Q9. When do the Kedarnath and Badrinath temples open in 2026?

Kedarnath opens on 22 April 2026 and closes approximately 11 November 2026 (Bhai Dooj). Badrinath opens on 23 April 2026 and closes approximately 13 November 2026. Gangotri and Yamunotri both open on 19 April 2026 (Akshaya Tritiya) and close around Diwali (10-11 November 2026). Always confirm final dates at bktc.net closer to your travel date.
Q10. Can I do Kedarnath-Badrinath Do Dham by road in 5 days?

Yes - 5 days is the minimum comfortable timeline. Day 1: Haridwar/Delhi → Guptkashi. Day 2: Kedarnath Darshan (trek or helicopter) → return to Guptkashi. Day 3: Guptkashi → Joshimath. Day 4: Joshimath → Badrinath Darshan → Joshimath. Day 5: Return to Haridwar/Delhi. Rushing in fewer than 5 days is not recommended on mountain roads.
Q11. What nearby attractions can I add to my Do Dham trip?

For Kedarnath-Badrinath: Mana Village (last Indian village, 3 km from Badrinath), Tapt Kund (hot spring at Badrinath), Triyuginarayan Temple, Valley of Flowers (seasonal, June-Oct), Hemkund Sahib. For Gangotri-Yamunotri: Harsil Valley, Surya Kund at Yamunotri, Gaumukh glacier trek (19 km from Gangotri). Ask us to add these to your itinerary.
Q12. Is Do Dham Yatra possible in monsoon (July-August)?

Technically the temples are open, but travel is risky. July and August bring heavy landslides, especially on the Rudraprayag-Gaurikund road and Uttarkashi-Gangotri road. Road closures can last multiple days. For road travellers, July-August should be avoided. Helicopter Yatras are possible in monsoon but flights are frequently cancelled due to cloud cover - always keep buffer days if travelling in this window.

blocks.text: Kerala is one of the top holiday destinations in India. This beautiful state in South India is famous for its unique houseboat rides, peaceful backwaters, historical places, lovely lakes, and wildlife parks. Tourists can also enjoy traditional dance performances like Kathakali, which is among Kerala's most celebrated art forms. Kerala is not only great to explore but also a perfect place for food lovers. Some dishes visitors should try: Sadya, Appam with stew, Puttu, and Kadala curry.

Apart from this, there are several adventure activities in Kerala , including water sports, trekking, paragliding, elephant rides, and more. Our Kerala tour packages include customisable trips to suit travellers from all over the country. You can enjoy the best deals and discounts on this trip. 24/7 service and support is available throughout your tour. Explore the main attractions and enjoy this unforgettable journey with My Quick Trippers.
Kerala Tour Packages 2026 - At a Glance

All packages include hotel, daily meals, AC vehicle transfers, sightseeing, and 24/7 support. Packages can be customised based on your group size, travel dates, and preferences. Contact us for an exact quote.

Our Kerala holiday packages include the best accommodations — whether you are looking for a luxury resort, a boutique stay, or a comfortable mid-range hotel. We provide transportation for sightseeing to make your travel around Kerala smooth and easy. Experienced guides are available on request. The trip can be customised according to your interest. Book now to plan this memorable journey.
Best Places to Visit in Kerala
There are several places to explore on a Kerala trip that make it special:

Cochin, also called Kochi, is a beautiful port city in Kerala. This spot is famous for its blend of cultures — Portuguese, Dutch, British, and Chinese influences are visible in its architecture and food. Tourists can explore Fort Kochi, Mattancherry Palace, the Jewish Synagogue, Chinese fishing nets, Cherai Beach, and more. The peaceful backwaters are ideal for boat rides. Cochin is often called the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea' and is the most common starting point for Kerala tours.

The Valara Waterfalls is located between Neriamangalam and Adimali, on the Munnar–Kochi highway (NH 85). The waterfall cascades from a height of about 1,000 feet and is visible from the highway. While visitors cannot get too close to the falls, the view from the road is impressive — particularly during and after the monsoon when the water flow is strongest. The nearby Cheeyappara Waterfalls (a seven-tiered fall) is also visible from the same stretch of road and worth a stop.

Munnar is situated at around 1,600 metres above sea level in the Western Ghats and is one of Kerala's most visited hill stations . It is famous for its rolling tea plantations, cool weather throughout the year, and fog-covered hills. The Tea Museum explains how tea is processed; Eravikulam National Park (home to the endangered Nilgiri Tahr and the Neelakurinji flower that blooms once every 12 years) is a short drive away. Anamudi Peak — the highest mountain in South India at 2,695 metres — is visible from within the park. Note: trekking to the Anamudi summit is restricted; visitors can explore viewpoints and the 2 km Rajamalai trail within the park's tourism zone.

The Edakkal Caves are among the oldest historically significant sites in Kerala, located in Wayanad district. Inside the caves, there are ancient petroglyphs — carvings and symbols believed to be around 6,000 years old — indicating early human settlements. The caves require a moderate uphill walk of about 1 km from the entrance. The carvings provide a fascinating glimpse into prehistoric life in South India.

Alleppey is Kerala's backwater capital and the most popular destination for houseboat stays . The Alleppey Lighthouse, constructed in 1862, stands 30 metres tall and offers views of the Arabian Sea and surrounding landscape. The broader Alleppey backwater network connects to Kumarakom, Kuttanad, and Vembanad Lake. A night on a houseboat drifting through the backwaters — with rice fields, coconut groves, and village life on either side — is the most iconic Kerala experience for most travellers.

In South Kerala, Varkala is a beach town set against dramatic red laterite cliffs. The Papanasam Beach at Varkala is considered sacred by many Hindu pilgrims, who believe bathing here helps cleanse sins — it draws regular pilgrims to this day. The Janardhana Swami Temple (believed to be around 2,000 years old) sits on the clifftop above. Water sports including surfing are available; the beach is also popular for yoga retreats and Ayurveda centres. Best visited between November and March.

Thekkady is home to Periyar National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary — one of the finest wildlife reserves in South India. Boat rides on the Periyar Lake offer chances to spot elephants, wild boar, Sambar deer, and otters along the lakeshore. The surrounding Spice Hills area grows cardamom, pepper, cinnamon, and cloves — spice plantation tours are a popular add-on. The Kadathanadan Kalari Centre in Thekkady hosts live Kalaripayattu (Kerala's ancient martial art) performances every evening.

Wayanad, in the northeastern corner of Kerala, is a district of forests, tribal communities, and misty plateaus. Key spots include Chembra Peak (the highest peak in Wayanad at 2,100 m, with a heart-shaped lake near the summit), Soochipara Falls , Banasura Sagar Dam (the largest earth dam in India and second largest in Asia), Pookode Lake , and the tribal settlements at Edakkal Caves. Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary shares its border with Nagarhole Tiger Reserve in Karnataka and is part of the broader Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve corridor.

Kovalam, about 16 km from Thiruvananthapuram, is Kerala's best-known beach resort town. It has three beaches — the main Lighthouse Beach (most popular), Hawa Beach, and Samudra Beach. The beach is calm and safe for swimming. Kovalam is also one of Kerala's main centres for Ayurveda treatments — traditional massage, detox, and panchakarma therapies are available at dozens of resorts and clinics. The season runs October to March.

Kumarakom, on the eastern shores of Vembanad Lake, is a bird sanctuary and backwater destination known for its luxury resorts and quieter alternatives to Alleppey. The Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary is a winter destination for migratory birds — Siberian ducks, herons, egrets, and other species arrive November to February (not monsoon season). Houseboat cruises and canoe rides through narrow channels are popular year-round.

items: Kerala has four main airports: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, Cochin International Airport (largest in Kerala), Calicut (Kozhikode) International Airport, and Kannur International Airport — all connecting to major Indian cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru, and Mumbai.

Airlines like IndiGo, Air India, and SpiceJet provide direct flights to Kerala from major cities. (Note: Vistara merged into Air India in November 2024.) Average flying time: 2–4 hours from North India; 1–2 hours from South Indian cities.
Cochin International Airport is the world's first fully solar-powered airport (since 2015) — a useful fact if you are looking for eco-conscious travel touchpoints.
Cochin International Airport is the most convenient arrival point for Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey, and Kumarakom. Thiruvananthapuram Airport is better for Kovalam and Varkala.

Kerala's main railway junctions are Thiruvananthapuram Central, Ernakulam Junction (Kochi), Thrissur, Kozhikode, and Alappuzha — connected to cities like Delhi, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Mumbai.
Key trains: Kerala Express, Netravati Express, and Rajdhani Express connect Kerala to Delhi (~38–42 hours). From Mumbai: approximately 27–36 hours. From Chennai or Bengaluru: 12–15 hours.
Train travel through Kerala's coast and backwaters is scenic — the Konkan Railway route (Mumbai to Kerala) and the coastal route from Chennai are both known for their views.
Book tickets at least 3–4 months in advance for peak season travel (November–February).

You can reach Kerala by private vehicle or public transport from nearby states — Bengaluru (~9 hours to Kochi via NH 544), Coimbatore (~4 hours to Palakkad), Mangaluru (~4 hours to Kozhikode), and Chennai (~12 hours to Kochi).
Travelling through national highways like NH 544 and NH 66 can be scenic, especially as you cross the Western Ghats and descend into Kerala's green landscape.
Long-distance AC sleeper buses from Bengaluru, Chennai, and Coimbatore to Kerala are a cost-effective option.
Kerala is a coastal state with sea access. The Cochin Port (Kochi) handles cruise ship arrivals — several international cruise lines include Kochi on their itineraries.

The Kerala backwaters are connected internally — you can travel between Kollam and Alleppey by the Government Boat (KSRTC water transport) which runs daily, taking about 8 hours through the backwaters.
Visitors can reach Kerala's Lakshadweep islands by ship from Kochi — sailings operate seasonally and require prior booking through Lakshadweep Administration.
Private AC vehicle: Most comfortable for sightseeing — all our Kerala packages include a private car with driver.
Auto-rickshaws: Widely available in cities and towns. Use metered autos in Thiruvananthapuram; negotiate fare elsewhere.
Ferries and boats: Government ferries connect Alleppey, Kumarakom, and Kottayam through backwater routes. Houseboat charters are arranged through operators.
Kerala KSRTC buses: Economical option for longer distances between cities. AC buses run between Thiruvananthapuram, Kochi, Kozhikode, and Thrissur.
Auto apps (Rapido, Ola): Available in Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, and Kozhikode.

blocks.text: Tourists can enjoy paragliding in the hills near Varkala, with views of the sea and beaches below. This is a popular adventure activity for those who want to fly over Kerala's coastal landscape. Best experienced during the October–March season when weather conditions are stable.

A houseboat cruise in Alleppey (Alappuzha) is the most iconic Kerala experience. Traditional kettuvallam (riceboat houseboats) have been converted into well-appointed floating hotels — most have 1–3 bedrooms, a kitchen, and a sit-out deck. You drift through the narrow backwater channels, past rice paddies, coconut groves, and small villages, with meals cooked fresh on board. Overnight houseboat stays are the most popular option — book 2–3 months ahead for peak season (November–February).

Wildlife experiences in Kerala are varied. Periyar National Park (Thekkady) is best for boat safaris on the lake — elephants, gaur, and deer come to the lakeshore. Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary borders the Nagarhole Tiger Reserve and is good for jeep safaris. Parambikulam Tiger Reserve (Palakkad district) is one of India's most biodiverse reserves and has guided treks. Kerala is also a good birdwatching destination — Thattekad Bird Sanctuary and Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary draw serious birders.

The Pettimudi area in Rajamala, near Munnar, offers views of tea gardens and the surrounding Rajamala hills. Note: Visitors should check current access status before planning a visit — the Rajamala/Pettimudi area has had restricted access due to safety reasons in recent years. For hilltop views near Munnar, Kolukkumalai (world's highest tea estate) and Meesapulimala ridge are excellent alternatives with clear Himalayan-range-comparable views.

Water sports in Kerala are available at several beach destinations. Kovalam and Varkala are the most popular — offering jet skiing, kayaking, parasailing, and surfing. Alleppey beach has water sports facilities as well. For those who want calmer activities, canoe rides through the backwater channels in Alleppey and Kumarakom are excellent. The Periyar Lake in Thekkady has bamboo rafting.

Kathakali is Kerala's most famous classical art form — an elaborate dance-drama with colourful costumes and face paint depicting stories from the Mahabharata and Ramayana. Kalaripayattu, Kerala's ancient martial art, is another major performance art. Both can be watched at cultural centres in Kochi (Kerala Kathakali Centre near Fort Kochi, Dr. B. Ipe's Kathakali Centre), Thekkady (Kadathanadan Kalari Centre), and Trivandrum. Shows are usually held in the evening — check timings and book ahead.

Kerala is India's primary destination for authentic Ayurveda treatment . Treatments range from a simple 60-minute Abhyanga massage to a full 14–21 day Panchakarma detox program. Kovalam, Varkala, Thiruvananthapuram, and Thrissur have the most established Ayurveda centres. For authentic treatment (not spa-style), look for NABH-certified Ayurveda centres with qualified Ayurvedic doctors. June–August (monsoon) is considered the best time for intensive Ayurveda treatment — the body is believed to be most receptive to therapies during this season.

Outdoor activities like trekking, houseboat rides, and beach visits are most enjoyable. Skies are clearer and the landscape is fresh after the monsoon. This is also the peak tourist season, so book accommodation and houseboats 2–3 months in advance.

blocks.text: Kerala cuisine is distinct from the rest of South India — coconut, fish, and rice are the backbone of almost every meal. Here's what visitors should not miss on a Kerala tour :

items: Sadya — the traditional feast served on a banana leaf, with rice, 20+ side dishes including avial, thoran, sambar, and payasam. Essential during Onam and at most traditional restaurants.
Appam with Stew — lacy rice flour crepes served with a mild coconut milk-based vegetable or chicken stew. One of Kerala's most popular breakfast dishes.
Puttu and Kadala Curry — steamed rice cake layered with coconut, served with spiced black chickpea curry. A hearty breakfast found everywhere in Kerala.
Kerala Fish Curry — fish cooked in a clay pot with raw mango, coconut milk, and Malabar spices. Every region of Kerala has its own version.
Karimeen Pollichathu — pearl spot fish wrapped in banana leaf and grilled or shallow-fried. A speciality of the Alleppey backwater region.
Kerala Prawn Curry — prawns in a rich coconut milk and tamarind gravy. Available at coastal towns from Kochi to Trivandrum.
Avial — a mixed vegetable dish cooked in coconut oil and yogurt. A staple of the Kerala Sadya.
Unniyappam — small round rice cakes with jaggery, bananas, and coconut — a popular temple prasad and street snack.

blocks.text: Shopping in Kerala - What to Buy

items: Spices: Cardamom, pepper, cloves, cinnamon, and nutmeg — best bought from Thekkady spice markets or Kumily (better prices than airport shops).
Kasavu Sarees: Kerala's traditional sarees with gold borders — available in Thrissur and Kochi. Good quality from Bhraman Textiles and Co-optex.
Coir Products: Mats, baskets, wall hangings made from coconut fibre — widely available in Alleppey and Trivandrum.
Wooden Handicrafts: Rosewood and teakwood sculptures, carved elephants — best from Kochi's Jew Town antique shops and Trivandrum's SMSM Institute.
Kerala Murals (reproductions): Traditional temple mural art on canvas — available in Thrissur and Guruvayur.
Coconut Shell Products: Bowls, spoons, lamps made from coconut shells — widely available in tourist markets.
Tea: Munnar tea direct from estate shops (cheaper than urban stores). Best bought from the Tea Museum outlet in Munnar.

blocks.text: Family packages are designed with children and seniors in mind — comfortable hotels, child-friendly sightseeing pace, wildlife visits, and cultural shows. Typical duration: 6–8 days covering Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, and Alleppey. Price range: ₹48,000–₹68,000 per person (double sharing, all meals).

Kerala is one of India's top honeymoon destinations. Honeymoon packages typically include houseboat stays in Alleppey, hill station accommodation in Munnar, beach resorts in Kovalam or Varkala, and candlelight dinners. Typical duration: 5–8 days. Price range: ₹50,000–₹75,000 per person (4–5 star hotels, all meals). Customised spa and private dinner add-ons available.

Group tours are the most economical option — AC coach, 3–4 star hotels, all meals, and guided sightseeing included. Fixed departure dates from major cities. Typical duration: 6–8 days. Price range: ₹45,000–₹65,000 per person. Good for office groups, family groups, and social clubs.

Ayurveda packages in Kerala range from short 3-day rejuvenation programs to full 21-day Panchakarma detox courses. Kovalam, Varkala, and Thiruvananthapuram are the most established centres. The monsoon season (June–August) is considered ideal for intensive treatment. Prices vary widely — from ₹8,000/day (budget centres) to ₹25,000+/day (certified luxury Ayurvedic resorts).

items: Carry light cotton clothing for the coast and plains; add a light jacket for Munnar and Wayanad (especially November–January nights).
Carry an umbrella or raincoat — rain can come without warning even in the peak season. This is especially true in Munnar and the hills.
Mosquito repellent is essential, particularly for houseboat stays and forest areas (Thekkady, Wayanad).
Dress modestly when visiting temples — cover shoulders and knees. Some temples (like Guruvayur) do not allow non-Hindus inside.
Carry some local currency (INR) for markets, small eateries, and waterfall entry fees — card machines are not reliable everywhere.
Book houseboat stays and Kathakali shows in advance, especially for travel between November and February.
For Ayurveda treatment, choose NABH-certified centres and consult the Ayurvedic doctor on the first day — don't book treatments blindly from a menu.
Respect the environment — Kerala's backwaters and forests are ecologically sensitive. Do not litter; support eco-friendly operators.

Prices above are for ground packages — flights from your city are additional (typically ₹5,000–₹15,000 return depending on origin city and booking time). Contact us for an exact quote with your travel dates and group size.
What is the best Kerala tour package?

For most first-time visitors, the best Kerala tour package is a 5–6 day itinerary covering Kochi (1 night), Munnar (2 nights), and Alleppey houseboat (1 night). This covers Kerala's three most iconic experiences — colonial history, hill station tea gardens, and backwater cruising — within a practical timeframe. Packages start from ₹15,500 per person. Add Thekkady (wildlife) or Kovalam (beach) for a longer trip.
How much does a Kerala trip cost from major Indian cities?

A 7-day Kerala holiday package including flights costs approximately ₹35,000–₹55,000 per person from Delhi, Mumbai, or Bengaluru (double sharing, all meals, standard hotels). Flights from South Indian cities are cheaper — from Hyderabad or Chennai, the same package runs ₹28,000–₹45,000. Budget travellers can do 5 days starting from ₹20,000 (flight + ground package).
How many days are enough for Kerala?

7–9 days is ideal to cover Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, and Alleppey with comfortable travel between destinations. A focused 4–5 day trip is enough for 2–3 destinations. If adding Wayanad, Kovalam, or Kumarakom, plan for 9–12 days. Rushing Kerala in under 4 days is possible but leaves little time for the experiences that make the trip worth it — houseboat stays, spice plantation walks, or evening Kathakali shows.
Which month is best for Kerala?

November to February is the best time for most Kerala destinations — beaches, backwaters, wildlife, and hill stations all offer good conditions. October is excellent for post-monsoon greenery and value pricing. August–September is ideal if your main goal is the Onam festival or Nehru Trophy boat race. June–August (monsoon) is good for Ayurveda treatment and waterfall visits but not for beach holidays.

blocks.text: Q1. Which beaches are best in Kerala?

Ans. The most popular beaches in Kerala are Kovalam (well-developed beach resort, safe for swimming), Cherai (near Kochi, famous for Chinese fishing nets nearby), Varkala (clifftop beach with a sacred bathing beach), and Bekal (near a 400-year-old fort in Kasaragod). Marari Beach (near Alleppey) is a quieter alternative popular with nature travellers.
Q2. What are the famous foods in Kerala that travellers should try?

Ans. The popular foods in Kerala are Sadya (a vegetarian feast on a banana leaf with rice and 20+ sides), Avial (a mix of vegetables in coconut gravy), Puttu (a steamed rice cake with coconut), and Karimeen Pollichathu (banana-leaf grilled pearl spot fish). Also try Appam with stew, Kerala fish curry, and Unniyappam for a complete local food experience.
Q3. How many days are enough to fully explore Kerala?

Ans. Around 7 to 9 days are enough to cover the main highlights — Kochi, Munnar, Thekkady, Alleppey, and either Kovalam or Varkala. A 4–5 day trip is enough for a focused tour covering 2–3 destinations. 10+ days allows you to add Wayanad, Kumarakom, and Kasaragod.
Q4. What are the unexplored places in Kerala?

Ans. Some of Kerala's lesser-visited destinations include Munroe Island (backwaters and traditional fishing culture near Kollam), Nelliyampathy (tea plantations and scenic views in Palakkad district), Vagamon (meadows and pine forests between Thekkady and Alleppey), and Beypore (ancient dhow-building port near Kozhikode).
Q5. Which is the best month to visit Kerala?

Ans. October to February is the best time for most tourists — pleasant weather across all regions. March to May is the shoulder season — good deals, fewer crowds, but warmer on the coast. If you want to experience Onam (Kerala's biggest festival) and the Nehru Trophy Boat Race, plan your visit in August–September.
Q6. What are some of the most popular travel destinations in Kerala?

Ans. Alleppey, Kumarakom, Wayanad, Thekkady, and Munnar are the most visited destinations. Kochi (Cochin) is the most common starting point. Kovalam and Varkala are the top beach destinations. Guruvayur, Thrissur, and Trivandrum are important for temple visits.
Q7. Which is the best place for a weekend trip in Kerala?

Ans. Munnar is the most popular weekend destination — it is 4–5 hours from Kochi and Coimbatore. Alleppey (for houseboat) and Varkala (for beach) are also popular weekend getaways from cities in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
Q8. Which is the coldest month in Kerala?

Ans. January is the coldest month in Kerala. On the coast, temperatures range from 22–29°C — comfortable but not bone-chilling. In the hills (Munnar, Wayanad), temperatures can drop to 5–10°C in January nights. December and February are also cool months.
Q9. Which is the most beautiful city in Kerala?

Ans. Munnar is consistently rated Kerala's most scenic destination — its rolling tea gardens, misty peaks, and cool climate set it apart. For a city experience, Kochi (Cochin) has the best combination of history, culture, food, and waterside beauty.
Q10. Which month is the hottest in Kerala?

Ans. April and May are the hottest months in Kerala. Coastal areas can reach 33–37°C during these months. The hills remain cooler (Munnar averages 20–25°C even in summer). The Southwest Monsoon arrives by late May/early June, bringing significant rain and lowering temperatures.
Q11. Is Kerala hot or cold?

Ans. Kerala has a tropical climate — warm and humid throughout the year. Coastal areas like Kochi, Alleppey, and Trivandrum stay between 22–35°C depending on the season. The hill stations (Munnar, Wayanad) are significantly cooler, ranging from 10–25°C. The best overall weather is from October to February when coastal areas are around 25–30°C and the hills are pleasant.
Q12. How can I plan a trip to Kerala?

Ans. The easiest way to plan a Kerala tour is to start with your budget, travel dates, and the type of experience you want — beach, backwater, hills, wildlife, or a mix. Choose a duration (4 days minimum for a short trip, 7–9 days for a comprehensive one). Book flights early (especially for December–January). Contact My Quick Trippers for a customised package based on your group size and preferences — we handle hotels, transport, houseboat bookings, and sightseeing.
Q13. Which is the best month to visit Munnar?

Ans. The best time to visit Munnar is from September to March . October–November is ideal to see waterfalls at full flow and the landscape at its greenest after the monsoon. December–February offers the coolest weather — temperatures can drop below 10°C at night. The Neelakurinji flower (blooms once every 12 years) last bloomed in 2018 — next bloom expected around 2030.
Q14. Is planning a Kerala tour more economical?

Ans. Kerala can be done on a budget (basic guesthouses, KSRTC buses, local eateries) or can be quite expensive (luxury houseboats, hill resorts, Ayurveda centres). Our packages start from ₹14,500 per person for 4 days. Compared to international holidays, Kerala offers excellent value — but it is not necessarily cheaper than North Indian hill stations. Shoulder season (March–May) offers better rates than peak season (November–February).
Q15. What are the must-see cultural experiences in Kerala?

Ans. The top cultural experiences on a Kerala holiday package are: Kathakali dance-drama (Fort Kochi, Thekkady), Kalaripayattu martial art performance (Thekkady, Trivandrum), the Thrissur Pooram festival (May), the Nehru Trophy Vallam Kali boat race (August, Alleppey), and a traditional Kerala Sadya meal on a banana leaf. A visit to a working tea factory in Munnar and a spice plantation tour in Thekkady are also worth adding.

blocks.text: Our handcrafted Narmada Pushkaralu Package gives you a chance to seek the blessings of Goddess Narmada and engage in various rituals that are bound to cleanse your soul. Narmada Pushkaralu is one of the most divine festivals wherein Narmada River is worshipped by the pilgrims. The river is believed to be sanctified by Lord Shiva’s divine presence.

Narmada Pushkaralu is one of the most sacred periods in the Hindu religion when the devotees worship the river fervently, offering them a chance to cleanse their soul and attain spiritual awakening. It is believed that the Narmada River gets infused during this time with divine energy. This celebration involves various cultural events, rituals, and spiritual experiences that will satiate your craving for spirituality and bliss. Pushkaralu is celebrated every twelve years coinciding with the transit of Jupiter into specific zodiac signs. This has a great influence on which areas of the river are auspicious for rituals. As you embark on this spiritual journey you’ll take a dip in the holy water of River Narmada to wash away your sins and achieve salvation.

Book the Narmada Pushkaralu Package from our website to experience cultural celebration and religious fervor like never before. As your journey comes to an end you’ll experience spiritual renewal and get transformed into a better soul. The best thing about our packages is that you can customize them as per your preferences ensuring you can have the best experiences of your life.

On the first day of the tour, you will arrive at Amarkantak from Hyderabad via a picturesque road journey. During the road journey, you will pass through various ashrams, religious spots, and scenic destinations. Amarkantak is a famous Hindu pilgrimage site known as "Teerthraj" - "the king of pilgrimages". The city is known for its natural and geographical richness. It is the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges meeting point, with the Maikal Hills being the most popular site. After arriving at Amarkantak you will check in to your hotel and have a delightful overnight stay reflecting upon the experiences awaiting you.

Today you will have a tasty breakfast at your hotel and then head to the Narmada Kund, one of the holiest sites in India. Narmada is worshipped here as the mother goddess who nurtures the world. The Narmada is not the only river that originates here. Two other rivers, Johila and Son, also originate from Amarkantak. A grand aarti ceremony is organized at the bank of the Kund giving you a chance to have the greatest spiritual experiences. As you partake in the aarti ceremony you’ll feel enamored by the divinity of this place. You can also offer your prayers to Goddess Narmada and absorb the tranquil atmosphere. Head back to your hotel in the evening and have a relaxing sleep in your room post a lip-smacking dinner.
Day 3 : Engage in various rituals, return to your hometown

Today you will wake up early in the morning and head to the Narmada Kund to engage in various rituals such as offering a Chunri and flowers to Goddess Narmada. You’ll also take a dip in the sacred waters of this river to abolish your sins and lead a pure life. See the pilgrims praying to the river and asking for forgiveness for the sins they have committed. Narmada Kund is considered to be the spot where the river Narmada emerges from the earth. You can also partake in various cultural and spiritual events that are organized around the river during the period of Pushkaralu. After the spiritual experience, you will say goodbye to Amarkantak and head back to your hometown.
