blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Babaji's Cave from Ahmedabad
The best time for Mahavatar Babaji pilgrimage is in the two windows: April-June and October-November .

In the first window, you get clear weather, which is ideal for trekking and even going for sightseeing in the nearby areas. In the second window, you can enjoy pleasant and cool weather. You can comfortably complete your pilgrimage and indulge in meditation and other activities with ease.

Also, we advise against booking your Mahavatar Babaji Yatra from Ahmedabad in the monsoon and winter season. In the former period, there's a risk of landslides and in the latter season, the trek trails become slippery and there are road blockages due to snowfall.
How to Reach Mahavatar Babaji Cave from Ahmedabad?
You can cover the Mahavatar Babaji trip from Gujarat by the following means:

Reaching Mahavatar Babaji Cave by flight is the fastest way to arrive here. However, there are no direct flights from Gujarat to Uttarakhand . What most pilgrims do is take a flight from Ahmedabad to Delhi first, and then from there, they take a road drive to Almora, Ranikhet, or Dwarahat.
It would take you around 6-8 hours on this hybrid plane-road journey.

You can also take the Babaji Cave tour by train. Simply use the railways to reach from Ahmedabad to Kathgodam (25 hours). Popular trains that run on this route are ADI-KGM Express and Porbandar-Ramnagar Express. From Kathgodam, take a cab or taxi to reach Almora and then Dwarahat (about 3-5 hours drive).
The total time taken on this journey will be around 30 hours .
You can also come to the cave by road if you prefer long road trips. The distance between the two is about 1500 km and takes about 2-3 days .

Ahmedabad → Udaipur → Bhilwara → Kishangarh → Jaipur → Delhi → Moradabad → Kashipur → Haldwani → Ranikhet → Dwarahat → Kukuchina → Babaji's Cave

blocks.text: Travel Tips for Mahavatar Babaji Tour from Ahmedabad
Here's some travel advice for your trip:

items: Since Babaji's Cave requires an uphill trek, we suggest you start preparing for it at least 15 days before. Start with light walking and some other exercise.
Book your Babaji Cave Travel Package from Ahmedabad at least a month in advance. This will help you get access to nice hotels.
Keep cash with you as ATMs are limited in the hilly regions.
Even if you're visiting in summer, keep warm clothes with you as the Himalayan regions experience cold in that period as well, especially in the morning and evening.
Go for a trek early in the morning. The ideal time is between 8 AM - 11 AM. Avoid going trekking after sunset. Also, avoid going solo.
Do not take the Babaji Yatra from Ahmedabad during the monsoon season as there's a constant risk of landslides. Also, the trek trail becomes excessively slippery and is dangerous to traverse.
Eat light before going for trekking. You can consume fruits, nuts, and ORS sachets.

Ans. No, there are no direct flights from Ahmedabad to Uttarakhand (Mahavatar Babaji's Cave location). What you can do is fly from Ahmedabad to Delhi, and from there, you can take cab/taxi to Almora/Dwarahat.
Q2. How difficult is the trek to Babaji's Cave?
Ans. The trek to Babaji's Cave is considered only moderately difficult, and the fact that it's only 3 km long makes it easily doable by people with average fitness.
Q3. Can senior citizens visit Babaji's Cave?
Ans. Yes, senior citizens can visit Babaji's Cave. However, it's advised for them to take regular breaks and also carry a stick during their trekking journey.
Q4. How many days are required for Mahavatar Babaji Yatra?
Ans. Typically, 4 to 5 days are usually enough for the Mahavatar Babaji Yatra. In this time span, you can comfortably do the meditation and visit the beautiful places nearby.
Q5. Is accommodation available near Babaji's Cave?
Ans. Yes, you can find decent accommodation in places like Kukuchina, Almora, Dwarahat, and Ranikhet. From budget stays like guesthouses to 3-star hotels, there are plenty of staying options here.

Best Time for Char Dham Yatra
The holy temples open every year around April or May and close in October or early November, depending on the weather.

items: May - June: Very nice weather and it is the best time for the holy trip.
July - August: Rainy season and travel can be hard due to heavy rain.
September - October: Clear sky, less rush, and nice travel weather.

items: Your Char Dham tour will start from Delhi, the heart of India.

blocks.text: Day 2 : Delhi - Haridwar - Drive: Time: 06 – 07 hrs.- 220 km

items: Wake up early in the morning and relish a tasty breakfast.
Post breakfast, you will check out from your hotel and embark on a pleasant drive to Haridwar.
You'll reach Haridwar by the evening and check in to your pre-booked hotel. After relaxing for some time, you will head to Har Ki Pauri, a sacred ghat in Haridwar.
You'll attend the Ganga Aarti at the ghat. After that, you'll return to your hotel and have a soothing sleep in your room.

blocks.text: Day 3 : Haridwar – Barkot - Time: 06 – 07 hrs.- Drive: 177 km

items: Savour a delicious breakfast in the morning at your hotel, and then you'll embark on a picturesque drive to Barkot.
On the way you will stop by Kempty Fall, a cascading waterfall surrounded by mountains and lush green forests.
Continue your journey to Barkot and then check in to your camp and have a mouth-watering dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your camp.

blocks.text: Day 4 : Barkot – Yamunotri – Barkot - Trek: 05 km- Drive: 45 km + 45 km

items: Today you will wake up early in the morning and relish a tasty breakfast. After breakfast, you will embark on a scenic drive to Jankichatti, i.e, the starting point of the trek to Yamunotri Dham.
You can trek or take a pony/doli to reach Yamunotri Dham . Once you have arrived at Yamunotri Dham, you will buy Prasadam from local shops.
Once you have reached the temple premises, you will take a holy dip in the holy water. After the bath, you will head to the main temple to seek blessings from Mata Yamuna.
Later you'll trek down towards Jankichatti. From Jankichatti you'll drive back to Barkot for dinner. Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 5 : Barkot – Uttarkashi - Drive: Time: 03 – 04 hrs.- 81 km

items: Have a tasty breakfast in the morning and then embark on a scenic drive to Uttarkashi. After arriving in Uttarkashi, you will visit Hanuman Temple and Vishwanath Temple.
Hanuman Temple is dedicated to Lord Hanuman and it is believed that carrying the mountain Sanjivani to Lanka Lord Hanuman rested at this spot.
Vishwanath Temple was constructed by Queen Khaneti Devi over an ancient altar that dates back to the era of Mahabharata.
Later you'll drive around 5 km. To reach your pre-booked resort.
You will check in to your luxurious resort for dinner. Post dinner you will have an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 6 : Uttarkashi – Gangotri – Uttarkashi - Drive: Time: 06 hrs-92 km one side

items: Wake up early in the morning and head to Gangotri Dham . During the sacred yatra, you will take a halt at Gangnani and take a dip in the hot water spring.
You will then continue your drive to Gangotri via Harsil.
Once you have arrived at Gangotri Dham, you'll perform pooja at the river Bhagirathi's bank and seek Goddess Ganga's blessings.
After pooja, you will head to the main temple and have Mata Ganga's darshan. Post darshan you will head back to Uttarkashi.

blocks.text: Day 7 : Uttarkashi - Guptkashi Time: 07 – 08 hrs.- Drive: 198 km

items: Have breakfast early in the morning. After breakfast, you'll embark on a scenic drive to Gupatkashi.

Once you have reached Guptkashi, you will check in to your pre-reserved resort for dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 8 : Guptkashi – Kedarnath - Trek: 19 kms- Drive: 45 kms.

items: Wake up early in the morning and then embark on a drive to Sonprayag.

From Gaurikund, you will begin your trek to Kedarnath. After arriving at Kedarnath/ you'll check in to the guest house.
Relax for some time and then you'll get ready to visit Kedarnath Temple to attend the evening Aarti.
Post Aarti you will return to your guest house and have an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 9 : Kedarnath – Rudraparyag - Trek: 18 kms- Drive: 75 kms

items: Today you'll wake up early in the morning and get ready to visit Kedarnath temple to attend the morning Aarti.
After the Aarti and darshan of Lord Kedar, you'll head back to your guest house and have a yummy breakfast.
Post breakfast you will pack your bags and embark on an 18 km long trek back to Gaurikund.
Drive to Rudraprayag from the road head. After arriving at Rudraprayag you will check in to your hotel and have a mouth-watering dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 10 : Rudraprayag – Badrinath Time: 06 – 07 hrs.- Drive:157 kms

items: Have a lip-smacking breakfast in the morning and then embark on a picturesque drive to Badrinath, which is situated on the Alaknanda River banks.
After arriving in Badrinath, you will check in to your hotel. Relax and unwind for some time, and then in the evening you'll head to Badrinath temple.
After the darshan of Lord Badri, you will head back to your hotel and have a mouth-watering dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Day 11 : Badrinath – Rishikesh - Drive: 295 kms.- Time: 10 – 11 hrs.

items: Have a yummy breakfast in the morning and then drive to Rishikesh via Devprayag.
You will stop by Devprayag to see the confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda Rivers from which the river Ganga formed.
You will then continue your journey to Rishikesh, admiring the scenic views.
Once you have arrived at Rishikesh, you will check in to your pre-booked hotel and have a tasty dinner.
Post dinner you will have an overnight stay at your hotel.

blocks.text: Important Travel Tips for NRI Pilgrims
To make your Char Dham pilgrimage tour for NRIs easy and happy, remember these simple tips:

Mountains have fast-changing weather; they become a different world in no time. Pack warm jackets, raincoats, and good walking shoes.
Some parts of the trip need walking. Light exercise before your trip is a good idea.

Follow what the temple asks, wear simple clothes, and respect local habits. Also book with a trusted tour operator as there is a chance; you may be trapped in booking scams by some fake operators as per the ANI news source .
Rooms fill up fast. Booking early gives you the best places to stay and travel.

blocks.text: Mahavatar Babaji Cave Tour Package, Dunagiri
Learn about the historical prominence of Mahavatar Babaji's Cave with our 2-night 3-day package from Delhi. See More

Mahavatar Babaji's Cave is believed to be the site where the immortal Babaji got the teachings related to Kriya Yoga from Lahiri Mahasaya in 1861 (as stated in the Autobiography of a Yogi that has been written by Paramahansa Yogananda).

The cave is situated at around 2600 meters above sea level. It is considered to be an embodiment of profound spiritual energy and peace. You can meditate and practice yoga amidst the breathtaking backdrop of the Himalayas at this place. Many Kriya Yogi devotees believe that Jesus and Mahavatar Babaji are one.

A moderately challenging trek through lush green forests takes you to this hallowed destination. For an average person, the trek to the cave takes around one hour. On the way, you can also visit Dunagiri Mata Temple and explore Dwarahat Town. Join us on the expedition to Mahavatar Babaji's Cave for a transformative experience filled with spiritual growth and peace.
Kriya Yoga is a spiritual practice involving breath control, meditation and discipline to connect with divine energy. It became famous through Paramahansa Yogananda’s book autobiography of a Yogi.

items: Breath Control - It is the practice of controlling the life energy (prana) using special breathing techniques that keeps the mind calm and energizes the body.
Meditation - It helps you to focus better and is beneficial for self-peace to connect with the divine.
Inner Peace - It helps to purify the mind and body that bring higher consciousness.

blocks.text: Activities to Do in Mahavatar Babaji Cave
There are several things to do in Mahavatar Babaji Cave that devotees perform while visiting the cave-

items: Meditation and Yoga - Many visitors practice yoga or meditation in the peaceful cave to relax their mind and achieve inner peace. People can easily focus in this relaxed environment and feel more balanced.

Trekking - Some visitors enjoy trekking to reach the cave, as it gives them a chance to connect with nature and enjoy peaceful surroundings. Trekking also gives a feeling of adventure that helps visitors to experience the spiritual vibes of the place.

Photography - Many tourists love to take pictures of the cave and its beautiful surroundings, which include green landscapes, scenic views, unique flora and fauna. Visitors can also enjoy capturing photos of wildlife.

Bird watching - You can see several bird species around Mahavatar Babaji Cave that makes it a perfect spot to enjoy birdwatching. There are many colorful Himalayan birds like thrushes, woodpeckers and sometimes rare species in that area.

blocks.text: Places to Explore near Babaji Cave
There are best places to visit near Mahavatar Babaji Cave that tourists must explore-

items: Dwarahat Temple - This ancient temple is famous for its beauty and historical importance, and it is located in the Dwarahat region. This temple is around 1,000 years old and dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Therefore, it attracts many visitors.

Pandukholi - This calm place is known for its natural beauty and ancient caves. It is also a perfect spot for meditation and stress relief. It is believed that the Pandavas stayed here during their 14 years of exile.
Chaukhutia - It is a small village known for its beautiful views and its close to spiritual sites. This village is surrounded by wonderful hills and forests. Nature lovers must visit this place.

Dunagiri Temple - This temple is surrounded by dense forests and stunning mountains. It is believed that Goddess Durga mediated here. Many people believe that visiting this temple brings good fortune and removes obstacles in life.

Ranikhet - It is one of the wonderful hill station often called ‘Queen of Kumaon’. Visitors can see the beautiful view of Himalayan peaks from Ranikhet, especially Nanda Devi and Trishul. This destination is also known for its pleasant weather that makes it a great spot to visit.

blocks.text: How to Reach Mahavatar Babaji Cave

items: The nearest airport is Pantnagar Airport (about 125 km from Dwarahat).
Travelers can take a taxi from the airport to Dwarahat
The cave is located near Dwarahat in Almora, visitors can reach Dwarahat by taxi or bus from Almora or Haldwani.
From Delhi or Nainital, go by road to Almora and take a taxi or other local transport to reach Dwarahat.
The closest railway station to Dwarahat is Kathgodam (around 108 km).
From Kathgodam, take a taxi to Dwarahat and continue to the cave.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Mahavatar Babaji Cave

items: The best time to visit Mahavatar Babaji cave is from April to June and September to November, because the weather is pleasant at this time and the paths are clear.
The trekking routes are easier to follow during these months.
Avoid visiting during the monsoon season.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. How long is the trek to Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. You will have to undertake a 3 km long trek to reach Mahavatar Babaji's Cave. Depending on your pace you won’t take more than an hour to reach the cave via trekking. The trail is well-paved with stones and you’ll encounter breathtaking scenery during the trekking expedition.
Q2. What is the relevance of Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. Mahavatar Babaji Cave is the place where Lahiri Mahasaya is known to have spent a previous incarnation. Lahiri Mahasaya received Kriya Yoga initiation here from Babaji, and then he started spreading it out worldwide. You can meditate in the cave and practice yoga. The cave is surrounded by Himalayas offering you an unadulterated view of breathtaking sceneries
Q3. What is the best time to visit Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. Mid-February to mid-June (summer and spring seasons) are considered the best to visit Mahavatar Babaji's Cave. This period offers clear blue skies, pleasant weather, and cool and comfortable temperatures for a spiritual expedition. The awe-inspiring scenic views enhance the overall travel experience.
Q4. How can you reach Mahavatar Babaji's Cave from Delhi?

Ans. From New Delhi, you can embark on a scenic drive to Ranikhet lasting around 10 to 11 hours. From Ranikhet, you can drive towards the cave via Kukuchina Village and Dwarahat. Once you have arrived at the road’s tail end you will undertake a 3-kilometer long trek to the cave.
Q5. What can you do at Mahavatar Babaji's Cave?

Ans. At Mahavatar Babaji's Cave, you can meditate and practice yoga. You can also absorb the cave’s positive energy and appreciate the beauty of the surroundings. If you have time you can explore the places near this cave.

blocks.text: Delve on a fascinating expedition in the bewitching states of Jaipur and Delhi. See More

An exploration into breath-taking palettes of Jaipur's "Pink City" will take you around some astonishing architectural heritage like Hawa Mahal and City Palace. Experience the incredible Rajasthani culture at the Chokhi Dhani Village Resort while relishing authentic food and captivating folk performances. Discover the kingly splendor of the Amber Fort before transferring to the crowded parks of metropolitan Delhi. Be it the captivating sights the cultural immersion or the culinary delights, this tour is guaranteed to offer you an experience that you will fondly remember forever.

Travel to Delhi and stay there to absorb the energetic feeling and deep-rooted heritage that is characteristic of India’s capital.

blocks.text: Delhi - Jaipur - Majestic cities of heritages and royalty.

Famous for Jaipur and Delhi, are both very popular destinations in India, decked with impressive monuments, heritage sites, and thriving pop culture. Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan is the “Pink” City which gives a grand view of the wonderful forts, and impressive palaces among other things. On the other hand, Delhi the bustling capital is a blend of ancient monuments and modern marvels. No matter whether it is the glorious City Palace of Jaipur or the hectic pace of Old Delhi - each city grants you a kind and unforgettable experience.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What type of hotels/ accommodations will be provided in the Delhi- Jaipur Tour?
Ans. You will get good 3-4-5 star category hotels on twin/ double sharing rooms. Don’t worry the facilities and amenities in the hotel rooms are up to the mark.
Q2. How far is Jaipur from Delhi?
Ans. The distance between Delhi and Jaipur is approximately 280 kilometers by road. It takes only 5-6 hours by road to reach Jaipur.
Q3. What is the best time to visit Jaipur and Delhi?
Ans. the winter months from October to March is the best time to travel to Jaipur and Delhi. The weather remains pleasant and ideal for sightseeing.
Q4. Are there any guided tours available for exploring Jaipur and Delhi?
Ans. Yes, we provide tour guides for travelers who need valuable knowledge of tourist places and assistance during the trip. We also provided guided tours for exploring Jaipur and Delhi on budget.

blocks.text: Plan a trip to Guwahati, the largest city in Assam! Also known as a gateway to the Northeast, this place’s beauty will make you fall in love with it at first glance. See More

With this 2 Nights and 3 Days Guwahati temple tour package with Meghalaya , you get to visit all the important sightseeing places – whether it’s the popular limestone caves, ancient temples with deep-rooted Tantric significance, or the simply picturesque lakes that impress you in a heartbeat – you’re bound to go on a trip of your dreams. Book My Quick Trippers’s package to avail all the tour-related amenities – from accommodation to meals to transport services.

To tell you more about this tour plan, the package covers most of the popular temples and sites of Guwahati to make your trip worthwhile. We have also selected comfortable stays that provide delicious meals. With our service, you also get to avail the service of guided tours that will offer you historical insights into every temple you visit. In a nutshell, it is a short trip created for working professionals or people who prefer not to compromise on their work commitments. Book the package to Guwahati & Meghalaya now and enjoy the most affordable prices in the industry.

blocks.text: DAY 1 - Arrival in Guwahati – Sightseeing in Shillong (100 km /3 hrs)

items: Welcome to Assam! Upon your arrival at Guwahati Airport/Railway station, our tour representative will greet you with a warm welcome. From here on, you’ll be transferred to Shillong .

Along the way, we’ll make a stop at the magnificent Umiam Lake (Barapani Lake), which is also the largest artificial lake in Meghalaya. Surrounded by pine-covered hills, it makes for an excellent photo-op. Also, do not forget to capture the shimmering waters of the lake during the sunset. The views are just simply another world!
Once you arrive at Shillong, check into your pre-booked hotel. Freshen up!

If time permits, we’ll set out on a mini sightseeing tour in the cool mountain air of the city. Visit the local markets, such as Police Bazaar, for shopping of handicrafts. Also, try authentic Khasi cuisine like Jadoh (rice with meat).
Return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: DAY 2 - Elephant Falls - Sightseeing in Cherrapunji - Transfer to Guwahati (100 km/3 hrs)

items: Savour some delicious breakfast in the morning.
After that, we'll take you on a tour of Elephant Falls . This three-tiered cascading waterfall makes for an excellent photograph. Stand at the bottom tier if you want to capture the best views.

Later, we’ll transfer you to Cherrapunji, the most rainy place in the world (a 60 km drive; 2 hours driving time). Also known as the "Scotland of the East", it's famous for its unique natural wonders. You’ll go sightseeing at: Seven Sisters Falls: Watch the gushing water as it falls down from seven streams side by side. Mawsmai Cave: This cave is popular for its narrow passages and stunning limestone formations. You’re advised to carry a flashlight inside the cave for better views. Thangkharang Park: Overlooking the Bangladesh plains, you get to enjoy the most beautiful panoramic views of the valley here. Don’t forget to take your camera up there!
After your sightseeing tour is over, we’ll drive you back to Guwahati for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: DAY 3 – Temple tour in Guwahati and Departure

items: Get up early in the morning, as today you're up for a full-day tour of Guwahati city!

We’ll start our day early, around 4 AM, and will visit the holy Kamakhya Temple at Nilachal Hill. This is one of the revered 51 Shakti Peethas , and we recommend getting a VIP pass, which costs around INR 500 per person. This will help you skip long queues.
Also, explore nearby temples dedicated to Maa Tara, Maa Kali, Maa Chhinnamasta, Maa Bhuvaneshwari, Maa Bagalamukhi, Maa Bandurga, and Dhumapati , which are all located within walking distance.
Now take a ferry to Peacock Island on the Brahmaputra to the Umananda Temple . Photo op moments galore! This island is also home to the endangered Golden Langur. You’ll be lucky if you spot one!
Have breakfast, and after that, we’ll take you on a half-day excursion in Shillong.
This concludes your trip with us. Now, you’ll be dropped off at the railway station or airport, as per your choice. Hope you have made great memories on this tour!

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is the best time to explore Guwahati?
Ans. The best time to visit Guwahati is from October to April when the weather is nice for sightseeing.
Q2. How far is Guwahati from the airport?
Ans. Guwahati is 25 kilometres from Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, and it takes about 45 minutes to reach.
Q3. Is the Brahmaputra River Cruise included in the package?
Ans. Yes, the package includes an evening cruise ride on the Brahmaputra river.
Q4. Apart from tourist attractions, what is famous in Guwahati?
Ans. Assam is famous for its silk Sarees, tea and handicrafts using bamboo. You can explore and shop these items from Fancy Bazar and the Handicraft market.
Q5. Is it safe to travel solo in Guwahati?
Ans. Yes, Guwahati is a safe place for solo travellers. However, you must stay alert and take care of your belongings.
Q6. Can we take photographs inside Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. You can take photos of the temple complex. However, capturing pictures of the temple sanctum is prohibited. You can capture the outside of the temple architecture though, which is really beautiful.
Q7. How far is Shillong from Guwahati?

Ans. Shillong is located about 100 km from Guwahati. If you get on NH6, you can easily cover this distance in under 3 hours. The journey is quite scenic, and many people make a stop at the beautiful Umiam Lake along the way.
Q8. What kind of clothes should I pack for this tour?

Ans. As the weather in Shillong is quite cool, you’re advised to bring some light woollen clothes with you, along with jackets. We also recommend carrying rain gear and comfortable walking shoes with you. Also, you should have modest clothes on you if you're planning to visit temples.
Q9. What are the local food specialities to try in Shillong?

Ans. While visiting Shillong, we recommend trying the local, authentic cuisine. You must try Jadoh (red rice with pork), Dohneiiong (pork with black sesame), and Tungrymbai (fermented soybeans), as these are some of the most popular dishes there. Also, you can easily avail of vegetarian options as well.

blocks.text: Immersed in the history of ancient times, in possession of a kind of architecture that you don’t see anywhere else, and proud of having the land where Gods themselves walked, Dwarka is where you find cultural gems at every other corner. The sacred city is where Lord Krishna himself established his home - spirituality is just in the air here! Besides, there are so many things to do here. Many Dwarka tour packages include things like going on a temple spree, enjoying the coastal charm, sauntering around beaches, and much more! Come to Dwarka and get enchanted by its ancient allure.

items: Best Places to See on the Dwarka Tour
Top Things to Do on the Dwarka Tour

blocks.text: Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Dwarka Tour Packages?

The city of Dwarka is every pilgrimage’s dream. From temples with beautiful architecture to coastal landscapes to places with profound history, there are just too many sites to visit to experience Dwarka in its full glory. To make this exact task easy for you, we bring you our custom-curated Dwarka travel packages, so you can enjoy travelling while leaving the hectic overheads to us! In our trip packages, we include sightseeing, accommodation, meals, local transport, and more. Enjoy the holy city carefree and leave the work to us! Book your Dwarka trip today!

The best time to visit Dwarka is during the winter months - October to March . The weather is very pleasant and cool (with temperatures ranging between 12°C and 28°C) during this time and is therefore ideal for pilgrimage, temple tours, and sightseeing.
Moreover, if you travel during this period, you get to take part in the celebration of festivals like Makar Sankranti (January), Diwali (October/November), and Shivratri (February/March).
A tip : Many people book their Dwarka holiday package during Janmashtami (August/September) as well, to witness the larger-than-life celebrations celebrations at Dwarkadhish Temple!
Best Places to See on the Dwarka Tour

The holy city of Dwarka is steeped in spirituality, mythology, and history. Not only do the Krishna Bhakts love to flock to this ancient city, it’s also a travel favourite for many history buffs as well. To enjoy every aspect of this ancient city, make sure to include the following places in your Dwarka travel packages:

As the name suggests, this temple is dedicated to Dwarkadhish, the king of Dwarka, and that is none other than Lord Krishna! Needless to say, it’s a must-addition to your Drwarka tour packages. As per the legend, he created the city of Dwarka by asking the sea god to provide some land. And so the sea god did, and the rest is history!
Once you reach the temple, do not miss the Mangala and Sandhya Aarti , as the temple atmosphere gets another-worldly spiritual then.

Temple Specialities: Devotees just love the ‘ Shringar Darshan’ , where the temple’s main idols are dressed in traditional attires made of silk/brocade in vivid colours like yellow, green, pink, red, etc. In addition, he is also adorned with beautiful jewellery like stone-studded gold crowns, necklaces, bracelets, and anklets. It’s really a sight to behold!

Architecture: Another thing tourists love here is the stunning architecture of the temple. The 2000 year old structure enchants visitors with its whopping 72 intricately carved pillars and a whole five-storeyed building. Devotees also excitedly wait for the flag ceremony where the flag is changed a full five times!

While you’re out for your trip to Dwarkadhish Temple, give Gomti Ghat a visit as it’s right adjacent to the sacred temple. Many pilgrims take a holy dip at the Ghats and watch the majestic confluence of the Gomti River and the Arabian Sea. And sunrise here are simply picture-perfect and incredibly serene! Come in the early morning and enjoy calm surroundings with little to no crowd.

Just a 20-minute boat ride from Okha, this picturesque island sits pretty amid azure waters and pristine surroundings! This place is quite popularised through its various mentions in Mahabharata and various other scriptures. In addition, it holds high spiritually significance as this is believed to be the original residential place of Lord Krishna. Mnay tourists include this on their Dwarka weekend package .

Another fascinating thing about this place is that it has the only temple ( Hanuman Dandi Temple ) in India where Lord Hanuman is shown with his son Makardhwaja. The other specialty of this island is conch shells, which tourists often collect as souvenirs. Besides these, you can soak in the calm surroundings and stroll around the beaches.

This is an essential addition to your Dwarka trip package as this is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. As strong the architecture is, equally strong is the presence of the divine in here. Enter the shrine and you’ll see a 25-meter-tall magnificent statue of Lord Shiva. It is said that the shrine protects the devotees from all the evil forces. In addition, people enjoy the serene atmosphere in the temple, highly conducive for meditation.

Want to saunter along the sandy shores, say hi to dolphins, and get immersed in the vast Arabian Sea views? If yes, then head straight to Dwarka Beach. Either find seashells along the shore or simply sit and watch the sun go down, you’re in for a treat through and through. You’ll also see people taking photographs and enjoying a relaxed stroll amid the backdrop of scenic views! In addition, there are several stalls where you can find quirky seashell jewellery and unique souvenirs.
Top Things to Do on the Dwarka Tour
Dwarka is a unique blend of natural beauty, mythology, and deep spirituality. To get a wholesome experience of all its facets, include the following things on your Dwarka tour packages:

This is an essential visit on your Dwarka trip as this is the prime temple of the entire state, and also one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites. Also, most travellers who visit Dwarka, come to visit this temple, so don’t miss out on this tourist hotspot.

items: Visit the temple at both morning and evening for Mangala Aarti (early morning) and Sandhya Aarti (evening) as the vibe is completely different (yet beautiful) at both the times.
Seek the blessing of the Lord and eat Prasad.

blocks.text: Go for a Camel Ride on the Gomti River Banks

Gomti has two banks and you can go for a camel ride on either one. One thrilling aspect of the ride is that the camel walks right next to the river, making it a bit of an adventurous ride on an otherwise a rather slow walking camel.

Do not forget to add this place to your Dwarka trip packages as there is no better place than Sudama Setu to watch sunrise. Here, the cable bridge connects the two edges of the Gomti River. The whole view – the sunrise, the bridge, and the Gomti meeting with the sea as the fresh sunshine falls on it, is just a pure whimsical experience. Moreover, the sunset views from the bridge are amazing too! However, the Sudama Setu is ticketed, so you have to wait until the ticket counter opens.
Witness the Change of Flag of Dwarkadhish Temple

There is a 52-yard flag at Dwarkadhish temple and it is changed 5 times a day - three times in the morning and two times in the evening. There’s a family that sponsors the flag and they bring it in a huge festive vibe with dancing and singing. Then the Guggali Brahmin climbs the topmost point of the temple (also known as Shikhara) and proceeds to change the temple. The crowd witnessing the flag change burst out in cheer and celebration, every time the new flag comes out.
Watch the Sunset at the Beach

The best place handsdown to watch the sun go down on your Dwarka trip is at the Bhadkeshwar Mahadev Temple. This is a small but ancient temple with high spiritual significance. You can seek Darshan at the temple and then later on enjoy the unobstructed, clear views of the sunset.

If the Lord Krishna is the Dwarkadheesh (king of Dwarka), then Rukmini is the queen of Dwarka. Your visit to the city is incomplete without her temple visit! Moreover, tourists just love the intricate carvings on the temple, especially the gajatharas (elephants) and the beautiful sculptures of Gods and Goddesses.

When in Dwarka, why not visit the place where Lord Krishna was his mischievous best? Yes, we are talking about the place where he frolicked with Gopis! This sacred pond witnessed countless playful meetings between God and many, many Gopis. The yellow sand around the pond is considered super sacred and is popular as Gopi Chandan . Devotees often add this lovely location to their Dwarka tour packages!
Buy the famous delicious Gujarati snacks and sweets at local markets near Dwarkadhish Temple. For souvenirs, people are seen buying small idols of Lord Krishna, conch shells, handicrafts, and beads.
Take a Holy Dip at Gomti Ghat

This sacred Ghat marks the meeting point of Gomti River and Arabian Sea. People plunge into the river, offering their prayers ad whispering sacred mantras. Come in the early morning to take in the serene and peaceful atmospheres.

items: Gujarati cuisine has a lot of lip-smacking vegetarian dishes that you must try on your Dwarka trip, such as:
Traditional Gujarati Thali : It usually consists of Roti/Puri, dal, Kadhi, seasonal vegetable curries, rice/Khichdi, Papad/pickles/chutneys, and sweet dishes.
Gujarati Snacks : Dhokla, Khandvi, Thepla, Khakhra, and more
Sweets and Desserts : Shrikhand, Basundi, Gulab Jamun, Ghooghra etc.
Dry Snacks : Gathiya, Sev, and Thepla
Local Street Food : Pani Puri, Chaat, Dabeli, Bhajiya, etc.

blocks.text: Frequently Answered Questions about Dwarka Tour Packages
Q1. How to plan Dwarka trip?
Ans. Planning for a Dwarka trip is easy, just keep in mind the following things:

items: 1. Decide travel duration: Choose whether you want to see the basics of Dwarka (requires 2-3 days) or want an extended trip (requires 4-5 days) to include nearby locations as well, like Porbandar, Somnath, etc.
2. Plan itinerary: Decide on what places to visit and on which day.
3. Set budget: Decide on your expenses, picking from budgeted travel to luxury tours.
4. Book transport: Check the suitable options to travel (by air, rail, or road) Dwarka from your location.
5. Select accommodation: Book a hotel in advance to avoid accommodation problems.
6. Start packing: Carry modest, lightweight clothes for temple visits. Also, pack hat, sunscreen, and comfortable shoes.

blocks.text: Q2. What is the ideal duration for my Dwarka trip?

Ans. Generally, a 2-3 day visit is perfect for exploring all the key tourist attractions, like Dwarkadhish temple, Dwarka Bet, etc. However, if you plan to extend your trip to include nearby locations, such as Somnath and Porbandar, then 4-5 days are required for your trip.
Q3. Is photography allowed at temples?
Ans. Photography is not allowed inside the temple premises. However, you can click pictures on the outer premises. When in doubt, ask the temple staff or check for signage.
Q4. What are some festivals that are celebrated with great zeal in Dwarka?
Ans. The festivals like Janmashtami, Shivratri, Holi and Diwali are observed with grand celebrations with temples being beautifully decorated and special prayers offered.
Q5. How much does a Dwarka trip cost?
Ans. The Dwarka trip cost depends on your travel style, accommodation type, transport modes, meal inclusion, etc. Here’s a quick guide to Dwarka trip budget:
Budget Package (₹5,000–₹7,000/person): This includes budget hotels/Dharamshalas, non-AC buses/shared cabs for transportation, sightseeing of only major attractions, and limited meals.
Mid-range Tour Packages (₹8,000–₹12,000/person): This includes mid-range hotels/guesthouses, AC cars/deluxe buses for transportation, guided tours etc.
Luxury Tour Packages (₹15,000–₹25,000/person): This includes stay in luxury hotels/resorts, transportation by luxury cars, guided tours with additional services, and more.
Ans. You can reach this cultural city in many ways:
By Air : The nearest airport is Jamnagar Airport, about 110 km away from Dwarka. From the airport, you can take a bus or taxi to reach the city.

By Train : Dwarka Railway Station is the in-house railway station of the city. It is well-connected to cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Rajkot, Ahmedabad, and Vadodara. To check train availability and further updates, you can use IRCTC website.
By Road : There are many buses run by private and Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation from Dwarka to nearby cities.

blocks.text: Ajmer, a city in the heart of Rajasthan, India, holds profound cultural and historical significance, making it a compelling destination for travellers seeking a blend of spirituality, heritage, and natural beauty. Ajmer tour packages offer an enchanting exploration of this city’s multifaceted charm, catering to various interests and preferences.

At the heart of Ajmer lies the revered Ajmer Sharif Dargah, a Sufi shrine dedicated to Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, attracting pilgrims from diverse backgrounds worldwide. Tour packages often revolve around this spiritual center, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the serene atmosphere and witness the rich cultural tapestry of devotion.

The city also boasts architectural marvels like the majestic Taragarh Fort, offering panoramic views of Ajmer, and the tranquil Ana Sagar Lake, a picturesque spot ideal for leisurely strolls or serene boat rides.

Ajmer’s historical legacy is further depicted through the Akbari Fort & Museum, showcasing artifacts and relics from various periods of Rajasthan’s history, providing an insightful glimpse into its royal past.
Moreover, these packages frequently include visits to Pushkar, a town adjacent to Ajmer famous for the sacred Pushkar Lake and the Brahma Temple, making it a significant pilgrimage site.
Shopping enthusiasts can explore the vibrant local markets, such as Naya Bazar and Dargah Bazar, known for their traditional Rajasthani handicrafts, textiles, and vibrant souvenirs.

Tour packages to Ajmer often encompass comfortable accommodation options, guided tours to significant landmarks, transportation facilities, and insights into the city’s rich cultural heritage, offering travellers an immersive and fulfilling experience amidst the historical and spiritual tapestry of this captivating city in Rajasthan.

blocks.text: The Adi Kailash Yatra is a sacred pilgrimage to the revered “Chhota Kailash,” located in the remote Himalayan region of Uttarakhand near the Indo–China border. Adi Kailash is considered one of the most holy abodes of Lord Shiva and holds deep spiritual significance for devotees. The journey offers a unique blend of devotion and natural beauty, surrounded by untouched mountains, rivers, and peaceful valleys. A key highlight of this Yatra is Om Parvat, where the naturally formed “ॐ” symbol on the mountain attracts pilgrims from all over the country.

Our Adi Kailash tour packages are planned to make the journey smooth and accessible, while still keeping the spiritual essence intact. The route passes through scenic Himalayan locations such as Pithoragarh, Dharchula, Gunji, and nearby remote villages, giving travelers a close look at mountain life and raw natural landscapes. The journey includes travel assistance, stays, and guided support throughout the route.

If you are looking for the best Adi Kailash Yatra package in 2026, My Quick Trippers — a Ministry of Tourism approved operator — offers road and helicopter options starting from ₹48,500 per person, with complete ILP registration support. Book now to secure your preferred departure date for the 2026 Yatra season.

ILP Permit — 100% Handled by Our Team The Inner Line Permit (ILP) at SDM Dharchula is mandatory for every pilgrim and the single biggest logistical concern on this yatra. Our ground team manages your entire application — Aadhaar copies, medical certificate coordination, police verification, and submission. You do not spend a day at a government office.

Private Vehicle Throughout — Not Shared Transport Innova Crysta for groups up to 4, Tempo Traveller for larger groups. Your vehicle does not get shared mid-route. Beyond Dharchula, only private SUVs are permitted on BRO roads — we ensure this is pre-arranged, not sorted on arrival.

Acclimatisation Built Into Every Itinerary A planned overnight at Gunji (approx. 3,300m) before proceeding to Jyolingkong (4,572m) is not filler time — it is medically essential. We carry a basic oxygen cylinder and high-altitude first aid kit on all road-based departures.
KMVN-Coordinated Stays Accommodation is at KMVN rest houses and pre-verified private guesthouses in Dharchula, Gunji, and Kalapani — booked in advance, not arranged upon arrival.

624/7 Trip Coordinator Support A dedicated coordinator is reachable by phone throughout the yatra. Emergency rescheduling, weather-related plan changes, and any mid-trip assistance are managed from our Dehradun operations base.

blocks.text: Places You Will Visit on the Adi Kailash Yatra

items: Adi Kailash (Chhota Kailash) — 5,945m The crown of this yatra. Lord Shiva's earthly abode in the Kumaon Himalayas, considered a sacred mirror of Mount Kailash in Tibet. Pilgrims who behold this peak are said to attain spiritual liberation.

Parvati Sarovar (Gauri Kund) — Jyolingkong A sacred glacial lake at the base of Adi Kailash. According to Shiva Purana, this is where Goddess Parvati bathed before her union with Lord Shiva. A holy dip here is one of the key rituals of the yatra.

Om Parvat — Nabhidhang, approx. 3,600m A peak whose snow naturally forms the "ॐ" symbol, visible on clear mornings between 7–9:30 AM. Best viewed from the Nabhidhang viewpoint. Considered among the most spiritually charged sights in the Himalayas.

Kalapani — Source of Kali River, approx. 3,600m A restricted-zone site near the India–Nepal–Tibet trijunction. The Kali Mata temple here sits at the precise origin of the Kali (Sharda) river. Access is possible only with a valid ILP.

Vyas Cave & Pandav Fort — near Jyolingkong Located 1–2 km from the Adi Kailash base, these mythological sites are believed to be where Maharishi Vyas composed the Mahabharata and where the Pandavas rested during their final journey.

Gunji Village — approx. 3,300m A high-altitude border village and mandatory overnight stop. Acclimatisation here before proceeding to Jyolingkong (4,572m) is critical. The village offers a rare glimpse of Kumaoni border culture.

Dharchula — Gateway to the Yatra The last town before the restricted zone. ILP registration happens here. Last ATM, last mobile network, last pharmacy — everything beyond Dharchula must be planned from here.

Who Issues It: Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Office, Dharchula — or through KMVN (Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam). Official portal: kmvn.in

blocks.text: For photography and Om Parvat clarity — September and October are definitively the best months. The OM symbol in snow is sharpest in post-monsoon light.
For first-time pilgrims — May–June offers gentler conditions and a less crowded yatra circuit.

By Air: The nearest airport is Naini Saini Airport, Pithoragarh — connected to Delhi by scheduled and charter services (approx. 1 hour). Pantnagar Airport (Udham Singh Nagar) has better connectivity from Delhi, Mumbai, and Lucknow; it is 210 km from Pithoragarh (5–6 hours by road). Our team arranges pickup from both airports.

By Train: Kathgodam Railway Station (Haldwani) is the nearest railhead — 175 km from Pithoragarh (5–6 hours by road). Well-connected to Delhi, Lucknow, and Agra. Key trains: Ranikhet Express (12039) and Uttarakhand Sampark Kranti from Delhi. Our road package includes Kathgodam pickup.

By Road: Delhi to Pithoragarh: approx. 490 km via Moradabad–Rampur–Tanakpur (12–14 hours). Lucknow to Kathgodam: approx. 430 km (9–10 hours). Beyond Dharchula, only private SUVs are permitted on the BRO single-lane road — commercial vehicles are not allowed.

Weather / Force Majeure: If the route closes due to landslide, BRO restriction, or natural calamity, we reschedule your trip to the next available departure at no extra cost, or issue a 12-month credit note. Cash refunds are subject to recovery of non-refundable third-party costs.
Q1. What is the cost of the Adi Kailash Yatra package in 2026?

Ans. The road package starts at ₹48,500 per person on twin sharing (8 nights/9 days from Kathgodam). The helicopter package starts at ₹58,500 (4 nights/5 days from Pithoragarh). The extended helicopter package including Mt. Kailash views and Old Lipulekh Pass is ₹65,500. Prices include accommodation, meals, transport, and ILP assistance.
Q2. Is registration mandatory for Adi Kailash Yatra 2026?

Ans. Yes. An Inner Line Permit (ILP) is legally mandatory for all Indian citizens to travel beyond Dharchula. It is issued by the SDM Office, Dharchula. When you book with us, our ground team handles the complete registration — you only need to provide documents.
Q3. When does the 2026 Adi Kailash Yatra season open and close?

Ans. Phase 1 (main summer) opened on May 8, 2026 and runs till mid-June. Phase 2 (post-monsoon) runs mid-September to mid-October. The route is closed November to April due to snowfall, and July–August travel is not recommended due to active landslides.
Q4. Is the Yatra suitable for senior citizens?

Ans. Yes. The BRO road now reaches Jyolingkong (Adi Kailash base) — no mandatory trekking is required. Senior citizens in reasonable health can complete this yatra comfortably. KMVN's practical upper age limit is 70 years. A medical fitness certificate is required for the ILP.
Q5. What documents are needed for the Adi Kailash permit?

Ans. You need: Aadhaar Card (original + 4 photocopies), 4 passport-size photos, a medical fitness certificate (from any registered doctor), a police verification form or passport photocopy, and a notarised indemnity affidavit on ₹30 stamp paper. Our team provides the exact formats.
Q6. Can I see both Adi Kailash and Om Parvat in one trip?

Ans. Yes. All our packages include both. Adi Kailash Darshan is from Jyolingkong, and Om Parvat is viewed from the Nabhidhang viewpoint. The two sites are covered on separate days, each with an early morning start for optimal visibility.
Q7. What is the best time for Om Parvat Darshan?

Ans. The "ॐ" snow symbol on Om Parvat is clearest between 7:00 AM and 9:30 AM. Cloud cover builds from the valley by 10–10:30 AM and can completely block the view. All our itineraries schedule departure from Gunji by 5:45–6:00 AM on Om Parvat day.
Q8. Are there any hidden charges?

Ans. No. Lunches, personal expenses, travel insurance, medical certificate fee, and any costs due to weather disruption are listed explicitly in our exclusions. There are no charges added after booking confirmation.
Q9. Can foreigners or NRIs do the Adi Kailash Yatra?

Ans. The standard ILP is available to Indian citizens only. Foreign nationals and NRI cardholders (OCI/PIO) require a Protected Area Permit (PAP) from the Ministry of Home Affairs — this must be applied for at least 2–3 months in advance and is a separate, more complex process.
Q10. How far in advance should I book the 2026 package?

Ans. For Phase 1 (May–June): 8–10 weeks in advance. For Phase 2 (September–October): 6–8 weeks. Helicopter slots fill faster — book as early as possible for the helicopter package. Our team responds within 2 hours on business days.

Ever since it was brought to light by Gautam Buddha at a very young age it has brought with it a sense of peace and belonging among its followers. According to some scholars, the basic roots of Buddhism is deeply steeped in the teachings of Hinduism. Being the world’s 4th largest religion it has over 520 million followers i.e. about 7% of the world population. Just like in any other religion, pilgrimage forms a very important part in Buddhism as well. Since the wheel of dharma was set forth in the eastern gangetic plains, most of these spiritual Buddhist centres are concentrated in those parts of the subcontinent. With the development and encouragement of tourism in India, the connectivity of these places have developed massively. The Buddhist tour packages ensure a convenient travel experience to these spiritual centres. Throughout the journey you will experience a sense of peace and calm that will leave a lasting impression in your heart for a long time. A Buddhist pilgrimage is said to provide liberation or nirvana. This pilgrimage goes from Lumbini to Bodh Gaya and explores various sites, stupas and places related to the teachings of Buddhism. The whole pilgrimage is all about offering an experience that will be a refreshing experience in itself while also looking forward to the future.

Buddhism is one of the oldest and majorly followed religions in the world. Originating in Bihar around 5th century BC this religion has garnered a huge following all over the world. The philosophy of the religion was developed from the teachings of Gautam Buddha or the awakened / enlightened one. Ever since its birth the teachings made its way across borders like China, Korea and Japan. Seekers and religious students started to make their way to India in order to learn more about this unique religion that was being taught by Gautam Buddha himself in Nalanda University.

Buddhism was preached in the language of the masses that was Pali and Sanskrit, the same language in which the literary texts and source of the religion survives till date. This was one of the most appealing features for the spreading of Buddhism as a religion tenfold. This day, Buddhism stands as one of the majorly followed religions in the world.

The founder of Buddhism was called Siddharth Gautam who lived from c. 563 to 483 BCE. He was born in a royal family as a son of an Indian warrior king in Lumbini (present-day Nepal). Gautam led a very extravagant and privileged life which was the direct result of his position and social standing. However, soon he got very bored and started feeling unfulfilled of his privileges and got the urge to look for something more, a different purpose in life. He left the royal indulgences, his wife and his child, to pursue the greater meaning in life.

He started wandering and during one of these instances he met with an old man, an ill man, a corpse and an ascetic who made him believe that all worldly pleasures need to be renounced. He came to the realisation or gained enlightenment while meditating under a Peepal tree (Ficus religiosa) in Bodh Gaya — this sacred tree is now known as the Bodhi Tree. After achieving salvation, he decided to walk all over India while spreading the teachings of dharma, beginning with his first sermon at the Deer Park in Sarnath .
With a rich historical background there are several interesting aspects and facts about Buddhism. Here are some facts about Buddhism:

items: Half of the world's Buddhist population resides in China according to research. Still, they make up for only about 18% of the country's population. Other than this, 13% of the Buddhist population resides in Thailand, 9% in Japan and only 1.4% of the Buddhist population outside Asia.

Buddhism in Asia is a matter of both practice and identity. Various journalists and scholars have studied that many people living in Asian countries may even engage in various Buddhist practices without recognizing themselves as a part of any other organised religion.
The first mention of Buddha in western writing is in the writings of Clement of Alexandria that dates around 2 AD.
The Buddha founded the concept of Sanghas which is an order of monks and nuns that helps in preserving the knowledge and teachings of Buddhism even to this day.
There is no single holy book when it comes to Buddhism. Various scriptures about its teachings are preserved in a variety of Asian languages.
Buddhism emphasises on mindfulness and meditation because of which it is often considered as a form of psychology over a widely practised religion.

blocks.text: The primary feature of any Buddhist teaching is the concept of four noble truths in life. These are: the truth of suffering, the truth of the cause of suffering, the truth of the end of suffering and the truth of the path that leads to the end of suffering. To put it simply, suffering exists, it stems from somewhere and eventually it has to come to an end. The intention of talking about suffering is not to create a negative view of the world but a rather more pragmatic approach to deal with the world as it is along with the attempts to rectify it.

Unlike the concept of karma in contemporary society, the Buddhist interpretation of karma does not refer to preordained faith. Karma according to Buddhism refers to the good and bad actions that a person takes in their lifetime. The weight of these actions is determined by certain conditions such as: frequent and repetitive actions, determined intentional action, actions performed without regret, action against extraordinary persons and action toward those who have helped one in the past.

Karma plays out in the Buddhism cycle of rebirth. There are 6 separate planes into which any living being can be reborn which consists of — three fortunate realms and three unfortunate realms. People with favourable and positive karma are born in the fortunate realm and the realm of man is considered as the highest realm of rebirth. In the same manner, the inhabitants of the unfortunate realm suffer from untold suffering.

Places of Buddhist relevance mostly lie in the Indo-Gangetic Plain of Nepal and North India. These are the places where Gautam Buddha was born, lived, achieved salvation and taught Buddhism. Here are the four main pilgrimage sites listed by Buddha himself:

items: Lumbini, Nepal: Birthplace of Siddharth Gautam and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Maya Devi Temple marks the exact birth spot. Also visit the Ashoka Pillar (249 BCE), Bodhi Tree, and the zone of international monasteries from 20+ countries.

Bodh Gaya, Bihar: The most sacred site in Buddhism — where Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree. The Mahabodhi Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Also visit the Great Buddha Statue, Niranjana River, and Sujata Temple.

Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh: Where the enlightened Buddha delivered his first sermon in the Deer Park. Located 10 km from Varanasi. Key sites: Dhamek Stupa, Chaukhandi Stupa, and Sarnath Archaeological Museum (houses the original Lion Capital of Ashoka).
Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh: Where Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (final liberation). The Mahaparinirvana Temple houses a reclining Buddha statue. The Rambhar Stupa marks the cremation site.

blocks.text: The extended Buddhist circuit also includes:

items: Rajgir, Bihar: Where Buddha spent several rainy seasons and delivered important teachings. Visit Gridhakuta (Vulture's Peak) and Shanti Stupa (Japanese Peace Pagoda, accessible by ropeway).
Nalanda, Bihar: Site of the ancient Nalanda Mahavihara — one of the world's first residential universities where Buddhist scholars from across Asia came to study. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Vaishali, Bihar: Where Buddha delivered his last sermon before Mahaparinirvana. The Ashoka Pillar here is among the best preserved. Also visit the World Peace Pagoda.
Sravasti, Uttar Pradesh: Where Buddha spent 24 rainy seasons. The Jetavana Gardens and Sahet-Mahet ruins are the main pilgrimage sites.

Q1: What Is The Buddhist Pilgrimage Route?

The core Buddhist pilgrimage route covers the four main sites: Lumbini (Nepal, birthplace), Bodhgaya (Bihar, enlightenment), Sarnath (Uttar Pradesh, first sermon), and Kushinagar (Uttar Pradesh, Mahaparinirvana). The extended Buddhist circuit adds Rajgir, Nalanda, Vaishali, and Sravasti. Most dedicated tours start from Delhi or Bodhgaya and cover 8 to 17 days depending on which sites are included.
Q2: Which City Is The Holy City For Buddhism?
Lumbini — the birthplace of Gautam Buddha — is considered the holiest Buddhist city for Buddhists.
Yes. Gautam Buddha was born in a Hindu family.
Q4: What Is The Symbolism Of Buddhism?

The wheel of dharma is the primary symbol for Buddhism. It represents the Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath and the path to liberation. The Dharma Chakra also forms the central motif of the national flag of India.

After cremation at Kushinagar, the ashes and relics of Buddha were distributed and enshrined in Stupas at locations connected to his life — Lumbini, Bodhgaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar, Vaishali, and Rajgir among them. The Rambhar Stupa in Kushinagar marks the cremation site.
Q6: How Many Days Are Needed for a Buddhist Pilgrimage Tour in India?

For the four main sites (Lumbini, Bodhgaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar), 8 to 10 days are sufficient. For the full extended Buddhist circuit including Rajgir, Nalanda, Vaishali, and Sravasti, 12 to 17 days is ideal. My Quick Trippers offers packages from 5 days (Ajanta-Ellora) up to 17 days (Footsteps of Buddha full circuit).
Q7: What Is The Cost of a Buddhist Pilgrimage Tour Package?

Packages start from ₹14,500 per person (5-day Ajanta-Ellora tour, twin sharing). The standard 8-day Buddhist Pilgrimage Tour starts from ₹24,500 per person. The 17-day Footsteps of Buddha complete circuit starts from ₹48,500 per person. Prices vary based on hotel category, group size, and season. Contact us for a custom quote.
Q8: Is a Visa Required for Lumbini (Nepal)?

Indian citizens can enter Nepal without a visa using a valid photo ID — Aadhaar card, voter ID, or passport. International visitors need a valid passport and Nepal visa (available on arrival at the border). My Quick Trippers handles all border crossing formalities for packages that include Lumbini.
Q9: Is There a Buddhist Circuit Tourist Train?

Yes. IRCTC runs the Mahaparinirvan Express — a dedicated Buddhist Circuit Tourist Train covering Delhi, Gaya (for Bodhgaya), Varanasi (for Sarnath), Kushinagar, Lumbini, Sravasti, and back to Delhi. My Quick Trippers is IRCTC affiliated and can arrange Buddhist Circuit Train tour packages.
Q10: Can Non-Buddhist Travellers Book These Packages?

Yes. The Buddhist circuit is open to everyone — Hindus, non-Hindus, historians, heritage travellers, and spiritual seekers of all backgrounds. The combination of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, ancient university ruins, living monasteries, and Gangetic plains scenery makes it one of India's most unique heritage circuits.
Q11: What Is Included in the Buddhist Tour Package?

Standard inclusions: AC vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing, hotel accommodation (twin sharing), daily breakfast and dinner, driver allowance, tolls, fuel, and airport or station pickup and drop. Exclusions: airfare or train fare, monument entry fees, Nepal border charges (if Lumbini included), lunch, and personal expenses. Customized packages may vary — confirm at the time of booking.

blocks.text: Day 1: Arrival at Bhubaneswar (the capital of Odisha)

When you reach Bhubaneswar Airport or Railway Station, our representative will welcome you and take you to the hotel. Next you will visit the twin hills of Khandagiri and Udayagiri, where you can explore Jain Temple and Elephanta Caves, including the Lion Cave and Queen Cave from the first century BC. Bhubaneswar is famous for its temples built from the 7th to the 13th centuries. In this temple city, you can see the temples like Lingaraj, Mukteshwar, Kedargouri, Parashurameshvara Mandir, and Bindusagar.
Note: Nandankanan, the State Museum, and the Tribal Museum are closed on Mondays and state holidays.
Day 2: Bhubaneswar - Dhauli - Pipli - Konark - Puri

After breakfast, drive to Konark and stop to explore Dhauli (a Buddhist Stupa and peace pagoda) and Pipli (a popular village for its decorative work). When you reach Konark, visit the famous Konark Sun Temple. It was constructed in the 13th century by King Narasimha. Now, proceed to Puri, and on the way, visit Chandrabhaga Beach, which has amazing clean sands, and ramachandi Temple. Then, go to Puri and check into the hotel. In the evening, explore Puri and visit Shri Jagannath Temple, this temple is important in Odisha’s culture and religion. Over the years, many kings, religious leaders, worshippers, and devotees come to visit. It is famous around the world. Next, stay overnight at a hotel.
Note: Travelers cannot visit the Jagannath Temple during the “Anavasara’’ period, from the Krishna Paksha of Ashada month until the Jagannath Rath Yatra begins.
Day 3: Depart from Puri to Bhubaneshwar (60 kms /2 hours)

After breakfast, end your ‘Puri Konark Tour’. Return to Bhubaneswar, on the way stop at Raghurajpur, a village popular for its Pattachitra paintings, palm leaf art, wooden toys and more. You will also pass through Pipli and Dhauli. The trip ends at Bhubaneswar railway station.

blocks.text: If you want to see the natural beauty, ancient architecture, and hustle-bustle of an active metropolis, all rolled into one, then come to Vietnam! This country enchants you with its green rice fields, mist-covered mountain peaks, rivers lakes, and unique floating villages! While you’re falling for its scenic landscapes, Vietnam will take you by surprise with its modern skyscrapers and vibrant city life. And that’s not all! Vietnam has a long history and places of sublime cultural importance - a true paradise for history buffs. Tourists often choose Vietnam tour packages to enjoy its rich heritage and one-of-a-kind charm

items: Best Places to Visit during Vietnam Trip
Top Things to Do on Your Vietnam Trip

blocks.text: Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Vietnam Tour Packages?

Whether you like to splay out on sandy beaches near azure waters, cycle through the peaceful, pristine villages in the countryside, or explore the rich history of Vietnam, there is something for everyone here! This postcard-perfect country is a must-visit, at least once in your life. To make your travel easy and truly hassle-free, we bring you the best of the best Vietnam travel packages . A Vietnam trip with us will give you the best experience of Vietnam! So don’t wait, witness its unparalleled charm and book your Vietnam tour today!
Best Places to Visit during Vietnam Trip

Vietnam has it all – from calm, serene countryside to a modern world, like no other! So do include a mix and match of these places in your Vietnam travel packages to make the most out of your trip. Here’s a list of must-visit places in the Asian country:

The capital city of Vietnam, Hanoi, is a city with a charm of its own kind! From boasting of modern vibrant places to possessing colonial charm to still practicing ancient traditions, Hanoi captures the past and present spirit of Vietnam supremely well and therefore is a must-visit on your Vietnam trip.

items: Old Quarter : This complex of narrow streets will wow you with cafes, traditional shops, and must-try street food.

Hoan Kiem Lake : This serene lake is perfect for refreshing yourself. In addition, it holds Turtle Tower and Ngoc Son Temple at its centre. They are a sight to behold and therefore should definitely be on your Vietnam holiday package.
Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum : Pay homage to Vietnam’s one of the most revolutionary leaders, Ho Chi Minh, as this is his final resting place!
Temple of Literature : Visit Vietnam’s very first university, dedicated to renowned Chinese philosopher Confucius.
Vietnamese Women’s Museum : Get to know how Vietnamese women changed and influenced the culture and history of the country over the years in this class-apart museum.

blocks.text: This UNESCO World Heritage Site must be added to your Vietnam travel packages as it’s famous for its dreamlike karst limestone formations and pillars rising from emerald waters.

items: Enjoy a nighttime traditional junk boat cruise and soak in the stunning views.
Take Kayaking through hidden lagoons and also caves, such as Sung Sot.
Go see the rare floating villages like Cua Van.
Discover with your own eyes the incredibly beautiful Bai Tu Long Bay. (Recommended for a Vietnam trip as it’s less crowded)
Opt for a luxury cruise with premium amenities and services.

blocks.text: Get your camera ready as you’re up for enjoying a picturesque town. Nestled in the vast mountains, Sapa is especially famous for its rich hill tribe culture and beautiful terraced rice fields. It is advised to add this beautiful location to your Vietnam holiday package during winter (December-February), mainly for the coveted views of snow-clad mountains. You can also come here in September to watch those golden rice fields in their full glory.

items: Go for jaunting trekking to scenic villages like Lao Chai, Ta Van, and Cat Cat village.
Visit the Fansipan Mountain, also known as the "Roof of Indochina". Most tourists either hike or take a cable car to reach the summit, to enjoy the breathtaking panoramic views.
Walk into the famous Sapa market and shop for local textiles and ethnic handicrafts.

Note on Snow at Sapa: Snow at Sapa is possible in December-January but is not guaranteed every year. Climate patterns have changed significantly. Do not plan specifically to see snow — treat it as a possibility, not a certainty.

blocks.text: This central Vietnam attraction was once the imperial capital of the country! Today, it’s a proud tourist hotspot for exploring ancient architecture and the history of Vietnam. Many Vietnam trip packages include this destination to give the travellers a taste of the country’s heritage.

items: Imperial City (Citadel): This vast complex houses gardens, temples, and even palaces for a wholesome sightseeing experience. An essential visit for your Vietnam trip!
Tombs of Emperors : See the ancient royals resting in peace by visiting the graves of the greats like Tu Duc, Khai Dinh, and Minh Mang.

Thien Mu Pagoda: Located on the Perfume River, this beautiful seven-storeyed temple lures tourists with its rare architectural structures. It once acted as the major organising point for the Buddhist movement and now it’s the unofficial symbol of Hue! Also, many travellers love to take a fun dragon boat ride on the Perfume River during the evenings!

blocks.text: Fancy some downtime near turquoise waters and swaying palm trees? If yes, then head straight to Phu Quoc Island on your Vietnam trip. This tropical paradise pleases its tourists with refreshing clear waters and sandy beaches. You’re really in for a treat! People generally include this destination on their Vietnam tour packages during November-April as this is the most pleasant season.

items: Sao Beach : Come take a dive in its crystal blue water or saunter around in white sand.
Phu Quoc National Park : Spot the interesting wild animals or go for unforgettable hiking adventures.
Night Market : Visit the night market for some souvenir shopping or gorge on some local seafood.

blocks.text: Offering lush greenery and oh-so-stunning karst landscapes, the beautiful city of Ninh Binh is an all-time tourist favourite. Also known as “Halong Bay on land”, this site is famous for its incredible picturesque sceneries.

items: Visit Hoa Lu, the ancient capital of Vietnam. Once highly politically significant, it now serves as an excellent tourist hub.
Enjoy the thrilling boat rides through Tam Coc or Trang An’s waterways.
Enjoy the vast panoramic views of rice fields by climbing the Mua Cave.

blocks.text: This is the largest city in Vietnam, and therefore expect to see a bustling, vibrant metropolis. Located in southern Vietnam, it is famous for both – its modern skyscrapers and rich history.

items: War Remnants Museum : Visit this amazing museum which showcases the Vietnam War in a rather somber but fitting manner.
Cu Chi Tunnels : Get a movie-like thrill exploring this underground tunnel network, used exclusively during the war!
Ben Thanh Market : It’s perfect for relishing street food and shopping for local goods.

blocks.text: Dotted with palm trees, this coastal town is a popular beach resort with stunning hotels and restaurants. The wind condition is mostly steady and therefore it’s popular for water sports like sailing, kitesurfing, and windsurfing. Moreover, it’s a popular gateway from Ho Chi Minh City, therefore, many Vietnam travel packages include this coastal escape in the itinerary.

Frequently Asked Questions about Vietnam Tour Packages
Q1: What is the best time to visit Vietnam?
Ans. The best time to visit Vietnam is from March to April, as the weather is pleasant with clear skies and therefore this time is perfect for sightseeing and outdoor activities.
Q2: How many days are ideal for visiting Vietnam?
Ans. There are two recommended durations:
5-7 days : You can cover major tourist hotspots like Ho Chi Minh City, Ha Long Bay, and Hanoi.
10-14 days : In this window, you can include additional destinations like the Mekong Delta, Sapa, Hue, and Hoi An.
Q3: How much does a Vietnam tour package cost from India?
Ans. The cost of a Vietnam tour depends on various factors, like your travel style, duration, and sights in the itinerary. Here’s a quick summary:
This includes budget hotels, eating local and street food, transport through public or shared transport, and basic entry fees for sightseeing.

Q4: What should I pack for a Vietnam tour?

Ans. Pack breathable, lightweight clothes as Vietnam’s climate is humid and warm. However, for northern regions like Hanoi or Sapa, pack a sweater or light jacket. Carry swimwear for beaches and hotel pools. Bring sunscreen and a hat for protection from the sun.
Q5: How to plan for a Vietnam trip with family?

Ans. A 7-10 day trip is recommended for a Vietnam family trip. Sights like Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, Mekong Delta, Ha Long Bay, Hoi An, Da Nang, and Ho Chi Minh City must be included in your Vietnam tour packages. Some family-friendly activities include cycling through villages & rice fields, relaxing on beaches, going on cruises, and exploring the natural beauty of the country.

Shimla Manali Honeymoon Tour Itinerary Package

Upon arriving at your designated point of arrival in Chandigarh you will be greeted by our tour manager. After greeting, you will be transferred to your next destination of the day in Shimla. After a blissful morning breakfast and post-checking out of your hotel, you will be transferred to your next destination in Manali. En route a visit to the Beas Sutlej link project will take place. This will also include visits to places like Pandoh Dam and the scenic Kullu Valley. By evening you will be arriving at your allotted hotel in Manali. Finally, the remainder of the day will be free for you to indulge in leisure activities. The night will be followed by dinner and an overnight stay.

The morning will start off on a beautiful note. The breakfast will be followed by a full day of sightseeing experiences in Manali. The drive will take place to the Rohtang snow point. Post-Rohtang fun you will be taken for a spiritual Darshan at the Hidimba Devi Temple. After the temple visit you will be taken for souvenir shopping at the famous mall road in Manali. Night and dinner will be done at the hotel in Manali.

After a delicious breakfast, a visit through the Atal Tunnel will take place. This tunnel is famous for being the world’s longest high-altitude tunnel at 10,040 feet above sea level. On the other side of the Atal Tunnel, Sissu Waterfall visit will be done. After this an adventure visit to Solang valley will happen. This will include experiences such as paragliding, hiking, zorbing, zip lining etc. after having thrilling experiences you will be headed back to your hotel in Manali for dinner and an overnight stay.

Post check out from the hotel in Manali you will be taken for a fun river rafting experience on the Beas River. Finally, you will be headed to your hotel in Chandigarh. blocks.text: The best time to visit Shimla depends on what kind of experience you're looking for. Here's a breakdown of the seasons:

items: This season offers pleasant weather to enjoy the best views of Shimla and enjoy the adventure activities. It is also the best time to enjoy trekking, boating and enjoying the lush green landscapes. Also look for Shimla Summer Festival. It's one of the most popular festivals in Shimla held in May- June in the Ridge area. You will enjoy the local Himachali culture with folk music and dance performances like Nati and Gidda.
You will also behold various handicraft exhibitions, fashion shows, flower shows, and enjoy savoring delicious cuisines at the food stalls in this festival.

Marked by the clear skies and cool mountain breeze, this season of the year is for people who love to explore nature spots. The vibrant cultural festivals like Dussehra, Diwali make this time of the year best for the travelers looking for a perfect blend of nature and cultural experiences in Shimla. During this time, you will also witness less crowds than in the summer months.

items: The scenic Ridge is the heart of Shimla. It is one of the most popular points of tourist interests in Shimla. Surrounded by the majestic Himalayan mountains, you will be spellbound by the panoramic views.

It is the best place for shopping, leisurely walks and capturing the beauty of the mountains. The place has many statues of the eminent figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Indira Gandhi, Dr. Y.S. Parmar, and Atal Bihari Vajpayee. It also includes the iconic Christ Church and the Tudorbethan-style State Library.

Don't miss Mall Road in Shimla as it is the best place if you truly want to understand the local culture and lifestyle. The vibrant atmosphere of Shimla is delightfully chaotic. It is the best place for shopping in Shimla.
You will also witness many food stalls offering the best street food of the mountains. The beautiful views of the valley and colonial era buildings are major sights to behold.
The highest peak in Shimla, Jakhu Hill houses one of the majestic 108 ft statues of lord Hanuman.
Usually, people visit Jakhu Temple through trekking. You will witness beautiful Deodar forests along the way.

While on his way to gather information on Sanjeevani Booti (medicinal Herb) Lord Hanuman stopped on Jakhu Hill. The temple is a place where his footprints are still kept intact. The idol of Lord Hanuman is a self-manifested idol in the Sanctum.
Kufri, located a few km away from Shimla is a must visit Hill Station to enjoy fun-filled picnic and adventure activities.
It's a very famous place to enjoy winter sports like skiing, snowboarding. You will also capture the beauty of Mahasu Peak, the highest viewpoint of the region.

Apart from adventure activities, this place is best to enjoy Yak rides, nature walks, picnics, enjoying fun activities at amusement parks like Kufri Fun World and Indira Tourist Park and wildlife spotting at Himalayan Nature Park.

blocks.text: Viceregal Lodge - Indian Institute of Advanced Studies

items: Viceregal Lodge - Indian Institute of Advanced Studies is a landmark destination of Shimla. It is of immense historical and political importance in Shimla.
The architecture of Viceregal Lodge is a sight to behold. It was built between 1880 and 1888 in the Jacobethan (Jacobean + Elizabethan) style by British architect Henry Irwin.
It's an observatory hill which has many beautiful gardens, houses, a Research Institute and opulent halls.
Christ Church is a popular spiritual destination to visit in Shimla. It is the second oldest Church in North India.
You will be amazed to see the beautiful neo-gothic style architecture. It has five stained-glass windows which represent Christian virtues.
It's a peaceful spot for self-retrospection and don't miss its silhouette. It's one of the most captured landmarks in Shimla.

items: Ice Skating in Shimla is a must not miss. This exciting adventure activity is enjoyed in an open-air rink which offers best views of majestic Himalayan Mountains.
