blocks.text: Travel Tips for fun-filled Shimla Trip
Here are some of the most useful tips to follow if you want to enjoy a memorable holiday in Shimla with your loved ones.

items: Best Time to Visit - Prefer Peak tourism season (summer and winter) to enjoy accessibility to all the famous places and adventure activities in Shimla.

What to Pack- Always pack weather appropriate clothes to enjoy the best of Shimla Tourism in comfort and style. You need to carry warm woolens, thermals, gloves, mufflers and sturdy footwear in both summer and winter season as the temperature during these seasons are freezing. The nights get colder and even in day time, you will feel the need to wear light warm clothes. In high- altitude areas you can wear light breathable clothes as the sun rays will be strong. Carry sunscreen moisturizer and polarized sunglasses to enjoy sightseeing.

Cash- Carry enough cash to support small business as the shopkeepers may not have digital payment modes at remote locations. At popular bazaars and city areas you will get ATM facilities but in remote, high-altitude areas these facilities may not be available.

Plan in advance - Book your hotel and tickets in advance to enjoy Shimla holidays during peak season. Booking at the last minute will be frustrating and you may not get your desired hotel due to peak tourism season. So, it is best to book your tickets and hotel in advance.

Enjoy on Foot- If you don't have mobility issues and are comfortable to walk then explore some of the most popular places in Shimla like the Mall Road, Ridge, Bazaars by foot to experience the soul of Shimla. You can hire local buses, taxis or scooters to reach Kufri and Mashobra.
Be a responsible Tourist- Protect the natural beauty of Shimla. Don't use plastic as it is banned in Himachal. Don't litter anywhere. Use reusable bags to carry your stuff.
Emergency - Always carry emergency numbers of your tour operator and relevant people who you can approach during the time of emergency.
Licensed operator - Hire licensed operator to try adventure activities in Shimla. Check their ID proof for your safety.

Places to Visit in and Around Muktinath on your Trip

In 2025, Muktinath Dham witnessed a significant rise in tourist footfall. It welcomed around 539,872 domestic tourists and 138,664 were foreign tourists from around 72 countries.(Source: TravelandTourworld ). The place gained more popularity after PM Narendra Modi's visit. There are many beautiful places to visit in and around Muktinath Temple. Mentioned here are some of the best places to visit in and around Muktinath Dham, covered in our itineraries. You can also customise your Muktinath Tour package and add many places of your choice-

rows: Muktinath Temple is a central pilgrimage site for Hindu and Buddhist devotees. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Mukti in Sanskrit means salvation and Nath means Lord. Hence, Muktinath means- God of Salvation. Devotees from all over the world visit Muktinath to attain salvation.

Jwala Devi Temple is a must visit place after visiting Muktinath. It is dedicated to the goddess of fire. The temple is very famous for its Eternal flame which has been burning continuously for decades naturally.

Mukti Dhara is a 108 holy water spout located behind the temple of Muktinath. Devotees who take holy dip in these 108 water spouts attain spiritual purification and salvation from the cycle of birth and death.

Located at the North side of Muktinath Temple, one must visit Mharme Lhakhang Gompa which is also known as Narsingh Gompa (Temple of 1000 lamps). The Gompa is dedicated to Guru Rinpoche (Padmasambhava).
At the left of the entrance gate of Muktinath Temple lies the sacred monastery of Sangdo. It's an important sacred site for Buddhist worship and meditation.

Situated in central Nepal at an elevation of around 3700 meters, Ranipauwa Village is the main resting point for pilgrims who are visiting Muktinath Dham and trekkers who are crossing Thorong-La Pass. This village has many guesthouses, hotels, restaurants, shops, souvenir shops for pilgrims and trekkers.

Don't miss this historic Tibetan village in the Mustang district of Nepal. It is located in the valley of Kali Gandaki River. It is one of the oldest Himalayan villages. You will get the chance to understand authentic Tibetan culture and breathtaking views of Nilgiri and Tilicho peaks.

Located in the Myagdi District of Nepal's Annapurna region, at an elevation of about 1,200 meters, Tatopani Hot springs is one of the best places to visit around Muktinath Dham. These geothermal hot springs are very popular for their medicinal properties. The mineral rich water offers nourishment to the muscles. Here you will also witness beautiful Himalayan landscapes, terraced slopes, forests, and waterfalls.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Muktinath Temple
Some of the best things to do in and around Muktinath Dham for spiritual upliftment and to rejuvenate your soul are-
Blessings of lord Vishnu and Guru Rinpoche at Muktinath

items: Get the divine blessings of lord Vishnu at Muktinath Dham. Lord Vishnu hare is known as Mukti Narayan. Devotees from all over the world visit here to pay respects to Lord Vishnu. It is believed that Lord Vishnu has taken refuge and liberation here in the form of Shaligram stone.

It is also a prominent pilgrimage site for Buddhists also as this place is one of the 24 holy tantric sites where Guru Rinpoche is believed to have meditated. For Buddhist devotees, Muktinath Temple is known as Chumming Gyasta or Hundred waters.

blocks.text: Take Holy Dip in Mukti Dhara

items: Located behind the Muktinath Temple are 108 water spouts known as Mukti Dhara. As the name suggests, Mukti Dhara refers to the water of Salvation.
If any devotees take holy dip in these 108 water spouts, he/she is believed to attain spiritual salvation and freedom from the cycle of Birth and death.
Pay your respects and bow down to the revered eternal flame at Jwala Devi Temple. The temple of Jwala Devi is located at the temple complex of the sacred Muktinath Dham.
The eternal flame at Jwala Devi Temple has been burning since time unknown, blessing the pilgrims with divine energy and spiritual upliftment.
If you are visiting Muktinath then you must also try the Annapurna Circuit trek. It is one of the most sought-after trekking trails for adventurers, spiritually inclined travellers and nature lovers.
This route starts from Nayapul or Besisahar and heads towards Thorong Phedi. After that trekkers prepare to cross the highest point known as Thorong La Pass.

items: In Muktinath, you can enjoy the local and traditional cuisines like Dal Bhat, Momos, Yak butter tea, Thukpa, Yak Meat and Cheese and Tibetan Bread.
These cuisines will introduce you to the Nepali and Himalayan culinary traditions.

Some of the best souvenirs and items to buy in and around Muktinath Dham are Shaligram stones, Tibetan prayer flags, metal statues, Tibetan Thangka Paintings, Rudraksha Beads, jewelry, Handmade Woolen products of Yak or sheep wool.
These items will introduce you to the local artistic traditions of Nepal.

blocks.text: Travel Tips to Make Your Pilgrimage Trip to Muktinath Memorable
Follow these helpful travel tips to make your Muktinath Pilgrimage Tour memorable-

items: Plan your Visit - Always plan your visit to the revered Muktinath Dham during the peak tourist season (Sep-November) and March to May. During these months, the temperature will be pleasant for sightseeing and trekking. You will also enjoy local festivals like Dashain and Tihar. Book your accommodations in advance to make your Muktinath Tour memorable as if you delay your bookings, you may not get your desired hotel in advance.

Dress Modestly- While visiting the sacred Muktinath Dham and other temples, dress modestly. Respect the culture and traditions of the sacred sites. Don't wear revealing clothes. Cover your head, knees and shoulders properly.

Stay hydrated and acclimatize gradually - In high-altitude regions like Muktinath, you must stay hydrated for smooth Darshan. It is very essential for your physical fitness during the tour. Also, don't try to rush and trek the entire route in one go. Acclimatize gradually to high altitude, give your body enough time to adjust to avoid altitude sickness.
Carry Cash - carry enough cash while buying souvenirs from small vendors and shopkeepers. You may not find any option for digital payment and ATMs might not function properly.

Do not go alone- If you are a first-time traveller do not try to take unusual routes as you may get lost in high-altitude regions. Always follow your tour guide and keep emergency contact numbers to approach the right person for help.
Responsible Tourist -As a tourist, it is our responsibility to keep the Himalayan sites serene and clean. Do not litter, carry eco-friendly items and avoid the use of plastic.

blocks.text: Q-1: How many pilgrims can a helicopter carry for the Muktinath Tour?

Ans: The helicopter is designed to accommodate only five to six people at a time to Muktinath. It will be really expensive if you are planning to do the whole helicopter tour for just 2 or 3 people but you can minimize the cost by choosing your journey with 5 to 6 people to divide the expenditure evenly.
Q-2: What are the best months to plan a Muktinath Tour?
Ans: The months of March, April, May, June, September, October and November are the only times in the entire year when the skies are clear and the weather is pleasant for you to visit this Dham.
Q-3: Are there any permits required to do the Muktinath Dham Tour?

Ans: The temple lies within the trekking and conservation zone of Nepal and for this purpose 2 main permits are required which are - Annapurna Conservation Area Project Permit or ACAP and the other one is Trekker's Information Management System Permit or TIMS. Entering this zone without these two permits is considered an offence and you will not be allowed to enter this region without it. If you avail a package all the permits' requirements will be taken care of.
Q-4: Is It Possible to Visit Pokhara Instead of Making My Way Back to Kathmandu?

Ans: Yes, it is possible for you to make your way to Pokhara and spend a few days there as well before heading back to Kathmandu since it falls en route to the helicopter journey. From Pokhara you can make your way back to Kathmandu easily via a tourist bus, cab or taxi. By road the journey takes around 7.5 hours.
Q-5: Why do people visit Muktinath Dham?

Ans: People generally visit Muktinath Dham as it holds immense significance in the lives of devout Hindus. Here Vishnu Ji is worshipped as - Muktinath - or the god of salvation. People come here to take a holy bath under the chilled water flowing through the 108 spouts since it is believed that doing so will free them from all the sins that they have committed in their entire life. So, in short, visiting Muktinath is said to bring salvation to devout pilgrims.
Q-6: How much time will the helicopter take to complete Muktinath Dham Journey?

blocks.text: Sanchi, located in the state of Madhya Pradesh in India, is a significant historical and religious site renowned for its ancient Buddhist monuments and UNESCO World Heritage Site status. Sanchi tour packages offer visitors a chance to explore the rich history, architectural marvels, and spiritual ambiance of this fascinating destination.

Sanchi is primarily known for its Great Stupa, a massive hemispherical dome-shaped structure that is considered one of the oldest stone structures in India. Built to house the relics of Lord Buddha, the stupa is adorned with intricately carved gateways, known as Toranas, which depict scenes from the life of Buddha.

Apart from the Great Stupa, Sanchi is home to numerous other Buddhist structures and monasteries, such as the Ashoka Pillar, the Gupta Temple, and the Eastern Gateway. These architectural wonders showcase the mastery of ancient Indian craftsmanship and provide insights into the rich Buddhist heritage of the region.

Sanchi tour packages often include visits to nearby attractions like Udayagiri Caves, Vidisha, and the Archaeological Museum. The Udayagiri Caves feature elaborate rock-cut sculptures and caves that were once used as dwelling places for monks. Vidisha, located close to Sanchi, houses ancient temples, ruins, and the famous Heliodorus Pillar, which is of historical significance.

The Sanchi tour experience is enhanced by the serene and picturesque surroundings of the town. Visitors can enjoy peaceful walks amidst lush green gardens and soak in the tranquil atmosphere that pervades the area.

Sanchi tour packages provide a unique opportunity to delve into the ancient Buddhist heritage of India, explore remarkable architectural marvels, and experience a sense of spiritual tranquillity in a historically significant setting.

blocks.text: The Munnar Alleppey Tour Package offers a perfect blend of hill station charm and serene backwaters over four days.

Your journey begins with a scenic drive from Cochin to Munnar, a picturesque hill station known for its lush tea plantations, wildlife sanctuaries, and cool climate. After settling into your hotel, you can relax and enjoy the natural beauty of Munnar before embarking on a sightseeing tour the next day. Explore the stunning Rajamalai National Park, the picturesque Mattupetty, and the scenic Top Station, known for its vast tea plantations and breathtaking views.

On Day 3, you'll travel to the tranquil town of Alleppey, famous for its backwaters, houseboats, and picturesque landscapes. After a relaxing evening on a houseboat or in a hotel, enjoy a delicious breakfast before heading back to Cochin on Day 4 for your departure. This 4-day, 3-night tour ensures a memorable experience, combining Munnar's natural beauty with the serenity of Alleppey’s backwaters, leaving you with lasting memories of Kerala's finest landscapes.

On arrival at Ernakulam Railway Station/Cochin Airport you will be welcomed by our representative and he will take you transfer to Munnar (Approx 155KMs/ 5hrs). Munnar means “The three rivers” which are situated at the confluence of three mountain streams Nallathanni, Muthirapuzha (Kannimalayar), and Kundala. Munnar is an attractive hill station full of natural resources located at an altitude of 6000 ft from sea level; this hill station is the part of Idukki district. The temperature stays here between the range of 5 °C to 25 °C in winter, and 15 °C to 25 °C in summer. There are several hot plantations of tea, cardamom, coffee, and other spices, dark forests & wildlife sanctuaries.

At arrival to Munnar just check in to your hotel, Welcome drink would be offered after you get fresh at the comfort of your room. Rest of the time enjoy leisure at the hotel, you can enjoy the scenic beauty of Munnar also. Stay overnight at the hotel in Munnar.
Post breakfast, get ready to experience an amazing local sightseeing of Munnar, which includes the visit to Rajamalai National Park, Mattupetty, and Top Station.

Rajamalai National Park- this national park is also known by the name of Eravikulam National Park, it is situated in Idukki, which is the bordering district of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. You can see some of the rare animal species can be found here- you may see Elephant, Nilgiri Marten, Nilgiri Langur, small-clawed otter and a rare tiger or leopard and the Nilgiri wood pigeon etc.
Mattupetty- It is approx 15 KMs away from Munnar, this is an extremely picturesque hill station.

Top Station– is placed at the approx distance of 40KMS from Munnar, and a well-known spot for the highest tea plantation in India. Later on arrive back and check in to the hotel. Overnight stay at the hotel.

Just finish your breakfast, we’ll take you to Alleppey (190 KMs / 5 Hrs). Alleppey is a scenic and popular town for its marvellous backwaters, it will attract you by its natural appeal. Alleppey is also known for its Boat races, Beaches, Houseboats, Marine Products and Coir Industry. In evening return back to your hotel/houseboat and check in to relax overnight.

In the morning time enjoy your breakfast at hotel/ houseboat. Later check out from the houseboat/hotel and we’ll take you towards the Cochin airport (90 KMs /2 hrs) / Ernakulam Railway Station (60KMs/1 Hr 15Min Approx) for your onward journey. blocks.text: Egypt Tour Packages – Book Egypt Packages

Egypt is a place with varied geography located in North-Eastern part of Africa with Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea on its coasts and its vast history and eventful past, to make it an absorbing place to be on Tour Package. Egypt was the place to give birth to one of the oldest civilizations and memorials, ruins and relics of ancient and medieval times make it a paradise for those who are interested in history. Surrounded by desert on East and West and numerous temples, hieroglyphs, mummies and above all pyramids make Egypt a captivating place for travelers on Tour Package.

The Pyramids of Giza and Sphinx have attracted millions of people from around the globe since ages and even today are most sought after destination on Egypt Tour Package. In Giza one can see three pyramids each one of different King of Egypt and facing these pyramids is a massive architecture with cat like face known as Abu Al-Hol or Sphinx, carved out of single block of stone exemplifying the technique and skills of sculptors of that time. Pyramids of Giza and Sphinx is must visit places on Egypt Tour Package.

Close to Giza lies another huge attraction of Egypt, the Abu Simbel, one of the most recognized monuments in the country. These twin temples were originally built by Pharaoh Ramesses II and in 1960 were shifted 60 meters away on to a cliff to protect them, each block was reassembled exactly in the same way and with exact relation with the sun to maintain its charm and charisma. Sound and light shows organized every evening are not to miss attraction of this place on Egypt Travel Package.

Cairo is one of the oldest cities of the world and is full of interesting buildings, churches, mosques and markets built in ancient times. Some of the major historical attractions of this city are the Citadel, Khan Khalili Bazaar, Ibn Tulun Mosque is one of the largest mosques in the world and Al Azhar Mosque which houses world’s oldest university started in 970 AD. Strolling past the market places one can see many handmade items and things to purchase and can also see many interesting things like beautifully carved ancient gates and walls, this city is full of surprises for tourists and one shall devote ample time to explore this city on Egypt Holiday Package.

If one thinks that Egypt Tour Packages are all about history and ancient monuments than it is in correct as this country has natural splendors which are enchanting and enthralling for visitors. The Oasis of Siwa is one such place which is soothing and exciting in the lap of desert. One can swim, relax and enjoy fresh olives at this place, close to Libyan border this place is also famous due to the fact that Alexander the Great stayed here on his way to Oracle of Amun. A truly mesmerizing place and certainly deserves a visit on Egypt Holiday Packages.

There are many other must visit places and plethora of activities to do on Egypt Travel Packages as this country offers much more than one can expect and cover in one trip. Sailing in the river Nile, Temples of Karnak, visiting Valley of the Kings, Hurghada and many more, there is no dearth of tourist attractions in this country.

blocks.text: Explore the charm of Sri Lanka, a beautiful island in the Indian Ocean. See More

It is a wonderful destination for travelers and is famous worldwide for its rich culture, amazing wildlife, top beaches, and everything is surrounded by green landscapes. Sri Lanka is known as the ‘Land of Ancient Civilizations'. To fully experience this amazing place, visitors can see the kingdom of Ravana, where Sita was trapped, and the locations where battles took place.

Ramayana places in Sri Lanka are important not only for religious reasons, but they are also filled with natural beauty, ancient culture and history. This trip will cover the key destinations, such as Chilaw, famous for peaceful beaches, Sigiriya has ancient fortresses, Trincomalee is known for its temples, Nuwara Eliya is popular due to tea plantations and Colombo, popular for shopping and modern attractions. It is an 8-day Sri Lanka group tour package, including the best sightseeings, comfortable hotels, easy online booking and the best transportation options. Let's discover and make new memories.

items: Tour Name Sri Lanka Group Tour Packages
Destination Covered Colombo Airport → Chilaw → Sigiriya → Kandy → Nuwara Eliya → Ella Kataragama → Galle
Pickup Time Depend on your Flight Timing
Tour Benefits Best price & enjoyable travel guarantee
Covers beautiful sights in Sri Lanka like Chilaw, Sigiriya, Trincomalee, Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Ella, Kataragama, and Colombo.
The tour includes the best hotels, easy online booking and transportation options.
Our representative will welcome you at Colombo Airport.
We will travel to Sigiriya and stop at Chilaw to visit two important temples:
Manavari Temple: This is where Lord Rama placed the first lingam, known as the Ramalinga Shiva.
Munneswaram Temple: After killing Ravana in battle, Lord Rama prayed here to remove the curse of killing a Brahmin. Therefore, Lord Rama was advised to place four lingams to remove the curse.
Next, continue your journey to Sigiriya.
Check into the hotel. Enjoy dinner and stay overnight.
After breakfast at the hotel, visit Trincomalee to explore and learn about its important historical places and sacred sacred sites.
Go to Shankar Devi Temple, a Shakti Peetam built by King Ravana. The original temple was destroyed, but the statue is now worshiped in a nearby temple.
Visit Thirukoneswaram Temple, constructed by Rishi Agastya as per Lord Shiva’s guidance. This temple is also filled with interesting history.
Now, proceed to Kanniya Hot Wells, where it is believed that Ravan’s trishul (trident) created seven hot water springs during his mother’s funeral.
After visiting Trincomalee’s sacred places, return to Sigiriya for a relaxing evening. Then, stay overnight at your hotel and have dinner.
After breakfast, move towards the Sigiriya Rock Fortress, an important historical site in Sri Lanka.
Sigiriya is called the ’Eighth Wonder of the World’ and is popular for its palace.
The rock fortress is a part of the Ramayana and it is connected to the story of Ravana and SIta.
In Sigiriya, visitors can see the Cobra Hooded Cave has ancient drawings where Ravana kept Sita.
On the way to Kandy, visit an Ayurveda and Herbal Garden, popular for its healing benefits and it is connected to the story of Hanuman.
After your visit, check into your hotel in Kandy for a night stay.
Have your breakfast, and visit Sita Kotuwa, known as the spot where Ravana kept Sita captive.
Sita Kotuwa is a beautiful place surrounded by waterfalls and greenery, which is connected to the stories of the Ramayana.
In the afternoon, go back to Kandy to explore Sri Dalada Maligawa, a popular UNESCO spot with Buddha’s holy tooth relic.
In the evening, enjoy a dance event and thrilling fire-walking.
Stay overnight in Kandy and have dinner.
After breakfast, begin your day with the Kandy trip, where you can enjoy the beautiful views, green landscapes and visit craft centers.
On the way, travel to Nuwara Eliya and enjoy the scenic views.
Visit the Tea Gardens to see Sri Lanka’s popular tea plantations, learn the tea-making process, and taste fresh Ceylon tea.
Now, stop at Sri Baktha Hanuman Temple, dedicated to Lord Hanuman. It is believed that this is the place where he searched for Sita.
Next, enjoy Ramboda Falls, one of the tallest and beautiful waterfalls in Sri Lanka.
When you reach Nuwara Eliya, check into the hotel, enjoy dinner and stay overnight.
Go to Gayathri Peedam, where it is believed that Ravan’s son Meghanath got magical powers from Lord Shiva.
Travel to Amma Temple, the believed site of Sita’s captivity, you can see the river where she prayed and the rocks with Hanuman’s footprints. You can also visit Hakgala Botanical Gardens.
Go to Divurumpola, the place where Sita proved her purity through Agni Pariksha.
Visit Ella, a village connected to Ramayana history, and explore Ravana Ella Cave and Ravana Falls, where Sita used to bathe in a pool.
Explore Kataragama Temple, dedicated to Lord Karthikeya Subramaniam, who protected Rama in the battle to defeat Ravana.
Next day, start the morning with a Pooja at Kataragama Temple, then enjoy breakfast.
Travel to Colombo in two famous places- Rumassala Mountain, where it is believed that Lord Hanuman dropped part of the Sanjeevani Mountain, popular for its healing benefits.
Now, visit Panchamuga Anjaneyar Temple in Sri Lanka, there is a chariot dedicated to Lord Hanuman, and an annual chariot festival is also celebrated here.
Next proceed to Kelaniya Temple, where Vibhishana was made King of Lanka. The temple has paintings of his crowning and a statue dedicated to him.
Stay overnight in Colombo and have dinner.

blocks.text: The Indian Himalayas are a goldmine for exquisite scenic beauty. No matter which road you take or where you head to, the wonderful Himalayan ranges will never fail to fascinate. Manali is one such Himalayan hamlet. Situated on the banks of the ancient Beas River, Manali is a favourite among travel lovers. Blessed with a mystic charm and adorned with fun sightseeing locations, it has rightfully been called the queen of hills. The peaceful environment, surrounded by historical wonders and adventure experiences, makes a tour in Manali truly memorable. Manali is a hill station that can be easily reached throughout the year. From beating the scorching summer heat to having some fun in the snow, a wholesome time is guaranteed.

Over time, the beauty and magical realm of Manali has opened doors to all sorts of tourists. With a plethora of accommodation and sightseeing options, people from all over the world are making their way to this wonderful Himalayan town. It has also turned into a favourite among people on their honeymoon. Honeymoon goers from across the globe make their way to this peaceful little hill town to get some much-needed break. Every newly married couple wishes to start off their married life on a happy and a tension free note. What better way of doing that than heading to one of the most romantic places in India? Manali honeymoon packages have become an ideal way of exploring the heritage town.

With lush greenery all around, rolling green hills and awesome adventures in every corner, a honeymoon in Manali feels like a dream come true. Create memories by staying in quirky hotels, checking out interesting sightseeing locations, going on hiking excursions, parasailing, paragliding and more. A world of adventures and memories awaits. Manali also represents a combination of spirituality and adventure. Couples can get blessings at Hidimba Devi Temple as well as Siyali Mahadev Mandir. Shopping at the Manali Mall Road is a different experience in itself. Trying out delicious local meals and cuisines will bind the whole experience of a happy and memorable honeymoon together.

Why look for a relaxing peaceful solitude elsewhere when you have the wonders of Manali? A place where bonfire nights meet calming scenic vistas and allows couples to bond stronger together. Over time this humble little town has grown into a full-fledged tourist town with several branches one could explore. Be it going for a drive till the other side of Atal Tunnel in Sissu, going for a hot water dip at the Vashishth spring or simply chilling riverside at some cafe or hotel, this place has it all. No matter which time of the year you decide to go, Manali will welcome everyone with open arms and lots of love. After all, nature is the cure for everything and Manali is a blessing when it comes to feeling closer to the wilderness. The next time you are wondering where to go for a honeymoon, make sure Manali makes the list.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is included in the Northeast India travel package?

Ans. Our Northeast India travel package provides tourists with accommodation, food, and local transport. In addition, you’ll be provided with an English-speaking tour guide so that you won’t have trouble with the local languages there. We’ve also included multiple sightseeing locations in your itinerary.
Q2. What should I pack for the Northeast India tour?

Ans. The weather in the northeastern region of India is cold, even in summer. Therefore, pack warm woollen clothes for this journey. Also, carry an umbrella and a raincoat. Good, comfortable walking shoes are also a must.
Q3. What’s the best time to visit Northeast India?

Ans. The best time to visit northeast India is from October to April. The weather is very delightful in these months, and therefore it’s a good time for sightseeing and other activities. If you’re looking for a cultural experience, then visit Kohima in December when the Hornbill Festival is celebrated.
Q4. Is the Northeast India tour suitable for senior citizens?
Ans. Yes, the tour is safe and suitable for senior citizens. However, there might be some trekking involved in the Dzuleke and Benreu areas, so be prepared for that.
Q5. What kind of accommodation is provided in my Northeastern tour?
Ans. You can expect heritage homestays, boutique guesthouses, eco-lodges, and mid-range hotels on your Northeastern tour.

blocks.text: Embark on a 3 day tour to Assam and let the surreal breezes of Northeast India embrace you. Capture the beauty of Guwahati with our carefully curated package including safe travels, cozy hotel stay, delicious meals and guided tours. Guwahati is the largest city in Assam located on the banks of Brahmaputra river.

Visit the key attractions and sacred temples in Guwahati with us. Book the best package to Guwahati now and prepare for an extraordinary trip full of spiritual experiences as well as thrilling exploration.

items: Visit Kalakshetra and get familiar with Assamese culture, history and traditions.
Explore the vibrant markets Fancy Bazaar and Handicraft market for local traditional items.
Seek Darshan at one of the holiest Shakti Peethas, Kamakhya temple.
Offer prayers at other temples located on Nilachal hill.
Visit Umananda temple located on the peacock island.
Enjoy a scenic sunset cruise on river Brahmaputra.
Savor Assamese cuisine by indulging in the traditional dishes like Pitha and Masor Tenga.

blocks.text: Once you arrive at Guwahati Airport or Railway station, you will be welcomed and assisted to your pre-booked hotel by one of our representatives. Once you are settled, get ready to explore the key attractions of Guwahati.

The first stop will be Kalakshetra where you will have an opportunity to get familiar with Assamese culture, traditions and history at this cultural center where the essence of Assam is depicted in a beautiful way.

The next stop will be Fancy Bazaar and Handicraft market where you can take a stroll through the Bazaar and explore local handicrafts, vibrant fabrics and traditional items from these popular Assam markets.
After exploring the markets, return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Guwahati.
Day 2 : Guwahati city and Temple tour
Begin your day early as the whole day is packed with exploration and sightseeing.

The first stop will be the sacred Kamakhya temple situated on Nilachal Hill, known as one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. It is recommended to obtain a VIP pass (₹501 per person) from the temple counter to avoid long queues.
You can also visit and offer prayers to the following temples lies close to Kamakhya Temple at Nilachal Hill:
Dhumavati Temple, Tripureswari Temple, Maa Tara Temple, Maa Kali Temple, Maa Chhinnamasta Temple, Maa Bagala Temple, Maa Bhubaneswari Temple and Maa Banadurga Temple.
You can customize the rest of the day according to your preference. You can choose from the given recommendations:

items: 3. Assam State Zoo or Botanical Garden

blocks.text: After completing the temple visit, you will get a ferry ride arranged by us to Umananda temple which is situated on the smallest island on the earth known as Peacock Island.
Later on, you can enjoy the River Cruise on the Brahmaputra River (charges applicable).
After a blissful day of sightseeing, you will return to your hotel to stay for the night.

items: In order to offer a special ritual or puja at Kamakhya temple, inform us a day prior so that we can make the necessary arrangements.
Every year during the period of Ambubachi, the Kamakhya temple remains closed i.e from 22 June - 25 June.

When the temple reopens, a big ceremony named Ambubachi Mela is held. The Mela goes on for a week making the temple premises and local streets extremely crowded. Therefore, plan your trip accordingly.

blocks.text: Ans. Guwahati is well connected to other cities by air, rail and road. Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport operates flights to and from all major cities, Guwahati Railway Station is also linked to other cities, and National Highways are accessible too by road.
Q2. How many days are required for a trip to Guwahati?
Ans. A 2-3 day trip is ideal to explore the key attractions and sacred temples of Guwahati.
Q3. What kind of food can I expect in Guwahati?
Ans. Traditional dishes like Masor Tenga (tangy fish curry), Pitha (rice cakes), and thali are popular in Guwahati. Assamese cuisine is flavorful and unique that makes it a must try.
Q4. What are the famous temples in Guwahati?
Ans. Kamakhya temple, Umananda temple, Navagraha temple, Vashishta temple and Balaji temple are some of the most famous temples in Guwahati.
Q5. Is Guwahati safe for tourists?
Ans. Yes, Guwahati is a safe tourist destination. However, tourists must stay alert in crowded places and take care of their belongings to avoid any unpleasant incident.
Q6. What adventure activities are there in Guwahati?
Ans. You can engage in activities like river rafting on Brahmaputra, trekking to temples on Nilachal Hill, and wildlife safari.

The Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas , draws pilgrims from across the country, while the famous Bhasma Aarti at 4:00 AM remains one of the most distinctive temple rituals in India.

blocks.text: Considered as a Moksh-puri (salvation place), Ujjain is full of spiritual glory, ancient historical treasures, and captivating architecture. Whether you want to experience its rich cultural heritage or discover your spiritual connection with the divine, Ujjain has it all. Our Ujjain travel package picks all the must-see and the to-do activities to give you an all-round, full-fledged experience!
There are several destination here that should be on your itinerary. Here's the list:

This temple is glorified for having a strong divine presence. And therefore, no wonder, it is probably the most famous destination in the city and that's why many Ujjain tour packages include a trip to this famous temple. This temple is also one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. And one thing that makes it stand out is the fact that Aarti here is performed with sacred ash itself, known as Bhasma Aarti!

Darshan timings: 4:00 AM to 11:00 PM daily. Bhasma Aarti at 4 AM requires advance booking at shrimahakaleshwar.com. The Mahakal Lok corridor — a 900-metre walkway with Shiva sculptures along Rudra Sagar lake — is part of the same complex and free to visit.

Ram Ghat is a pious bathing Ghat in the city. Devotees from all over India come here to take their holy dips, especially during Simhastha Mela and Kumbh Mela. It is situated on the banks of Shipra River and is a sight to behold during the evening Aartis. The evening Aarti at Ram Ghat takes place daily at sunset — no booking required, free to attend.

As the name suggests, this temple is dedicated to Kaal Bhairav — a highly fierce form of Lord Shiva. He is also considered to be the guardian deity of the city of Ujjain. And thus, a visit to this temple is a must and should definitely be on your Ujjain holiday package. This temple is famous for its vibrant atmosphere and unique rituals like the traditional offering of liquor (sharaab) to Kaal Bhairav — this is the only temple in India where such an offering is part of the official temple ritual

You are in for a treat when you visit this Lord Ganesha temple. The temple is remarkably beautiful and has a superior architecture. It is widely believed that worshipping Lord Ganesha here can remove all obstacles from your life.

This popular astronomical observatory was built by the famous astronomer-king Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur, who also built similar observatories at Delhi, Jaipur, Mathura, and Varanasi. It was specially designed to make astrological calculations and study celestial bodies. What once served as the astronomical observatory, is now a popular tourist spot of the city — making almost on every Ujjain travel package. Also known as the Jantar Mantar, tourists flock here to see this 17th century gem for its notable collection of instruments (such as Sun dial).

This Ashram is famous as the place where Lord Krishna and Balram received education from his guru Sandipani. Devotees come here to find a peaceful place for meditation and inner reflection. Besides the serene atmosphere, people love to see the ancient stone idols and the ashram ruins.

This one surely needs to be on itinerary of the history buffs. This fort, although now in complete ruins, once served as the powerful shield to protect the city from neighbouring kingdoms. Historical enthusiasts just love this age-old structure for its strategic importance. Tourists also enjoy the surrounding views from here and make it a part of their Ujjain travel package.

This temple is one of the Shakti Peethas and holds a special importance in the hearts of Aadi Shakti devotees. The temple is dedicated to Goddess Harsiddhi and she is believed to grant her followers with prosperity and strength. The entire temple complex provides a very peaceful, serene environment. Also, during the Navaratri festival, the temple brims with cheer and liveliness. During Navratri (Oct 2026 — exact dates per Hindu calendar), the temple hosts special puja sessions and is illuminated throughout the night. This is the most crowded but also the most vibrant time to visit.

The Mahakal Lok is a 900-metre open corridor connecting the main gate to the Mahakaleshwar temple entrance. Inaugurated in October 2022, it features hand-carved sandstone pillars, murals depicting stories from Shiv Purana, and a landscaped walkway along Rudra Sagar lake. Entry is free. Best visited early morning (before 8 AM) or after 7 PM when the pathway is illuminated.
To make the most out of your Ujjain holiday trip, make sure you include the following activities in your plan:

items: Take a Dip in the Shipra River: This is one of the most sacred things that you can do in Ujjain and it's often a part of an Ujjain travel package. It is a widely held belief that bathing at the Ghat absolves your sins and provides spiritual growth. Pilgrims can be found offering D iyas along the riverbank in the morning and evening.

Attend the Bhasma Aarti: The distinct ritual of Bhasma Aarti (Aarti performed with real sacred ash) is performed only at the Mahakaleshwar Temple. Bhasma Aarti happens daily at 4 AM — advance booking at shrimahakaleshwar.com is mandatory as seats are limited.

Visit Temples: Ujjain is home to various temples and visiting them is a must for any Ujjain tour. Some notable mentions are Kaal Bhairav Temple, Chintaman Ganesh Temple, Harsiddhi Temple, Mangalnath Temple etc.
Take a Boat Ride on the Shipra River : The boating experience is especially beautiful during sunrise and sunset.

Shop in the Local Markets: You can buy anything from local handicrafts to traditional clothes to souvenirs here. The markets also sell prasad and other religious items. Markets near Ram Ghat and Mahakaleshwar Temple are the most vibrant and popular ones.
Explore Historical Sites : Ujjain houses a number of ancient monuments, archaeological sites, and ruins. Noteworthy mentions are Ujjain Fort, Siddhavat, and Bade Ganeshji Ka Mandir.

Ujjain is about 55 kilometres away from the airport. After reaching the airport, you can either hire a taxi/cab or use the local transport like bus. It takes about 1.5 hours by road from there on. Bhasma Aarti booking: Book at shrimahakaleshwar.com. For regular days, slots open 1 week ahead. For Maha Shivaratri (15 Feb 2026) and Shravan month, book months in advance. Offline counter seats exist but are not guaranteed.
Arrive by 3:30 AM for Bhasma Aarti: The aarti starts exactly at 4 AM. Latecomers are not permitted entry. Keep your booking confirmation and ID ready at the gate.

Dress code at Mahakaleshwar: Men entering Garbhagriha must wear dhoti — no kurta, no pants allowed inside. Women must wear saree. Dhoti available for rent near the entrance for approximately ₹50. Western clothing will be turned away.
Monday crowds: Every Monday, general queue at Mahakaleshwar can reach 4–8 hours. If your visit falls on a Monday, book Sheeghra Darshan or arrive before 6 AM.

Cash at Ujjain: ATMs are available within 500 metres of Mahakaleshwar. Withdraw before entering the temple lanes — the alleys get extremely congested during peak hours and ATM access becomes difficult.

Omkareshwar — plan a full day: Omkareshwar is 130 km from Ujjain (2.5–3 hours each way). Darshan queue there can take 2–4 hours. Do not plan Ujjain and Omkareshwar on the same day — it makes both rushed. Our 4-day packages allocate a dedicated day for Omkareshwar.
Summer heat: April–June temperatures in Ujjain reach 42–45°C. Plan all temple visits between 5–9 AM and after 6 PM. Carry water and ORS sachets.
Photography: Photography is prohibited inside Mahakaleshwar sanctum and during Bhasma Aarti. Allowed in outer areas and Mahakal Lok corridor.

blocks.text: Force Majeure: Temple closure, government restriction, or natural disruption — full rescheduling or credit offered. Bhasma Aarti tickets follow the temple trust's own refund policy (typically non-refundable). Confirm on shrimahakaleshwar.com at booking time.
Q1: Is Ujjain safe for tourists?

Ans. Yes, Ujjain is generally a safe tourist spot. The city has a calm vibe with a strong religious background. Locals are used to tourists. Nonetheless, exercise caution and be mindful of your belongings and follow safety protocols.
Q2: Is there a dress code for temples in Ujjain?

Ans. It is crucial to dress modestly while visiting temples as Ujjain is a deeply religious city. For both men and women, it's recommended to cover shoulders and knees. Many temples may have their own dress code so do your research before visiting a temple.

For Bhasma Aarti specifically: men must wear dhoti (no upper garment for Garbhagriha entry); women must wear saree. This is strictly enforced at Mahakaleshwar. Dhoti rental available near temple entrance for approx. ₹50.
Q3: Is Ujjain good for solo travellers?

Ans. Yes, Ujjain is good for solo travellers. The serene environments of the city are often seen as a conducive environment by tourists for introspection and personal reflection. Also, being a solo traveller, you can explore historical sites, temples, markets etc. at your own pace.
Q4: How long should I stay in Ujjain?
Ans. 2–3 days covers Ujjain city comfortably. To add Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga (130 km away), budget 4 days minimum. For Ujjain + Omkareshwar + Maheshwar + Mandu, a 5–7 day tour is ideal.
Q5: What are some local foods that I should try?

Ans. The Madhya Pradesh local cuisine offers a variety of delicious dishes such as, Dal Bafla, Poha, Bhutte Ka Kees, and sweets like jalebi and Malpua. Ujjain near the temple zone is fully vegetarian — non-veg food is not available within the temple precinct area.
Q6: How do I book the Bhasma Aarti at Mahakaleshwar in 2026?

Ans. Visit shrimahakaleshwar.com to register online. Select your date, fill in personal details, and upload a valid ID proof. Pay the fee online and collect your confirmation. For Maha Shivaratri (15 Feb 2026), Shravan month, and Mondays, book well in advance — slots fill fast. Our team handles this booking for guests on 3-day and longer packages.
Q7: What is the Bhasma Aarti timing and what makes it special?

Ans. Bhasma Aarti begins daily at 4:00 AM and ends around 6:00 AM at Mahakaleshwar Temple. It is the only ritual in India where Lord Shiva is worshipped with sacred ash (bhasma) as the primary offering. The ritual is conducted before sunrise in a setting that has continued uninterrupted for centuries. Advance booking is mandatory — walk-in entry is not permitted.
Q8: What is the cost of an Ujjain tour package from Delhi in 2026?

Ans. The 8-day Best of Madhya Pradesh tour from Delhi starts at ₹32,500 per person (twin sharing), covering Delhi–Bhopal–Ujjain–Indore–Mandu. For Ujjain-only packages starting from Indore, the 2-day option begins at ₹6,250. Contact our team for a quote based on your dates and group size.
Q9: What is included in the Ujjain tour package?

Ans. All packages include accommodation (twin sharing, 3-star hotels), daily breakfast and dinner (vegetarian), private AC vehicle for all transfers, guided sightseeing, and GST. Bhasma Aarti booking coordination is included in 3-day and longer packages. Airfare, lunch, personal expenses, and temple ticket fees are not included.
Q10: Is there any entry fee at Mahakaleshwar temple?

Ans. General darshan is free — no entry fee. Bhasma Aarti attendance requires a paid ticket (fees vary by category — check shrimahakaleshwar.com for current rates). VIP Darshan and Sheeghra Darshan also have separate fees payable at the official portal or counter.
Q11: What documents are needed to visit Mahakaleshwar?

Ans. General darshan needs no documents. For Bhasma Aarti and VIP darshan, carry a government-issued photo ID matching your booking name — Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, or passport. Foreign nationals must carry their passport.
Q12: Is Ujjain suitable for senior citizens?

Ans. Yes. The Mahakaleshwar complex has wide pathways and the main darshan hall is accessible. However, general queue on Mondays and during Shivaratri can involve 4–8 hours of standing — we strongly recommend Sheeghra or VIP darshan for senior travellers. Ram Ghat, Mahakal Lok, and Kaal Bhairav are all walkable without steps. Ground-floor rooms arranged on request.
Q13: Can I customize the Ujjain tour to add Indore or Bhopal?

Ans. Yes — all packages are fully customizable. Common additions: Indore (55 km, street food + Rajwada Palace), Bhopal (190 km, Bhimbetka rock shelters + Sanchi Stupa), Maheshwar and Mandu (included in our 4-day packages). Share your interests when enquiring and we build the itinerary accordingly.
Q14: What is the best time to visit Ujjain in 2026?

Ans. October to March is the best season — pleasant weather (8°C–28°C), Kartik Mela, and Maha Shivaratri. Maha Shivaratri 2026 falls on 15 February (Sunday) — the biggest Shiva festival at Mahakaleshwar, but book accommodation and Bhasma Aarti slot at least 3 months ahead. Avoid April–June (45°C heat). Shravan (Jul–Aug) is spiritually significant but very crowded.
Q15: What vehicle is used for the Ujjain packages?

Ans. All packages use Ministry of Tourism approved private AC vehicles — Innova Crysta for up to 4 passengers, Tempo Traveller for groups of 5–8. All toll, parking, driver allowance, and fuel are included in the package price.
Q16: What is the cancellation policy?

Ans. Cancellations 60+ days before departure: 10% charge. 45–59 days: 25%. 30–44 days: 40%. 15–29 days: 60%. 8–14 days: 80%. 0–7 days: 100% non-refundable. Force majeure events qualify for rescheduling or credit. Bhasma Aarti tickets follow the temple trust's own refund policy — confirm at shrimahakaleshwar.com at booking time.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Varanasi from Chennai

The best time to visit Varanasi is hands down in the winter season ( October to March ). The weather in this window is delightfully pleasant, letting you enjoy sightseeing comfortably. The cool weather and with little to no chance of rain, further make it easier to cover your temple tours.

Also, we advise against going on Kashi trip from Chennai in the summer (April to June) and monsoon (July to September). In the former season, it's quite hot where the temperature crosses 40 degrees Celsius. And in the latter, your experience gets marred by frequent rains and road blockages.
How to Reach Varanasi from Chennai?
You can reach Varanasi by a variety of means . Here's a travel guide to Varanasi from Chennai:

There are direct flights from Chennai to Varanasi. Simply, take a plane from the Chennai International Airport (MAA) and land in Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport (VNS) in Varanasi. The whole journey can be covered in under 2.5 hours. Airlines like IndiGo, Air India, SpiceJet, ad others cover this route.

You can also opt for our Chennai to Varanasi train package. Take a train from the Chennai Central and get off at Varanasi Junction/Banaras Railway Station. Regular trains are available for this route, such as Ganga Kaveri Express, Saptagiri Express, and more. The whole ride takes around 36 hours and it's an economic way to reach Varanasi.

You can also visit Varanasi from Chennai by road. The two cities are located about 1,700 km apart and this is perfect for those who love long road trips. You can either hire a cab or go in your private vehicle.
Route Map from Chennai to Varanasi
The total distance between Chennai and Varanasi is 1,950 km. You can take your private vehicle to cover this journey. Here's the Chennai to Varanasi route map:
Chennai → Nellore → Ongole → Vijayawada → Nagpur → Jabalpur → Varanasi

In all My Quick Trippers's packages, your travel logistics will be completely handled by us - ranging from meals to hotels to transport. You can also book our Varanasi tour package with flight from Chennai where we'll also take care of your plane tickets and smooth transfer from the airport.
You can also go for our other advanced packages, such as Varanasi temple tour (INR 9,800) or the Allahabad Varanasi tour (INR 12,500). Have a look below at our packages and see what suits you best!
Top Places to Visit in Varanasi
Varanasi is home to a lot many interesting places - spiritual and historical both. Here are some places that must be a part of your Varanasi family holiday package from Chennai:

items: Evening Ganga Aarti : This is the star attraction of any Banaras tour package from Chennai! Watch the grand spectacle as the surroundings are lit by lamps while the divine chants are echoed in the background.
Subah-e-Banaras : The city offers cultural program in the morning. You can enjoy the classical music & yoga at Assi Ghat and feel the real essence of Varanasi up close.
Boat Ride on the Ganges : The Ganga river boat ride must be added to your Chennai to Varanasi tour itinerary. Capture the serene and spiritual aura of the place, especially at sunrise.

Temple Trips : Varanasi is called the "City of Temples" for a reason. You can visit here plenty of temples beyond just the usual Kashi Vishwanath Temple tour. Some popular temples here include Sankat Mochan Hanuman, Annapurna Devi, and Kaal Bhairav.

Shopping : You got to visit the local markets like Godowlia and Vishwanath Gali . You'll find a lot of Varanasi specialities there. While you're there, do look for Banarasi Silk Sarees , brass idols, and wooden toys. You can also shop for religious souvenirs such as Rudraksha Malas and idols.

Try Local Dishes: Varanasi is famous for so many things, and food is one of them. While on your trip, do relish Kachori-Sabzi, Banarasi Paan, Malaiyyo (a winter dessert), and everybody's favourite Lassi.

blocks.text: Here are some travel tips that might come in handy on your Varanasi tours from Tamil Nadu:

items: When visiting temples, make sure you wear modest clothes. Always keep your knees and arms covered. Traditional attire works best in this city.
You'll have to do walking on the Ghats. Therefore, keep light but sturdy footwear handy.
While you're at the cremation Ghats, avoid clicking pictures.
If you're going to local markets, you'll be buying from local vendors who might not accept cards. Therefore, always carry cash with you on such trips.
If you want to attend the Ganga Aarti, always reach the Ghats an hour earlier in order to secure a good spot.

blocks.text: Somnath is the unofficial religious city of India – housing the greats like Jyotirlinga, the confluence of three holy rivers, places where the Gods left their body for heavenly abodes…and much more! You haven’t seen the real spirituality until you go on a Somnath trip. And there’s more! Witness the epic carved gates giving a peek directly into ancient India. The history associated with this place is truly soul-stirring! Many Somnath tour packages include sites that are a blend of spirituality, history, and natural beauty, because really, Somnath has all three! So come here and experience the journey of your lifetime.

items: Best Places to See on the Somnath Tour
Top Things to Do on the Somnath Trip

blocks.text: Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Somnath Tour Packages?

Somnath is a sacred jewel of Gujarat and is venerated as one of the most religious locations in India. Renowned for having some of the greatest pilgrim sites, the city attracts tourists from all across the globe. The holy city has a lot to offer and proper planning is required to make the most out of your Somnath trip. And this is exactly where we come in! We work hard, so you can enjoy without worrying about the little…and big things.

With My Quick Trippers, you can be assured of getting top class services like pre-booked hotel, timely meals, proper local transports between the hotel & the tour locations, and sightseeing. Our expert-created tour itineraries are perfect to see the best of the best of Somnath. So why wait? Book your Somnath travel package today!

blocks.text: The best time to go on a Somnath trip is during winter – from October to March. The weather during this time is pleasant (10°C to 25°C) with clear skies and is therefore ideal for sightseeing, pilgrimage, and exploring other attractions like beaches.

Moreover, if you come during this period, you get to enjoy Mahashivratri (February/March) festival which is celebrated here with great zeal and fervour. Also, Kartik Purnima (November) also falls in this window and warrants a visit as it’s a highly significant religious day, celebrated with special events and prayers.
In addition, beach visits are a breeze during the winter season.
Best Places to See on the Somnath Tour

Somnath is a perfect place where you can enjoy natural, serene locations as well as see age-old remarkable architecture. And on top of that, there are some highly significant temples that you must visit, at least once in your life. To enjoy all aspects of the city, make sure to add the following to your Somnath trip packages:

It goes without saying that you should add Somnath Temple to your Somnath tour package! Moreover, this temple is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva , and therefore, must be visited on a Somnath trip.

The very first thing that will capture your attention will be the temple’s beautiful architecture. What you see here is a Chalukya-style architecture , dating back to the 11th century. The whole form of the temple is in ‘Kailash Mahameru Prasad’, showcasing the excellent skills of the masons of that era! Another tourist-favourite thing about this magnificent monument is the intricate designs carved on the temple.

And you have to see the evening Aarti! It is organised with a grand Light and Sound Show, keeping the entertainment of the visitors in mind. Moreover, since the temple is located at the seaside, you can soak in the mesmerizing views of the Arabian Sea, which are especially gorgeous at nighttime.

As the name implies, this is the confluence point for three rivers - Hiran, Kapila, and Saraswati. This is a highly tranquil area with picturesque views and therefore it is recommended to include it in your Somnath holiday packages. Moreover, this is also a site of pilgrimage, so you’ll often see people taking holy dips in hopes of cleansing their sins. Tourists also wander off to nearby ghats as they are equally serene and perfect for a relaxing stroll.

This place is incredibly important for all the Lord Krishna bhakts because as per the legends this was where he was mistakenly shot and left his earthly body. What you find here is a serene temple of Lord Krishna with a beautiful idol of him shown in a reclining pose – symbolizing the event. There’s also a marker here that points to the exact spot where he was hit by the arrow. You’ll also find many scenes from his life, adding to the wholesome experience of exploring God’s life.

This cave is famous for the Gufa the Pandavas resided during their exile. It’s also believed that Pandavas worshiped Lord Shiva here to seek his blessing in their difficult times. However, the main shrine inside the case is of Goddess Hinglaj Mata, a highly revered deity. Many pilgrims come here to offer their prayers and offerings. Also, there are many altars here as well dedicated to Pandavas and some other gods.
The place draws in history enthusiasts as well because of its cultural importance and its association with Mahabharat lore!

Just a short walk away from the Somnath Temple lies a beautiful beach surrounded by aquamarine waters. Take a leisurely stroll, enjoy Gujarati snacks & beverages at a food stall, or go for a camel ride, this place is bountiful of fun and rich experiences. Moreover, the sunrise and sunset are quite a sight here and you’d find many here just relaxing and taking in the serene views. Golden sands, lapping waves, and postcard-perfect view - this site is ideal for getting into a quick photography session, and unsurprisingly, many tourists do. It’s just that tempting!

This historic gate once was a gateway to Somnath, acting as a major entry point for both pilgrims and other tourists. Now, it’s a historic structure with immense culture and heritage. On the gate, you’ll find traditional Gujarati architecture with ornate designs and intricate carvings of floral patterns, mythological figures, and more. The gate is glorified further with its three majestic arches , embellished with motifs and inscriptions - signifying the grandeur of ancient India!
Top Things to Do on the Somnath Trip
Somnath trip is a highly cultural and spiritually enriching journey. To make your experience truly wholesome, add these quintessential and quirky things to your Somnath travel package.

Experience the divine firsthand by attending both the morning and evening aarti at the Somnath temple. The entire experience is truly another level of spiritual and must be a part of your Somnath trip. The evening aarti is especially gorgeous with its backdrop being the setting sun.
Attend the Light and Sound Show
The Light and Sound show is a mesmerizing experience that consists of stunning visuals and compelling storytelling. The narration is the story is generally available in Hindi and Gujarati.
Expect a rich storytelling that narrates the riveting history of the temple – how it underwent destruction and reconstructions over the centuries.

It also emphasizes the temple’s spiritual significance as one of the 12 Jyotirlingas. And to top that are the stunning visual effects, supported by the advanced lighting technology that lights up the whole temple and the surrounding areas. And the whole show is further powered by the captivating sound effects with stirring background music and voiceovers – transporting viewers to the bygone era.

However, the Light and Sound Show is not just an entertainment, but a deeply moving experience that highlights the temple’s spiritual legacy and rich heritage. It’s a must-attend on your Somnath trip.

Other than the Light and Sound Show, the Somnath Museum is another great way to know the history of the Somnath temple. Here you see the visual exhibits in the form of miniature models that depict the temple’s history and present-day form – perfect for visitors to understand the temple’s evolution over the centuries.

In addition, on display are pottery, coins, and utensils from the previous eras, giving visitors a glimpse into the lifestyle of ancient times. You can also spot age-old inscriptions here in Sanskrit and other ancient languages!

Take a little detour from Somnath and meet the regal lions at the Gir Forest National Park. Many tourists opt for a combined Somnath Gir tour package to enjoy the wildlife at its full glory on their Somnath trip!

Located on the serene Triveni Sangam, Gita Mandir’s calm and spiritual vibe couldn’t get elevated any further with this strategic location. Dedicated to Lord Krishna, the temple walls are ornate with inscribed Gita verses. Moreover, the temple is designed to have an echo feature , which essentially means whenever the mantras are chanted in the temple premises, they get echoed around, creating a truly whimsical spiritual experience!
Gujarati cuisine is super delicious involving multiple flavours. Try the following dishes on your Somnath trip:

items: Gujarati Thali : This wholesome mean includes Rotis, Dal, Kadhi, Shak, Khichdi, and Thepla. It is served with Chaach, Papad, and pickles.
Dhokla : Enjoy the soft and spongy yellow snack.
Undhiyu : Gorge on this seasonal vegetable dish, slow-cooked with a blend of spices.
Fafda : Relish this savoury & sweet crispy snack.
Thepla : Do not forget to try this thin wheat flatbread, frequently paired with yogurt and pickles.
Handvo : Enjoy this salty rice and lentil cake, topped with sesame seeds.
Sweet Dishes : Give a nudge to your sweet tooth and try local desserts like Ghari, Mohanthal, and Shrikhand.

items: Locally embroidered Kurtas, Dupattas, and bags

Frequently Answered Questions about Somnath Tour Packages
Q1. How many days are sufficient for a Somnath trip?

Ans. Typically, tourists cover all the major attractions in a span of 1-2 days. In case, you want to cover the nearby tourist hotspots on your Somnath travel packages (such as Porbandar and Dwarka) as well, then 3-4 days are required.
Q2. What should I pack for a Somnath trip?

Ans. For Somnath trip, it’s ideal to pack modest clothes as they come handy during temple visits. Also, bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat to protect yourself from the sun heat. Also, carry comfortable shoes.
Q3. What are some key attractions near Somnath?
Ans. While in Somnath, tourists often add nearby key attractions, like:

items: 1. Dwarka: Come here to visit the famous Dwarkadhish temple and Nageshwar Jyotirlinga.
2. Gir National Park: Home to the Asiatic lion, this wildlife tourist hotspot is often added to Somnath trip packages.
3. Diu: Just about 85 km away, this site is famous for Portuguese architecture and pleasant beaches.

blocks.text: Q4. Can Somnath and Dwarka be covered in one trip?

Ans. Yes, many people add Dwarka to their Somnath holiday package, as they lie in close proximity (230 km apart) and share religious significance. You’ll often see Somnath itineraries including stops like Bet Dwarka, Dwarkadhish Temple, and Nageshwar Jyotirlinga.

blocks.text: South India is well-known for its historic temples and rich cultural legacy. The country as a whole is aware of its colorful festivals and varied traditions. There are numerous historic temples spread throughout the southern states of India, such as Tamil Nadu, Chennai, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. In addition to its religious importance, South India is well-known for its verdant coffee plantations. If you are planning to visit the temples in South India , we have curated a 10 day tour package to South Indian temples from Mumbai.
South India Temple Tour Itinerary Package
A representative from our team will pick you up from Mumbai airport and transfer you to the pre booked hotel. You will stay overnight at the hotel.

Following breakfast, you will explore a few of Mumbai's well-known locations. The Gateway of India will be the first stop. You can then explore the Crawford Market, Colaba, Mangaldas Market, and the Prince of Wales Museum. In addition, you will see the Jain temple, the Hanging Garden, and the Gandhi Memorial Museum. In the evening, you will also go to the Siddhivinayak temple. You will then be driven to the airport via the Bandra Worli Sea Link. After that, you'll take a flight to Chennai. Once you arrive, you will spend the night at your hotel after checking in.

Today you will explore some majorly popular temples in the city namely Kapaleeshwarar temple , Parthasarathy temple and Adeeswar temple . Each temple has its own cultural and historical heritage. Visit one of the longest beaches in the world situated in Chennai, Marina beach. Later return back to your hotel, have dinner and spend a restful night.

You will start your journey after breakfast to one of the most popular temple cities Kanchipuram also known as Kanchi. Here you will visit Ekambareswarar temple, Kamakshi Amman temple, Varadharaja Perumal temple. Afterwards, you will continue your journey to Mahabalipuram where you will see Krishna Mandapam, Arjuna Penance, the Shore temple, and Mahishasura Mardini cave. You will rest for the night in a hotel in Mahabalipuram.

After breakfast you will leave for Pondicherry, a Union Territory town. It is a French Colonial settlement. Take a rickshaw when you reach there, witness the distinctive fusion of French and Indian architecture. and take in Pondicherry's tranquil landscape.

Start the journey by visiting Auroville Ashram which is a spiritual learning hub. After that you will visit Promenade beach, Manakula Vinayagar Devasthanam temple, Mahatma Gandhi statue and the French Memorial. Head back to your hotel for the night.

From Pondicherry, you will drive to Tanjore today. You can take a stop at Thillai Nataraja temple in Chidambaram. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. After visiting the temple, continue your ride to Tanjore. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel and relax.

The first visit of the day will be Brihadeeswarar Temple in Tanjore . Drive to Trichy to visit Sri Ranganathaswamy temple, Rockfort temple and Thiruvanaikaval temple. Continue your drive to Madurai to stay for the night.

Today you will explore the town of Madurai. You can visit Thirumalai Nayak Palace. Visit one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites, Meenakshi Amman temple which is a must visit temple included in South India pilgrimage tour . After enjoying the sightseeing in Madurai, you will head back to your hotel in Madurai to spend the night.
This will be the final day of your journey. You will be dropped at the Madurai airport in order to take a flight to Mumbai.

blocks.text: FAQs for South India Temple Package
Q1. What Distinguishes The South Indian Temple?

Ans. The South Indian temple is essentially composed of a square-chambered sanctuary topped by a superstructure, tower, or spire and an attached pillared porch or hall (maapa, or maapam), surrounded by a peristyle of cells within a rectangular court.
Q2. Which Of The Following Is The Oldest Temple In South India?

Ans. The magnificent Siva temple of Thanjavur, built by Raja Raja I in 1009, and the Brihadisvara Temple of Gangaikonda Cholapuram, completed around 1030, are both fitting memorials to the two Chola emperors' material and military achievements.
Q3. In South India, Which City Is Also Known As The City Of Temples?

Ans. Although Kanchipuram is popularly known as the "City of a Thousand Temples," there is no prescribed circuit and no comprehensive temple listing or map to guide visitors. Rather, the thousands of pilgrims who visit the city every day are usually only familiar with the five most famous temples.
Q4. What Is South Indian Temple Food?

Ans. Temple food is always sattvic, which means it contains no meat, fish, onion, or garlic and is typically composed of grains, vegetables, fruits, and dairy products. "The food offered in South Indian temples is almost always cooked at the temple, unlike in North India, where you can offer store-bought food,"
Q5. What Is The South Indian Food Culture Like?

Ans. South Indian food dishes are generally lighter and revolve around a rice-based diet, as opposed to wheat-based North Indian food. Many of the world's most coveted ingredients, such as curry leaves, peppercorns, tamarind, coconut, and chilies, are grown in South India.

Here are some top places to visit in Vietnam :

It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site where limestone islands rise like emerald towers from jade waters. You must make time to cruise through misty mornings, kayak into hidden caves and watch sunsets that feel otherworldly.
Hanoi is often referred to as the soul of Vietnam - and that is certainly true. The city is filled with a blend of French architecture, bustling streets and ancient pagodas.
Formerly Saigon, it is Vietnam's beating urban heart. You can explore war museums, rooftop cafes and vibrant local markets that buzz from dawn till midnight.

Hoi An is a riverside town that is frozen in time. In fact, every evening you can see the city glow under thousands of paper lanterns. Its narrow streets, silk shops and tailor studios certainly make it one of Asia's most enchanting towns.
Do you know that this city was once the imperial capital of this country? You can still find temples and tombs here that tell stories of emperors and dynasties.

This is often called "Ha Long Bay on Land". The limestone cliffs, rivers and rice paddies here create the perfect postcard-perfect landscape. Also make sure to take a rowboat here - it is sure to be an experience for you.

Located in the northern mountains, Sapa is home to vibrant hill tribes and terraced valleys that change colour with every season. Also make some time for trekking here - it will feel like stepping into a painting.

A labyrinth of rivers and floating markets, the Delta is Vietnam's life source. Drift past fruit orchards, small villages and houseboats that capture rural Vietnam - the simplicity is something that you cannot take your eyes away from.
This is Vietnam's modern coastal city, known for its clean beaches and the iconic Golden Bridge held by giant hands. It is the perfect mix of relaxation and adventure.
White sands, turquoise waters and swaying palms - Phu Quoc is Vietnam's tropical paradise. This place is ideal for couples and beach lovers.

Q-2: How many days are enough for Vietnam?
Ans: A 6 to 8 days itinerary should be enough to cover significant places like Hanoi, Ha Long Bay and Ho Chi Minh City comfortably. You can also add a few days if you wish to include Hai An or Sapa.
Q-3: What is the best time to visit Vietnam?

Ans: Yes, Vietnam is one of the safest and most welcoming destinations in Asia. We partner with verified local operators to ensure your comfort and security.
Q-5: What currency is used in Vietnam?
Ans: The Vietnamese Dong (VND) is used in the country. Most places accept cards and ATMs are easily available in cities.
Q-6: What should I buy in Vietnam?
Ans: Silk lanterns, lacquerware, coffee, conical hats and handicrafts from Hoi An and Hanoi's night markets.

blocks.text: Best Places to visit Manali on your Trip

Manali is an ideal destination for couples on their honeymoon, spiritual seekers and people looking to get away from the chaos of city life, or solo travelers (it is a highly safe place) it offers a plethora of fun-filled and refreshing activities for people of all ages. It witnessed a significant rise in tourist footfall in 2024.It recorded the highest number of visitors (2.8 million visitors) among other districts of Himachal Pradesh . Source-( Times of India ). Here are some of the most popular places covered in our Manali itinerary -

items: Don't miss Manali's adventure capital- Solang Valley. It is one of the best places to visit in Manali if you are an adventure lover.
Enjoy activities like paragliding, skiing, and zorbing amidst stunning mountain views.
You will also witness lush green meadows and snowcapped mountains depending on the season. It offers the best natural views for nature photography.
Hadimba Temple is a historical wooden temple dedicated to Hadimba Devi, wife of Bhim, one of the five Pandavas.

The temple is surrounded by the beautiful cedar forests. Its unique architecture and serene ambiance will transport you into the realm of bliss. It is one of the most beautiful temples to visit in Manali.

Enjoy the breathtaking mountain views and snow adventure activities at Rohtang Pass. It is one of the most scenic mountains passes to see in Manali. It is also a gateway to visit Lahaul and Spiti Valley.
It is best for adventure and nature excursions. You can reach here from May to November. It is closed in winter due to heavy snow.
Don't forget to visit this beautiful pilgrimage site for Sikhs and Hindus in Manali- Manikaran Sahib. It is renowned for its hot springs.

Located on the banks of Parvati River, the spiritual ambiance of Manikaran Sahib offers an eternal peak for solace seekers. Devotees from all over India come to Manikaran Sahib to seek blessings of the Guru.
Visit Manali most revered spiritual and wellness destination- Vashisht Temple and Hot Springs. The temple is believed to be over 4000 years old.
Pay your respects to Sage Vashisht, one of the ancient Saptarishis and the Guru of Lord Rama. The temple is also famous for its hot springs known as Vashisht Kund.
The hot waters are believed to have medicinal properties which can heal skin and joint ailments.
Located across the Manalsu River, old Manali is a must not miss if you like to explore the quieter part of Manali. Enjoy the bohemian vibe and explore quaint cafes at Old Manali.
Here you will witness beautiful apple orchards, scenic trekking trails, cedar forests and bustling markets which offer leather goods, winter clothing, handmade jewelry, and local produce.
If you like leisure nature walks, peaceful temple hopping and visiting cafes then Old Manali will delight your soul.
Manu Temple is dedicated to Sage Manu who is known as the creator of Humanity in Hindu mythology. It is one of the most popular temples to visit in Manali.
It is said that sage Manu meditated at the temple spot and saved the Vedas and seven sages from flood.
It is also the origin point of Manali known as Manu-Alaya (abode of Sage Manu)

items: Bear River in Manali is one of the main landmarks of Manali. Capture beautiful sights and sceneries. The chilled water offers opportunities for thrilling adventure activities like white water rafting.
Surrounded by the beautiful alpine meadows, you can also enjoy Beas Kund Trek.
Also stay at Luxury camps and capture the beauty of the Beas River and majestic Himalayan Mountains.
Along the river roads, you will find many shops to buy warm clothes, handicrafts and souvenirs etc.
It is also a great place to enjoy fun-filled picnics with your family in Manali.
Manali is one of the best places to enjoy paragliding. You can try this amazing adventure in Solang Valley, Fatru or Marhi etc.
Paragliding lasts for 8 to 30 minutes. You will be guided by certified paragliding instructors. So, it's beginner friendly.
You can enjoy this activity in March-June, September to November.
Camping is something you must try in Manali. Not only it offers peaceful nature retreats with family but also offers adventures in beautiful settings.
You can enjoy camping in Manali at various places like Solang Valley, Kothi Village and Beas River etc.
Some camps even offer adventure activities like paragliding, skiing, trekking, and bonfire evenings. June to September is the best time to enjoy camping in Manali.
Trekking and enjoying leisure nature walks will melt your heart in Manali as you will be mesmerized by the stunning views of majestic Himalayan peaks.
There are many scenic trekking trails and nature destinations in Manali like Jogini Waterfalls, Hampta Pass, or Beas Kund and Great Himalayan National Park.
At Great Himalayan National Park, you can enjoy forest walks, bird watching, and exploring alpine meadows.

blocks.text: Top Places to Visit in Assam on Your Trip

Assam is among the fastest developing tourist destinations in India. In 2024- 2025 till December, Assam welcomed around 57,48,772 domestic tourists and 14,000 foreign tourists which makes it one of the top choices for tourists to visit in India. Source- ( Business Standard ). Assam has many amazing tourist attractions. Naming all at once would not be possible but here is a list of must visit places in Assam which are covered in our Assam itineraries. You can also add as many places as you want according to your choice.

items: Explore Kaziranga National Park in Assam, it is one of the most popular wildlife destinations for adventure and nature lovers. It shelters two-thirds of the world’s population of one-horned Rhinos.

You have to book a thrilling Jeep Safari or Elephant Safari in advance to witness the rich biodiversity of the park and wild creatures like Rhinos, Tigers, Elephants, wild buffaloes and various bird species which includes migratory birds and endangered bird species.

Situated in the serene Brahmaputra River, Umananda Island is a must visit place in Assam. It’s a scenic natural wonder worth visiting for awesome natural views. It hosts the beautiful Umananda Temple which is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Seek divine blessings of Lord Shiva, spot golden langurs and enjoy a ferry ride to this beautiful island.

You must visit Kamakhya Temple in Assam. It is one of the landmark destinations due to its spiritual significance for Hindu Devotees. The temple is a Shakti Peetha, dedicated to the mother goddess Kamakhya.

It is located in the Nilachal Hill in Guwahati. In this temple location, it is believed that the Yoni (reproductive organ) of goddess Sati fell. Ma Kamakhya is a symbol of fertility and feminine creative power in Hinduism.
The festival of Ambubachi celebrates the feminine energy and annual menstrual cycle of Goddess Kamakhya.

Majuli Island is one of the famous tourist places in Assam to capture awe-inspiring Naturescapes. It is the world's largest river island which is very famous for its Neo- Vaishnavite culture and monastic institutions.
During Monsoon, the island submerged under water. May is the best time to explore Majuli Island.
Haflong Located in Dima Hasao district of Assam, Haflong is an enchanting hill station in Assam. It is in fact the only Hill station of Assam.
Capture the scenic beauty of lush green forests, scenic hills, enjoy boating and fun-filled picnics with your loved ones.
It is very famous for Vibrant Dimasa tribal culture, trekking, paragliding and local flower gardens.

Sivasagar used to be the capital of Ahom Kingdom. It is a very popular tourist attraction in Assam for history , heritage and culture. There are many ancient temples like Sivadol, palaces like Rang Ghar, Kareng Ghar and large water tanks.
You will also witness beautiful heritage attractions like Charaideo Maidam which displays Assam’s archaeological and royal past.
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Assam, Manas National Park is a paradise for wildlife enthusiasts. Spot rare wildlife like golden Langurs and pygmy hogs.
Enjoy river rafting, jungle safaris along with the scenic views of Manas River, alluvial grasslands, tropical evergreen forests, and majestic Himalayan hills.

blocks.text: Things to Do in Assam on Your Trip
