items: Perfect for nature lovers, romantic couples and families, Visit Kakochang waterfalls in Assam. This scenic waterfall flows between the rubber and coffee plantations of Jorhat.

It attracts tourists throughout the year. Enjoy scenic views of the ruins of Numaligarh and lush green tea plantations. Post-monsoon months are the best months to explore the scenic beauty of this enchanting waterfall.

It is one of the most interesting places to visit in Assam. Established in 1911, it is one of the oldest tea research stations in the world. Assam’s tea quality needs no introduction. So, here you will witness how authentic research on extraction, cultivation and processing of tea is done.
The research is done to enhance the nutritional value of tea. It also conducts tea tasting tours for the tourists.
Don’t miss the ancient pilgrimage site in Assam known as Hajo. Located on the serene banks of Brahmaputra River. It features many ancient temples and sacred artifacts.
Hayagriva Madhava Temple and Hajo Powa Mecca are the two most prominent tourist attractions which you must not miss.
Your Assam holidays will be incomplete without enjoying thrilling wildlife safaris in Assam at various national parks like Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri National Park etc.

Assam is a very popular tourist destination for wildlife lovers. Its forests, wetlands, grasslands shelter various rare and endangered faunas and floras making it one of the best biodiversity spots to explore in India.
Don’t miss the enchanting Silk Village of Assam - Sualkuchi. It is also known as the Manchester of Assam.
The village is very famous for the craft of Silk weaving which dates back to ancient times. You will witness various types of Silk like Muga, Pat, Eri (Ahimsa silk), and Endi cloth here.
Explore Brahmaputra River in Assam. It is a must visit spot to enjoy the beauty of Assam Tourism. Not only it’s a popular destination for nature lovers but also, it’s a paradise for adventure lovers.
Enjoy adventure activities such as river rafting and cruises on the Brahmaputra, kayaking, trekking and birdwatching.

blocks.text: How to Reach Varanasi from Nagpur?
There are multiple ways by which you can reach the holy city from Maharashtra. Here's the quick travel guide:

You can easily go to Varanasi from Nagpur by flight. This is the fastest way to travel, and you can land in the holy city in less than 2 hours. You'll find airlines like IndiGo, Air India, and Akasa Air running on this route, for both direct and connecting flights.
In case you can't find a direct flight, take a plane to Delhi first and from there fly to Varanasi.

Trains are a great way to travel, especially for those looking for affordable Varanasi pilgrimage package for Nagpur. Simply take a train from Nagpur Junction and get off at Varanasi Junction. The whole ride takes around 15 hours, and you can find trains like Sanghamitra Express, Kamayani Express, Nagpur-Varanasi Express, and Gyan Ganga Express for this route.

The Nagpur to Varanasi distance is about 710 km, and you can cover this journey in a span of about 11-12 hours. For the Nagpur to Varanasi road trip, get on NH44 for Nagpur to Jabalpur segment, and after that, you need to take the NH30 or NH19 to go from Jabalpur to Varanasi. On this journey, the route is quite scenic, lined with forest stretches and even rural areas. There are also buses that run on this route (but direct connectivity is limited).
Here's the route map from Nagpur to Varanasi:
Nagpur → Seoni → Jabalpur → Rewa → Mirzapur → Varanasi

You can avoid all this hassle of going through multiple segments by simply choosing our Varanasi Tour Package with flight/train from Nagpur. Once you book the package, all your travel worries are ours. All you need to do is sit back and relax while we take full care of your trip - from the beginning to the very end!
Top Places to Visit in Varanasi
Whether you're going on a full-fledged five-day trip or have opted for a Varanasi weekend package from Nagpur, these are some places that must be a part of your trip :
This is the most famous temple of Varanasi. Dedicated to Lord Shiva, it's also one of the 12 Jyotirlingas . It's a must-addition to any Varanasi travel package from Nagpur!
This is ideal for the Ganga Aarti Varanasi tour! Come here in the evening, and you'll find the surroundings beautifully lit by lamps and Diyas.
Compared to the Dashashwamedh Ghat, this is a more serene and calmer Ghat. You can come here to enjoy boat rides or have a yoga session. The vibe is just so calm and pleasant here.
Take a short drive from Varanasi and you'll land at the place where Lord Buddha gave his very first sermon. Also, visit the Dhamek Stupa and museum here.
This is the main cremation Ghat of the city. Come here and ponder on the recurrent cycle of life and death!

Visit this large residential university that houses the New Vishwanath Temple. The peaceful vibe here will give you a refreshing break from the hustle-bustle of the cities. A great addition to any Nagpur to Varanasi trip!
There are plenty of things that you can do on this trip. Here's a typical Nagpur to Varanasi tour itinerary:

items: Day 1 : Welcome to the 'city of temples', Varanasi! Enjoy Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat in the evening.
Day 2 : Indulge in the sunrise boat ride on the Ganga in Varanasi. Later, go for a visit to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. After that, go shopping at the local markets.
Day 3 : Visit the Sarnath Buddhist site in Varanasi! In the latter part of the day, visit the Assi Ghat, which is known for its serene and peaceful vibe. You can engage in yoga and meditation here.

Day 4 : Visit the Manikarnika Ghat, which is a famous cremation Ghat of the city. After that, visit some other popular places in the city. It's also a great idea to take a Varanasi heritage walk old lanes. In the evening, go for the Ganga Aarti again or enjoy the cultural shows.
Day 5 : Have a leisurely morning, and after that, bid the holy city goodbye and return home!

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Varanasi from Nagpur
The best time to visit Varanasi is in the winter season ( October to March ). The weather in this period is quite cool and pleasant. You can comfortably do your sightseeing and go on temple tours.

The summers are quite hot and therefore make the temple and Ghat visits quite unpleasant. Monsoon, on the other hand, offers you lush greenery, but the weather is so humid that it becomes too uncomfortable to carry on. Also, because of heavy rain, you have to deal with road blockages and other rain disruptions.
Cost of Varanasi Trip from Nagpur

The Varanasi Travel price Package from Nagpur starts from INR 5,400 per person . My Quick Trippers offers you tour plans, where all your tour logistics will be completely handled by us - ranging from your meals to accommodation to transfers. Also, all our packages are fully customizable.
You can also book our combo packages, such as Varanasi Prayagraj Ayodhya Vindhyachal Yatra (INR16,350) or the full-blown Uttar Pradesh Darshan Tour (INR 20,700).
Travel Tips for Varanasi Trip from Nagpur
Here is some travel advice for your trip:

items: To skip crowds, start your day early. For Ghat visits and temple trips, make sure to reach there early in the morning.
Wear modest clothes, especially when you're visiting the temples. Make sure your knees and shoulders are covered.
Boat rides are in high demand in the morning. Therefore, book in advance enough to get your desired slot.
To travel around Ghats, use e-rickshaws which are a common mode of local transport there.
While visiting markets, keep cash handy with you, as local vendors might not accept cards.
Always book your Maharashtra to Varanasi pilgrimage tour in advance.

blocks.text: If you are planning a pilgrimage to Kedarnath from Kolkata, there are several tour packages available that cater specifically to this journey. Kedarnath, nestled in the lap of the Himalayas, is a revered destination for Hindus and attracts devotees from all over the world. The Kedarnath tour packages from Kolkata offer a convenient and well-organized way to embark on this spiritual journey. Kolkata, being a major city in eastern India, is well-connected to various transportation modes, making it easier for pilgrims to reach Kedarnath. The tour packages generally include transportation, accommodation, and other essential services to ensure a hassle-free experience.

These Kedarnath tour packages provide different options based on your preferences and budget. You can choose from helicopter packages, trekking packages, or a combination of both. Helicopter packages are ideal for those who want to save time and energy, as they offer a quick and comfortable way to reach Kedarnath. The packages usually include helicopter transfers from Dehradun or Guptkashi to Kedarnath, VIP darshan at the temple, and accommodation in nearby hotels or guesthouses. Trekking packages are suitable for adventure enthusiasts who want to experience the scenic beauty of the Himalayas and immerse themselves in the spiritual journey. These packages include transportation from Kolkata to Gaurikund, the starting point of the trek, accommodation in tents or guesthouses along the trekking route, and assistance from experienced guides and porters.

The duration of the tour packages varies, ranging from a few days to a week or more, depending on the itinerary and activities included. Some packages also offer additional visits to nearby attractions such as Badrinath, Yamunotri, and Gangotri, allowing you to explore more of the Char Dham circuit. Before selecting a tour package, it is advisable to compare different options, consider the inclusions and exclusions, check customer reviews, and ensure the reliability of the tour operator. By choosing a well-planned tour package, you can have a memorable and smooth journey to Kedarnath, focusing on your spiritual quest and enjoying the beauty of the Himalayas.

Kedarnath is renowned for its ancient and revered Kedarnath Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple, believed to have been built by the Pandavas, stands at an altitude of 3,583 meters (11,755 feet) amidst the picturesque Kedarnath range. The temple is a marvel of architecture and exudes a sense of spiritual grandeur. Surrounded by snow-capped peaks, lush green meadows, and the gushing Mandakini River, Kedarnath offers a serene and breathtaking environment that captivates the hearts of pilgrims and travellers alike.
Best Places to Visit in Kedarnath:

Kedarnath Temple: The focal point of any visit to Kedarnath, the Kedarnath Temple is a sacred site where devotees seek blessings and embark on a spiritual journey. The temple’s intricate architecture and serene ambiance create a deeply moving experience.

Vasuki Tal: Situated at an altitude of 4,150 meters (13,615 feet), Vasuki Tal is a glacial lake surrounded by snow-clad peaks. The trek to Vasuki Tal offers mesmerizing views of the Himalayan landscape and is a paradise for nature lovers and adventure enthusiasts.

Chorabari Tal (Gandhi Sarovar): Located at an altitude of 3,900 meters (12,795 feet), Chorabari Tal is a pristine lake known for its crystal-clear waters. It is believed to be the spot where Lord Shiva imparted knowledge to the Pandavas.

Triyuginarayan Temple: Around 24 kilometres (15 miles) from Kedarnath, Triyuginarayan Temple is a significant pilgrimage site. According to Hindu mythology, it is the place where Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati got married.

Sonprayag: Situated at the confluence of the Mandakini and Basuki rivers, Sonprayag is a picturesque destination known for its natural beauty. It serves as the starting point for the trek to Kedarnath.

Plan in Advance: It is advisable to plan your Kedarnath Yatra well in advance, especially during peak seasons. Make reservations for accommodation, helicopter services (if required), and other necessary arrangements to avoid any last-minute challenges.

Acclimatize and Stay Hydrated: Kedarnath is located at a high altitude, so it is essential to acclimatize yourself before undertaking the trek or engaging in any physical activities. Drink plenty of water and stay hydrated throughout your journey.

Dress Appropriately: Due to the high altitude and unpredictable weather conditions, it is recommended to dress in layers and carry warm clothing, even during the summer months. Additionally, wear comfortable shoes suitable for trekking.

Carry Essential Medications: It is advisable to carry a basic first aid kit and any necessary medications you might need during your journey. Consult your doctor before undertaking the trek, especially if you have any pre-existing health conditions.

Respect Local Customs and Traditions: Kedarnath holds immense religious significance, so it is important to respect the local customs, traditions, and the sanctity of the temple. Follow the guidelines provided by the authorities and maintain cleanliness and hygiene during your visit.

The best time to visit Kedarnath is from May to June and September to October. During these months, the weather is pleasant, and the trekking routes are open for pilgrims. The monsoon season (July to August) should be avoided due to heavy rainfall and the risk of landslides. The winter months (November to April) witness heavy snowfall, and the temple remains closed during this period.

By Air: The nearest airport to Kedarnath is Jolly Grant Airport in Dehradun, which is well-connected to major cities in India. From the airport, one can hire a taxi or take a shared cab to reach Gaurikund, the starting point of the trek to Kedarnath.
By Train: The nearest railway station to Kedarnath is Rishikesh, which is well-connected to major cities in India. From Rishikesh, one can hire a taxi or take a bus to reach Gaurikund.

By Road: Kedarnath is accessible by road from various cities in Uttarakhand. Buses and taxis are available from major towns like Rishikesh, Haridwar, and Dehradun to Gaurikund. From Gaurikund, one can trek or hire a pony or palanquin to reach Kedarnath.

It is important to note that the last stretch of the journey from Gaurikund to Kedarnath involves a 16-kilometer (10-mile) trek that can be physically demanding. It is advisable to be prepared, have a basic level of fitness, and consult a doctor if needed before embarking on the trek.

blocks.text: India is a country of diverse religions and faiths. There are historical and religious tales to be found all around our nation, every temple has a specific history and significance. The pilgrimage sites around the country are always seen crowded with thousands of devotees and South Indian temples are one of the most revered pilgrimage sites in India. Therefore, we have created a 12 day tour package from Delhi to South India temples which includes accommodation with basic necessary amenities, meals, transfers and a dedicated tour guide.

Start your spiritual journey from Delhi airport. Board the flight to Chennai. It usually takes 3 hours to reach Chennai from Delhi by air. Once you arrive in Chennai, one of our representatives will pick you from the airport and get you checked-in to the hotel we have booked for you. You will be staying at the hotel in Chennai overnight.

After having breakfast at the hotel, you will head for Tirupati temple Darshan located in Andhra Pradesh. It will take 3 to 4 hours to reach Tirupati. Once there, you will visit some of the famous temples in Tirupati like Sri Padmavathi Temple, Sri Kalahasteeswara Temple, Sri Kodandaramaswami Temple, Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Govindaraja Swamy Temple and Kapila Theertham. After Darshan at all the temples you will travel back to your hotel in Chennai and stay for the night.

Today you will leave for Mamallapuram and will stop at Kanchipuram enroute. After sightseeing at the temples in Kanchipuram, you will head towards Mamallapuram also known as Mahabalipuram. You will check-in to the hotel once reached. Take some rest and go out exploring Mamallapuram. You will visit Shore Temple and Krishna Mandapam. Later you will travel back to your hotel and stay there for the night.

Post breakfast, you will travel to Tiruvannamalai. Visit Arunachala temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and offer prayers. After exploring, you will travel towards Puducherry. Check-in to the hotel where you will stay overnight.

Today will be spent exploring the French Colonial settlement, Puducherry which is a Union Territory of India. Visit Sri Aurobindo ashram, Church of the Sacred Heart Jesus, the Sacre Coeur Church and Pondicherry Museum. You will also visit Manakula Vinayagar Koil Temple which is dedicated to Lord Ganesha. Afterwards, head back to your hotel for dinner and a relaxing night.

Today’s destination will be Thanjavur, earlier known as Tanjore. The journey is about 5 hours long. You will be stopping over at Chidambaram for a quick excursion. Visit the Nataraja temple which is solely dedicated to the cosmic dancing form of Lord Shiva i.e Nataraja and signifies the art of Bharatanatyam. After that continue the journey further to Thanjavur. Once arrived, check-in and stay for the night.

Visit Brihadeeswara temple in Thanjavur which is a UNESCO world heritage site and is said to be one of the oldest temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. After Darshan you will head to Trichy and check in to the hotel there. You can enjoy the evening strolling around at nearby places or markets. Stay overnight at the hotel.

You will start your journey after breakfast at the hotel. The first stop will be Srirangam located on an island. Visit Sri Ranganathaswamy temple surrounded by the river Kaveri. Next you'll visit the famous landmark of Trichy which is the Rock Fort. Lastly, you will travel to Madurai. Check-in to the hotel and stay for the night.

Post breakfast, explore the sacred town of Madurai located on the bank of river Vaigai. Visit Meenakshi Amman temple which is dedicated to Goddess Parvati and Lord Shiva. You will attend the evening ceremony at the temple and seek blessings from the divine. After sightseeing and temple visit, you will head back to your hotel in Madurai for an overnight stay.

You will leave for the southernmost tip of India, Kanyakumari, today. The journey is about 4 to 5 hours long. Once you reach, visit Swami Vivekananda’s memorial, Kumari Amman Temple and Thiruvalluvar Statue. Once you finish exploring and visiting all the key attractions, you will be staying at the hotel in Kanyakumari itself for the night.

In the morning after having your breakfast you will travel to Trivandrum which is a 3 - 4 hours long ride. Once there, check in at the hotel and take some rest. After relaxing a little, you will visit Padmanabha Swamy temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu and also visit Napier Museum. After sightseeing, you will head back to your hotel and stay overnight.
This will be the final day of your South Indian pilgrimage tour. You will check-out and will be dropped at the airport. You can then fly back to Delhi or your native place with beautiful memories.

blocks.text: Tibet Tour Packages takes one to completely different world which is peaceful, calm and serene. Adorned with mesmerizing snow covered mountains, lush open grasslands, ancient Buddhist monasteries, unique wildlife and tranquil lakes, this place is a paradise. This place is called as Land of Gods and is the best place to understand Buddhist culture and religion. Far away from the clamor of urban civilization in the lap of nature there is no other place in the world like Tibet and it pulls thousands of visitors every year on Tour Packages to captivate them in its divine and whimsical charm.

Lhasa is the center of economic, social and political activity of Tibet, situated at the height of 1380 meters above sea level and at the bank of river Kyichu, it is a 1300 years old city. Apart from its natural beauty this place has many places to see on Tibet Travel Packages and Potala Palace is the most popular amongst them. Potala Palace is a majestic architectural work built in 7th century and renovated in 17th century. Mostly the work is of stone and timber but this massive structure is 13 storey high and 400 meter long and 350 meter wide sitting in all its majesty at the peak of Red Hill. Today this place is winter palace of Dalai Lamas, the topmost storey has golden roofs and glisten from the height of 117 meters.

Another popular place in Lhasa for tourists to visit on Tibet Holiday Packages is Jokhang Temple, this is another ancient construction built in 7th century, it is four storied amazing architecture. The murals inside the temple are antics and display the life of Kings and saints and preaching of Buddhism. This golden roof temple is spiritual center of the country and holiest destination for visitors on Tibet Travel Packages or for Tibetan Buddhist pilgrims. Drepung Monastery in Lhasa is another enchanting place to visit on Tibet Holiday Packages, this is the biggest monastery of the country and has historical relics, ancient Buddhist scriptures, arts and crafts.

Gyantse, Shigaste and Zhangmu town are situated at thousands of feet above sea level and have many monasteries and ancient architectures worth seeing on Tour Packages to Tibet including the fascinating beauty of the surrounding areas. The Himalayas stand and spray their charisma in Tibet like they do at none other place, Mt Everest and Mt. Kailash are two peaks famous for different reasons but sure places to see on Tour Packages. The landscapes of Himalayas in Tibet are quixotic and as many as eight peaks above 8000 meters height of Himalayan range are in this part of the world. Tranquil lake Mansarover, a sacred place for Hindu and Tibetan pilgrims on Mt. Kailash is famous for its serenity and divine beauty.

Tsetang valley is the oldest place in Tibet and one of the most visited place by tourists on Tour Packages because of its phenomenal beauty. Ruins of Guge Kingdom in Tsada are spread over an area of 180000 Sq. meters beholding five magnificent temples and more than 300 caves. Yamdok Yumtso is one of the three largest lakes of Tibet and treated as sacred lake lying close to Lhasa, this too is a must see place on Tour Packages.

blocks.text: Pick Your Choice from Our Best Kashmir Tour Packages List
Here is a list of our best Kashmir itineraries to make your holidays in Kashmir memorable. We have customised Kashmir Tour Packages for all budget types.
Every season in Kashmir has its own charm. March to May is the best time to explore Kashmir's beautiful landscapes. Let's know in detail about the best time to enjoy Kashmir Tourism .

These months are the best to enjoy the beautiful landscapes of Kashmir. The weather is extremely pleasant to enjoy Kashmir sightseeing along with different adventure activities. You can enjoy shikara boat rides on Dal Lake, trekking, visiting gardens and lakes, and capture the scenic beauty of the lush green valleys of Kashmir. You can also enjoy the Tulip Festival.

These months are also perfect to enjoy Kashmir sightseeing tours with your family and friends. The mornings and evenings will be cooler but the days will be warmer for enjoying sightseeing and adventure activities. You can enjoy photography, apple-picking, peaceful nature walks, and festivals like Autumn Harvest Festival.

If you love to see snowfall and enjoy snow adventure activities then these are the best months to plan Kashmir holidays. During these months, you can enjoy Winter sports such as skiing and snowboarding (Gulmarg and Pahalgam), cozy houseboat stays in Srinagar, and snow sightseeing.

These months are not favorable for Kashmir tourism as you will witness heavy rainfall with potential landslides and road blocks. But if you are tolerant of rain and still planning to visit Kashmir in Monsoon then you can enjoy leisure nature walks, nature photography. These months are perfect for budget travelers seeking discounts.
Best Places to Explore in Kashmir on Your Trip

Nestled in between the Pir Panjal Mountain range and the Greater Himalayas, Kashmir Valley offers a peaceful respite. In the first half of 2025, Jammu and Kashmir received over 95 lakh domestic tourists which shows Kashmir is one of the top choices for holiday destinations for tourists in India. Source ( Kashmirilife ). Here is a list of some of the best places to visit in Kashmir , covered in our itineraries.

items: Located in Pir Panjal range of Kashmir, Gulmarg is one of the most beautiful places to visit in Kashmir.
It has one of the world's highest cable cars- The Gulmarg Gondola which ascends to around 3,980 meters, offering stunning views of snow-capped Himalayan Mountains.
It is also the best winter destination to visit in India. You can try Skiing, snowboarding, Gondola Ride, Heli Skiing, Snow Trekking, Sledging and Tobogganing, ice skating and snowman building.
Also known as Meadow of Gold, Sonmarg's beauty will melt your heart. It is surrounded by beautiful Himalayan Peaks, turquoise lakes, and lush alpine meadows.
Don't forget to visit the scenic Baltal Valley, it is also the base camp for Amarnath Yatra. Enjoy Camping and the beauty of green meadows.
There are many other places like Nilagrad River, which offers a soothing natural setting perfect for picnics and relaxation. Zoji La Pass, Krishansar and Vishansar Lakes to explore here.
Pahalgam, the valley of Shephards is one of the most beautiful places in the Anantnag district of Kashmir.
Stunning alpine forests, snow-capped mountains, crystal streams and lush green meadows, makes this place worth visiting for a relaxing vacation with family.
There are many breathtaking places to explore in Pahalgam like Betaab Valley, Aru valley, Chandanwari, Baisaran Valley and Sheshnag Lake Etc.

Known for its natural beauty and rich cultural heritage, Srinagar is a must visit place in Kashmir. Here you will enjoy a serene boating experience in traditional Shikaras and visit floating markets which reflects the local way of life.
There are also many heritage places to explore in Srinagar like The Mughal Gardens - Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, and Chashme Shahi.
You will be mesmerized by the beauty of Dal Lake and Indira Gandhi Tulip Garden which is one of the largest gardens in Asia.
Kargil is one of the best places to visit in Kashmir for its historical significance and stunning natural beauty.
It is located in Dras. Kargil got prominence due to the 1999 Kargil war between Indian and Pakistan. Apart from the military importance, Kargil is culturally very diverse.
You will see a unique blend of Balti Muslim and Buddhist communities. There are also many places to visit here like Wakha village, Suru valley, Kargil war memorial, Phokar hill etc.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Kashmir on Your Trip

Kashmir is blessed with lofty green Himalayan ranges, glimmering lakes, gushing rivers, crisscrossing valleys, and Chinar tree-lined paths. The Sufi shrines, ancient temples, and quaint wooden bridges add a lot of cultural and historical value to this place. Here are some of the best things to do in Kashmir -
Shikara Ride on the Iconic Dal Lake

items: Shikara ride on Dal Lake is one of the best things to do in Kashmir. Dal Lake offers stunning views of majestic Himalayan Mountains, Mughal gardens and floating gardens, which looks beautiful at sunrise and sunset.
You can also buy fresh flowers, vegetables, and handicrafts directly from their boats.
It is a quintessential Kashmir experience which is a must not miss.
It is one of the most popular activities to do in Kashmir. The scenic trekking trails in Sonmarg offer the most breathtaking landscapes in Kashmir.
One of the best trekking trails in Sonmarg is Thajiwas Glacier, it's a short trek to view the frozen ice formations and glacial streams.
If you are more adventurous then you can also visit the Kashmir Great Lakes Trek which starts from Sonmarg and passes through alpine lakes like Krishansar and Vishansar.

Don't miss the best snow adventure in Gulmarg. Try snowboarding, Skiing, Gondola Ride, Heli Skiing, Snow Trekking, Sledging and Tobogganing, ice skating and snowman building. The Ski season starts from December and lasts till March.

Gulmarg also hosts winter festivals around December or February where you will get a chance to enjoy Traditional Kashmiri music, folk dances, and witness craft stalls and food stalls which offer authentic Kashmiri dishes like Rogan Josh and Gushtaba.
Kashmir has many enchanting pilgrimage sites to fine-tune your spirit with positive vibes and inner peace.
Devotees from all over India visit Amarnath Cave Temple, Vaishno Devi temple, Kheer Bhawani Temple, Charar-e-Sharief and many more sacred sites.
If you are planning your visit in Kashmir, book your pilgrimage tour especially to Amarnath and Vaishno Devi in advance in their peak tourism season.

blocks.text: Travel Tips for Unforgettable Kashmir Holidays
Here are some best travel tips to create fun-filled moments with your loved ones in Kashmir-

items: Safety - For safety check if there are any travel restrictions in any area of Kashmir you are planning to visit from local news and trusted sources. Always hire a safe travel agency for a safe trip if you are planning to explore offbeat destinations of Kashmir. Avoid travelling during any political unrest and protest.
What to Pack - You have to carry warm clothes all year around when you are planning a Kashmir Trip. Carry heavy woolens, sweaters, scarves, gloves, and comfortable shoes are must-haves.
Permits- Some remote or border areas such as Gurez, Keran, or Bangus near the Line of Control (LoC) require special permits obtained from local authorities. Get all the permits in advance.

Plan your Visit - March to October is the best time to travel to Kashmir as the weather is pleasant for sightseeing and enjoying adventure activities. If you love snowfall and winter sports then you should plan your visit in winter months-December to February).
Respect Culture and Customs - Avoid wearing revealing clothes in culturally sensitive areas. Dress modestly in temples and other sacred sites.
Carry Enough Cash - If you are visiting remote locations in Kashmir then carry enough cash for souvenir shopping. You may not find ATM's or any digital payment options.

blocks.text: Singapore Travel Guide - Festivals, Food, Shopping

In Singapore, there is a constant buzz of delightful activities, which travellers will enjoy a lot. People of Singapore celebrate one festival after another almost every month of the year. Let's know in detail about the vibrant Festivals Celebrated in Singapore -

items: Chinese New Year - it falls between mid-January and mid-February. It is celebrated for two days. People feast and give Hong bao, red packets of 'lucky money'.

Thaipusam - This is a Hindu festival celebrated between January and February. At this festival, devotees worship Lord Murugan and practice mindfulness. The festival begins at dawn at the Srinivasa Perumal Temple in Serangoon Road.

Dragon Boat Festival - This festival is celebrated to honor a Chinese patriot, Qu Yuan, who drowned himself in 278 BC as a form of protest against the imperial court. On this day small packets of rice are thrown into the water to distract fishes, and people decorate their boats with dragon heads and tails.

Vesak Day - This festival is celebrated to honor Lord Buddha's birth, death and enlightenment. At dawn, you will see a huge candlelight procession by the devotees. As a part of the celebration, caged birds are released, and free meals are offered to the poor and needy.

Singapore Food Festival - Don't miss this festival, as you will get to taste Singapore's rich flavors. This festival celebrates Singapore's rich culinary heritage, which features local perennial food favorites such as Hainanese chicken rice, Chilli crab, Laksa, and satay.

Theemithi Festival - It's a unique festival which you must witness in Singapore. It is celebrated at Sri Mariamman Temple on South Bridge Road. Male devotees walk barefoot across glowing coals in honor of Draupadi, a legendary heroine of Mahabharata deified by South Indians.

blocks.text: Due to Singapore's cultural diversity, you will get various cuisines here. You will never go hungry on this beautiful island. The life of the people of Singapore revolves around food. There has been a constant debate about where to get fresh crabs, spicy chilli sauce, Indian food, chicken rice, etc. From Indian, Japanese, Korean, and Thai to Middle Eastern, you can sample different cuisines without any hassle. Let's know in detail about some of the best food to try in Singapore -

items: Chinese Dishes - Peking Duck and Wok-fried A5 Wagyu Beef, Dim Sum, Double Boiled Soups, Hakka Noodles, Chilli Chicken and Peking Duck.
Indian Cuisine - Biryani, seafood, Dosa, Thali meals, fish head curry (invented in Singapore), Indian Rojak, and Indian-style mee goreng, etc.
Malaysian Food - Beef Rendang, Ayam Bakar (grilled chicken), Sambal Goreng, traditional Kuehs, Bak Kut Teh, etc.
Peranakan Food - Ayam Buah Keluak, Babi Pongteh, Chap Chye, Otak-Otak, Laksa, Kueh Pie Tee and Nyonya Popiah.
Singaporean Food - Hainanese Chicken Rice, Chilli Crab, Fish Head Curry, Laksa, Satay, Char Kway Teow, Kaya Toast, Mee Rebus, Mee Siam, Fish Head Curry, and Bak Kut Teh.

blocks.text: Shopping centers in Singapore are open from 10 a.m. to around 9 p.m. So, you can shop throughout the day. There are many famous places for shopping in Singapore you must not miss to amaze your senses and buy beautiful souvenirs.

items: Orchard Road - Orchard Road is the busiest shopping district in Singapore. It is filled with malls that have department stores, retail outlets, and designer boutiques.
Marina Bay - Visit here for shops selling clothes, shoes, bags, electronic equipment, books and sports apparel.

Civic District - There are numerous modern malls, boutique shops, and unique local finds, which is a great deal for shopaholics. Visit here for buying street fashion brands, lifestyle stores, cosmetics, Asian-style artwork, trinkets, and fashion items, etc.
Kampong Glam - You must visit here to go buy fabrics, leather bags, rattan goods, purses and shoes and handwoven baskets.
Little India - Come here to buy Indian souvenirs, imitation Jewellery, bangles, Sarees and Salwar Kameez, gold Jewellery, spices and traditional sweets.
Chinatown - Visit here to buy decorative chopsticks, silk robes, Zodiac Keychains, Chinese calligraphy, fans, lucky cats, dragon candles and street opera masks.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit in Singapore

Singapore is one of Asia's best travel destinations. It has many incredible tourist routes and tones of historical marvels, cultural attractions, clubs, and nature reserves. Let's know some of the popular places to visit in Singapore to make your trip awesome.
This district of Singapore will take your breath away with many colonial buildings, museums, memorials and institutions. It is the cultural heart of the city. Some of the best places to see here are

items: St Andrew Cathedral - It is a Gothic-style church built by Indian convict laborers by using a special plaster material called Madras Chunam. The recent structure you see here today is designed by Ronald MacPherson.
The Padang- Padang is a popular historical marvel in Singapore which was used as a platform for Europeans to play cricket and socialise in the cool evenings.
City Hall - City Hall is one of the major historic landmarks of Singapore. It was constructed in 1929 to house the municipal council.

Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall - This place was used as a social hall to conduct public meetings and events. Now it is used as a place to witness theatrical performances, concerts, and festivals. Both the buildings display beautiful neoclassical architecture.
Raffles Landing Site - A place where Sir Stamford Raffles first landed on January 28th, 1819. Here you will also see a white poly-marble statue of Sir Stamford Raffles.
Mica Building - Once upon a time, it used to be the largest government building in Singapore, which was used to house the Hill Street Police Station and barracks.

blocks.text: This district in Singapore is very popular for its large number of museums. By visiting the museums, you will be able to know about Singapore's early stories through art and war relics. If you are planning to visit here, then explore-

items: Fort Canning Park - Also known as Forbidden Hill, it is one of the best places to visit in Singapore. Fort Canning used to be a home of Malay kings who ruled in the 14th century. Sir Stamford Raffles also built his residence here in 1819.
Singapore Philatelic Museum - You will get unique insights on Singapore's history. See postcards, first-day covers and stamps from the private collections of many famous philatelists.
Peranakan Museum - Learn about the history, culture and heritage of Peranakan. It was set up by Hokkien immigrants to preserve their cultural heritage.
National Museum - The National Museum was designed by J.K. McNair in 1887 in the Neo-Palladian style. Witness the most beautiful glass rotunda, elegant Palladian motifs and fish-scale zinc tiles.

blocks.text: Marina Bay is a prominent waterfront area which is famous for its cultural landmarks, entertainment hubs and beautiful display of the city's skyline. If you are visiting here, then explore-

items: Marina Bay Sands - It is a beautiful luxury resort with three towers which connect Sand Sky Park. It features a casino, luxury hotel, high-end boutiques, restaurants, nightclubs, bars and convention facilities.

Red Dot Design Museum - It's a perfect place to explore for creative souls in Singapore for product innovation, art, technology and global design trends. It is run by a German body that presents the prestigious Red Dot Award.
Gardens by the Bay - Embrace the beauty of this futuristic marvel with giant super trees, cloud forest conservatories and flower domes.
Merlion Park - It's the best place to capture pics with your loved ones in the beautiful backdrop of the Marina Bay skyline.

blocks.text: It's a place where Singapore's modern history began. If you take a trip along the river, you 'll see beautiful colonial-era bridges, state buildings and conservation shophouses.

A river cruise is the best way to explore the iconic sights along the banks. It will be a 30-minute cruise in an electric bumboat. You will get a chance to click some of the most beautiful landmarks, such as

items: The Esplanade Theatre on the Bay

blocks.text: Every season in Singapore has its own charm. Ideally there is no best time to visit Singapore, as you will find something to do in every season. Let's know in detail-

It's perfect to plan a fun-filled holiday trip to Singapore with family. You can beat the heat by exploring attractions like Jewel Changi, SEA Aquarium and Universal Studios. You will also get a chance to see National Day celebrations on August 9 and food festivals.

Isn't it interesting that winter and monsoon seasons overlap in Singapore? This means you will be able to enjoy cool weather with frequent rain showers at the same time. These months are very good for sightseeing and festive celebrations such as Christmas, Chinese New Year and New Year. These months are also the peak tourism months, so book your flights and hotels in advance.

These months are also perfect for cultural tours and leisure walks. You can enjoy sightseeing in Kampong Glam, Little India and Tiong Bahru. Also, you will get a chance to see the beauty of Chinatown as it will be lit up for the Mid-Autumn Festival.

Indian citizens will be required to obtain a tourist visa to travel to Singapore. You can do the visa process online or through reputable visa agents. My Quick Trippers also assists in the visa application process. To get a visa, you need these documents.

items: A valid passport of at least six months
Passport-size photo with a white background
Confirmed return tickets and hotel bookings
Bank Statements, Salary Slips or IT Returns
Student ID (if applicable), Employment or Business Letter

Pick up time is flexible for Delhi sightseeing Tour. As per your convenience time we can arrange pick up services from Railway station, from any hotel or residence that located in Delhi or the national capital region.
Monument open timing for Delhi sightseeing Tour :

Delhi Monuments open from sunrise to sunset. Our Driver/ Guide will update you with the exact timings of the monuments in Delhi. During summer time people start early Delhi tour because of day time is very hot weather.
Tips for the first-time travelers to the Delhi sightseeing Tour:

We suggest our customers to enjoy the street foods of Delhi during a day trip. The best Delhi street foods are served in the Chandni Chowk market. Rickshaw ride will be a great enjoyment in narrow lanes and centuries old residence of the Chandni Chowk market. One can visit the Spice Market in Old Delhi popularly known as Khari Baoli. Khari Baoli’s market shopkeepers speak Hindi/English language. So you will not face any language bar there in the Delhi markets. Evening you can plan to go for Sound and Light show at Red Fort or Old Fort. Boat riding, cycle tour and heritage walk in old will be a great idea during Delhi day trip.
Best time for Delhi sightseeing tour

It is said that Delhi doesn’t have it’s own weather. City Delhi is completely effected by neighboring states. In the winter season when snow falls starts at Himalayan range, Delhi gets colder. In the summer season heat wave from Rajasthan makes Delhi warmer. During winter season Delhi average temperature stay between 4 – 18 degree Celsius. While in the summer mercury goes up to 45 degree Celsius. That is why we suggest to take Delhi sightseeing tour between October to March are the best time. Since Delhi is the capital city of republic India so it has visitors round the year. When someone plan to visit make sure that one day is not enough to see all the places of Delhi. Two days tour of Delhi is the best options but one can decide as per his convenience.

items: Sun glass and hat specially when someone travel in the summer season
Camera to shoot some memorable pictures
Keep change money or cards during Delhi Day Tour
Hand Sanitizer is one of the most necessary item
Get an umbrella for monsoon and summer season
Carry your original passports to get discount at the Monuments entry fee that is applicable on SAARC countries travelers
A diary and pen is good to make notes for students or who loves the history

For upscale marketing in Delhi traveler can find options in Khan Market, M Block Market Greater Kailash and South Extension market. Handicrafts and jewelry markets are available in Delhi sightseeing tour. Ambience Mall Vasant Kunj and Saket Select City walk malls are quite popular among the tourists. Tourists love to go Janpath market but avoid to travelling very crowed area. People also visit Atta Market in Noida and Gurugram for shopping.
Dinning option in Delhi Tour package:

A travel package is not only you visit the main attractions of the particular city, but it is also to enjoy the delicious cuisine of the city. Delhi Tour Package offers many dining options from an economical budget to luxury options. Delhi is also famous for street foods like Chandni Chowk and Karol Bagh. For a mid-scale budget, one can taste at many restaurants available at Panadara Road near the India gate or Karim’s for Kabab. For a high budget range, one can look for The Great Kabab Factory, a world-famous Bukhara restaurant in the ITC Maurya hotel. Besides being known for its geographical diversity, the country shows diversity in almost every aspect like culture, language, food, and also flora and fauna found in different regions of the country. blocks.text: India, a land of ancient history, rich culture and age-old traditions is also home to some of the most amazing and soul-stirring pilgrim tours. All these yatra journeys are spread across all throughout the landscape of India making it one of the most spiritual destinations in the world. These pilgrimages to the home of the gods and goddesses ensure that you have one of the most rejuvenating times here. Designed to suit your needs and crafted keeping in mind the best for you these tours are incredibly sacred and unique. A peaceful time here is guaranteed.

Witness the glories of Hinduism by going on these Hindu tours. Explore the deeply seated religion in this old nation which will easily be one of the most refreshing experiences that you will ever have in your life. Book your Hindu tour as per your need right away.

India is the birthplace of Buddhism which can be experienced through one of the several Buddhist Tours. From visiting the birthplace of Gautam Buddha to his place of Mahaparinirvana and enlightenment, you will be taken across some of the richest jewels of Buddhism in the world.

A honeymoon tour in India will take you across some of the most magnificent and memorable landscape in india. What better way to start a new life together than visiting some of the most unique destinations ranging from beaches, wildlife, untouched beauty and unique experiences. From the thriving forests of the north to the serene beaches of the south and from the romantic moonlit nights in kutch to the adventure thrill of the east we have packages available for everyone. The packages offered by My Quick Trippers are tailor made to make your romantic getaway a peaceful and tension free experience. Witness the beauty of nature, memorable sunsets and create lifetime memories.

India is a diverse land with innumerable places to explore. However if you want to discover the majestic subcontinent then you can do so by planning your India tour by region. Experience the real culture and traditions of the people here and know what makes India a unique journey.

Visit the land of colour, gods and goddesses and remarkable history from one region to the next. From the northern Himalayan regions to the southern edges and from the Kutch on the west to the beaches of the east. A glorious time for you in Different parts of India awaits so book your travel package for Indian regions now and have one of the most memorable vacations.
Q. Is it safe to travel in India?

A. Yes. India is a very safe place to travel. The people are welcoming and humble and are always ready to help out in any situation. People within India always go for solo trips and foreign travellers coming in India from outside have no problem of safety in case of travel.
Q. Can I travel to India with my kids?

A. India is a great place to travel with the kids. The colors, foods, culture and activities will be an eye opening experience for them. You can go to Manali, Rajasthan, and Kerala or somewhere in the northeast. India will incite a feeling of curiosity in their young minds.
Q. When is the best time to travel to India?

A. It entirely depends on what your travel plans entail. It is mainly because there is a wide range of different weather conditions in different parts of the country throughout the year. If you are looking for some Himalayan winter, then the months of September to March is ideal.

If it is the amazing summer tropics you are looking for, or experience some Indian beach life, then remember to avoid the rainy seasons and explore those places during the months of January to June. These are also the months where you can check out some impeccable wildlife.
Q. What is the internet situation in India?

A. Internet connection and mobile data on a local number is easily available anywhere in India, especially in the major towns and cities. However, just like in any other remote place in the world, internet connection is lost and there is no internet or even mobile phone connection in the remotest regions like on the hills or deep in some national park or a forest. This is because the hills and trees act as a barrier to the phone and internet signals.
Q. Is it safe to travel to India alone as a girl?

A. It doesn’t matter if you are a girl or a boy, India is safe for everyone. You just have to dress up appropriately, stay away from shady and seedy places and not roam around at wee hours. These are some of the general rules anyone follows while travelling to a foreign country.
Q. Which is the best place to travel in India for a first timer?

A. If you are travelling to India for the first time, then you have a lot of thinking to do. The plethora of options here is magnanimous and will leave you astounded. This traveller’s delight should be on everyone’s bucket list. To start off you can divide the entire country in 4 parts and decide which you would enjoy exploring more and suits your taste.

You can go to the north for some hiking trips, spiritual Hindu pilgrimage of Char Dham Yatra, checking out the Himalayan way of life, or experience camping, trekking, and going to remote places tucked a way on the mountains. In the west, you can go beach hopping from Gujarat to Mumbai, Goa, and many others. You can also go to the northeast to experience the living Root Bridge, Nohkalikai Waterfalls, and Dawki River along with tea gardens exploration.

In the south you will be spoilt for choices, from the backwaters of Kerala to the iconic temples, delicious food, and amazing lakes. Central or the heart of India is home to some amazing wildlife culture like in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
Q. Can I drink alcohol in India?

A. Alcohol drinking is allowed in India. Except for Gujarat, Bihar, Mizoram, Nagaland and Lakshadweep. There are wine and beer shops available if you wish to buy or you can go to one of the numerous cafes, bars and restaurants that offer this facility. Remember public drinking is prohibited.
Q. I am weak in English and don’t know Hindi. Will it be difficult for me to travel to India then?

A. English is known in India and almost everyone understands it but not a lot of them speak it. If you don’t know English then it would benefit you to learn a couple of common phrases and words that everyone understands. This would make your travels in India much easier.

If that is not possible then, it would be a good idea to book a travel package from a trusted agency that will also provide you with a guide who is good in English. This will be the best option for you if you are still unsure.
Q. I have heard lots of stories about people getting sick by eating contaminated food and drinking water. Is it true? What can i do to avoid this situation?

A. It sure is safe. However, do not drink directly from the tap, instead drink filtered water. Foods available in cafes and restaurants are safe to eat, without a doubt. Remember that Indian foods require the use of spices that your stomach may not agree with, but it differs from person to person.
Q. How should I dress while visiting a religious or a holy site?
A. There are no stringent rules regarding what you need to wear at a holy place of worship. However, Indians are deeply religious and very sensitive when it comes to clothing at a place of worship.
You can wear a traditional Salwar Kameez or go for Jeans and Kurta or Jeans and T-shirt. Remember to keep your knees and shoulders covered to show respect to the culture and tradition of India.
Q. I am travelling with my partner to India, where should I go for a romantic getaway?

A. Some of the most popular and most amazing holiday getaway destinations in India include, Shillong, Cherrapunji, Manali, Kerala and Goa. Meghalaya is also a good option if you are looking for some time away from the crowd. Other than that, it entirely depends on you and your partner’s likings while travelling.
Q. Do Indian ATMs accept foreign cards? What is the cash situation there?
A. There are ATMs available everywhere throughout the country. You will never end up in a cashless situation in India. It allows a withdrawal of around rupees 10,000/- per day.
Q. What are the best things to buy in India?

A. India is a unique country offering lots of traditional and ethnic souvenirs which are unique to every region. To be more specific, you can look for Indian textiles, herbs and spices. Ayurveda skincare and hair care products are also popular. Traditional handicrafts, artifacts and sculptures of gods and famous places is something you can buy as a gift for yourself or for someone you love.
Q. What is the cheapest airport or city to fly into?

A. Mumbai and Delhi international airports are 2 of the cheapest airport options where people from the USA or any other countries can enter India. Another thing is that, there are just a couple of international airports in India and Delhi is one of the most popular one.
Q. Which festival should I experience in India?

A. When it comes to festivals India is super diverse. The same festival is celebrated in different styles in different parts of the country. You can plan your travels around Holi or Diwali. Holi is the festival of colors and Diwali is the festival of lights. These are 2 of the most famous festivals in India and are celebrated with great enthusiasm.
Q. How do I travel around from city to city?

A. Once you reach India, getting from one city to the other is very easy and inexpensive. The cities are connected to each other through extensive roadways, railways and flights. One of the best and inexpensive ways is to travel by trains. Another way is to travel by flights wherever an airport is available. Buses are also a great option but they are kind of time taking. You can choose however you wish to travel, depending on your travel budget.

A. India has a population of over 1.2 billion with tourists filtering in from all over the world. So yes, it will be crowded. Not to mention the loss of your personal space, especially in the market places and tourist places.
Q. Which is the most adventurous place to visit in India?

A. If it is a pure adventure you are looking for, then visit north India. Here you will have the option of choosing from going for Bungee Jumping to Rafting, Hiking, Trekking, Camping, Mountaineering, Kayaking and even hardcore mountaineering if that is what you are into.
People on the hills are extremely welcoming, warm and humble. It makes travelling solo extremely easy and simple.
Q. What should I avoid in India?

A. For a safe and delightful, memorable trip to India, avoid these things - don’t wear shoes inside a temple, do not wear skimpy clothes, don’t show affection in public places, don’t touch anyone with feet (it is considered impure), do not think of eating beef (cows are auspicious), so not stick to the popular tourist places, you can go offbeat as well!
Q. I want to have a soul searching experience in India, like eat, pray, love. What do you recommend?

A. First off, remember to keep your hearts and minds open. It may be a bit overwhelming for you, but remember, that is what India is all about. This is one place which is devoid of judgements. From unpredictable weather conditions to delicious local foods and amazing people anywhere you decide to go will be one of a kind.

You can go to one of the many ashrams in Rishikesh. Take up a yoga or Vipassana course there or in Ladakh and Spiti. Go on walking trails in the streets of Uttarakhand, Himachal, and Rajasthan. There is so much going on everywhere that walking will provide a deep immersive experience, just like eat, pray, love.
Q. I don’t want to travel on a budget. I want a luxurious Indian experience. What should i do and where should i go?

A. Travelling in luxury to India is an experience of a lifetime. Palace on wheels should definitely not be missed out on. Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore are your best bets for getting the most exclusive and 5-star hotels along with top notch services and immaculate amenities.
Q. Where can I have the best wildlife experience in India?

A. India is blessed with a varied landscape which is home to a plethora of flora, fauna, insects and birds. For jeep safaris and nature walks you can go to Jim Corbett National Park, Ranthambore National Park, Gir National Park, Nanda Devi Bio Reserve, Marine National Park and many others.
It is a great way to start your holiday in India, especially if you are travelling with your family and kids.
Q. What are some important items I should definitely pack for travelling to India?

A. First of all while travelling to India, remember to keep an open mind and heart and forget the idea of personal space. There are some things in India you cannot just do without and it may be difficult for you to find depending on where you are travelling. These are the things you should definitely pack - charcoal tablets, toilet paper, electrolyte, ear plugs, cable locks, convertor, sunscreen and insect repellant.
Q. What are some medical precautions I should take while travelling in India?

A. If you are a foreign national, then you should remember to get your vaccinations done, as recommended by CDC and WHO, prior to travelling in India. These include - Hepatitis A, hepatitis B, typhoid, cholera, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis, rabies, meningitis, polio, measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), Tdap (tetanus, diphtheria and pertussis), chickenpox, shingles, pneumonia and influenza.
Make a small medical pouch containing pain medications, anti-diarrhea medicines and any other medicine you think that you may need after getting proper advice from your doctor.

Best Time to Visit Kerala from Chennai
The best time to visit Kerala is from September to February. The weather is pleasant with less humidity. It's a great time to enjoy the backwaters, beaches, hills, and other beautiful places.
During this time, Kerala celebrates many festivals, and visitors enjoy lots of fun and happiness.

Summer (March to May) - Summer in Kerala is from March to May. It gets quite hot and humid, with temperatures between 32 to 38°C. It's not the best time for outdoor fun, but if you enjoy warm weather you might like it.

Monsoon (June to September) - During this time, Kerala experiences heavy rainfall and temperatures go between 24°C and 30°C. The rain makes the place green but it may cause travel delays. Still, many travelers enjoy the monsoon weather.
Winter (October to February) - From October to February, the weather in Kerala is cool and pleasant, with temperatures from 20 to 24 degrees Celsius and low humidity.
Most Famous Tourist Places in Kerala
There are lots of amazing places to visit in Kerala that every traveler should experience once in their life-

Kumarakom is a peaceful village near the big Vembanad Lake. It is famous for its beautiful backwaters and green surroundings. You can enjoy relaxing boat rides here and see many kinds of birds if you love nature. The calm water and fresh air make it a perfect place to take a break from busy city life.
Time Required to Explore- 2 to 3 days

Munnar is a beautiful hill station in Kerala. It is famous for its tea gardens, lovely valleys, waterfalls and many kinds of animals. Munnar has a rare flower called Neelakurinji that blooms only once every 12 years. During the bloom season, the hills are covered in blue flowers that makes the place truly magical to visitors.
Time Required to Explore- 3 to 4 days

Alleppey is well known for its peaceful canals surrounded by palm trees. These canals are called backwaters. There are many Ayurvedic centers here where visitors can relax and refresh themselves while enjoying the calm surroundings. The Alleppey beach is very popular for its unique beauty and should not be missed.
Time Required to Explore- 3 to 4 days
How Many Kilometers from Chennai- 734 km

Wayanad is a green hill area known for its beautiful forests and cool weather. It is also famous for old caves and waterfalls that are perfect for adventure lovers. Many rare animals, like the shy Malabar civet and Lion-tailed macaque, live here. That's why Wayanad is great for people who love wildlife and photography.
Time Required to Explore- 2 to 3 days
How Many Kilometers from Chennai- 609 km
How to Reach Kerala from Chennai
From Chennai to Kerala travelers have many options like trains, buses and cars. You can choose one that fits your schedule and budget-

By Flight - Many travelers prefer flights to save time. Kerala has four airports and almost all domestic airlines operate daily nonstop flights between Chennai and Kerala. You can fly to Cochin (Kochi), Trivandrum (Thiruvananthapuram), Calicut (Kozhikode) or Kannur airports in Kerala.

By Train - Trains from Chennai to Kerala are comfortable and budget-friendly. Many trains run every day from Chennai to cities in Kerala like Ernakulam and Trivandrum. Journey usually takes around 12 hours.
By Road - There are several options like buses, cabs, or driving your own car. These travel options go directly from Chennai to various cities in Kerala.

Q1. What is the Nainital to Corbett National Park Distance?
Ans. Nainital is around 130–140 km from Corbett National Park, and it takes roughly 3–4 hours to drive, depending on traffic and road conditions.
Q2. What is the best time to visit Nainital and Jim Corbett?
Ans. The best time to explore Nainital and Corbett is March to June for nice weather and wildlife spotting, or September to November for cooler, clearer and less crowded days.
Q3. What animals can we see on a Corbett jeep safari?
Ans. While visiting, you can see tigers, elephants, leopards, deer, and different birds. Seeing these animals in the forest is a wonderful experience.
Q4. Can we customize the tour package?
Ans. Absolutely! Tour packages can be customized. You can extend your stay, choose different hotels or add extra sightseeing places so the trip matches your personal interests and comfort.
Q5. Are road conditions good between Nainital and Corbett?
Ans. Main roads are usually well maintained but in the hills some areas are narrow. Take your time while driving and enjoy the journey safely.

At the beginning of 2026, Bali’s tourism continued to grow strongly, building on nearly 7 million international visitors in 2025. This steady rise reinforces its position as a leading global tourist destination.

What attracts travellers to Bali is its variety of unique experiences, which are one of a kind. For instance, visiting Trunyan village would be one of the most enchanting experiences as it is very famous for its unique burial traditions. The mesmerizing Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple is actually a storytelling performance of Ramayana in Balinese style. Do indulge in the Bali traditional dance and cuisine.

items: Witness the Subak Irrigation Technique. It's a technique unique to Bali. This ancient irrigation system has nurtured Bali's rice terraces.
See the volcanic black sand beaches like Amed and Lovina. These rare coastal landscapes will blow your mind away. The Bali nightlife and beach clubs are something to die for!
Try Kopi Luwak (Civet Coffee), it's the rarest coffee produced through a unique process which involves civet cats.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Sri Lanka

In Sri Lanka, every season has its own charm. Trips to this beautiful island at different times of the year offer different experiences. Every time you visit it, you'll discover a new facet of this country. The trip time depends on the traveler's preferences for places and experiences. Here's a detailed overview of the best time to visit Sri Lanka -
Peak Tourism Months: December to April

items: If you love the beaches of South Sri Lanka or the West coast beaches, then this is a perfect time to travel to Sri Lanka with family for a relaxing tour. You can also explore hill country like Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, and Ella.

The weather will be pleasant with delightful rains and mist, especially in the afternoons. You also get to experience the vibrant celebrations of Christmas (late December) and Tamil New Year (mid-April).

blocks.text: Shoulder Months: April, September, and October

items: If you want to explore all the major destinations in Sri Lanka, then these months are best due to fewer crowds.
During this time, you will see the beauty of Udawalawe National Park, Polonnaruwa, Anuradhapura, Trincomalee, and Galle at its peak.
Monsoon is the best time to explore Sri Lanka for nature lovers.
It is the best time to explore the eastern coast beaches of Sri Lanka and many cultural events in the north.
You can enjoy festivals like Esala Perahera (July–Aug), Poson Poya (June), Nallur Festival (July) and explore Yala National Park, Arugam Bay, Passekudah, Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil (Jaffna), Colombo.
If you hate crowds and want to enjoy a quiet trip, opt for a Sri Lanka holiday package during October to November.
The weather is overall pleasant with occasional rainfall.

With fewer tourists, you get to explore the mesmerizing beauty of Sri Lanka in a much more relaxed and uncrowded environment. If you want a Sri Lanka trip on a Budget, then check out our best Budget tours for Sri Lanka.

blocks.text: Why You Should Come to Sri Lanka?

Sri Lanka welcomed over 2 million international tourists in 2024, and the momentum continues in 2025-26. Indian tourists contributed over 2,40,000 arrivals in the first half of 2025 alone — making India one of the top source markets for Sri Lanka tourism.

It has become a favorite destination globally due to its rich culture. It offers a blend of scenic beaches, wildlife parks, tea plantations, and traditional art tours, which keep the day of the tourists memorable.
Other Reasons to Visit Sri Lanka

items: Anuradhapura is one of the oldest planned cities in South Asia, with over 2,300 years of recorded Buddhist civilisation. It remains one of the most sacred pilgrimage destinations in Asia and a recognised UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Sri Lanka has kept the genuine Buddha tooth relic with great care. It is one of the best things to explore in Sri Lanka.
You can also witness prehistoric art, which dates back over 2000 years, depicting animal and Buddhist motifs.

For Science lovers or curious travellers, Sri Lanka tourism offers an interesting opportunity, like Whale watching with marine biologists near Mirissa. Those who love to know about Marine biodiversity must experience this once in their lifetime.

If you are an Indian National and planning a trip to Sri Lanka, then it's good news for you. Indian Nationals don't need a Visa to travel to Sri Lanka ; they only need an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) through the official Sri Lanka ETA website .
The ETA is needed for short-term purposes. It is granted for 30 days to an Indian tourist. Double entry facility is also an option from the date of first arrival to Sri Lanka within 30 days.

To apply for an ETA, submit an application form online to the Department of Immigration and Emigration. Pay the required processing fees and submit the application. After submission of the form, you will receive an acknowledgement promptly.
You also need to have a valid passport of not less than 6 months from the date of arrival.
You can extend your ETA up to 6 months at the Immigration Services Centre in Colombo or at the Department of Immigration and Emigration in Battaramulla.
