blocks.text: Places to Visit during the Sri Lanka Trip

A Sri Lanka trip must include an exploration of its stunning beaches, diverse wildlife, and ancient temples. Most Sri Lanka travel packages involve these aspects to give you a rich, fulfilling experience. Here are the top places that must be on your Sri Lanka itinerary :

This is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka and also the largest city here. Colombo is best known for providing cultural experiences through its colonial architecture. Meanwhile, you also get to experience the modern development spread throughout the capital. It's the best of both worlds, really! Top attractions here include:

items: Colombo National Museum: It's an absolute must for history buffs who would like to learn about the island's rich history and culture.
Pettah Market: This market is perfect for collecting souvenirs and purchasing local goods.
Galle Face Green: This urban park provides a gorgeous backdrop for your sunset strolls.
Gangaramaya Temple: This is a Buddhist temple that houses a museum within itself. Tourists admire it for its remarkable architecture.

blocks.text: This city is a serene hub, surrounded by lush green forests. Moreover, it's also a UNESCO World Heritage site and therefore must be included in your Sri Lanka Heritage Tour Package . The best tourist places here are:

items: Temple of the Tooth: This temple holds a very sacred relic of the Buddha and is therefore considered the holiest Buddhist site in the entirety of Sri Lanka.
Kandy Lake: This man-made lake is nestled in the heart of the city. Tourists often saunter around here during the early mornings.

Cultural Show: Don't miss the traditional Kandyan dance here which is native to Sri Lanka. The dance is often accompanied by the drum performance and is a great evening show for the travellers. Many Sri Lanka tour packages include this show in the itinerary.
Royal Botanical Gardens: This is one of the largest and oldest botanical gardens in Asia. Travellers love the orchid collection here.

blocks.text: Sigiriya is an ancient fortress complex on the island. Tourists and even locals are so impressed with this monument that they often label it as the eighth wonder of the world! Top attractions here include:

items: Sigiriya Rock: This rock formation is as high as 200 meters. On top of it lies the palace. Tourists often enjoy climbing the rock and soaking in the panoramic views of gardens and frescoes down below.
Pidurangala Rock: This is another rock formation that provides scenic views. The sunset views from here are otherworldly.

blocks.text: This was once the capital of Sri Lanka in ancient times, and now is a recognized UNESCO World Heritage site! Here, you get to experience the sacred sites and old ruins. It definitely should be included in your Sri Lanka holiday package if you are a history enthusiast. Top Attractions here include:

items: Sri Maha Bodhi Tree: Meet the oldest historically documented tree in the world! This tree is believed to have grown from the original tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment.
Abhayagiri Monastery: This is a huge monastic complex that is as old as two millennia.
Ruwanwelisaya Stupa: This site is especially important if you are a Buddhist pilgrim. This massive Stupa houses the largest collection of Buddhist relics in the whole world.

blocks.text: Located in the central highlands, Ella is a beautiful hill station that has picturesque views and majestic waterfalls. It's also great for tourists who love hiking, as it has long hiking trails. Notable attractions here are:

items: Ella Rock: Get the bird's-eye view of the stunning valleys and tea plantation when you hike on Ella Rock. Many Sri Lanka tour packages include this site as the panoramic views here are to die for.
Nine Arches Bridge: This scenic bridge has a lot to offer to your Sri Lanka trip. Built during the colonial era, it is surrounded by lush greenery and immerses you in a serene atmosphere.
Ravana Falls: Get a rejuvenating dip in this beautiful waterfall. It's a hit with both tourists and locals alike!

blocks.text: Often called 'Little England,' Nuwara Eliya sits at 1,868 metres above sea level and is unlike anywhere else in Sri Lanka. The cool, misty climate, colonial-era bungalows, and vast tea estates feel like a completely different world from the tropical coast. Whether you are doing a beach + hill country combination or simply want to experience Ceylon tea at its source, Nuwara Eliya is essential. Top attractions include:

items: Pedro Tea Estate: One of Sri Lanka's finest tea estates, offering a guided factory tour from leaf to cup — with free tasting at the end. About 2 hours.
Gregory Lake: A serene man-made lake at the heart of town, perfect for a morning walk or a short boating session.
Horton Plains National Park: About 30 km away. Home to 'World's End' — a sheer 870-metre drop with sweeping views of the southern plains on clear mornings.
Victoria Park: A beautifully maintained botanical garden home to many migratory bird species between March and August.

blocks.text: Galle is a coastal city on Sri Lanka's southwest tip, best known for its 17th-century Dutch colonial fort — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk the ramparts at sunset and the Indian Ocean views are unforgettable. The fort's cobblestone lanes have boutique cafes, galleries, and excellent restaurants. Galle combines history and beaches in a way that no other Sri Lankan city does. Top attractions include:

items: Galle Fort: Walk the full perimeter of the fort walls — the lighthouse and the Dutch Reformed Church are the most photographed spots.
Unawatuna Beach: One of Sri Lanka's most beautiful beaches, just 6 km from Galle. Calm, curved bay perfect for swimming and snorkelling.
Galle National Museum: Colonial-era artifacts and local heritage. About 1 hour.

blocks.text: Yala holds the highest density of wild leopards of any protected area in the world. Jeep safaris operate twice daily — at dawn (5:30–6:00 AM) and afternoon (3:00 PM). Beyond leopards, Yala is home to elephants, sloth bears, saltwater crocodiles, and over 200 bird species. Best visited between February and July when wildlife activity peaks. Most of our Sri Lanka Heritage Tour and Group Tour packages include a Yala safari stop.
Things to Do during the Sri Lanka Trip

There is a plethora of activities you can do in Sri Lanka. Whether you are an adventure seeker, a history buff, or a nature lover, you're in for a treat when in Sri Lanka. Here are a few things you must include in your Sri Lanka tour package:

items: Sri Lanka is a treasure trove of cultural and historical landmarks with a number of temples, cities, and monuments to discover.
Some must-visit sites include Sigiriya Rock Fortress, Temple of the Sacred Tooth, Anuradhapura, Dambulla Cave Temple, Galle Fort, and Polonnaruwa.
The central highlands of the island are famous for their lush tea plantations. While you are on your Sri Lanka trip, do not miss the tea factory tour.
You can go see how Ceylon tea is made from scratch and sample the finest teas.
You can visit the Dambatenne Tea Factory in Haputale or the Pedro Tea Estate in Nuwara Eliya for a top-notch experience.

blocks.text: The island is famous for its beaches. Some popular tourist beaches here are Unawatuna, Mirissa, Arugam Bay, Bentota, and Nilaveli.

items: Sri Lanka is home to various national parks and reserves where you can enjoy wildlife.
Some popular parks are Yala National Park, Sinharaja Rainforest, Wilpattu National Park, Udawalawe National Park, and Minneriya National Park.

blocks.text: Sri Lanka is an adventure lover's paradise. You can enjoy plenty of adventure activities here, like hiking (at Horton Plains National Park and Baker's Falls), white-water rafting (at Kitulgala), and hot-air ballooning (at Galle).

Between November and April, the waters off Mirissa are home to Blue Whales — the largest animals ever to have existed on Earth. Sperm Whales and pods of Spinner Dolphins are also regularly spotted. Morning boat departures operate at 6:30 AM from Mirissa harbour. Tours run for approximately 4–5 hours with licensed operators. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience that many travellers rate as the highlight of their entire Sri Lanka trip.
7. Scenic Train Ride — Kandy to Ella

The 7-hour train journey from Kandy to Ella through Sri Lanka's central highlands is consistently rated one of the most beautiful train rides in the world. Passing through misty mountains, tea estates, waterfalls, and jungle valleys, it is an experience worth planning your itinerary around. Reserve a seat in the observation car in advance — it fills up fast during peak season. Sit on the left side when travelling from Kandy for the best valley views.
8. Visit a Tea Factory in Nuwara Eliya

The central highlands produce world-famous Ceylon tea. Both the Pedro Tea Estate in Nuwara Eliya and the Dambatenne Tea Factory in Haputale offer guided tours showing the full production process — from picking and withering to rolling, fermenting, and drying — ending with a free tasting. About 1.5 to 2 hours per visit. A fascinating experience even if you are not a tea drinker.
What to Eat during the Sri Lanka Trip

Sri Lankan cuisine is a delicious mix of flavors like spicy, tangy, and aromatic. The food is mainly centered on fresh vegetables, meat, seafood, and rice. Here are some of the dishes you must try on your Sri Lanka trip:

This is the staple diet of the island. The meal consists of a big serving of steam rice along with a number of small servings of curries (either vegetable, dhal, fish, or meat curry). Often these are supplemented with condiments like pickled vegetables and spicy sambals.

Hoppers are rice flour pancakes that are soft in the center and crispy around the edges. They are eaten as a breakfast or dinner and often served with dhal or lamb curry. The hoppers come in three varieties — plain hopper, sweet hopper (sweetened with palm sugar), and egg hopper (cooked with egg at the center).
This is a common street food prepared by stir-frying Godamba roti with meat, eggs, and vegetables. It is cooked on a griddle and served with a dipping sauce to make a savory and spicy dish.
This traditional Sri Lankan dish is made with fresh local fish like mackerel or tuna. To give it a spicy and tangy flavor, it is cooked with tamarind and Sri Lankan spices.
This delicious meal is made of vegetables, curry (generally meat curry), and rice and is then wrapped in a banana leaf and steamed.

Sri Lanka's signature dessert — a steamed custard pudding made with coconut milk, eggs, and kithul palm jaggery. Silky in texture, subtly spiced, and mildly sweet. Found on the menu at almost every good Sri Lankan restaurant. Don't leave the country without trying it at least once.

Delicate steamed noodle cakes made from rice flour, served with coconut sambol and dhal curry. A popular breakfast and dinner across Sri Lanka, especially in the central highlands and coastal towns. Lighter than regular hoppers and a favourite among first-time visitors to Sri Lankan food.
Sri Lanka produces some genuinely excellent things worth bringing home. Not just souvenirs — quality items you will actually use and enjoy.

items: Ceylon Tea: Buy directly from estate shops or trusted brands like MLESNA and Dilmah. Available in loose leaf and gift-pack formats. Choose from single-estate teas or classic Ceylon blends.
Ceylon Cinnamon: Real Ceylon cinnamon is softer, lighter, and sweeter than the cassia variety common in India. A meaningful and inexpensive gift. Best bought in Pettah Market or spice shops.

Gemstones: Sri Lanka is one of the world's leading producers of blue sapphires, cat's eye, and moonstones. Purchase only from certified dealers — look for the Sri Lanka Gem & Jewellery Association certification. Avoid roadside shops.
Batik & Handloom Fabrics: Beautiful hand-printed textiles. Fixed-price government stores (Laksala) are reliable for quality. Bargaining is possible in local markets.
Wooden Masks & Crafts: Traditional Kolam masks from Ambalangoda are distinctive and make excellent wall decor. Look for handmade pieces over machine-pressed ones.
Ayurvedic Products: Sri Lanka has a strong Ayurvedic tradition. Herbal oils, soaps, and creams made from local ingredients are widely available and affordable.
Pettah Market, Colombo — for spices, fabrics, everyday goods
Odel Shopping Mall, Colombo — for branded clothing and souvenirs
Kandy City Centre — for gems and handcrafts
Galle Fort boutiques — for premium artisan goods
Laksala Government Handicrafts — reliable fixed-price quality
Local tea factory shops — for estate-fresh Ceylon tea

blocks.text: Colombo has a lively nightlife scene — rooftop bars, beach clubs, and live music venues. The Galle Face area and Colombo Fort neighbourhood have the highest concentration of spots. Most close around 2 AM. Galle's fort area has excellent wine bars open late. Mirissa and Arugam Bay have relaxed beach shack atmospheres, especially during peak season.
Major Festivals — Plan Your Trip Around These

rows: Sri Lanka's most spectacular event — elephant parade, fire dancers, drummers honouring the Sacred Tooth Relic. Hotels in Kandy book up months ahead.
Celebrates birth and enlightenment of Buddha. Lantern displays, free food stalls, and illuminated floats across the country.
Commemorates the introduction of Buddhism to Sri Lanka. Huge lantern displays and pilgrimage walks.
Traditional New Year with rituals, sweets, and family gatherings. Public holidays across the country.
Major Hindu festival at Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil — colourful processions, devotional music, and rituals.
Festival of Lights celebrated by Hindu communities across Sri Lanka.

blocks.text: How to Reach Sri Lanka from India
Sri Lanka is one of the easiest international destinations to reach from India — no long-haul flight, no complicated connections. Just a short hop across the Palk Strait.
Direct flights operate from several Indian cities to Colombo's Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB):

items: One-stop options: Travellers from Pune, Ahmedabad, or Kolkata can connect via Mumbai or Chennai — total travel time around 5–8 hours including layover.
Booking tip: Flights from Chennai and Kochi are typically the most affordable. Book 6–8 weeks in advance during peak season (December–March) for the best fares.

blocks.text: A ferry service connecting Nagapattinam (Tamil Nadu) to Kankesanthurai (northern Sri Lanka) is available for travellers who prefer sea travel or are exploring northern Sri Lanka. Check current schedules before planning as availability may vary.
Once you land in Colombo, navigating Sri Lanka is straightforward. Here are your main transport options:

items: Private AC Vehicle (included in our packages): The most comfortable option for inter-city travel. All our packages include a dedicated private vehicle with driver — no public transport hassles, flexible stops, and air-conditioned comfort throughout.
Scenic Train: The Kandy–Ella route is world-famous. Book reserved seats (especially the observation car) well in advance during peak season — they sell out fast.
Tuk-Tuk: Perfect for short distances within towns. Always agree on the fare before you get in. Average city ride: equivalent to ₹30–80.
PickMe App: Sri Lanka's equivalent of Ola/Uber. Reliable in Colombo and major tourist towns. Download before your trip.
Bus: Most economical but not recommended for long distances if you are on a schedule. Suitable for short hops between nearby towns.

blocks.text: Sri Lanka Travel Tips for a Memorable Vacation
Here are some practical as well as destination-specific travel tips to make your Lanka trip fun-filled with your family and friends-

items: Try Unique Places: Explore all the unique places and try different activities to enjoy the best of Sri Lanka Tourism . Your itinerary should have a blend of history , culture, adventure, nature, and spiritual trips.
Don't miss the Fun: Don't miss the Mirissa adventure tour if you are in Sri Lanka. You will learn very unique and interesting insights into Marine biology.
Village tours for authentic experiences: You can also explore Sri Lankan villages and experience their lifestyle and culture for an enriching Sri Lanka trip.

Pack Wisely: Sri Lanka enjoys tropical weather, so pack your clothes accordingly. For temple hopping, you must cover your shoulders and knees. Modesty is the best policy when you are on a spiritual tour. If there is any sacred offering, receive it with both hands to show respect.
Hotels near main destination: For nature and wildlife enthusiasts, book hotels, lodges, or guesthouses near the main destination.
Sample Cuisine Wisely: Not everything will suit your taste buds in Sri Lanka. So, sample the cuisines wisely. Avoid too many spicy foods.

When to visit: You can avoid the monsoon if your priority is not a specific trip. Consider December - March the best time to go west, south, and hill country in Sri Lanka. For east tours, consider April to September.
Affordable Calls: In Sri Lanka, the major local SIM card providers are Dialog and Mobitel. So, buy a local SIM from city outlets or airports to make your calls and text messages affordable.

Currency & ATMs: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR) is the local currency. ATMs are widely available in Colombo and major tourist towns. Carry some cash for national park entry fees, smaller towns, and temple donations. Most hotels and larger restaurants accept credit cards.

Dress Code at Temples: Carrying a light scarf or shawl is more reliable than relying on temple-provided sarongs. Remove footwear before entering any temple premises. Never turn your back to a Buddha statue for a photo.

Book Yala Safari in Advance: During peak season (December–April), Yala National Park jeeps fill up days in advance. Do not assume you can book on arrival. Our packages include pre-booked safari slots to avoid disappointment. Note: Yala briefly closes in September each year — check dates when planning.

blocks.text: Is Sri Lanka Expensive for Indian Travellers

A luxury trip to Sri Lanka will cost around INR 2,00,000, which will include top-tier hotels, private tours, fine dining, and other exclusive activities, but it is also affordable for budget travellers. For Indian travellers who are budget-conscious, the trip to Sri Lanka will cost around INR 75,000. You can book our all-inclusive Sri Lanka Budget Tour Packages for the best value.

For affordable stays : Look for guesthouses, lodges and homestays near prime locations.
Eat Like a Native: Try local eateries as they offer food at the cheapest rates.
Plan low-cost activities : Visiting beaches, exploring ancient temples, or hiking will not cost you much.

Travel via Chennai or Kochi: Flights from these cities to Colombo are often ₹5,000–₹10,000 cheaper than from Delhi or Mumbai. If you are flexible about your departure city, this simple choice can make a significant difference to your total trip budget.

blocks.text: Taiwan has been a favorite destination for tourists on Tour Packages since long time. Taiwan is called ‘Ilha Formosa’ which means ‘Beautiful Isle’ in Portuguese which it really is, this island is adorned by soaring mountain peaks covered in mist and lush green forests with magnificent coastal land and basins. Spread in over 36 thousand sq. kilometer this island has population of more than 22 million. People of Taiwan have preserved their culture and heritage but have also kept themselves abreast with modernism, this is evident at once when one steps in this country on Tour Packages and which makes this even more enjoyable destination.

In the cities of Taiwan visitors on Tour Package comes across skyscrapers and malls and other commercial facilities which herald Taiwan’s economic status but ubiquitous pagodas, ancient temples and well preserved buildings show the deep roots of past and culture in the hearts of Taiwanese people. The country side has some breathtakingly beautiful waterfalls, lakes, landscapes and dense forests which make it a fascinating place for tourists on Taiwan Tour Packages.

Taipei is the capital city of Taiwan and one of the most modern cities of Asia. Yangmingshan National Park is the prime attraction of this city for tourists as this place has vast mountain range which overlooks the city and add up to the beauty of this park. This park is a peaceful place and has variety of flora and fauna to enchant visitors on Taiwan Travel Packages, there are numerous hot springs in the park which provide soothing time away from hustle and bustle of the city.

National Palace Museum in Taipei is another destination visited by tourist on Taiwan Holiday Packages, this is museum and an art gallery, and is believed to possess maximum number of Chinese artifacts and artwork in the world. Some stunning exhibits of this place are carved olive-stone boat, Jade cabbage and painting of ‘One hundred Horses’. Dragon and Tiger pagodas in the city of Kaohsiung is another attraction for tourists on Taiwan Tour Packages, it is a seven tiered architecture with paintings of heaven, hell and 24 obedient sons. These pagodas lie in Lotus Pond accompanied by Tung Confucius Temple and Chi Ming pagoda.

Green Island is just at 10-12 minutes air ride away from Taipei and has beautiful beaches with fascinating coral reefs, rich flora and fauna and steep seaside cliffs. Aquatic life of Green Island is rich and famous and glass bottom boat ride make it an enjoyable place on Taiwan Travel Packages. Fort Santo Domingo is a historical site built in 16th century at the coastal town of Tamsui. This fort has interesting history and was won and destroyed quite a few times, today it has a museum and is an interesting place to visit on Taiwan Holiday Packages.

Sun Moon Lake in Nantau is another popular place to visit on Taiwan Tour Package, this lake covering an area a shade less than 8 Sq. KM is a mesmerizing place. The poetic setting of this lake and variety of birds that are seen around this lake make it a romantic and enchanting place for visitors. Close to lake is an area which is recognized as habitation of an Aboriginal Tribe called as Thao tribe.

blocks.text: The Grand city of Jodhpur reverberates tales of the distant past in the barrenness of the desert. Jodhpur located in Rajasthan is popularly known as “The Sun City”. It is called so because it remains bright and sunny almost throughout the year. This city was founded by Rao Jodha (a chief) in 1459, and thus got its name Jodhpur. Previously this city was known as Marwar. It is the second largest city in Rajasthan. Jodhpur was partitioned into two divisions, namely the old city and the new city. A 10 km long wall surrounds the old city. Tourists from all over the world used to come and witness this sculpted city of Rajasthan located in the commercial heart of the city. Every element in Jodhpur reflects the deep architectural grandeur and great Rajputana history. Here you can witness the Mehrangarh Fort and the grand sandstone palace of Umaid Bhawan.

Jodhpur offers a lot of tourist destinations namely the Mehrangarh Fort, Umaid Bhavan Palace, Jaswant Thada, and Rai ka Bag Palace. The Mehrangarh Fort in Jodhpur soaring to about 125 meters offers an amazing architectural spot to be visited by travelers. With many graceful palaces, forts, and temples, Jodhpur brings alive the remarkable historical greatness, art, music, and tradition of people that have failed to allure travelers, since time immortal. The Jodhpur lifestyle is simple and traditional, displaying the royal India tradition. The people in Jodhpur wear costumes that are artistically designed and fabricated. The colorful festivals and the rich culture have always attracted tourists from around the entire globe. One of the important festivals is the Marwar Festival which is celebrated yearly and is one such impressive bonanza.

The Balsamand Lake and Gardens in Jodhpur is an idyllic places for excursions. Jodhpur in Rajasthan is also home to many fascinating temples. The Sun Temple, Kali temple, Sachiya Mata Temple, etc. are some of the prominent temples in Rajasthan. blocks.text: Odisha is known as the soul of India for good reason. A well-planned Bhubaneswar Puri Konark Tour Package lets you experience the state's most iconic destinations within a compact 70 km triangle — Puri, Konark Sun Temple, and Bhubaneswar. Puri is one of the four sacred Char Dhams, home to the Jagannath Temple and the world-famous Rath Yatra. Konark's Sun Temple, built in the 13th century, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the finest examples of Kalinga architecture. Bhubaneswar, with over 600 ancient temples, is the historic capital that started it all. See More

This Bhubaneswar Puri Konark trip covers all three cities in 4 days and 3 nights. Hotel stays, daily breakfast, private AC vehicle, airport pickup, and an English-speaking guide are included. You visit the Jagannath Temple, Konark Sun Temple , Chilika Lake, Khandagiri-Udayagiri Caves, Dhauli Stupa, and Pipli village — in a well-paced circuit that works for first-time visitors, families, and pilgrims alike.

Rath Yatra 2026 falls on July 16. If you plan to visit around that date, book at least 8 weeks in advance — hotels across Puri fill up fast. The Jagannath Temple also closes for 14 days during Anavasara (after Snana Purnima, roughly June–July) when Darshan is not available. Our team flags these dates at the time of booking.
Best Time to Visit Puri, Konark & Bhubaneswar

rows: Pleasant weather, active dolphin season at Chilika, clear skies at Konark
Warm but manageable; good for temple visits in early morning

items: Rath Yatra — July 16, 2026: Lord Jagannath's chariot procession from the main temple to Gundicha Temple. The Jagannath Temple remains closed this day, but all visitors — including non-Hindus — can have darshan of the deities on the chariots. Puri hotels fill up 2–3 months ahead.
Bahuda Yatra (Return) — July 25, 2026: The chariots return and the Suna Besha ritual follows — deities adorned in gold.
Anavasara Closure — approx. mid-June to early July 2026: Temple closed for 14 days after Snana Purnima. Exact dates confirmed by our team at time of booking.
Konark Dance Festival — December 1–5, 2026: Classical dance performances at the open-air amphitheatre at Konark Sun Temple.

blocks.text: Konark Sun Temple Light & Sound Show 2026

The Konark Sun Temple hosts a nightly Light & Sound Show after regular visiting hours. The 40-minute show narrates the history of King Narasimhadeva I and the Sun God Surya through projected lights and audio. Wireless headphones are provided in Hindi, English, or Odia.

items: March to November: 7:30 PM and 8:20 PM (two shows nightly)
December to February: 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM (two shows nightly)

blocks.text: Ticket Price: ₹30 per person (separate from temple entry ticket of ₹40)

Tickets are available at the Konark site entrance or online on the ASI e-ticketing portal. Online booking is recommended during peak season (October–February). This show is an optional add-on — not included in the package price. If you want to attend, let us know at the time of booking and we will adjust the Day 2 schedule to allow for it.

By Air Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar (IATA: BBI) is connected to Delhi (approx. 2 hours), Mumbai (2.5 hours), and Kolkata (1 hour). Puri is 60 km from the airport, around 1.5 hours by road. Our representative meets you at the terminal exit.

By Train Bhubaneswar Railway Station is on the Howrah–Chennai main line. Key trains from Delhi: Bhubaneswar Rajdhani (22–25 hours). From Kolkata: multiple express trains (5–6 hours). Puri Railway Station also receives direct trains from Kolkata and Delhi — pickup from both stations is available.

By Road Delhi to Bhubaneswar: approx. 1,750 km via NH44 (26–28 hours by overnight bus or self-drive). Kolkata to Bhubaneswar: 480 km via NH16, 7–8 hours. All transfers within this tour — Bhubaneswar to Konark (65 km), Konark to Puri (35 km) — are covered by the package vehicle.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is the price of the Bhubaneswar Puri Konark tour package in 2026?

Ans: Starting from ₹13,250 per person on twin sharing (4 days/3 nights from Bhubaneswar). Price covers hotel, daily breakfast, private AC vehicle, guide, and all transfers. Meals other than breakfast and entry fees are extra.
Q2. What is included in the package?

Ans: Hotel stay (twin sharing), daily breakfast, private AC vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing, airport/railway pickup and drop, English-speaking guide, drinking water, driver allowance, toll, and parking. GST included.
Q3. Are there any hidden charges?
Ans: No hidden charges. Monument entry fees are extra — Konark Sun Temple ₹40 (Indians), Khandagiri-Udayagiri Caves ₹15 (Indians). Lunches, dinners, and personal expenses are also not included.
Q4. Can non-Hindus visit the Jagannath Temple?

Ans: Non-Hindus are not allowed inside the main temple. They can view the 65-metre Vimana tower and Sudarshana Chakra from the Raghunandan Library rooftop, opposite the main gate. During Rath Yatra (July 16, 2026), all visitors can have darshan of the deities on the chariots.
Q5. What are the Jagannath Temple darshan timings?
Ans: Temple opens at 5:00 AM and closes at midnight. Best time: before 8:00 AM or after 4:00 PM. Mid-day sees partial closures for ritual food offerings. Entry is free for all Hindu devotees.
Q6. When is the Jagannath Temple closed in 2026?
Ans: The temple closes for 14 days during Anavasara (after Snana Purnima, approx. June–July 2026). Exact dates are confirmed by our team before booking is finalised for June–July travel.
Q7. What is the Konark Light & Sound Show and is it included?

Ans: It is an evening show at Konark Sun Temple — 40 minutes, two shows nightly, tickets ₹30. It is not included in the package. If you want to attend, inform us at booking and we adjust the Day 2 schedule.
Q8. Is this tour suitable for senior citizens?
Ans: Yes. All sites are accessed by vehicle with short, flat walks. Jagannath Temple has priority entry for senior citizens. Chilika is a boat ride with no trekking involved.
Q9. What is the best time to visit Puri and Konark?
Ans: October to February is the most comfortable — cool weather and active Chilika dolphin season. Avoid May–June (extreme heat). For Rath Yatra, plan around July 16, 2026 and book 8 weeks ahead.
Q10. How many days are enough for this Odisha circuit?
Ans: 4 days/3 nights is sufficient for the main highlights. A 5-day extension can include Raghurajpur Craft Village or Sakshi Gopal Temple. Contact us for customised options.
Q11. Can I customise this package?
Ans: Yes. Duration, hotel category, and departure point can all be adjusted. Call or WhatsApp +91-8171158569 for a custom quote based on your group size and dates.
Q12. How do I reach Bhubaneswar from Delhi or Kolkata?

Ans: From Delhi: direct flights (2 hours) to Biju Patnaik Airport or Rajdhani Express (22–25 hours). From Kolkata: express trains to Bhubaneswar (5–6 hours) or direct to Puri. Pickup from both airport and railway station is included.

blocks.text: Established on the banks of the River Ganges, Haridwar is a holy city located in the state of Uttarakhand. It's a widely held belief that taking a dip in the sacred River Ganga here makes one free from all committed sins. In addition, devotees come here to receive the blessings of the Goddess Ganga in order to lead a life full of prosperity and happiness. If you too want to seek the blessings of the Goddess Ganga, then check out My Quick Trippers's well-crafted Haridwar Tour Packages and set out on this divine trip!

This beautiful northern state attracts millions of travellers during the grand celebration of Kumbh Mela which is organised every 12 years. This beautiful northern state also holds a myriad of mythological tales and happens to be one of the four areas where Garuda spilled the drops of Amrit. Devotees visit this city with an unflinching faith all the time. To go on a comfortable trip here, simply book our Haridwar Pilgrimage Tour, and enjoy a smooth & convenient tour.
Why Book Haridwar Holiday Package with My Quick Trippers?

The packages that we offer our travellers are equipped with all the basic and required amenities for the journey. This includes cosy & comfortable stay, smooth & air-conditioned transport service that takes you from one place to another, and amazing food quality. We'll also arrange your special requests, if you have any, such as certain food preferences or any other services.

So, if you want to witness the incredible beauty and the spirituality of this wonderful city, then check out our best Haridwar Tour from Delhi , Kolkata, Ahmedabad, and Surat and enjoy a wonderful travel experience with your family, friends, and loved ones!
The best time to visit Haridwar is in the window of October to March . The weather in this window is quite pleasant and therefore makes for a perfect time for sightseeing and going on temple tours.

Also, we advise against buying your Haridwar Travel Package in the monsoon season (July–September), as the levels of the Ganga River rise during this time, which poses a risk. Therefore, it's best to avoid this season.

items: By Air : If you're travelling by air, then you can land at Jolly Grant Airport in Dehradun. From here, Haridwar is just 35 km away. Also, the airport is well-connected to all major cities in India.

rows: Visit one of the most iconic Ghats of not only Haridwar but of the entire India! Enjoy the morning and evening Aarti here, where thousands of Diyas float by, creating a magical sight. Definitely include this in your Haridwar itinerary!

Haridwar is more than just visiting temples and ashrams. It's a journey to the divine and discovering the spiritual self! Q1. What is the best time to visit Haridwar?

Ans. The best time to go to Haridwar city is between October and February. Also, before you leave for Haridwar, you must update yourself with its temperature and a go through a few travel guide to get detailed and authentic Haridwar tourist information.

Ans. Haridwar is nationwide famous for hosting various important spiritual events and being home to various temples. It's also reckoned as a gateway to various prominent places for devotees. Kumbh Mela happens to be one of the most auspicious events celebrated in the city. You must have heard of the beautiful Mansa Devi Temple, where devotees visit to fulfil their desires.
Q3. How many days are enough for Haridwar and Rishikesh?

Ans. In general, two days are enough to cover this trip. What most tourists do is set aside one day for sightseeing in Haridwar and the other day is reserved for enjoying adventure activities in Rishikesh.
Q4. How much is a taxi from Haridwar to Rishikesh?

Q6. What is the famous food of Haridwar?
Ans. While in Haridwar, make sure you enjoy Aloo Kachori, Jalebi, Rasmalai, Chaat, Samosa, Chhole Bhature, etc. These are few of the most liked food items in Haridwar.
Q7. Which is the famous temple in Haridwar?
Ans. Mansa Devi Temple is one of the most famous temples in the holy city of Haridwar. Although the city houses lots of temples, this is one of the most eminent shrines in the city!
Q8. Which God is there in Haridwar?

Ans. As the name suggests "Hari" i.e. Lord Vishnu, the city worships Vishnu. However, Haridwar is the land of gods, and there are various other gods as well that get worshipped with devotion here. Lord Shiva and Goddess Shakti are among the few main deities that are revered the most, besides Lord Vishnu.
Q9. What can I buy in Haridwar?
Ans. Haridwar is very popular for religious items. If you're looking for things like incense sticks, sandalwood, Rudraksha, etc., then you can find them easily here.
Q10. Which is better Rishikesh or Haridwar?

Ans. Both cities are beautiful and better in their own terms, and there is no comparison between them. The only thing that makes Rishikesh a bit more exciting is that in this city, you can enjoy some really enthralling adventure activities like bungee jumping, river rafting, cliff jumping, and more.

blocks.text: The best time to visit Gaya is September to March as it aligns with the major festivals and pilgrimage events and rituals. Let's know about the best time to visit Gaya in detail-

items: These months are the peak tourism season in Gaya. During these months' festivals like Pitru Paksha Mela, Buddha Purnima, Navratras take place.
The large crowd of pilgrims and tourists gather here during these months. The price of hotels is also high due to the peak season.
The weather during these months is also best for sightseeing and participating in spiritual rituals.
During these months in Gaya, Shravani Mela and Pitrapaksha Mela are celebrated. Another notable event in the Buddhist circuit is Chokhor Duchen, also called the Dharma Wheel Festival.
So, you can consider Monsoon if you want to witness these festivals. The weather during this time will be humid due to heavy rains.
Terrains may also interrupt your temple visits.
Summer is not the most preferred time to visit Gaya as the heat and high temperature might get unbearable for sightseeing.

During these months Buddha Purnima is celebrated with great pomp and show. So, you can still consider these months to visit if you want to experience the culture and take part in celebrations which include day-long prayers, meditation, and rituals.

blocks.text: Best Places to Explore in Gaya on Your Trip

In 2024 Gaya witnessed a significant rise in tourist footfall. It welcomed around 22 lakh pilgrims. This shows the rising interest in spirituality and involvement in spiritual events. Source: ( Times of India ). Here are some of the best places to see in Gaya covered in our Gaya itineraries-
Vishnupad Temple- Realm of Lord Vishnu

items: Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, Vishnupad Temple is one of the most famous spiritual places to explore in Gaya. It is situated on the banks of the sacred Falgu River.
Here you will witness the actual footprints of lord Vishnu which is impressed in a stone when he killed demon Gayasura.
The temple houses a sacred Akshayvat Tree which is believed to grant Moksha to the ancestors.

Mangala Gauri Temple in Gaya is a famous temple of Goddess Sati in Gaya. It dates back to the 15th century. It is one of the eighteen Maha Shakti Peethas where Goddess Sati's breasts are believed to have fallen which is a symbol of nourishment.
The temple also offers scenic views of Mangala Gauri hill as the temple itself is perched on this hill.
Also witness the sacred Akhand Deep (eternal flame) burning continuously within the temple premises.

blocks.text: Pind Daan Ghats- Honor the Ancestors

items: If you are visiting Gaya, Pind Daan might be one of the specific reasons as this is a famous destination to offer Pind for ancestors.
Visit three sacred spots in Gaya for Pind Daan ceremony such as Phalgu river banks which serve as the main place for pilgrims to perform Pind Daan rituals.

Vishnupad Temple which is also the most auspicious place for offering Pind Daan and Akshayavat Tree located within the Vishnupad Temple. This ancient banyan tree is believed to grant eternal blessings to ancestors.

blocks.text: Gayatri Shakti Peeth Gaya- Abode of Goddess Gayatri

items: Dedicated to goddess Gayatri, divine mother of the Vedas and the personification of Gayatri Mantra, Gayatri Shakti Peetha is a prominent Hindu temple to visit in Gaya.
The temple is famous for its beautiful idols of Gayatri Mata along with depictions of Kundalini and Savitri.
You can take part in the divine rituals, daily prayers and chant the auspicious Gayatri Mantra.
Also known as Brahmayoni Hill, Brahmajuni hill is the highest hill in Gaya. It represents the female Yoni of Lord Brahma.
Atop the hill is a temple of five-headed female deity worshiping the representation of Brahma's energy.
It is one of the best places to offer Pind Daan during Pitrapaksha Mela.

blocks.text: Best Things to do in Gaya on your Trip
Gaya is a spiritual place and the best activities in Gaya will revolve around spiritual activities. Here is a list of some of the best things to do in Gaya -

items: Phalgu is one of the most sacred rivers to explore in Gaya. It holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus, and Buddhists.
Visit here during Pitrapaksha Mela to offer Pind Daan for your ancestors.
It is also a significant place for Buddhists as it is believed that Gautam Buddha practiced asceticism and achieved enlightenment near its banks.
Located in Gaya, Dungeshwari caves is an important spiritual site. It is also known as Mahakala caves.
These are the rock cut caves which date back to the 3rd century BCE.
It is believed that Gautama Buddha mediated here for six months before attaining enlightenment in Bodhgaya.
Just 24 km from Gaya, Barabar Caves is a must visit spot. It is one of the oldest surviving rocks which dates back to the 3rd century BCE.
These caves were primarily used by ascetics of the Ajivika sect, a spiritual group in Buddhism and Jainism founded by Makkhali Gosala.
There are some inscriptions in the caves which bear the name of Emperor Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya which proves that they patronized the caves.

Gaya is a wonderful place to indulge in shopping for art and handicrafts. Gaya is famous for its wood craft art which you will witness idols of Buddha and other religious artefacts made of Gamhar wood.

Some of the other notable things to buy here are artistic textiles, pottery works, Tikuli paintings, Fresco rock paintings, Khatwa works, brass works, and block printing on cloths, bamboo products, Jewellery products, and Zari Works in various markets of Gaya.
Try authentic food in Gaya to tickle your tastebuds with the rich flavors of the region. The food of Gaya is connected with the spiritual heritage. You will get vegetarian meals.
Some of the best foods to try in Gaya are Litti Chokha, Sattu Paratha, Kadhi Bari, Thekua, Maitha, Peda, Tilkut, Balushahi, Khaja and Dal Puri.

blocks.text: How to Reach Gaya by Air, Rail and Road

For most tourists, the fastest way to travel to Gaya is by a flight from Delhi or Kolkata to Gaya International Airport, followed by local cab to reach Gaya or Bodhgaya. By Train, Mahabodhi Express is the best option to reach Gaya . It is also a budget friendly option for many travellers. By Road you can take NH 83 which offers scenic views of rural Bihar. Let's know in detail how to reach Gaya by Air, Rail and Road-

rows: Gaya International Airport, the only international airport in Bihar, is the best way to reach Gaya. It is located 12-15 km from Gaya which receives both domestic and international flights.

Gaya is connected with major cities like Delhi, Kolkata and Varanasi domestically. International routes include Bangkok, Yangon (Myanmar), Paro (Bhutan), Colombo, Singapore, and Tokyo (seasonal charters).
1.5 to 2 hr. flight from Delhi. From Patna - 40 min flight or 3-4 hr. drive
Operated under East Central Railway, Gaya Junction is the major railway station on Delhi- Kolkata Grand Chord Line. It is the busiest railway junction in Bihar.

By Rail, Gaya is connected with Patna, Varanasi, Mumbai, Chennai, Nagpur, Indore, and Lucknow. You will get Major trains: Mahabodhi Express (Delhi-Gaya, 16 hr.), Rajdhani Express (Delhi-Gaya, 12-13 hr.), Howrah Rajdhani (Kolkata-Gaya, 6 hr.).
Delhi-Gaya: 12-16 hr.; Kolkata-Gaya: 6 hr.; Patna-Gaya: 3-4 hr.
You can reach Gaya via NH-83 and NH-2 (Grand Trunk Road). The GT Road connects Delhi-Kanpur-Allahabad-Varanasi-Gaya-Kolkata. You can also opt for regular state and private buses to reach Gaya.

From Patna - 3-4 hr. drive; Ranchi - 5 hr.; Delhi - 14-16 hr.

blocks.text: On the way back to Shillong, you can visit Elephant Falls. Overnight stay at the hotel in Shillong.
Day 3 : Shillong – Mawlynnong – Dawki Day Visit

Get a delicious breakfast from the hotel on the 3rd day of your tour, then take a visit to Mawlynnong. The first stop will be Jingmaham Living Root Bridge, a unique structure that reflects the creativity of the residents. Along the way, you'll see numerous beautiful waterfalls.

Then, head towards Dawki (34 km from Mawlynnong Village). Once there, enjoy a boat ride in Umngot River and explore nearby places. Return to Shillong after sightseeing. Stay at the hotel for the night.
Post breakfast, transfer back to Guwahati. Once you reach, visit the Assam State Museum (closed on public holidays).

Afterwards, take a tour of the Handloom Centre. Enjoy the sunset cruise ride on the Brahmaputra River (subject to operations and available on direct payment). Later, return to your hotel for an overnight stay in Guwahati.
You can start early by visiting famous temples like Kamakhya Temple, Dhumavati Temple, Maa Tara Temple, Maa Chhinnamasta Temple, and Maa Bhuvaneshwari Temple.

items: Assam State Zoo cum Botanical Garden

blocks.text: After visiting the temples, our guided team will take you on a ferry to Umananda Temple on Peacock Island, the smallest island on Earth.
In the evening, you can take a river Cruise on the Brahmaputra River and after this adventure, you will head straight to the hotel to take a rest and an overnight stay.

items: In order to offer a special ritual or puja at Kamakhya temple, inform us a day prior so that we can make the necessary arrangements.
Every year during the period of Ambubachi, the Kamakhya temple remains closed i.e from 22 June - 25 June.

When the temple reopens, a big ceremony named Ambubachi Mela is held. The Mela goes on for a week making the temple premises and local streets extremely crowded. Therefore, plan your trip accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth going to the Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the Golden Triangle is worth visiting because it includes 3 popular cities like Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur, where you will explore amazing sights and it's a great way to experience India’s rich culture and history in a short trip.

mainEntity.name: What adventure activities visitors should try on a Delhi tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Delhi, visitors can try many adventure activities, like hot air balloon rides for a unique view of the city. In Gurgaon, rock climbing in the Aravalli hills is also a perfect option. Apart from this, bungee Jumping at Adventure Island in Rohini is also the best part to enjoy.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to visit the Golden Triangle Tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The perfect time is between October to March when the climate is cooler and more pleasant.

mainEntity.name: What are the other best places to explore in Jaipur?

acceptedAnswer.text: Travelers must explore Panna Meena Ka Kund due to its beautiful well with unique architecture and a peaceful atmosphere. Moti Dungri Fort is also nice and a small fort with lovely views of Jaipur which is rarely crowded.

mainEntity.name: What Is The Golden Triangle’s Significance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The national capital, New Delhi, and the cities of Agra and Jaipur are connected by a tourist route known as the “golden triangle” of India. The three states of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan make a triangular shape on a map, hence the moniker “Golden Triangle.”

mainEntity.name: When Is The Ideal Time Of Year To Visit The Golden Triangle In India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Since there will be a lot of walking involved, the best time to visit the Golden Triangle is from October to mid-April, when temperatures vary from 22 to 32 °C. Delhi may endure frigid spells in January and February and hot 45°C temperatures in May and June as a result of the Himalayan influence.

mainEntity.name: Why Is The Golden Triangle In India Called That?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Golden Triangle got its name because gold was originally stored here. Gold was used for more than only transporting goods to Delhi and Agra; it was also used to make ornaments and coins, among other things.

mainEntity.name: .Is A Trip To The Golden Triangle Worthwhile?

acceptedAnswer.text: This area of history-rich jungle and foggy mountains is well-known for its history of opium cultivation. Even though the Golden Triangle is a well-known tourist site nowadays, it is still highly recommended.

mainEntity.name: .How Many Days Would You Need In India’s Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: When Can You See the Golden Triangle? Most visitors decide to travel the entire Golden Triangle in three to seven days, but I strongly advise at least a week.

Day 1: Arriving in Ayodhya - Feel the divine presence of Lord Rama

On the first day, our tour representative will pick you up from your designated location (station/airport) and transfer you to your pre-booked hotel. After some relaxation, you will enjoy a guided Ayodhya Tour. We will explore the following places-

items: Ram Janmabhoomi- Ram Janmabhoomi is a landmark temple as it is the birthplace of Lord Rama. devotees from all across the world visit here to get the divine blessings of Lord Rama. After a long held wait of many years, the sacred consecration of the temple took place on Jan22nd 2024.

Kanak Bhawan Temple- Kanak Bhavan has kept the stories of Treta Yuga. This sacred temple was a gift to Lord Rama and Goddess Sita just after their wedding by Kaikeyi. It used to be their personal residence.

Dashrath Mahal - It is a popular Siddha Peetha, and divine abode of King Dasharatha, (father of Lord Rama). You will see the beautiful idols of Lord Rama, Devi Sita, Lakshman, Shatrughan and Bharat here.

Hanuman Garhi- Hanuman Garhi is dedicated to Lord Hanuman who is considered as a protector of Ayodhya. It is said that Lord Hanuman resides in a cave and watches over the entire city of Ayodhya to protect them from all the evils.

blocks.text: Best Places on Your Trip to Visit in Agra
Agra is one of the most visited tourist destinations in India and the world. In 2024 there Agra’s Taj Mahal welcomed around 6.9 million tourists (Source- ceicdata.com). (nofollow)

Agra is all about timelessness, UNESCO world heritage sites, and represents the Mughal Empire in a very well-preserved manner. Apart from Taj Mahal, there are other places to explore. Here is a list of best places to visit in Agra covered in our Agra travel itineraries-

items: Taj Mahal needs no introduction, it is the most visited tourist destination in India. It is also one of the new Seven Wonders of the World.

Taj Mahal was constructed primarily with white Makrana marble sourced from Rajasthan. It was built by Shah Jahan, the fifth Mughal emperor between 1632 and 1648 in the memory of his beloved by Mumtaz Mahal.
Located in the city of Agra, Agra Fort stand still in pride keeping alive the history and legacy of Mughal empire. It was built by Mughal emperor Akbar in 1565 but completed in 1573.
The fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its beautiful red marble walls stretch 2.5 km in a crescent shape. Inside the fort there are many palaces, gardens, halls and mosques.
Its architecture is a beautiful fusion of Persian and Indian architecture styles.
Itimad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb is one of the top tourist attractions to visit in Agra. It is an inspiration behind the architecture of the Taj Mahal.
It was built between 1622 and 1628 by Empress Nur Jahan in the memory of her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg.
The tomb displays beautiful inlay work known as Pietra Dura with semi-precious stones which forms exquisite floral and geometric patterns.
Mehtab Bagh or Moonlight Garden is a popular point of tourist interest in Agra. It is located on the northern banks of Yamuna River, facing the Taj Mahal.
It is said that Shah Jahan planned to built one more replica of Taj Mahal in black color (Black Taj Mahal) at Mehtab Bagh.

The garden is designed in a classic Persian style Charbagh. It is very famous for its beautiful sunset views. It’s also a photographer’s delight due to the scenic garden views along with the Taj Mahal in its backdrop.
Jama Masjid in Agra was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in 1637 under the patronage of his daughter Jahanara Begum.

it is one of the largest mosques in India. The mosque displays the beauty of Mughal style architecture. It is a blend of red sandstone and white marble with beautiful inlay work, calligraphy, beautiful arches and domes.
Sikandra is a tomb of Mughal emperor Akbar which was supervised during his lifetime according to Turkic tradition. After the death of Akbar Jahangir, his son finalized the construction of Sikandra.
The tomb has a five storeyed pyramidal structure built in a red sandstone and with the top part in white marble.
The arcaded verandas with beautiful floral and geometric patterns will take your breath away.
The UNESCO World heritage site- Fatehpur Sikri is also a prominent tourist attraction to visit in Agra. It was founded by Akbar in 1571. The place served as Mughal empire’s capital until 1585.
The city’s grandeur lasted only for 14-15 years as it was later abandoned due to water shortages and Akbar’s military focus in the areas of Punjab.
There are many monuments to see in Fatehpur Sikri like Tomb of Salim Chishti, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai Palace, Birbal’s house and Anup Talao etc.

blocks.text: Top Things to Do in Agra on Your Trip
Agra Tourism offers blend of the sightseeing of historical monuments and cultural experiences . Here are some of the best things to do in Agra recommended by My Quick Trippers-

items: Agra is one of the best destinations for Heritage Tours. See all the historical monuments in Agra to know about the life and times of Mughal Empire and its rulers.
Capture cool pictures to boast on social media platforms. Agra does have monuments which are worth capturing.
Some of the most popular historical monuments to see in Agra are Taj Mahal , Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Mehtab Bagh, Ram Bagh , Jama Masjid, Itmad-ud-Daula’s Tomb etc.
One must not miss this wonderful opportunity of a scenic boat ride on Yamuna River. You will get specular views of Taj Mahal.
You can access the boats from the east gate of The Taj Mahal located close to the hotel Amarvilas.
If you want to see the iconic monuments without crowds, this is a great chance. It offers rare vantage point for photography.

Never miss a chance to shop for souvenirs in Agra . Agra has some of the best markets where you will get silk Sarees, handicrafts, inlay products, leather goods, jewelry, traditional embroidery and textiles.
Some of the most popular markets to visit in Agra are Kinari Bazar, Subhash Emporium, Raja Ki Mandi etc.
Mohabbat The Taj – Kalakriti Dance Drama Show at Kalakriti Cultural and Convention Center near Taj Mahal is a must not miss performances when you are in Agra.
The show runs for 80 to 90 minutes at around 6:15 pm or 6:30pm. The show is a narration of the epic love story of Mughal emperor Shah Jahan and Mumtaz.

The show will overwhelm your senses. You will witness the artists in Mughal Era costumes and the stage will be set according to the Mughal times. You will also see the replica of the Taj Mahal made with Makrana marble weighting 8500kg.
When you are in Agra, you must look for workshops in Taj Ganj, Nai Ki Mandi and Gokulpura etc. for learning Marble inlay craft known as Parchin Kari.
You will learn the craft passed down through generation from skilled artists and it is one of the best things to do and learn in Agra.

Ans: Yes, Agra is safe for travellers but basic precautions need to be followed. Avoid talking to strangers and don’t encourage random people to click your pictures. Ans: Taj Mahal opens 30 minutes before sunrise and closes 30 minutes before sunset. Don’t worry, with us you don’t have to worry about time, we prepare best guided itineraries for Taj Mahal visit. On Fridays, The Taj Mahal is closed for public visits.
Q-17: Can I Visit Agra’s monuments during Night?

Ans: No, you cannot view Agra’s monuments at night all the time. You can only view the monuments if you have booked in advanced for night viewing at the official site on select full moon nights when the night viewing tour is available.
Q-18: What languages are spoken in Agra?
Ans: In Agra, Hindi is the main language. But it is also one of the popular tourist places for international travellers too, English is also understood by the locals.
Q-19: Is there any dress code to be followed in Agra?
Ans: No there is no strict dress code to follow for Agra Tour. You can wear breathable fabrics and comfortable footwear. But, avoid clothes which are too revealing.
Q-20: What is the ticket price for Taj Mahal Entry?

Ans: For Indian tourist the ticket price for Taj Mahal entry is INR 50 and for international traveller is INR 1100. Both domestic and international tourist also have to pay INR 200 extra for mausoleum visits.

blocks.text: Morocco has many destinations for tourists to enjoy on Tour Packages. This country has natural landscapes, cultural sites, mountain peaks, sprawling forests and wonderful coast line to provide memorable time on Morocco Tour Packages. With Mediterranean Sea at the backdrop and long rich history, the charm of this country draws tourists on Tour Package from all over the world and over and over again.

Rabat is the present capital of the country and was built in 12th century having many attractions for tourists on Morocco Travel Packages. The minaret of an incomplete 12th century mosque called as Tour Hassan, the Chellah is a place with Roman ruins, delightful gardens and wonderful monuments are popular places to visit. Rabat is also famous for its fabulous gates built centuries ago, the Gate of the Ambassadors and Oudaias Kasbah Gate are most famous amongst all. The Mohammed V Mausoleum is an outstanding example of Moroccan architecture, the Royal Palace and many fort and castles around the city are not to miss attractions of Rabat on Morocco Tour Package. Mamora forests lies on the outskirts of the city and is a popular destination along with exotic beaches, during summer these beaches are perfect place to relax on Morocco Travel Package.

Fes in Morocco is the oldest and the most interesting city for visitors on Tour Packages. Built in 8th century this place has all the charm of an ancient city, it has history and mystery more than any other place in Morocco. Nejjarine Square and fountain, the Er Rasif Mosque, Andalous Mosque, the Royal Palace, the Kasbah and Dar Beth Museum are chief attractions of this magical city. The old city area of Fes is in UNESCO world heritage list, the windy streets with bustling covered markets and ancient mosques this place is full of magnificent structures of Hispanic-Arabic architecture. Medina Bazaar is the biggest market in the world and there are many things which tourists can purchase on Morocco Holiday Package. On the North of this fascinating city the valley of Ouergha is another not to miss attraction along with ancient mosques and interesting shopping places on Morocco Tour Packages.

Marrakech too was once capital of Morocco and today very interesting tourist destination on Tour Packages. This city not only offers captivating historical places but also provides outdoor activities to enjoy. The 12th century mosque Koutoubia dominates city’s skyline and is higher than Notre Dam. Another very exciting and sometimes bewildering place is the City Square or Djeema el Fenaa meaning ‘the place of the dead’, this place comes alive in the night with dance and music shows, fortunetellers, storytellers, acrobats and snake charmers, it is an exotic spectacle and not to be missed in Marrakech. The area on UNESCO world heritage list is full or architectural master pieces and has a large Medina which is not to be missed on Morocco Holiday Package.

The city of Meknes is full of castles and fortresses along with UNESCO world heritage site. This city is also one of the imperial cities of the country and has many historical attractions for tourists. For beach fun tourists on Morocco Tour Package head to El Jadida which has a beautiful Portuguese fort and exotic beaches on Atlantic coast.

blocks.text: Trivandrum, also known as Thiruvananthapuram, is the capital city of Kerala, India. It is a vibrant and culturally rich city that offers a wide range of experiences for visitors. Trivandrum tour packages provide an opportunity to explore the city’s historical sites, religious landmarks, beautiful beaches, and diverse cuisine.

One of the major attractions in Trivandrum is the iconic Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Vishnu. This magnificent temple is known for its stunning architecture, intricate carvings, and religious significance. It is a must-visit for spiritual seekers and those interested in Indian mythology and culture.

Trivandrum is also home to several museums and art galleries that showcase the region’s history and art. The Napier Museum, known for its Indo-Saracenic architecture, houses a vast collection of artifacts, including ancient sculptures, bronze idols, and historical artifacts. The Kerala Science and Technology Museum and the Natural History Museum are also worth exploring.

For nature lovers, Trivandrum offers beautiful beaches such as Kovalam and Shanghumugham. These beaches are known for their golden sands, clear waters, and breathtaking sunsets. Visitors can relax on the beaches, indulge in water sports, or simply enjoy the tranquil atmosphere.

Trivandrum is also a hub of traditional Ayurvedic treatments and wellness centres. Travellers can indulge in rejuvenating Ayurvedic massages, therapies, and yoga sessions to unwind and revitalize their senses.

Food enthusiasts will delight in the diverse cuisine of Trivandrum. From delectable seafood dishes to traditional Kerala delicacies like Appam, Puttu, and Fish Curry, the city offers a gastronomic journey that will tantalize the taste buds.

Trivandrum tour packages offer a blend of history, spirituality, natural beauty, and culinary delights. Whether you are interested in exploring ancient temples, relaxing on pristine beaches, or immersing yourself in the rich cultural heritage of Kerala, Trivandrum has something to offer for every traveller.

In Gurgaon, rock climbing in the Aravalli hills is also a perfect option. Apart from this, bungee Jumping at Adventure Island in Rohini is also the best part to enjoy.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to visit the Golden Triangle Tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The perfect time is between October to March when the climate is cooler and more pleasant.

mainEntity.name: What are the other best places to explore in Jaipur?

acceptedAnswer.text: Travelers must explore Panna Meena Ka Kund due to its beautiful well with unique architecture and a peaceful atmosphere. Moti Dungri Fort is also nice and a small fort with lovely views of Jaipur which is rarely crowded.

mainEntity.name: What Is The Golden Triangle’s Significance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The national capital, New Delhi, and the cities of Agra and Jaipur are connected by a tourist route known as the “golden triangle” of India. The three states of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan make a triangular shape on a map, hence the moniker “Golden Triangle.”

mainEntity.name: When Is The Ideal Time Of Year To Visit The Golden Triangle In India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Since there will be a lot of walking involved, the best time to visit the Golden Triangle is from October to mid-April, when temperatures vary from 22 to 32 °C. Delhi may endure frigid spells in January and February and hot 45°C temperatures in May and June as a result of the Himalayan influence.

mainEntity.name: Why Is The Golden Triangle In India Called That?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Golden Triangle got its name because gold was originally stored here. Gold was used for more than only transporting goods to Delhi and Agra; it was also used to make ornaments and coins, among other things.

mainEntity.name: .Is A Trip To The Golden Triangle Worthwhile?

acceptedAnswer.text: This area of history-rich jungle and foggy mountains is well-known for its history of opium cultivation. Even though the Golden Triangle is a well-known tourist site nowadays, it is still highly recommended.

mainEntity.name: .How Many Days Would You Need In India’s Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: When Can You See the Golden Triangle? Most visitors decide to travel the entire Golden Triangle in three to seven days, but I strongly advise at least a week.

blocks.text: The Madurai Rameshwaram tour is one of Tamil Nadu's most rewarding pilgrimage and sightseeing circuits. Four days. Two cities. And more sacred sites, living legends, and coastal beauty than most people expect. See More

The journey starts in Madurai — home to the Meenakshi Amman Temple, one of India's grandest Dravidian temples with over 33,000 sculpted figures. From there you travel to Rameshwaram, the sacred island city where the Ramanathaswamy Temple — one of the 12 Jyotirlingas — stands at the edge of the sea. This is where Lord Rama himself is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva before crossing to Lanka.

Apart from temple Darshan, you'll explore the iconic Pamban Bridge with its spectacular sea views, the haunting ruins of Dhanushkodi, and the birthplace of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam. Thousands of pilgrims and families have trusted My Quick Trippers for a smooth, guided experience here — and we make sure you don't miss a single important stop.

blocks.text: Madurai is one of India's oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a history stretching back over 2,500 years. It is the cultural capital of Tamil Nadu and the second largest city in the state. The city revolves around the Meenakshi Amman Temple at its literal centre — the city's streets were laid out in concentric squares around the temple.

For pilgrims, Madurai offers the Meenakshi Amman Temple, the Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple (one of Murugan's six sacred abodes), and the Koodal Azhagar Temple (one of the 108 Divya Desams). For those interested in history, the Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace and the Gandhi Museum add depth. And Madurai's food — particularly the Jigarthanda cold drink and the famous mutton biryani — is a destination in itself.

Rameshwaram is situated on Pamban Island in the Gulf of Mannar, connected to mainland Tamil Nadu by the Pamban Bridge. It is one of the holiest sites in Hinduism — a place where Lord Rama is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva before crossing the sea to Lanka to rescue Goddess Sita.

The Ramanathaswamy Temple here is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas and part of the all-India Char Dham pilgrimage (the four dhams being Badrinath in the north, Dwarka in the west, Puri in the east, and Rameshwaram in the south). The temple's corridor is 1,212 metres long — the longest temple corridor in the world. The Theertham Snanam ritual, involving 22 sacred wells inside the temple, is unique to Rameshwaram and forms the spiritual centrepiece of the visit.

Excellent connections from Chennai (Vaigai Express, Pandian Express — 8–9 hrs), Bengaluru, Coimbatore, Trichy, and other major cities. This is the most convenient and budget-friendly option for most travellers.

Madurai is on NH-44 (the North-South corridor). Regular bus services from Chennai (460 km, 7–8 hrs), Coimbatore (220 km, 3.5 hrs), Trichy (140 km, 2.5 hrs), and Kanyakumari (244 km, 4 hrs). State government SETC buses and multiple private operators run overnight routes from Chennai and Bengaluru.

items: Dress code: Strict at both Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples. Men: dhoti or full-length trousers (no shorts). Women: saree or salwar-kameez (no sleeveless, shoulders and knees covered). Dress codes are enforced at the entrance.
Theertham Snanam: Carry a change of clothes in your day bag — you get completely wet from bucket-poured water. It is not a light sprinkling. Allow 1.5–2 hours for all 22 wells.
Sphatik Linga Darshan: Happens only at 5:00 AM. Arriving in Rameshwaram on Day 1 evening is the only way to experience this. Do not skip it.
Photography: Restricted inside Ramanathaswamy Temple and Meenakshi Amman Temple. Camera fees apply at select spots. Check at the entrance before shooting.

Dhanushkodi access: Private vehicles are not allowed beyond the Dhanushkodi checkpost. The last 18 km to the island tip is sand — only beach jeeps (local, approx. ₹50–₹150 per person) cover this section.
Cash: Carry ₹2,000–₹3,000 in cash. Temple hundi, beach jeeps, and local prasad shops are cash-only. ATMs in Rameshwaram work but can run short during peak pilgrim season.
Early mornings: Ramanathaswamy Temple opens at 4:00 AM. Early darshan (4–7 AM) means shorter queues and a more peaceful experience. Afternoon queues can stretch to 2–3 hours during peak season.
Senior citizens: Wheelchairs are available inside both Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples. Inform us at booking if special assistance is needed.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. How many days are enough for Madurai and Rameshwaram?

Ans. Four days are enough to visit all major temples, sightseeing spots, beaches, and nearby attractions in both Madurai and Rameshwaram while still having time to relax. If you plan to add Kanyakumari, allow 6 days total.
Q2. Can this Madurai Rameshwaram tour package be customised?

Ans. Yes. The itinerary, number of days, hotel category, and activities can all be customised. Common additions include Kanyakumari (2 extra days), Kodaikanal (1–2 extra days), or Thanjavur Brihadeeswarar Temple (1 day). Contact us on WhatsApp to plan your specific tour.
Q3. What is the best time to visit Madurai?

Ans. October to March is the best time — weather is pleasant (22°C–32°C), ideal for sightseeing and temple visits. Summers (April–June) are hot but manageable if you plan early morning visits. Avoid the peak monsoon months for outdoor sightseeing.
Q4. What are the accommodation options in Rameshwaram?

Ans. Rameshwaram has a full range of options — budget guesthouses, mid-range hotels, beach resorts, and premium properties like the Daiwik Hotels and Hyatt Place. Our package covers standard, deluxe, and luxury categories, with 2 nights in Rameshwaram included.
Q5. How do I reach Rameshwaram from major cities?

Ans. The Rameswaram Express is one of the fastest train options and connects Chennai directly to Rameshwaram (approx. 10–12 hrs). From Madurai, it is 173 km by road (3–4 hrs). Our package includes all ground transport from Madurai Airport or Railway Station — no separate Rameshwaram travel booking needed.
Q6. Is Rameshwaram part of the Char Dham Yatra?

Ans. Yes — Rameshwaram is one of the four Char Dhams of India: Badrinath (north), Dwarka (west), Puri (east), and Rameshwaram (south). This is distinct from the Chota Char Dham of Uttarakhand (Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath). Rameshwaram is also one of the 12 Jyotirlinga shrines of India.
Q7. What is Sphatik Linga Darshan in Rameshwaram?

Ans. Sphatik Linga (also called Mani Darshan) is a naturally formed crystal Shivlinga inside Ramanathaswamy Temple. It is believed to have been installed by Goddess Sita herself and is not man-made. The darshan is available only at 5:00 AM before general temple hours. Our 2-night Rameshwaram stay ensures you can attend this.
Q8. What is Theertham Snanam at Ramanathaswamy Temple?

Ans. Theertham Snanam is the ritual of bathing in water drawn from all 22 sacred wells inside the temple corridors. Each well has a different name and is believed to have unique purifying properties. Temple priests pour water in sequence over pilgrims. The ritual takes about 1.5–2 hours. Carry a change of clothes — you will be fully drenched.
Q9. Is photography allowed inside Meenakshi Amman and Ramanathaswamy temples?

Ans. Photography is restricted inside both temples. Camera fees apply at permitted spots. Phones and cameras must be left at the token counter at Ramanathaswamy Temple. Check with the entrance staff on the day of visit for current rules — these are occasionally updated.
Q10. What should I eat in Madurai and Rameshwaram?

Ans. Madurai is famous for its Jigarthanda (a cold drink made with milk, almond gum, and ice cream — the original version is sold on West Masi Street near Meenakshi Temple), Madurai mutton biryani, and parotta-salna. Rameshwaram is predominantly vegetarian near the temple area — fresh seafood is available at local restaurants away from the temple zone. All hotels in our package serve South Indian breakfast.
Q11. What documents do I need for this tour?

Ans. No special permits are required for Madurai or Rameshwaram. Carry a valid government photo ID (Aadhaar, passport, or driving licence) for hotel check-in. For senior citizens or anyone with health conditions, carry your prescription and a brief medical history card.
Q12. What is the cancellation policy?

Ans. Free cancellations and amendments are available up to 7 days after booking confirmation. blocks.text: Delhi is rich in history! From its heritage buildings to its palaces to trendy markets, there's just so much to see here! Book our Delhi Tour Packages and we'll take you to all the great places here. With our services, you get meals, hotels, and transport, which will make your trip utterly comfortable and luxurious. Contact us now and let us help you uncover the real glory of the capital!
Visiting Delhi means enjoying the following:

First stop, Old Delhi! Imagine for a second several blocks of narrow streets with the smell of various tasty foods and the sound of the packed crowd. There, you can admire the Jama Masjid , which is a beautiful mosque with splendid domes. The awe-inspiring Red Fort is the next, a place of monumental importance and history. Furthermore, cast a glance at Qutub Minar , an old monument that towers high and carries lots of stories within itself.

We move our focus now to New Delhi and see everything glistening and brand new. In this place, you can probably observe super-high skyscrapers and government facades. The Presidential Palace, or the Rashtrapati Bhavan , in which the President lives, is a very beautiful building! Definitely add these to your Delhi Sightseeing Tour!
A Feast for the Senses: A Feast for the Senses

Delhi offers some good food also. Away from spicy street food like chaat, there is equally rich Mughlai food to please every mood or requirement. So come on, take a bite, and let your taste buds go on the tour.

Walk to Lodhi Colony, a street where every stone is aching to serve as a means of expression. In addition, visit the city museums and galleries, which are a wonderful avenue to learn about the history and tradition of Delhi.
Delhi has a lot to offer you and these varieties of destinations should definitely be a part of your Delhi Tour Package.

items: Top places to explore in Delhi
Delhi has always been a hub of culture while the megalopolis' past space of many ethnicities weaving together is full of stories hundreds and even thousands of years old.
It simply exudes a unique blend of old and new, classic and contemporary. Embracing a whole spectrum of tastes and propensities.

Because we have spiritual, historical & political interests here, we will travel to Central Delhi next. There, we can see the Raj Ghat , India Gate , Bangla Sahib , Rashtrapati Bhavan , and the Parliament House , which are all located in proximity.
Delhi tourism offers several occasions to experience its kaleidoscope of festivals, lip-smacking food, majestic monuments, sparkling museums, and nightlight flamboyance.
The journey to Delhi can be made very economical by choosing our affordable Delhi travel packages curated by travel experts.

blocks.text: Delhi offers diverse transport options. The Indira Gandhi International Airport set the scene for air travel links to main cities. On top of that, there's a railway network. Locally, you can also enjoy your Delhi tour with buses, taxis, and the Metro. Our Delhi tour package with hotel and guide helps you with transport in and around the city as well.

Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport provides robust air connectivity as it operates both domestic and international flights. Departures from Terminals 1D and 3 correspond to different airlines and offer outstanding service through shuttle buses, metro, and taxi pre-booking for onward travel to the city center.

Delhi's railway network, including principal stations like New Delhi, Old Delhi, and Nizamuddin, makes it possible to connect several cities from different parts of the country. Upon getting off at the station, travellers can easily get a taxi, take a Metro, or use the buses of DTC for local transport.

Delhi has a well-established network of roads linking it with the neighbouring states and cities using buses and private motor cars. Interstate bus terminals and national highways have options for traveling to Delhi and beyond, from short to long distances.

Delhi's local transport has many varieties. You have many options like DTC buses, taxis, Metro, auto rickshaws, and eco-friendly options like electric rickshaws and smart bikes. Each transportation system has its particular purpose for travellers, ensuring accessibility and convenience in the busy streets.
With our Delhi Holiday Packages, you don't have to worry about the local transport, as we'll provide you with a private luxury car that will take you to all the destinations in this trip.

Delhi's seasons promise varied experiences: summer mango festivals and indoor fun, monsoon rejuvenating art gallery visits and park explorations, winter demanding festive mood, and sightseeing in smog being a necessity with season-specific safety measures.
The best time to visit Delhi is from October to March . It's perfect for enjoying pleasant weather. Moreover, you also get to witness the vibrant festivals that happen here in this window.
However, if you're looking for a full spectrum of Delhi experience, then here's a season-wise breakdown.

rows: Best for Luxury spas, Indoor Ice Skating, Bars and Clubs, Delhi Summer drinks and ice- creams, Karting, etc. It's time for the International Mango Festival.
Enjoy Fun- filled activities with your loved ones

Visiting art galleries, museums, Parks, road trips, North Indian cuisines, Rooftop restaurants and cafes, etc. It's time for Red Earth's Monsoon Festival
Enjoy the refreshing weather and visit all the parks in Delhi
Carry Umbrella and mosquito repellent cream. You will get good deals on hotels this time. Visit all the parks for nature's best views.
