blocks.text: Dotted with several beautiful heritage sites, mesmerizing beauty, and an incomparable culture, Nepal offers its visitors some of the most memorable experiences. The best time to visit Nepal is September to November and March to May. Let's know in detail-

items: These are the best months to plan your trip to Nepal. The skies are crystal clear with dry weather. You will get high visibility for enjoying scenic treks. You will witness more crowds at popular tourist spots. Book your hotels in advance. It is also a time to enjoy vibrant festivals like Dashain and Tihar.

The season offers warm weather to enjoy sightseeing comfortably. It is also the best time for trekking and outdoor activities. You will also witness many wild flowers and Rhododendrons in full bloom. It's the best time if you enjoy nature photography.
Holi, Buddha Jayanti, Ghode Jatra are some of the most famous festivals celebrated in these months.

It is not a favorable time to plan your trip in Nepal. You may witness heavy rains due with potential risks of landslides, roadblocks etc. These months are not suitable for trekking and adventure activities.
Your sightseeing plans may get postponed or delayed due to heavy rain. But you can enjoy Teej, Gai Jatra, Krishna Janmashtami festivals in these months.
It is the best time for cultural exploration but one should only plan a Nepal trip during winter if they can bear the cold.

If you like less crowd, high-altitude trekking trails and cold weather, these months are best for you. Losar, Maghe Sankranti, Basant Panchami are some of the most popular festivals celebrated in these months.

blocks.text: Best Places to visit in Nepal on your Trip

items: The capital of Nepal, Kathmandu is one of the oldest inhabited places in the world. You will be amazed to know that its history dates back to the 2nd Century AD.

There are many places to explore in Kathmandu for sightseeing such as Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath Stupa, Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple etc. You will find a perfect blend of history, culture and vibrant city life.

For Hindu Devotees, The sacred Pashupatinath Temple is an important pilgrimage site here which is dedicated to Lord Shiva and the scenic Boudhanath Stupa is a prominent Buddhist site. Don't miss the lively Thamel district which is very famous for shopping and exciting nightlife.
In Pokhara you will witness breathtaking natural landscapes and opportunities for amazing adventures. It is one of the best places to explore in Nepal.

Pokhara is also known as Lake City as it is very popular for breathtaking Phewa Lake. You can enjoy boating and capturing mesmerizing sights of Mt Annapurna. Adventurers must try trekking to the world renowned Annapurna Peak.
Some other notable tourist attractions to see in Pokhara are Devi's fall, Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave, Mahendra and Bat Caves, World Peace Pagoda, Begnas Lake and Bindabasini Temple.

Chitwan is a paradise for adventure and nature lovers in Nepal. It's popular because of Chitwan National Park which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its awe-inspiring biodiversity and wildlife. Here you will see one horned Asiatic rhinoceros, Bengal tigers, elephants, and over 500 bird species.
You can also enjoy exciting jungle activities like safaris, birdwatching, canoe rides, and visits to indigenous Tharu villages.
Witness stunning sunrise and sunset views at Siraichuli Hill and enjoy birdwatching and hiking at Bishazari Tal (Twenty Thousand Lakes).
Located in the northeastern part of Nepal, Khumbu Valley is one of the must visit tourist destinations in Nepal. It is also known as the Everest region.
Witness iconic sights of Mt Everest and the scenic Khumbu glacier.
Trekkers from far are drawn to Khumbu valley for trekking to Everest base camp. There are many beautiful Sherpa villages to explore such as Namche Bazaar, Khumjung, and Khunde.
Some of the most prominent tourist attractions to explore here are Syangboche Monastery, Everest View Point, and Kala Patthar. Also enjoy Sherpa culture with festivals like Mani Rimdu.

Muktinath in Nepal is a prominent attraction for Hindu devotees as it houses the iconic Muktinath Temple which is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. It is also one of the 108 Divya Desams of Lord Vishnu worshipped by Vaishnavas.
One of the most important key features here is 108 sacred water spouts which are known as Mukti Dhara. It is believed that taking holy dip in these spouts will free you from karmic backlogs.
Muktinath is also important for trekkers as it is an important stop on the popular Annapurna Circuit trekking route. You will get stunning views of Annapurna Mountain and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Nepal on your Trip

Covered in our Nepal Itineraries are a mix of adventure, cultural, natural and spiritual activities. Based on your interests, you can also customize your Nepal Tour Packages and include activity according to your preferences. Here is a list of our best recommended activities to do in Nepal-

items: If you are planning to explore Nepal then, Everest Mountain Flight is something you must not miss. It is the most scenic flight from Kathmandu. You will get guaranteed window seats to witness the breathtaking views of Mt Everest and other Himalayan Peaks.
From above you will also witness aerial panoramas of glaciers, valleys, and peaks like Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu without trekking.

September to April is the best time to enjoy paragliding in Nepal. It is one of the best activities to enjoy here. You can enjoy it in Pokhara in Sarangkot which is the most popular paragliding destination in Nepal.
Paragliding in Pokhara offers scenic views of Annapurna Peak, Dhaulagiri mountain, Manaslu Peak, Pokhara Valley and Phewa Lake.

Nepal is blessed with deeply sacred spiritual places which you must visit in your Nepal Tour. Not only will it enrich your mind with divine grace but also fine-tune your tired spirit from the chaos of the world.

Some of the most popular spiritual places you must visit here are Boudhanath Stupa, Pashupatinath Temple, World Peace Pagoda, Kopan Monastery, Muktinath Temple, Lumbini, Swayambhunath and Namo Buddha etc.

Bungee jumping is one of the best things to do in Nepal as it has some of the world's highest Bungee jumping points. Out of many Bungee Jumping points, you must try Bhote Koshi River Bungee jumping point which is a 160 m drop from a suspension bridge.
The next iconic Bungee Jumping point is Kushma Bungee Jump which is the second highest Bungee Jump. It is a 228 meter drop, offering intense adrenaline rush amidst the beautiful natural setting.

Your Nepal holidays will be incomplete if you don't indulge in a wildlife safari adventure here. There are many thrilling wildlife sanctuaries and national parks to enjoy nature and wildlife safari with your loved ones.

Some of the most notable National parks to explore wildlife and rich biodiversity of Nepal are Parsa National Park, Shuklaphanta National Park, Banke National Park, Chitwan National Park and Bardia National Park.

blocks.text: Nepal Visa & Entry Requirements for Indian Tourists 2026

items: Indian Citizens: No visa required to enter Nepal. However, you must carry a valid Indian Passport (minimum 6 months validity) OR a valid Voter ID Card issued by the Election Commission of India. Aadhaar Card is also accepted at most border checkpoints as of 2023.
OCI Card Holders & NRIs: OCI cardholders must carry their OCI card along with their foreign passport. A separate Nepal visa is not required but passport must be valid.
Other Nationalities: Most foreign nationals can get a Nepal Visa on Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. 15-day visa: USD 30, 30-day visa: USD 50, 90-day visa: USD 125.
Note: Land border crossing (Sonauli, Raxaul etc.) requires same documents as above.

blocks.text: Nepal Trekking Permits — What You Need to Know

items: TIMS Card (Trekkers' Information Management System): Required for most trekking routes. Cost: INR 600 approx. for SAARC nationals (Indians included). Available at Nepal Tourism Board office in Kathmandu or Pokhara.
Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP): Required for Annapurna Circuit, Poon Hill, and Muktinath treks. Cost: NPR 3,000 approx.
Sagarmatha National Park Entry: Required for Everest Base Camp trek. Cost: NPR 3,000 approx. for SAARC nationals.
Upper Mustang & Manaslu: Restricted Area Permit required — cost significantly higher (USD 500+ for Mustang). Contact us to arrange.
Currency: Nepalese Rupee (NPR). As of 2026, approximately 1 INR = 1.6 NPR (check current rates before travel).

Indian Rupees accepted? Yes — Indian currency notes of INR 100, 200, 500 are widely accepted in Nepal, especially near border areas and tourist zones. However, carry Nepalese currency for remote areas.
ATMs: Available in Kathmandu, Pokhara, and most tourist towns. Limit per withdrawal is typically NPR 35,000. Carry some cash for trekking routes.
Exchange: Best rates at authorized money changers in Thamel (Kathmandu) or Pokhara Lakeside. Airport exchange rates are less favorable.

blocks.text: Q-1: What is the best time to trek in Nepal to view clear skies and avoid rain?

Q-2: Do I Need a Visa to enter Nepal from India?

Ans: Indian visitors do not need a visa to enter Nepal. You need a valid Indian Passport (with minimum 6 months validity), Voter ID Card issued by the Election Commission of India, or Aadhaar Card (accepted at most checkpoints). OCI cardholders must carry their OCI card and foreign passport.

blocks.text: Kainchi Dham Tour Package from Delhi
Set out on a divine trip with a visit to the Kainchi Dham. See More

In addition, we’ll also take you for a sightseeing tour of Nainital. In this 2 Nights and 3 Days Kainchi Dham tour package from Delhi , you can seize a once-in-a-lifetime experience with a cozy stay at well-appointed nearby accommodation along with delicious vegetarian meals. Additionally, you can access the local cultural experience by visiting the nearby markets, temples and villages.
About Kainchi Dham and Neem Karoli Baba

Kainchi Dham is a serene Ashram known for its spiritual significance. The Ashram was established by Neem Karoli Baba , who was also known as Maharaj ji in the 1960s. Located near Nainital , Uttarakhand , it is believed to have performed many miracles in the lives of devotees. Celebrities like Steve Jobs , Mark Zuckerberg , Virat Kohli etc have visited the place due to its high popularity.

The moment you step in the Kainchi Dham Ashram, you are sure to experience an unmatched divine atmosphere that’s going to fill you with immense peace. The Ashram is dedicated to Lord Hanuman and also houses the Samadhi of Neem Karoli Baba. It can be a great place to unplug from the hassle of big cities and engage in meditation here.

Daily rituals, Pooja, spiritual practices like collective meditation are performed in the ashram. The Ashram also organizes a grand feast (Bhandara) on June 15th every year. One must experience the energy of the serene and peaceful environment of this place at least once in their lives.
Why Choose Kainchi Dham Tour Package?

Choose the right package for Neem Karoli Baba Dham Darshan to witness the spiritual essence along with the beauty of Nainital’s hills. Here’s some of the benefits of choosing My Quick Trippers’s package:

items: Transportation: We provide a comfortable travel option starting from your pick up point in Delhi to Kainchi Dham via a shared transport or private vehicle.
Accommodation: We provide the most comfortable hotels in and around Nainital to make your stay even better.
Sightseeing: You can go around and explore the nearby attractions of Nainital.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Kainchi Dham from Delhi

The best time to visit Kainchi Dham Ashram is between March and June (summer) or September to November (autumn), as the weather stays pleasant during these months, which helps enhance your overall tour experience.

In the peak season, that is summers, the ashram draws a large number of people from every corner of the world. And, therefore, it can sometimes get very crowded. Therefore, we suggest the autumn window, if you prefer fewer crowds.
There are many places to visit near Kainchi Dham that travellers must visit-

Naini Lake, also called Nainital Lake, is the main place to visit and a popular spot near Kainchi Dham. It is surrounded by seven beautiful hills and attracts travelers from all over the world. Many tourists come here, so it's known as one of the most visited lakes in India.

The name “Nainital” comes from two words- “Naina” means eye, and “Tal” means lake. In Hindu mythology, when Sati jumped into the fire, her eyes fell here, and the lake formed at this spot. Because of this, the lake is very special to many people. The boat ride is a relaxing and gives a unique experience that visitors shouldn’t miss. The views from the boat are wonderful for taking photos. A must-addition to the your Kainchi Dham Yatra package!

items: Entry Fee- There is no entry fee to visit Naini Lake. However, if you want to enjoy the boat ride, a small ticket fee is charged.

blocks.text: Bhowali is a peaceful town in Kumaon, located 1704 meters above sea level. This place is well known for growing great fruits like apples, peaches, strawberries, plums, and apricots that are sent to many places. The views in Bhowali are beautiful, and many travelers come here for camping, trekking, and enjoying nature. The place is peaceful and nice, so it’s good to visit anytime. You can often see animals like jackals, kakkar, Himalayan eagles, and pheasants here.

Neem Karoli Baba Ashram is a special place that many people visit for spiritual peace. It’s close to Kainchi Dham and is built in memory of the great saint Neem Karoli Baba. The ashram has a calm and positive atmosphere. It’s a nice place to relax and learn. People also take part in prayers and satsangs every day.

Pangot is a small and beautiful village approximately 28 km away from Kainchi Dham. It’s well known for its forests and a variety of birds. When you reach Pangot, it’s like entering a peaceful mountain village, away from all the city noise. If you enjoy birdwatching, you’ll love this place because more than 300 bird species can be seen nearby. Birds like woodpeckers, thrushes, and sometimes even eagles can be seen here. If you're looking for peace or enjoy spending time in nature, Pangot is a wonderful place to visit. If you're on a Kainchi Dham trip, do come here as it’s a refreshing visit.

The town of Bhimtal is named after Bhima, one of the well-known Pandava brothers in the Mahabharata. It is famous for its beautiful lake. People love it for its wonderful surroundings, and it is located at 1,370 metres above sea level. In the middle of Bhimtal Lake, there’s a small island with a big aquarium. Earlier, this aquarium was a restaurant. This lake is surrounded by natural beauty, has lovely views, and is well connected by road. It’s a good place to visit in any season.
How to Reach Kainchi Dham from Delhi?

Road trip from Delhi to Kainchi Dham takes around 6 to 7 hours and is the easiest way to reach there. You can either drive yourself or take a taxi. You can also travel from Delhi to Haldwani by bus or train, and then take a taxi from Haldwani to Kainchi Dham.

If you’re travelling by train, Kathgodam is the nearest station. Trains like the Ranikhet Express or Uttar Sampark Kranti Express take about 6 hours from Delhi to Kathgodam. From there, Kainchi Dham is 43 km away. You can easily find taxis or shared cabs outside the station. Road to Kainchi Dham is good and has lovely views of hills and forests.

If you want to travel by flight, the nearest airport to Kainchi Dham is Pantnagar Airport, around 70 km away. It is a small airport with limited flights. From there, you can take a taxi or a local bus to reach Kainchi Dham.
Here's what you should bring for a Kainchi Dham Darshan:

items: Medical Needs: Remember to carry motion sickness tablets (only if your doctor says it’s okay), some vomit bags, lemon candies, a small towel, and water to help you stay comfortable and fresh during the trip.
Comfortable Shoes: Choose comfortable shoes or sandals with a good grip so you can walk easily in the hills.
Power Bank / Portable Charger: Electricity may not always work well in the hills, so bring a power bank to keep your phone charged.
Snacks with High Energy: Carry energy bars, nuts, or dry fruits with you because shops can be far away, and these snacks will keep you active during walks or temple visits.

blocks.text: Travel Tips for Kainchi Dham Tour

items: Don’t go on Crowded Days: On June 15th, there’s a Bhandara, and thousands of devotees come. It’s better to skip that day unless you’re okay with big crowds.
Avoid Plastic and Keep the Area Clean: Try to keep the place clean. Don’t use plastic bags or bottles, and always throw trash in the dustbin.
Carry Some Cash: You’ll find only a few ATMs around, and they don’t always work. Many shops won’t take a card or UPI, so make sure you have some cash with you.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. Why is Kainchi Dham so popular?

Ans. It is a spiritual ashram located in Uttarakhand. It was established by Neem Karoli Baba, who was a spiritual guru. The ashram is believed to have performed many miracles and transformed the lives of many devotees.
Q2. How to reach Kainchi Dham?
Ans. It is located 20 km away from Nainital. The nearest Airport is Pantnagar airport, and the nearest railway station is Kathgodam.
Q3. Are meals included in the package?
Ans. Vegetarian meals are included in the package at the hotel and are served as Prasad at Kainchi Dham.
Q4. Is there any dress code to visit the Ashram?
Ans. There is no strict dress code, however, it is recommended to dress modestly, considering the spiritual nature of the ashram.
Q5. What activities are available at Kainchi Dham Ashram?
Ans. There are a variety of activities available at the Ashram. You can engage here in meditation, Satsang, Yoga sessions, Temple Rituals and even Seva.
Q6. How far is Kainchi Dham from Delhi?
Ans. Kainchi Dham is located about 330 km from Delhi. This 7–8-hour drive is quite scenic as you pass through the Himalayan foothills and forests.
Q7. When is the best time to visit Kainchi Dham?

Ans. The best time to visit Kainchi Dham is from March to June in summer. This window offers you quite pleasant weather where you can comfortably indulge in sightseeing and other things. Another great period to come down here is in the autumn season, that is, from September to November. The skies are clear in this season, and you get to enjoy fewer crowds.
Q8. Is photography allowed inside Kainchi Dham?
Ans. The Kainchi Dham is quite sacred, and therefore, to maintain its sanctity, the photography inside the ashram is restricted. However, you can capture the pics from outside!
Q9. Do I need prior permission to visit Kainchi Dham Ashram?
Ans. If you're visiting for a single day, you don’t need to obtain any prior permission. However, if you wish to stay inside the Ashram, special permission is required from the management staff.
Q10. Are there any accommodation facilities near Kainchi Dham?

Ans. Yes, Kainchi Dham has so many guesthouses and small hotels nearby it that you can easily stay near the Ashram. With our package, you get to enjoy staying in a comfortable accommodation, which will be booked by us on your behalf.

blocks.text: Step ahead and tick all the must-visit landmark destinations in Kathmandu and other temple sites of Nepal in one go with our all-inclusive Kathmandu Tour Packages. Cover essential sightseeing spots in Kathmandu, the famous Pashupatinath Temple, and other heritage architecture at Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Most of our Kathmandu travel packages include hotel accommodation, transportation, meals, and sightseeing at all places. So, don't miss any opportunity to mingle with locals and experience the vibrant Nepali culture throughout your journey with the most convenient and affordable package deals.

Nepal tourism is generally growing day by day due to improved infrastructure and rich hospitality. In 2025, there has been a significant rise in the number of tourists in Nepal. Over 577,000 tourists visited Nepal in the first half of 2025, among which most tourists visited Kathmandu ( Rising Nepal Daily ). Here is some essential information about Kathmandu tourism that will help you to plan your trip with family and customize your Kathmandu itinerary.

items: Kathmandu Durbar Square - Also known as Basantapur Durbar Square or Hanuman Dhoka Durbar Square, it is one of the most popular tourist attractions of Kathmandu. Revel in the charm of Newar architecture. It used to be the kingdom of Malla kings and the Shah dynasty.

Swayambhunath - Swayambhunath is Kathmandu's most iconic religious attraction. This beautiful stupa has both Buddhist and Hindu influences. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Kathmandu. It is also known as the Monkey Temple.

Pashupatinath Temple - Pashupatinath Temple is a sacred site to visit in Kathmandu. It's built in traditional Nepalese pagoda architecture. It is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Nepal dedicated to Lord Shiva. Before becoming a very grand temple in the Licchavi period, it was a basic shrine (Linga). It's also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Boudhanath Stupa - A UNESCO World Heritage site, the Boudhanath Stupa is one of the most beautiful and largest spherical Stupas in the world. Witness its golden spire, which is painted with Buddha's eyes. It is a major pilgrimage center for Tibetan and Nepali Buddhists.

Garden of Dreams - Garden of Dreams is a beautiful neoclassical-style garden located in Kathmandu. It was built in 1920. It used to have six beautiful pavilions in the garden, which represent six seasons of Nepal, though only three pavilions remain today. It has scenic fountains, ponds, and landscaped lawns perfect for leisure walks.

Kopan Monastery - Lama Thubten Yeshe and Lama Zopa Rinpoche established Kopan Monastery in 1969 at the outskirts of Kathmandu on Kopan Hill. If you are interested in doing some courses related to spirituality or capturing the scenic views of the entire Kathmandu Valley, then you must visit this place.

Chandragiri Cable Car - Enjoy the best views of the Himalayan mountain ranges and Kathmandu Valley through the Chandragiri Cable Car ride. It runs from Thankot to the top of Chandragiri hills. At the top of the hill, pay your respects at Bhaleshwor Mahadev Temple, which is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

rows: Explore Nagarjun Forest Reserve, Kirtipur hills, Godavari Botanical Garden, and Taudaha Lake.
Enjoy a cable car ride to Chandragiri Hills, hike around Phulchoki and Nagarkot to capture stunning sunrise and mountain views, and enjoy the views of Mt. Everest by helicopter.
Visit Swayambhu Stupa, Pashupatinath Mandir, Boudhanath Stupa, and Dakshinkali Temple to nourish your soul spiritually with divine wisdom.

Enjoy some of the most delicious items like Momos, Panipuri, and Newari dishes at Thamel and Freak Street, Snowman Cafe, and Janakpur Dahi Lassi Bhandar. You can also try Tingmo and Aloo Phing, Masco Bara, Sekuwa, Juju Dhau, Gundruk, Choila, Yomari, and Sel Roti in Kathmandu.

Visit Asan Bazaar, Indra Chowk, Kalimati Fruits & Vegetable Market, Khichapokhari Market, Patan Durbar Square Market, and Boudha Stupa Market for spice products, pashmina scarves, beads, handicrafts, Newari snacks, decor items, wood carvings, Paubha paintings, traditional Tibetan garments, and accessories.

Round Trip Flights for Kathmandu from Delhi

items: The price for round trip for Kathmandu (KTM) from Delhi (DEL) starts from INR 13,000 to 14,000 per person if booked in advance for economy category.
Some of the major airlines to get direct flights to Kathmandu are Indigo, Air India, Nepal Airlines, Bhutan Airlines and SpiceJet.

Based on your budget you will get good hotels to stay in Kathmandu. If you want Budget Hotels to stay in Kathmandu then the price range would be around INR 500 to 1500 per night in Hostels and guesthouses.
For mid-range hotels in Kathmandu, the price range would be around INR 1500 to 4000 per night in 3 stars to 4-star hotels.
If you are looking for luxury hotels in Kathmandu then you may have to pay around INR 6000 to 15,000 per night in mountain lodges, hotels with wellness centers, 4-5-star hotels.

blocks.text: For Lavish restaurants you have to pay 800- 2000 per day and for local food you have to pay around INR 400 TO 800 per day on average.

Local transportation in Kathmandu is quite affordable which includes buses, taxis, Tuk-Tuks and rickshaws. Depending on the distance the public bus tickets range from NPR 200 to 1000 per day within Kathmandu. For short rides, you can opt for Tuk-Tuk which will cost around NPR 10 to NPR 20.
Activities and Attractions Cost in Kathmandu

When not to visit Kathmandu - June to August

June to August are monsoon months in Kathmandu which can be avoided as you will experience heavy rainfall and humidity. In some areas you will also face landslides, flooding which can make your travel very challenging.

Major Airports with Direct Flights from India to Reach Kathmandu

items: To reach Kathmandu from India by road, the route is a bit longer. If you are adventurous and want to enjoy scenic views then only opt for this mode of travel. To reach here by road you have to cross the India Nepal border at Sonauli.

Ans: Some of the things which you must avoid doing in Kathmandu are-

items: Never drink water from Taps in Kathmandu. Only drink bottled water.
Never take things from your left hand as it is impolite and inauspicious in Kathmandu to accept anything from your left hand.
Wearing revealing clothes in sacred places is strictly prohibited.
Don't walk around Stupas anti-clockwise. Walking clockwise is a sign of respect.

blocks.text: Here we discuss places that must be added to your Varanasi travel itinerary . We also discuss the popular things to do in Varanasi for pilgrims:

rows: This is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva . The Kashi Vishwanath Temple tour must be a part of any Varanasi Package from Hyderabad! Take pictures of the golden dome and the sacred Ganga views from here.

Come here for the daily Ganga Aarti. You'll be stunned by the grand spectacle that takes place here everyday in the evening. The surroundings are lit by the bright lamps while the holy mantras are chanted in the background.
This is a Buddhist pilgrimage site located about 10 km from Varanasi. Also, enjoy the Dhamek Stupa and Ashokan Pillar here.
You can come at this Ghat to do yoga and meditation. Also, sunrise boat rides are a must-try experience here.
This is one of the oldest cremation Ghats in the city. More than just a burning ground for the dead, it symbolises the recurrent cycle of life and death.
Visiting here is a must on any Varanasi heritage tour. You can see the royal artefacts from the 18th century in this museum.
This university has the largest campus in the entire country. It also houses the New Vishwanath Temple, which has a modern architecture.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Varanasi from Hyderabad

The best time to come to Varanasi is hands down in the season of winter ( October-March ). The weather in this period is quite pleasant and cool, and therefore makes for an excellent time to come here and indulge in sightseeing and go on temple tours. It's the perfect time to book your Kashi Yatra from Hyderabad!
Also, we advise against coming here in the summers ( April-June ) when the weather is quite hot and humid and therefore is unsuitable for sightseeing.
How to Reach Varanasi from Hyderabad?
You're in luck because Varanasi is well-connected to Hyderabad by all three modes of transportation, such as air, train, and road. Here's the Varanasi travel guide from Hyderabad:

There are direct Hyderabad to Varanasi flights. All you have to do is take a plane from the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport to the Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport. You'll land in the holy city in just about 2 hours.
We also offer you the best Varanasi Tour Packages from Hyderabad with flights that will take care of your travel logistics, in addition to, all the plane-related arrangements.

You can also go from Hyderabad to Varanasi by train! This is an ideal mode of travel for the budget-conscious travellers. You will reach the holy city in about 25 hours. The regular trains on this route include Secunderabad-Varanasi Express and Hyderabad-Patna Express.

If you love a long road trip, then go for the Hyderabad to Varanasi road package. You can use the highways like NH44 and NH19. The journey through central India is quite scenic. And you'll love the lengthy drive that this journey offers you.
Varanasi is popular for so many things, ranging from religious articles to traditional garments. Here's what to shop for on your Varanasi tour from Hyderabad:

items: Banarasi Silk Sarees : Feel like royalty with this Varanasi speciality. For the best purchases, go to Chowk, Thatheri Bazar, or Godowlia Market.
Wooden Toys and Brassware : The holy city is famous for things like these. These items also make for a good souvenir for your friends and family.

Spiritual Items : Varanasi, being a holy city, makes for the perfect market to stock up on religious items at home. You can easily find good-quality Rudraksha beads and other sorts of Malas here. In addition, you can also get idols and holy books here.

blocks.text: There are so many popular foods in Varanasi . Here are some of the most famous dishes of the holy city:

items: Kachori Sabzi : This is often savoured as the breakfast. You get to enjoy Kachori with the thick gravy of Aaloo Sabji. Try it at least once on your Varanasi trip from Hyderabad!
Banarasi Paan : It's famous all over the country and even has a Bollywood song on it! It's often consumed after meals.
Tamatar Chaat : This street snack is commonly found in the alleys of Varanasi. This is a delectable combination of sweet and spicy flavors.
Malaiyyo : This creamy milk dessert is often relished after lunch meal. However, it's only available in winters. Do enjoy it if you come here in the colder season.
Lassi : Have a big refreshing glass of the thick Lassi with your food. The creamy taste of the beverage will give you the taste of heaven!

Hyderabad → Nagpur → Jabalpur → Rewa → Mirzapur → Varanasi
Travel Tips for Hyderabad to Varanasi Tour
Here are some travel tips for your tour in the holy city:

items: To avoid hassle and long queues, book your slot online for the Kashi Vishwanath Darshan.
When you're in the city, make sure you attend the Ganga Aarti at least once during your trip, as it's one of the most important experiences there.

Avoid taking pictures at the cremation Ghats such as Manikarnika Ghat.

For the best boat ride experience, go to the Ghats in the early morning.

Q5. Is photography allowed during Ganga Aarti?
Ans. Yes, you can take photographs during Ganga Aarti. However, do not use flash photography.

acceptedAnswer.text: Uttarakhand being located at a great altitude witnesses unfavorable climatic condition in monsoon months thus, we don’t recommend you to plan your holiday in the monsoon months. blocks.text: Best Places to Visit on your Trip to Uttarakhand

Uttarakhand has amazing destinations to captivate senses. No doubt, People have been visiting Uttarakhand ever since the beginning of time for performing meditation, spending time coexisting with nature, and observing the natural beauty blessed by the gods themselves. Here are some of the best points of tourist interests in Uttarakhand.

items: Visit this renowned pilgrimage town and “Yoga capital of the world”. The place attracts huge number of spiritual seekers, adventure lovers and solace seekers.

You can try amazing adventure activities like rafting, trekking, witness Ganga Aarti and visit ashrams, yoga and meditation hubs. It is also a getaway to the famous Chardhams – Gangotri , Yamunotri , Kedarnath and Badrinath Dhams.
Haridwar is one of the seven holiest places in Hinduism. It is a popular spiritual getaway to fine-tune your spirits looking for peace.
Embrace the peace of Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Paudi Ghat. Visit numerous temples and ashrams. It is also a best starting point for the holy Chardham Yatra.

Located in Chamoli district, the Valley of Flowers in Uttarakhand is one of the most popular places for nature lovers. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It will show you stunning natural views for photography.
The valley has rich floral wealth. It has floras with over 500 species of flowers including endangered flowers like Brahma Kamal, Blue Poppy etc.
Located in Nainital, it is India’s oldest Tiger reserves and National Park. If you love wildlife adventures then you must book a wildlife Safari in Jim Corbett National Park.

The park has 9 safari zones for wildlife viewing and nature sightseeing. Each zone offers unique natural views. Here you can try Jeep safari, Canter Safari, Bird watching, nature walks and elephant safaris etc.

No doubt. You must visit Chardhams in Uttarakhand- Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath Dham. Every traveller or devotee craves to get a once in a lifetime opportunity to visit these holy places.
If you plan your Chardham Yatra in summer (April- May) or in August to September, you will be able to get the divine Darshan of the duties.
These sites are considered the holiest pilgrimage places for Hindu devotees. You need to book in advance for this Yatra.
Don’t miss this picturesque Ski destination in Uttarakhand. It is the one of the best places to visit in Uttarakhand if you love adventure.
The beauty of Auli is unbeatable as it is surrounded by lush coniferous and Oak trees, attracting nature lovers also from all across India.
Try the best activity Ski here. Its slopes are good for both seasoned and beginner skier. Nearby Auli, you can also visit Adi Shankaracharya Ashram in Joshimath.

The city of lakes – Nainital is captivating the hearts of tourists for decades with its scenic beauty. It is one of the best hill stations in Uttarakhand for family vacations, honeymoon and solo weekend trips.

Nainital is a scenic wonder. It houses the most beautiful Naina Lake and a Shaktipeetha, Naina Devi temple. These two places are the most popular ones but don’t miss these iconic spots too like Eco cave garden, Mall Road, Snow view point, Naina Peak etc.

Embark on Soul Pleasing Spiritual Journeys

blocks.text: Dive Deep into the Enchanting Wilderness

You can book your wildlife Safari at Jim Corbett National Park, Rajaji National Park, Binsar wildlife Sanctuary or Ashok Musk Deer Sanctuary.
There are many rare Himalayan wild creatures to see like snow leopard, Musk deer and Himalayan Brown Bear etc. Also capture Tigers, Himalayan Monal, Serow, Red panda and Himalayan Tahr.

blocks.text: If Safari is Not Enough Try Thrilling Adventure Activities

items: Apart from wildlife safaris, you can also try numerous adventure activities like river rafting, bungee jumping in Rishikesh and Shivpuri, trekking in Valley of flowers, Nag Tibba, Skiing in Auli, camping in Rishikesh, Chopta and Dhanaulti.
You can also try paragliding in Ranikhet and Mukteshwar and mountain biking in Rishikesh and Mussoorie.

blocks.text: Uttarakhand Travel Tips for Unforgettable Memories with Your Loved Ones

items: Offbeat Beauty- We often plan trips to crowded and popular places. This time, try offbeat destinations too. The offbeat destinations in Uttarakhand are less crowded and beautiful. Some of our best picks are-Binsar, Munsiyari, Chakrata, Chopta, Sattal for peaceful moments.
Licensed Guides- Hire only licensed adventure guides to safely do your adventure activities. Accidents happen when we fail to take precautions and be careless about safety.

Dress Modesty- Respect the traditions and customs. Uttarakhand is known as Devbhoomi so it has numerous temples. If you are visiting any temples, dress conservatively. Cover your head, knees and shoulders.
Take Permission- Don’t take photos and videos of sacred sites without permission.
Enough Cash- Keep enough Cash as there are many remote places where you won’t find ATM’s or strong net connectivity for digital payments.
What to Pack- Pack weather specific clothes to get the best experience of sightseeing tours. Also, carry a comfortable footwear as you may have to walk a lot as Uttarakhand is a hill destination.

Physical Fitness- You need to be physically fit to try trekking and other adventure activities. People will mobility issues have limited options but they can visit the scenic hill stations, temples and indulge in having delicious cuisines etc.
Advance Planning- If you are planning your Chardham Yatra then you need to register your Yatra in advance from official website .
Cleanliness- Protect the serenity and beauty of the mountains. Keep your surroundings clean, don’t litter.

blocks.text: China is an ancient country and one of those nations where one of the great human civilizations was born and nurtured, with a history spanning over 5000 years it is a tempting place for tourists on Tour Packages. Not only history the vast and varied geography of China is a huge attraction in itself, extending from the deserts in the west and to the ocean in the east, snowcapped mountains and green carpeted hilly region, this place provides unforgettable time on Tour Packages.

Some of the topnotch attractions of China deserving to be a part of every tour package include historical places, natural spots, cities and architectural wonders. The Forbidden City or Palace Museum is at the center of the city of Beijing, a UNESCO world heritage site and imperial seat of Qing and Ming dynasty. The Great Wall of China is not to miss attraction of this country, an architectural grandeur which took more than 2000 years to complete. The views from the wall are mesmerizing and unending view of the wall captivates the visitors, truly a wonder and must visit on China Tour Packages.

Hangzhou is called China’s paradise on Earth, this city is cultural center of China and situated around famous West Lake. This city has greenery, tranquil temples, hills surrounding the city with green slopes and streets full of historical buildings. The atmosphere in the city is very relaxing and calm and one finds it soothing place to be on China Holiday Packages. Potala Palace in Lhasa is now a Chinese museum with imposing white walls surrounding the red colored majestic palace inside with golden roof. This palace used to be the seat of Dalai Lama but now houses many wonderful exhibits depicting history, art and culture of the country. Tibet is full of natural splendor and one must not miss a chance to visit this place on China Travel Packages.

No China Holiday Package is complete without visiting Xian, this city is one of the seven ancient capitals of China and served as capital for more than 1000 years. This city houses many ancient relics and remnants of China’s imperial history. Places like Entombed Warriors the eighth wonder of the world, two Buddhist Pagodas named as Big Wild Goose and Small Wild Goose Pagodas, the City Wall and Banpo Site a prehistoric museum are must see places of Xian on China Travel Packages.

One cannot miss Hong Kong while on China Tour Package. Named as Oriental London, this city has fusion of many cultures and an exotic display of amalgamation of modernism with ancient traditions. World’s most famous shopping paradise and a vibrant city has many natural places to visit, Lantau Island are one of them. Exotic beaches and nightlife is the biggest attraction of this city for tourists on Tour Packages. Guilin is famous for its stunning natural beauty and attracts people on Tour Packages by its verdant mountains, unique rockeries, crystal clear waters and unique caves and stones of different shapes. Ethnic minorities living here since ages add up to the cultural wealth of this city and makes it a captivating place to be on China Tour Packages.

Book your tour package to Lumbini and experience the best of hospitality and guiding, with our experienced tour guides in Nepal.

It is one of the growing tourist destinations and has also been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There are multiple architectural masterpieces in Lumbini and many different monasteries. Those who are scholars in religious studies also visit Lumbini for research. It is a place with a very rich cultural history. There are places like Maya Devi Temple which is known as the shrine of Lord Buddha’s mother, all these places are something you cannot miss.

One can also include Pokhara or Chitwan in your Lumbini package, both the places are mesmerizing and worth visiting once. Pokhara is a perfect holiday destination with rivers, greenery, and picturesque landscapes, you can do a lot of water activities in Pokhara and enjoy the nightlife. Chitwan is the first national wildlife park in Nepal where you can find many exotic animals.

blocks.text: Philippines Tour Packages are a trip to rich history and culture, exotic beaches, dense forests, ancient forts, museums, cool mountains, luxuriant man-made resorts and dazzling islands. Philippines Travel Packages offers more than 40 thousand kilometers of coral reefs with wide variety of aquatic life, this is the best place to enjoy sunlight surrounded by Pacific Ocean its sunrise and sunsets are exhilarating. Visiting country’s mountain villages, exploring vast pastoral lands and dense forests under the spell of cool mountain breeze is perfect setting for romantic and unforgettable Philippines Tour Package.

Manila is an ancient city and capital of Philippines and must see on Tour Packages. Ancient castles, forts and churches, stately museums, ancestral edifices and enchanting historical monuments are at each step in this city. Towards South of Manila lies enthralling place called as ‘Enchanted Kingdom’, an amusement park built on the theme of Disney land. People on Philippines Holiday Packages visit this place for thrills, excitement, fun, food and shopping. The old city of Intramuros, Rizal Park and Binondo area are other attractions around the city of Manila.

Boracay island has unsullied white-sand beaches with fine talcum powder like sand and cool waters perfect for swimming, fishing, sun-bathing and sailing. Countless hidden coves, tall coconut trees and exotic sunset are other attractions of this island. Siargao Island has white-sand beaches and surfing waves and this newly found attraction of Philippine Tour Packages is compared with islands of Hawaii, this place is called as surfing Mecca. Samal Island is a part of nine island Archipelago having cool weather and white-sand beaches with rock formations, coral reefs, mangroves and rolling hills. Tall swaying coconut trees make it perfect spot to enjoy sun and sea on Philippines Holiday Packages.

Palawan is known as last frontier of Philippines and its undefiled beauty is truly mesmerizing, it has white-sand beaches and rare flora and fauna found nowhere else. While visiting Palawan on Philippines Travel Packages tourists can see Tubbataha Reef, a water marine park and listed in World heritage list, Saint Paul National Park having caves nestling an underground river, El nido boasting of awe-inspiring seascape and limestone cliffs and Calauit Island with rich African and Philippine wildlife.

Baguio city is another popular attraction of Philippines Tour Packages as this city is called as ‘Summer Capital’ of the country. Lying amidst pine tree hills and valleys is famous for scenic views, cool weather, lawns of club John Hay, Burnham Park, Mansion house and Banaue Rice Terraces. Tagaytay is another place where tourists on Tour Packages to Philippines love to go as this city is at 2250 feet above the sea level and enjoying cool weather throughout the year. It overlooks Taal Lake, Taal volcano, Manila Bay, Laguna Bay and China Sea. The mountain province town of Sagada offers limestone cliffs, subterranean caves and unexplored forests, amongst other attractions of this place are Kitongan bottom less pit, Cavalry hill, Alipine Lake banao and Butang falls.

Apart from these there are many other attractions in Philippines for tourists on Tour Packages, Subic Bay, beaches of Sarangani Bay, Taal Lake, Taal volcano, Puerto Galarea, Hundred Islands, Pagsanjan falls and Hidden valley springs are other premier attractions of this country.

blocks.text: Aizawl, the capital city of Mizoram in northeastern India, is a captivating destination offering a blend of cultural richness, natural beauty, and vibrant traditions. Tour packages to Aizawl encapsulate a diverse array of experiences, catering to both adventure seekers and those craving a serene getaway.

These packages often include visits to prominent landmarks such as the iconic Mizoram State Museum, showcasing the state’s cultural heritage through its exhibits of tribal artifacts, traditional costumes, and historical relics. Travellers can immerse themselves in the local culture by exploring the bustling markets, like the Bara Bazaar, known for its indigenous crafts, handwoven textiles, and local delicacies.

Nature enthusiasts find solace in the lush landscapes surrounding Aizawl. Tour packages frequently encompass trips to the enchanting Durtlang Hills, offering panoramic views of the cityscape, and the Baktawng Village, home to the world’s largest family. blocks.text: Dalhousie is one of the most popular hill stations in the district of Chamba located in Himachal Pradesh. Dalhousie is present in the outskirts of the Dhauladhar ranges in Himachal Pradesh. The hill station is named after Lord Dalhousie – the founder of the place. Surrounding Dalhousie there are 5 hills and they are- Tehra, Bakrota, Balun, Kathlog and Petreyn. It covers an area of about 13 sq km. Dalhousie ranges between the altitude of 1,525m – 2,378m above the level of the sea. The Dalhousie Tour Packages include the entire area.

In 1903 the St Andrew’s Church also known as the Church of Scotland was built. It is a Protestant Catholic Church in Baloon. The St Francis Church is a replica of one the famous Church in England. The church has a striking blend of stone and glass work. Apart from these two churches, the Dalhousie Holiday Packages also include the St Patrick’s Church and the St John’s Church. Scottish and Victorian architecture is the main beauty of these monuments. In between a dense forest is the Bara Pathar Temple. The temple is famous for the forest. One of the most picturesque places to visit in Dalhousie is Panchpula. It is the stream in Panchpula that adds to the splendor of the place.

At a height of about 2,000 m above the level of the sea is located Khajjar. It is at a distance of 27 km from the town of Dalhousie. There is a small lake surrounded by deodar and pine trees. There is a 12th century temple in this lush green vicinity. The Dalhousie Tour Packages include Subhash Baoli,which is a famous spot named after Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose – an eminent freedom fighter of India. Kalatop is another spot that provides you with the picturesque view of the areas surrounding Dalhousie. It is located at a height of about 2,440 m above the level of the sea and is at 8.5 km from Dalhousie.

At a distance of 10 km from Dalhousie town is Bakrota hills. It is at a height of about 2,745 m above the level of the sea. The Bakrota hills are very famous among tourists as it provides you with a picturesque view of the mountains. Dainkund is one of the most famous locations included in the Dalhousie Travel Packages. It is at an altitude of about 2,745 m above the level of the sea. On a clear day you can see the rivers – Chenab, Beas and Ravi, flowing. It is located at 10 km from Dalhousie.

Adventure sports play an important part in the Dalhousie holiday packages. The Bakrota hills provide good trekking opportunities. Trekking via the Chobia pass from Chamba to Udaipur is very famous. Trekking along Mcleod Gang from Chamba through Minkiani pass is another favorite route. The other sport that is very famous in Dalhousie is camping. The Khajjar Lake is a beautiful location for camping. The best season to visit Dalhousie is from the month of May till the month of September.

blocks.text: Kedarnath, located in the Indian state of Uttarakhand, is one of the most revered pilgrimage sites for Hindus. It is home to the famous Kedarnath Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva. The town is nestled amidst the picturesque Garhwal Himalayas, providing a breathtaking backdrop for spiritual seekers and nature enthusiasts alike. If you’re looking to embark on a spiritual journey to Kedarnath from Surat, Gujarat, there are several tour packages available to make your trip convenient and memorable.

Kedarnath tour packages from Surat typically include transportation, accommodation, and guided tours to ensure a hassle-free experience. Surat, being a major city, offers various options for travellers to choose from. These packages usually include flights or train journeys from Surat to Dehradun or Rishikesh, followed by a road trip to Gaurikund, the gateway to Kedarnath. From Gaurikund, pilgrims can either trek for about 16 kilometres or hire ponies, palanquins, or helicopters to reach the temple.

Once in Kedarnath, visitors can immerse themselves in the divine atmosphere and seek blessings at the ancient temple. The temple is believed to have been built by the Pandavas from the Hindu epic Mahabharata. The rugged and serene surroundings of Kedarnath offer a sense of tranquillity, making it an ideal place for meditation and introspection. Apart from the temple, Kedarnath also offers stunning views of snow-capped peaks, lush valleys, and gushing rivers. Visitors can explore nearby attractions such as Vasuki Tal, Chorabari Tal (Gandhi Sarovar), and Shankaracharya Samadhi. These sites add to the overall spiritual and natural experience of the journey.

Kedarnath is believed to be one of the twelve Jyotirlingas (radiant lingas) of Lord Shiva and holds immense religious significance. The town is situated at an altitude of 3,583 meters (11,755 feet) above sea level and is surrounded by breathtaking landscapes. The main attraction of Kedarnath is the Kedarnath Temple, which is believed to have been built by the Pandavas from the Hindu epic Mahabharata. The temple is renowned for its architectural beauty and spiritual aura. It is a symbol of faith and devotion for millions of devotees who undertake the arduous journey to seek blessings and attain spiritual enlightenment.
Best Places to Visit in Kedarnath:

Kedarnath Temple: The Kedarnath Temple is the most important attraction in the town. It is a magnificent stone structure dedicated to Lord Shiva. The temple stands amidst the snow-covered peaks of the Garhwal Himalayas and exudes a serene and divine atmosphere. Pilgrims can participate in the daily rituals and prayers performed at the temple and seek blessings.

Vasuki Tal: Located at a height of 4,150 meters (13,615 feet) above sea level, Vasuki Tal is a serene glacial lake near Kedarnath. Surrounded by snow-clad mountains, the lake offers a breathtaking view of the surrounding landscape. It is believed to be the abode of Lord Vishnu and is often visited by devotees and nature enthusiasts.

Chorabari Tal (Gandhi Sarovar): Situated at an altitude of 3,900 meters (12,800 feet), Chorabari Tal, also known as Gandhi Sarovar, is a beautiful lake located around 3 kilometers from Kedarnath. It is named after Mahatma Gandhi, who visited this place during his journey to Kedarnath. The lake is fed by the Chorabari Glacier and is surrounded by snow-covered peaks.

Shankaracharya Samadhi: Located behind the Kedarnath Temple, the Shankaracharya Samadhi is the final resting place of Adi Shankaracharya, the great philosopher and theologian who revived Hinduism in the 8th century. The samadhi is a place of great reverence and attracts devotees seeking spiritual solace.

Fitness and Health: The Kedarnath Yatra involves trekking at high altitudes, which can be physically demanding. It is advisable to undergo a medical check-up and ensure you are fit for the journey. Regular exercise, including cardiovascular activities and strength training, can help prepare your body for the trek.

Acclimatization: Due to the high altitude of Kedarnath, it is important to acclimatize properly before starting the trek. Spend a day or two in nearby towns like Rishikesh or Dehradun to allow your body to adjust to the altitude.

Packing Essentials: Pack light but carry essential items such as warm clothing, sturdy trekking shoes, rain gear, a first aid kit, sunscreen, sunglasses, and a hat. It is also advisable to carry some energy bars, water bottles, and a walking stick for the trek.

Accommodation and Bookings: Plan your accommodation in advance, especially during peak seasons, as the number of accommodations near Kedarnath is limited. There are various guesthouses and Dharamshalas available for pilgrims. It is recommended to book your accommodation well in advance to avoid any last-minute hassles.

The best time to visit Kedarnath is during the summer months of May to June and September to October. The weather during this time is pleasant, with temperatures ranging from 15°C to 20°C (59°F to 68°F). The snow starts melting, and the trekking routes become accessible. However, it is important to note that the weather in the mountains can be unpredictable, and sudden changes can occur. It is advisable to check the weather forecasts and plan your visit accordingly.

By Air: The nearest airport to Kedarnath is Jolly Grant Airport in Dehradun, which is well-connected to major cities in India. From the airport, you can hire a taxi or take a shared cab to reach Gaurikund, the starting point of the trek to Kedarnath.
By Train: The nearest railway station to Kedarnath is Rishikesh, which is well-connected to major cities in India. From Rishikesh, you can hire a taxi or take a bus to reach Gaurikund.

By Road: Kedarnath is well-connected by road to various cities in Uttarakhand. You can take a bus or hire a taxi from major cities like Dehradun, Rishikesh, or Haridwar to reach Gaurikund. From Gaurikund, you have the option to trek or hire a pony, palanquin, or helicopter to reach Kedarnath.

It is important to note that the last 16 kilometres of the journey from Gaurikund to Kedarnath can only be covered on foot, as vehicles are not allowed beyond Gaurikund. The trek is moderate to difficult and takes around 6-8 hours to complete. The path is well-marked, and there are resting points and refreshment stalls along the way.

Best Time: Arrive before 9 AM or after 3 PM on any day to avoid peak crowd. On Tuesdays the ashram stays open till 9 PM — the evening kirtan session (6–9 PM) draws significantly fewer visitors than the afternoon.
Dress Code: Cover head, shoulders, and knees before entering the main temple hall. The ashram does not provide scarves — carry your own. Footwear must be removed at the entrance gate.

Cash Withdrawal: Withdraw adequate cash at Kathgodam or Haldwani before heading towards Bhowali. The nearest ATMs to Kainchi Dham are in Bhowali town (6 km) and may run out of cash on high-footfall days like Tuesdays and June 15.

Photography Rules: Photography is allowed in the ashram garden and outer areas. Strictly not permitted inside the main sanctum and Samadhi hall. Volunteers will remind you — keep your phone away before entering the inner temple.
Mobile Network: Network signal inside the ashram is weak. Inform family before entering — plan for 1–2 hours without connectivity during the main darshan period.
Packing for Weather: Kainchi Dham sits at approximately 1,400m. Even in May–June, evenings are cool — carry a light jacket. October–November nights drop to 8–12°C, so pack thermals for autumn visits.

Senior Citizens: No trekking is required — the ashram entrance and main darshan area are on flat ground. The pathway has ramps and is wheelchair accessible. Ground-floor hotel rooms can be arranged on request.

June 15 Bhandara: For the 2026 Pratishtha Diwas Bhandara on June 15, accommodation in Bhowali and Nainital fills up early. If you are planning for this date, enquire with our team immediately to check availability.

Ans: Kainchi Dham is a sacred Ashram founded by Neem Karoli Baba in Uttarakhand. It holds a profound spiritual significance for Hindu devotees. The ashram is set against the backdrop of lush green rolling hills.
Q2: Can Devotees Stay in Kainchi Dham? What are the other places to stay near Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Yes, devotees can stay in Kainchi Dham but prior permission is needed from the authorities. You can stay for a maximum of 3 days. You will also find the best hotels in places like Nainital, Bhowali etc. There are many guest houses, Dharamshalas and popular hotels and resorts like Amar Valley Resort, Guru Kripa Guesthouse, The Riverside Resort, Hotel Green Valley Inn, Kinara Resort to stay near Kainchi Dham.
Q3: Are there food facilities in Kainchi Dham?
Ans: The Kainchi Dham Ashram offers Sattvic meals as Prasad (sacred food). The food is prepared with great devotion. During any festival, the devotees get special Prasad items like Jalebis and Kheer.
Q4: Can foreigners visit Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Yes, Kainchi Dham Ashram welcomes foreigners. Anyone with great devotion can visit the Ashram. It is open to all.
Q5: Do you offer guided tours for Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Yes, we offer guided tour packages for Kainchi Dham at best rates. Our itineraries cater to the needs and preferences of the tourists. We offer 24/7 support throughout the tour for the best pilgrimage experience.
Q6: What makes Kainchi Dham Special?

Ans: Kainchi Dham is famous because devotees have strong faith in Neem Karoli Baba. Its peaceful natural setting adds more charm to the Ashram. Devotees take part in spiritual Satsang's and indulge in meditation to nourish their mind, body and soul with inner peace and positivity.
Q7: Can families visit Kainchi Dham Ashram?
Ans: Yes, it is the best place for profound spiritual experience with your family. It is best if your kid is a bit older. For toddlers, the place can be difficult to stay engaged for a long time.
Q8: Is Kainchi Dham wheel chair accessible?

Ans: Yes, the ramps and wide pathways in the ashram are built to make it wheelchair friendly. Those with mobility issues can navigate the ashram comfortably. We offer wheelchair assistance to enjoy a smooth pilgrimage experience in Kainchi Dham.
Q9: Is photography allowed in Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Yes, photography is allowed in outer zones like ashram premises, gardens and natural surroundings but it is not allowed in sacred and inner temple zones. Don't take photos of sacred sensitive areas without permission.
Q10: What should devotees wear in Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Devotees should wear modest clothes. It is a sacred place, so you need to cover your head, shoulders and knees. Don't wear clothes which are too revealing.
Q11: What are the popular festivals celebrated in Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Some of the most popular festivals celebrated in Kainchi Dham are Pratishtha Diwas, Hanuman Jayanti, Guru Purnima, Maha Samadhi Bhandara, Ram Navami, Navratri and Shivratri.
Q12: What type of Sewa is offered in Kainchi Dham by the devotees?

Ans: Sewa is an integral part to enhance your divine connection with Neem Karoli Baba. Devotees can offer Sewa by involving in cleaning activities of the ashram, assisting in cooking meals, joining the musicians in Kirtans and Bhajans, help in office tasks (clerical work), offering assistance in festivals etc.
Q13: What is the best time to visit Kainchi Dham?
Ans: March to June, September to November is the best time to visit Kainchi Dham. The weather will be pleasant for nature walks, meditation sessions, spiritual activities and sightseeing.
Q14: What are the visiting hours of Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Kainchi Dham timings are 6:00am to 7:00pm from April to October and 7:00am to 6:00pm from November to March. Timings may change during peak festivals. Confirm current timings directly with the ashram before your visit. On Tuesdays, darshan continues till 9:00 PM.
Q15: What is Kainchi Dham Ashram timings for Tuesday Visit?
Ans: Tuesday visits in Kainchi Dham are considered sacred so it has different timing. On Tuesday the ashram remains open till 9:00pm with Kirtans following the evening Aarti.
Q16: Are there any entry fees to visit Kainchi Dham?
Ans: No, the entry to Kainchi Dham is free for Devotees. Entry fees are not required.
Q17: Are there any restaurants near Kainchi Dham?

Ans: Yes, you can visit Kesari Restaurant & Stay, Mehra Paradise and Cafe, Anupam's pure veg restaurant, Bhagwati restaurant. These restaurants offer local Kumaoni, Indian, Chinese, and simple homely snacks.
Q18: What are the best adventure activities to enjoy near Kainchi Dham within 50 km?
Ans: You can enjoy Paragliding in Bhimtal, Boating in Nainital, Trekking in Mukteshwar and Ziplining and camping in Sattal. All these places are located within a 50km range from Kainchi Dham.
Q19: What are the popular trekking routes from Kainchi Dham?
Ans: Some of the most popular trekking routes from Kainchi Dham are

items: Bara Patthar → Kilbury → Pangot → Gugukham → Kainchi Dham
Tallital → Bhowali → Gethia → Garampani → Kainchi Dham

Q20: Can we go camping in Kainchi Dham?
Ans: No camping near the ashram and forest is prohibited by authorities but you can enjoy camping at Camp Kainchi Dham in Bhowali, Babaji River Campsite near Kosya Kutauli and Nainital River Camp.
Q21: What is included in the Kainchi Dham tour package price?

Ans: All My Quick Trippers Kainchi Dham packages include accommodation on twin sharing basis, daily breakfast and dinner (vegetarian), private AC vehicle for all transfers, and guided darshan at Kainchi Dham Ashram. Airfare to Delhi/Kathgodam, lunch, and personal expenses are not included.
Q22: Is Kainchi Dham suitable for senior citizens?

Ans: Yes. Kainchi Dham is one of the more accessible pilgrimage sites in Uttarakhand. The main Darshan area is on flat ground — no climbing or trekking required. The ashram has ramps and wide pathways. We arrange ground-floor hotel rooms on request and our driver stays on-call throughout the tour.
Q23: What is the cost of a Kainchi Dham tour package from Delhi in 2026?

Ans: The 2-day Kainchi Dham tour package from Delhi starts at ₹9,250 per person on twin sharing basis. The 3-day package starts at ₹12,400 and the 4-day packages (with Dunagiri Cave or Mahavatar Babaji Cave) start at ₹14,500. All prices include hotel, meals, and private vehicle. Contact us for current 2026 pricing.
Q24: Can I customize the Kainchi Dham package to include Nainital or Almora?

Ans: Yes. All our Kainchi Dham packages are fully customizable. Popular additions include Nainital (20 km), Bhimtal (19 km), Almora and Jageshwar Dham (65 km), and Mukteshwar (50 km). Share your preferences while enquiring and our team will build the itinerary accordingly.
Q25: What is the best month to visit Kainchi Dham in 2026?

Ans: March to June and September to November are the best months. For a spiritually significant experience, plan around June 15 — the Pratishtha Diwas Bhandara. If you prefer fewer crowds, September–October offers pleasant weather and a quieter ashram. Avoid July–August if possible due to monsoon landslide risk on the Bhowali road.
Q26: Can I cancel or reschedule my Kainchi Dham tour?

Ans: Yes. Cancellations 60+ days before departure attract only a 10% charge. Cancellations within 7 days are fully non-refundable. Rescheduling is possible subject to availability — contact +91-8171158569.
27: Is there any registration required to visit Kainchi Dham?

Ans: No formal government registration is required to visit Kainchi Dham Ashram — unlike Char Dham temples. However, during peak festivals like June 15 Bhandara, the Uttarakhand administration implements crowd management. Entry remains free for all devotees.

blocks.text: The best time to visit Rishikesh is in the summers ( March to June ) and winters ( October to February ). The summers are perfect if you're planning on doing rafting or going camping. Winters, on the other hand, pose as an ideal time to indulge in sightseeing or engage in yoga or meditation sessions.
Monsoon (July to September) is another pleasant time as the holy city treats you with lush greenery. However, adventure activities like rafting are closed in this period owing to safety reasons.
You can reach Rishikesh by all three modes of transport, that is, train, plane, and highway lanes! Here's a quick travel guide to the 'Yoga capital of the world':

items: By Air: The nearest airport to Rishikesh is in Dehradun (Jolly Grant Airport). It's situated about 21 km from the city, and you can easily hire a taxi or a cab to reach Rishikesh from here. Also, the airport serves all the major cities in the country, such as Delhi, Mumbai, etc.

By Train: You'll find the nearest railhead in Haridwar . The Haridwar Junction is about 25 km from Rishikesh, and transport like taxis/autos is easily accessible from here. Trains from major cities to Haridwar run on a regular basis.

By Road: Those who love road travel can take the NH 334. You can arrive here in your personal vehicle, or take the regular buses that run on this route from cities like Delhi, Dehradun, and Haridwar. The Delhi to Rishikesh road trip is one of the most popular options among travellers.

rows: The Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat is one of the best experiences the city can offer you. Watch the holy confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati rivers here.
Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula sightseeing should definitely be a part of your Rishikesh Tourism Packages! These Iconic suspension bridges are the best spots to capture the panoramic Ganga river views.
A Parmarth Niketan Ashram visit is a must as it's the largest ashram in the city. You can do yoga and meditation here.
Requiring just a short trek, this waterfall is so worth the effort. You can enjoy a picnic here while feasting your eyes on the cascading waterfall views!

The Beatles Ashram exploration is really exciting, for you get to see graffiti art here and some serene meditation huts. The place got super popular after the rock band 'The Beatles' visited here in 1968.

blocks.text: Here are some travel tips that will come in handy on your tour:

items: Pack woollen clothes for this trip, as the nights can get cold there.

Q1. What Is The Best Time To Visit Rishikesh?

Ans. The most preferred time to travel to Rishikesh is between February and mid-May, when the weather is quite pleasing. However, be aware of the fact that the temperature starts going down to sub-zero levels in the winter months hence, Rishikesh in winter witnesses chilly cold weather. And it might be interesting to note that Rishikesh welcomes a huge influx of tourists throughout the year, despite the season.
Q2. How Can I Plan A Trip To Rishikesh?

Ans. To plan the Rishikesh trip, you must first decide the time you're going to visit there. After that, you can plan your itinerary keeping in mind the places that you would like to see and the activities that you want to indulge in there. Also, it's always a good idea to book you stay in advance. Finally, decide on the mode of transport that you'd take to reach there, such as plane, trains or the good old road route.
Q3. What Can I Do In Rishikesh?

Ans. Despite being reckoned as a spiritual city, the destination offers you a great opportunity to get indulged in activities like river rafting, bungee jumping, mountain climbing, mountain biking, etc. Also, it is a perfect place to meet your inner self through meditation! This spiritual city in India really has a lot to offer its travellers.
Q4. What Is The Rishikesh Famous For?

Ans. Rishikesh is famous for several things like its ancient temples, sacred Ghats, adventure activities, and also for the local markets from where you can buy some really amazing souvenirs for yourself and your loved ones.
Q5. How Can I Go From Delhi To Rishikesh?

Ans. There are direct buses from Delhi to Rishikesh on regular basis. Rishikesh is not much far away from Delhi (at a distance of only 255.3 km) and both the cities are pretty well connected with the motorable roads. You can also take the plane or choose the railway systems to reach here.
Q6. What Is There To See In Rishikesh?
Ans. There is a lot to see in the city as it is home to various ancient temples, ghats, Ram Jhula, Laxman Jhula, local markets, waterfall, and much more.
Q7. What Time Is The Ganga Aarti In Rishikesh?

Ans. The Ganga Aarti takes place at the divine Triveni Ghat between 6 pm and 7 pm every day. However, the timings can change a bit depending on the season. Hundreds of devotees gather at the Ghat to be a part of this scared event.
Q8. What Is The Yoga Capital Of The World?
Ans. Rishikesh is considered to be the Yoga capital of the world as the city offers a perfect environment to perform meditation and yoga. The city also organizes Yoga Festival every year!

blocks.text: Almora, one of the best weekend gateway destinations is adorned beautifully with gorgeous hill stations and is the perfect place that offers you the cultural feel and is quite popular for its cultural and temple tours. No matter whether you are seeking for a long journey or a short trip, an adventure trip or a relaxing stay, Almora is one of the best weekend destinations where you can visit along with your family, friends, or colleagues and can enjoy a wonderful travel experience. After considering the vivid travel taste of travelers, we decided to design different travel packages and so we have brought several tour itineraries for our customers which they can check and select according to their travel taste and budget.

We also offer you the provision of bringing slight changes in the itinerary (if possible and it may cost you some extra charge). The packages that we offer our guests are inclusive of all the basic amenities viz. smooth and comfortable transfer via air-conditioned vehicle, comfy and clean hotel room, food with amazing taste and quality, etc. We also hire well-experienced and quite disciplined drivers and tour representatives for our guests so that they don’t have to face any hurdle and can make their trip one of the most worthy and memorable journeys of their life.

Located almost 1638 meters above the sea level, Almora looks quite stunning and appealing as it is encircled by gorgeous Himalayan Mountains and other picturesque landscapes that make it a panoramic wonderland and a perfect holiday destination. Being studded with natural beauties and scenic vistas, it is one of the most preferred destinations for nature lovers and photogenic as here they can click some amazing pictures amidst the green valleys. Also, if you are an adventure seeker and love trekking at high altitudes where you won’t find a massive crowd like other places then go ahead with your Almora trip with our Almora sightseeing tour packages and likewise this there are many more packages available on our website. The other thing that makes it more significant is that it is one of those few hill stations that were not discovered by Britishers and so visiting here gives you the feeling of a true Indian.

The lively bazaars full of different beautiful items, and the slate roof structures are the other key attractions of this site where you can feel the strong local aura along with purchasing some amazing craft items. Despite being popular for its natural charm, Almora is also famous for being a house of several beautiful temples including Katarmal Sun Temple, Chitai Temple, and Kasar Devi Temple where devotees from different corners of the country flock to seek the blessings of the deities and add a spiritual beauty to their journey. If you are planning for a long trip then you can also plan to visit the nearby destinations including Ranikhet, Baijnath, Kausani, Binsar, and so on. Let’s not wait more and check out the itineraries to select the most affordable and the best package for your Almora tour.

blocks.text: Witness the sacred temples resting on the lap of Nilachal Hills and experience the beauty of Northeast India with our well-crafted 2-day Kamakhya Temple tour package. The package includes comfortable hotel stays, daily breakfast, guided sightseeing, and safe AC transfers - ensuring a completely hassle-free pilgrimage journey. See More

Kamakhya Temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas in India and the only Yoni Peetha among them - the spot where the womb of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen. The temple sits atop Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam , and is dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya, the goddess of desire and feminine power.
Book this short trip to Maa Kamakhya with us and experience the divine presence of Maa Shakti in and around the temple. Ministry of Tourism, Government of India approved.
About Kamakhya Temple - The Supreme Shakti Peeth of India

Kamakhya Temple stands apart from every other temple in India. Perched atop Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam, it is the most powerful of the 51 Shakti Peethas - and the only Yoni Peetha, where the creative energy of Goddess Sati is believed to reside.

According to the Kalika Purana, when Goddess Sati self-immolated at Daksha's Yagna after her father insulted Lord Shiva, a grief-stricken Shiva carried her body through the universe. Lord Vishnu used his Sudarshana Chakra to divide Sati's remains into 51 parts. The Yoni fell here, on these very hills.

What strikes every first-time visitor: there is no idol inside the main sanctum. Devotees descend into a small, dark cave and offer prayers at a natural fissure in the rock - always moist from an underground spring. No statue, no image. Just the raw, living energy of the Goddess.

The temple's architecture follows the Nilachala style - a beehive-shaped dome surrounded by smaller shrines, different from anything in North or South India. The complex houses the full Dasa Mahavidya - ten great forms of the Divine Mother - each with its own temple on the hill.
Ambubachi Mela - Kamakhya's Most Sacred Annual Event

Every June (22nd-25th), Kamakhya Temple closes its doors for three days. This is Ambubachi - the annual period when Goddess Kamakhya is believed to undergo her menstrual cycle. The natural spring inside the temple is said to run red during these days.

When the temple reopens (from 26 June), the Ambubachi Mela begins and runs till 3 July. Lakhs of devotees, sadhus, and Tantric practitioners gather from across India. It is one of the largest spiritual congregations in Northeast India. If you plan to attend, book your Kamakhya tour package at least 3-4 months in advance - hotels fill fast.

Practical tip: Arrive before 8:00 AM on weekdays for shorter queues. Weekends and Hindu festival days are significantly busier. Purchase the VIP Darshan Pass (₹501/-) at the temple counter to avoid the general queue.
Best Time to Visit Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati

From practical experience: October to February is the sweet spot. The weather is pleasant, Darshan queues are manageable, and the Brahmaputra looks its most picturesque. Most families, senior pilgrims, and solo travelers prefer this window.
How to Reach Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati

The nearest airport is Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (LGBI), Guwahati - approximately 14 km from Kamakhya Temple. Direct flights connect Guwahati to Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Pune. Our package includes airport pickup.

Two railway stations serve the temple: Guwahati Railway Station (main, ~10 km from temple) and Kamakhya Railway Station (~2 km from temple, closer option). Major trains include Rajdhani Express, Brahmaputra Mail, and Saraighat Express from Delhi and Kolkata. Our package includes station pickup.

Guwahati is connected via National Highway 27. State buses, private taxis, and app-based cabs are easily available from the city. The temple hill is about 8 km from Guwahati city centre - roughly 25 minutes by road. Note: the final stretch up Nilachal Hill is by road or on foot (~200 steps).

blocks.text: Practical Tips for Visiting Kamakhya Temple

items: Reach early - Arrive before 8:00 AM on weekdays. The morning Darshan is calmer, the air is cooler, and the experience is far more personal.
Buy the VIP Pass - ₹501/- per person, purchased at the temple counter. Saves 2–4 hours in the general queue on busy days.
Carry cash - ATMs are at the temple base but can be crowded. Keep ₹500–700 in cash for the pass, Prasad, flowers, and small donations.
Wear appropriate clothes - Modest clothing — avoid shorts and sleeveless tops inside the temple. Sandals are easier than laced shoes.
Photography rule - Photography inside the main sanctum (the cave chamber) is strictly prohibited. Outer courtyard is fine.
Combine with Navagraha - Navagraha Temple is a 15-minute drive from Kamakhya. Very few tour operators include it — we do, on Day 2.
Ambubachi planning - Book 3–4 months in advance if visiting during Ambubachi Mela (late June). Hotels at Guwahati book up quickly.

Start early. The best time to reach Kamakhya Temple is before 8:00 AM on weekdays to avoid long queues. It is recommended to purchase a VIP Darshan Pass (₹501/- per person, paid directly at temple counter) to skip the general queue.

Visit the holy Kamakhya Temple, located on Nilachal Hill - one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and the supreme Yoni Peetha of India . The inner sanctum has no idol; devotees offer prayers at a natural stone fissure in a cave, continuously moist from an underground spring. The experience is raw, quiet, and deeply moving.
You can also visit the temples close to Kamakhya on Nilachal Hill:

After completing Darshan, proceed to Umananda Temple (~7 km from Kamakhya), located on Peacock Island in the middle of the Brahmaputra. Access is by ferry. Also visit the Navagraha Temple on Chitrasal Hill , dedicated to the nine planetary deities.
If time permits, stroll through Fancy Bazaar for local shopping and snacks.
You will then be dropped at Guwahati Railway Station or Airport for your onward journey.
