blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is included in the Kamakhya Temple tour package?

Ans. The package includes 1-night hotel accommodation (double sharing), daily breakfast, a private AC vehicle for all transfers and sightseeing, pickup and drop from Guwahati Airport/Railway Station, and all applicable taxes. Excludes VIP darshan pass, ferry/ropeway charges, personal expenses, and airfare/train tickets.
Q2. How many days are needed for the Kamakhya Temple tour?

Ans. Our standard package is 2 days / 1 night, which is sufficient to cover Kamakhya Darshan and all major Guwahati spiritual sites. If you plan to add Kaziranga National Park or Shillong, extend to 4–6 days.
Q3. What is the Kamakhya Temple tour package cost per person?
Ans. Standard package starts at ₹5,650 per person (double sharing, currently at 15% discount from ₹6,500). Deluxe and Luxury options are available on request. Use coupon WELCOME500 for extra savings.
Q4. When is the best time to visit Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. October to February is ideal — weather is pleasant (12°C–24°C), queues are manageable, and the Brahmaputra looks its most scenic. The Ambubachi Mela in late June is the most spiritually powerful time but requires advance booking due to massive crowds.
Q5. What is Ambubachi Mela and when does it happen?

Ans. Ambubachi Mela celebrates the annual menstrual cycle of Goddess Kamakhya. The temple closes from 22–25 June every year, then reopens with a grand Mela running from 26 June to 3 July. Lakhs of devotees attend. Book your Kamakhya Yatra package at least 3–4 months early if you plan to attend.
Q6. Is a VIP Darshan pass available at Kamakhya Temple?

Ans. Yes. The VIP Darshan Pass costs ₹501/- per person and is purchased directly at the temple counter. It allows faster entry and is strongly recommended on weekends, festivals, and peak season (October–February). This charge is NOT included in the tour package price.
Q7. What temples are covered besides Kamakhya in the 2-day package?

Ans. The itinerary covers all major Dasa Mahavidya temples on Nilachal Hill (Dhumavati, Tripureswari, Maa Tara, Maa Kali, Chhinnamasta, Bagalamukhi, Bhuvaneshwari, Banadurga), Umananda Temple on Peacock Island, Navagraha Temple, and a Brahmaputra sunset cruise (optional, direct payment).
Q8. Is Kamakhya Temple accessible for elderly or differently-abled visitors?

Ans. There are approximately 200 steps to the temple, but a road also goes up to Nilachal Hill by car. Elderly pilgrims can be driven to the temple entrance and walk only a short final stretch. Our driver and guide assist accordingly.
Q9. Can I arrange a special puja at Kamakhya Temple through this package?

Ans. Yes. Inform us at least 1 day before your tour date and we will coordinate with the temple priests to arrange special puja or ritual as per your requirements. Additional costs for puja materials and priest fees apply and are paid directly.
Q10. What is the pickup and meet-up process?

Ans. Our representative will be waiting outside the exit gate of Guwahati Airport or Railway Station, holding a placard with your name. Driver and cab details are shared 1 day prior to tour start. Pickups can also be arranged from your hotel or residence in Guwahati.
Q11. Is this tour available for solo travelers?
Ans. Absolutely. Solo traveler packages are available. Pricing differs from twin-share rates — contact us directly for a solo quote. We also run group departure tours that solo travelers can join.
Q12. Can I customize the tour or add more destinations?

Ans. Yes. We offer extended Northeast India packages combining Kamakhya with Kaziranga National Park (one-horned rhinoceros, UNESCO World Heritage Site), Shillong, Cherrapunji, Majuli Island, and Manas National Park. Contact our team for a customized itinerary and pricing.

blocks.text: Welcome to the Kaziranga National Park! If you’re into wildlife even remotely, then you must come here. See More

Not only do you get to see the elusive one-horned rhinoceros , you get to enjoy a myriad of other things, like bird watching, jungle safaris, spotting tigers, and serene landscapes that this place is just naturally blessed with! And if you want to have a seamless journey here, simply book our Kaziranga Tour Package!

With our well-planned itinerary, you get to see the best and most of the park in optimum time. In addition, we’ll also introduce you to the Assamese culture with the delightful cuisine and cultural insights. So what are you waiting for? Contact us now so that we can plan this exciting wildlife adventure for you!

items: Welcome to Guwahati. Our team rep will meet you at the Guwahati airport/railway station.

In the evening, you’ll be taken to the Orchid and Biodiversity Park. You can explore here: 600+ species of wild orchids Rice museum Fish pond Flower garden
Also, partake in the delicious Assamese cuisine.
Return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 2: Elephant and Jeep Safari in Kaziranga Park

items: Wake up early in the morning to go on the elephant safari in the Kaziranga National Park. You’ll be informed a day before whether you’ll be visiting the Bagori, Central, or Eastern zone.
Now is your chance to spot the famous one-horned rhinoceros.
Also, enjoy other animals here like tigers, wild elephants, deer, etc. Also, het delighted with a variety of bird species here.
Afterwards, you’ll be transferred back to the hotel for breakfast and some relaxation.
Now, you’ll be driven back to the Kaziranga Park for a thrilling jeep safari. This time you’ll be traversing a completely different zone.
Return to the hotel and get a restful night’s sleep.
Treat yourself to a hearty breakfast.
Now, you’ll be driven to the Maha Mrityunjay Temple, which is located near Nagaon.
Enjoy a brief stopover for lunch.
Now, you’ll be transferred to the airport/railway station from where you can start your journey home.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. What is the entry fee for Kaziranga?

Ans. The Kaziranga park entry fee is between INR 100 and INR 150 per person. However, the price range is about INR 650-INR 750 for the foreign tourists. If you're traveling with children (5-12 years), then their ticket fee is half that of the adults’.
Q2. Which safari is better in Kaziranga?

Ans. Both the elephant and jeep safari offer different kinds of experiences. If you’re looking for a closer view of the one-horned rhinos, then an Elephant Safari is better. And if your goal is to cover larger areas, spotting a wide variety of animals there, then a jeep safari is your best bet.
Q3. Which month is better to visit Assam?
Ans. The best months to visit the state of Assam are from November to April. The weather is pleasant in this window and is also great for going on safaris.
Q4. What is the cost of a Jeep safari in Kaziranga National Park?
Ans. The cost of hiring one jeep is INR 3,500 - INR 4,500. The jeep carries 5 to 6 people in one go and the expense is shared by the people. Also, the prices vary slightly from zone to zone.
Q5. Are there tigers in Kaziranga?
Ans. Yes, the Kaziranga Park has tiger. Actually, it has the largest density of tigers in India. However, you might find difficulty in spotting one as the park has dense grasslands.

blocks.text: Russia is a vast country with unique geography and jovial Russian people who take the adversities of life in their stride to make this country a favorite place for Tour Packages. There are many historical places, wonderful ancient architecture, museums and art galleries and of course mesmerizingly beautiful natural places for tourists to enjoy on Russia Tour Packages. Snowcapped mountains and vast landscapes with unique flora and fauna have made this country an interesting tourist destination since long time, central and North-Western region of Russia have most of the places of interest for visitors on Tour Packages.

Moscow is the capital of Russia and a city which holds many places of tourist interest for travelers on Tour Packages. This is an astonishing city which has seen aggressions from the time of Napoleon and till World War II but has repelled each one by its sheer grit and valor. Famous Kremlin is the biggest attraction of this city, this fortified structure has churches and cathedrals inside it which are simply amazing. Tretyakov art gallery in Moscow can take tourists on Russia Tour Packages into a different world of colors and sketches, private collection of famous painter Pavel Tretyakov, paintings belong to genres like symbolism, avant-garde and realism. Church of Christ the Savior is another huge attraction for visitors on Russia Tour Packages in Moscow.

Saint Petersburg is another popular destination for tourists on Russia Tour Packages, it is popularly called as ‘Window of Europe’ due to its distinctive European charm and cultural richness. Saint Isaak cathedral is a huge ancient complex which can accommodate more than 10,000 people at a time. Winter palace of Czars, Kazan Cathedral and Yusupov’s Palace are other places of immense tourist attraction in Saint Petersburg. The best time to visit this city is start of the winter and cruise to Moscow is one of the most charming and tempting activity tourists love to indulge in on Russia Travel Packages.

If one thinks that Russia Travel Packages are all about museums and palaces then it is completely incorrect as Kaliningrad is a seaport and hosts many lucrative beaches and spectacular tourist attractions. Situated at the mouth of river Pregolya and beholding Vistula Lagoon is a place with natural splendor. Konigsberg Cathedral, museum of the World Ocean, Amber Museum and Gates of Kaliningrad are few other attractions of this city for visitors on Russia Holiday Packages. Kaliningrad zoo is oldest zoo in this country with vast collection of flora and fauna including rare plants like Gingko tress. It houses more than 2000 different species of animals, stone figure of Orangutan and bronze statue of Elk. This zoo is must visit part of every Russia Tour Package.

Vladimir is the popular place to be on Russia Holiday Packages for enjoying sightseeing, live performances and seeing three UNESCO’s world heritage sites. The Golden Gates, St. Demetrius Cathedral and the Assumption Cathedral are three world heritage sites in Vladimir. This city houses many award winning art galleries, museums and theatres and live performances by internationally famous groups, artisans and artists happens quite frequently in this city. With many other places to visit Vladimir is a not to miss attraction of Russia Tour Packages.

blocks.text: The glistening white temple dedicated to goddess Ganga graces the bank of the gushing Bhagirathi River in Devbhoomi Uttarakhand. Being a crucial part of the holy Char Dham Yatra annual pilgrimage of India it is located in one of the most scenic and beautifully soothing regions of India. Gangotri tour packages play a vital role in witnessing the incredible spiritual aura of the pilgrimage to the utmost level. Reaching this humble temple when it opens for Darshan after remaining buried under snow for half a year, is a relatively an easy job. The temple is one of the rarest places of worship for Ganga Mata exclusively in country. The temple was built by the brave heart Amar Singh Thapa who realized the true value of this place and took the responsibility of preserving this place in his hand.

However, the current standing temple was remade and renovated by the Maharani of Jaipur. The place holds immense relevance in the life of every Hindu devotee with its history dating to as far back as the birth of Ganga. Ever since the temple was built and revived by the great saint and philosopher Adi Shankaracharya the temple witnesses a massive turnout of domestic as well as international devotees. It is believed that king Bhagirathi is responsible for bringing the heavenly river of Ganga to earth with an aim of providing moksha to he departed souls of his ancestors by immersing their ashes into this pious river. This tradition is now followed by Hindus and believers from all over the world.

According to the Hindu holy texts, it was near Gangotri Temple that the holy river had made her way into the earthly realm from the heavenly realm which is believed to be the matted hair of Lord Shiva. The Gangotri Tour Packages offered by us ensures that you experience the spirituality and divine power of this place just the way it was intended to be. From offering smooth pick-up and drop-off service, sightseeing options, comfortable stay, and delicious meal options this tour package is something you, your family and loved ones. Available exclusively at the best rates and enabling you to have a lifetime worth of spiritual and religiously evoking journey on the hills, this will be something you will remember forever.

The packages are designed in custom and a flexible manner to meet the entire travel requirement you may be expecting. Exploring this part of India will be an experience to remember and you may even keep coming back for more of the spiritual and adventure experience this place has to offer.
Q1: What is the best time to visit Gangotri?

Ans. Gangotri being nestled at a huge elevation witnesses harsh climatic condition in the monsoon and winter months hence, it is best to best to plan your Gangotri Trip between May and June or in September and October.
Q2: How can we visit Gangotri Yamunotri?

Ans. The devotees who are planning to seek the blessings of Goddess Ganga at Gangotri Dham and Yamunotri Dham shall read out the beautifully narrated travel guides to these temples and then plan accordingly.
Q3: Can we go to Gangotri in December?

Ans. The gorgeous Gangotri Temple receives huge snowfall in the winter months especially from December to February thus, we don’t recommend you for visiting Gangotri in December. Also, the shrine is closed at this time hence, it is not a great idea to witness the glory of Gangotri Tourism.
Q4: How do I get from Rishikesh to Gangotri?
Ans. One needs to cover a total distance of 257 km to reach Gangotri from Rishikesh and this distance can only be covered by roadways and this journey takes almost 12 hours.
Q5: How can I reach Gangotri from Uttarkashi?

Ans. Both the above mentioned destinations are situated at a distance of 100 km and to cover this distance the traveler has to opt for either roadways that will take 3 hrs or can plan for a helicopter ride which is however a bit economical.
Q6: How can I reach Gangotri?

Ans. The nearest railway station to the pilgrimage is Rishikesh railway station and Jolly Grant Airport in Dehradun is the nearest airport to Gangotri but if you want to make your journey less time consuming and more convenient then helicopter service is the best mode of transportation to reach the shrine.
Q7: Which God is worshipped in Gangotri?
Ans. As the name suggests, Gangotri is the shrine dedicated to Goddess Ganga and happens to be one of the most destinations of Ganga worshippers.

Why is Gujarat the Best Place to Travel?

Gujarat is a fantastic choice for travellers of all kinds. This year, in 2025, around 16.161 million people visited Gujarat, which includes both national and international travellers. The government has also spent a huge amount of money to improve the infrastructure facilities and to make the tourist places more stunning. Because of these developments at a rapid pace, tourists are expected to choose Gujarat as their best holiday destination.
Other Reasons to Come to Gujarat

items: Gujarat has the longest coastline, which stretches across 1600 km. The enchanting views will not end as long as you look for them.
Asiatic white Lions are the pride of Gujarat. Gir National Park in Gujarat is the only place in India where this majestic creature is found. You can enjoy thrilling jeep safaris in Gir.
The Statue of Unity (statue of Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel) is one of a kind. It’s the tallest statue in the world.
Don’t miss the scenic and vast White Salt Desert. - Rann of Kutch, where the annual Rann Utsav Festival is celebrated, is marked by folk dances, music, crafts and local cuisine.
When it comes to eco-tourism, Gujarat is the best place to visit. Do you know that Gandhinagar is the greenest capital city of Asia?

blocks.text: Best Time to Go for the Gujarat Trip

The best time to visit Gujarat depends really on the activities you want to do. However, most tourists prefer to come here in winter, from October to March. These winter months not only have nice, pleasant weather for sightseeing but also host a lot of cultural events during this period. So, it’s a good choice to choose Gujarat holiday packages during this time.
However, besides the peak season, there are other times too when you can visit the land of lions. Here’s the complete overview:
Winter (October to March) - Best Time to Visit
The weather is mostly pleasant with temperatures being anywhere from 12°C and 29°C.
Top Things to Do in Gujarat in Winter

items: Enjoy cultural sites like Dwarka, Somnath Temple, and Champaner-Pavagadh.

Take part in the celebrations of the Rann of Kutch festival (happening between November and February) and relish the mind-blowing cultural performances, moonlit desert views, exquisite crafts, and much more.
Go for wildlife safaris at Gir National Park (open only from October to mid-June)
Partake in the Garba nights and Dandiya Raas during Navratri (October).
Experience the colorfully dotted sky with kites during the International Kite Festival (January).

blocks.text: Festivals and Events in Gujarat in Winter

The weather is cool due to the rainfall around this time. One of the good things about visiting during this period is that the areas are less crowded, and therefore you can enjoy your Gujarat sightseeing in a much calmer and relaxed environment. However, you must avoid coastal areas during this time as they get flooded.
Top Things to Do in Gujarat during Monsoon:

items: Enjoy Gujarat's hill station, like Saputara, it is one of the best hill stations in Gujarat . During monsoon, it gets adorned with lush greenery during this period.
Enjoy the Saputara Monsoon Festival during this time.
Capture the scenic waterfall- Gira Waterfalls. It is also one of the best spots for a picnic in Gujarat with your family.
Visit Polo forest in the Sabarkantha district to enjoy camping, trekking, cycling, and capturing the beautiful temple ruins.
Enjoy bird watching and the scenic beauty of wetlands at Thol Lake Bird Sanctuary in Thol Village.

blocks.text: The weather can get extremely hot during this time, reaching well over 40°C. It’s perfect for tourists who are on a budget, as you can find very cheap accommodations in Gujarat.
Top Things to Do in Gujarat in Summer

items: Visit Mandvi Beach in the early mornings or evenings as temperatures are mild then.
Attend the Mango Festival, which is held in May-June. Here, the season’s fresh mangoes, especially the Kesar mangoes, are showcased.
Visit traditional fairs like the Bhavnath Fair (Junagadh) for cultural displays, performances, and purchasing local crafts.

blocks.text: Places to Visit on Gujarat Trip

Gujarat offers you everything from rich culture, fascinating history, amazing wildlife to calming spirituality. There are several interesting places here that are covered in your Gujarat travel itinerary. Here’s the list:
The capital has a lot of gems to offer to tourists, such as:

items: Sabarmati Ashram: This is a must to include on your Gujarat holiday package as this was the ashram where Mahatma Gandhi resided and also led the freedom struggle of India from here.
Calico Museum of Textiles: Do visit the textile heritage of India and experience the treasure trove with your own eyes.
Adalaj Stepwell: This stunning Stepwell architecture will blow your mind.
Kankaria Lake: This scenic lake is perfect for a family outing. You can also enjoy boating and the zoo here.

blocks.text: This white salty desert is famous for being one of the largest salt deserts in the world. The place has a lot to offer in terms of sightseeing, such as:

items: Great Rann of Kutch: This place needs to be included in your Gujarat travel package, especially during the Rann Utsav which is held from November to February. Also, you get to enjoy the unique landscape of this natural beauty.
Mandvi Beach: This beach is a great option to chill and relax. In addition, you can take a short trip to the famous Vijay Vilas Palace which is nearby.
Kalo Dungar: This is the highest point in Kutch. People love to climb this hill to catch the stunning panoramic views of the white desert around.

blocks.text: Watch the roaring Asiatic lion in its full glory at the Gir National Park. You also meet beautiful leopards, cute deer, fascinating bird species, and many more majestic animals. Don’t miss out on including this treasure on your Gujarat holiday package as the wildlife safari experience here is another level.
This ancient city is a big-time Hindu pilgrimage site and has several must-see places.

items: Dwarkadhish Temple: Dedicated to Lord Krishna, this temple is also considered to be a Char Dham pilgrimage site.
Gopi Talav: This holy pond has so many stories associated with Lord Krishna and is therefore a must-visit place for Krishna devotees.
Bet Dwarka: This serene island is stunning to the core and can be reached by a joyous ferry ride. It also has a lot of religious significance.

blocks.text: This is a highly revered temple of Lord Shiva as it’s one of the twelve Jyotirlingas in India. Devotees make sure to pay a visit to this temple when they are in the state.

Vadodara is a major city in Gujarat, known for its financial abundance, classic music, and beautiful architecture. You should include the following places in your Gujarat holiday package to make the most out of your trip:

items: Laxmi Vilas Palace: Get introduced to the Indo-Saracenic architecture and get bowled by the sheer opulence of this palace.
Sayaji Gardens: This gorgeous park has a museum and a zoo – a perfect day out with family.
Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park: This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with beautiful temples, mosques, and forts.

blocks.text: Bhuj is one of the key tourist destinations of the state. It never fails to impress its travellers with its intricate architecture, astonishing palaces, meandering streets, and authentic handicrafts. Make sure to add the following places to your Gujarat travel package.

items: Aina Mahal: This is a famous place where you see the hall of mirrors with ceilings and walls adorned with Venetian glass. The mirrors are gilded framed. On top of that, the whole aura is made even grander by the handcrafted chandeliers.
Kutch Museum: This is the oldest museum of Gujarat showcasing the state’s rich history and culture. A must-visit for all the history enthusiasts!

Prag Mahal: Located just next to Aina Mahal, this place showcases Gothic arches and Corinthian pillars. The walls are decorated with animal trophies and antique artwork, reflecting the grandeur of the time.

blocks.text: What to Eat on Gujarat Trip?

Besides being a tourist haven, Gujarat is also a foodie’s paradise. The flavorful and diverse cuisine is a hit with both locals and tourists. And you’re spoilt for choice – for you have a lot on your plate – from delicious street food to wholesome meals. Here’s what to try and relish on your Gujarat trip:
Gujarati Snacks: Enjoy the tangy, spicy, and sweet pleasure of Gujarat’s authentic finger-licking good snacks.
Bread Varieties: These flatbreads are every food lover’s delight.
Sweets and Desserts: Gujarat’s sweets are to die for!
Regional Specialties: From Kutch essentials to Vadodara specialties, these dishes must be tried at least once!
What to Buy on Gujarat Trip?

items: Dhalgarwad: You must visit Dhalgarwad in Gujarat; It’s a popular hub for Gujarati traditional dresses and Lehengas, Bandhani Sarees, Zari work, Patola dress materials, Chaniya Choli, woodcraft items of Surat and Kutch.
Manek Chowk: Famous bullion market packed with an amazing variety of chunky, silver and gold jewellery stores, combined with famous street food stalls.
Sindhi Market: Renowned for Gujarati Textile products, it’s a must-visit market. Look for a variety of Sarees, dress materials, bed sheets, etc.

Raipur Gate: Brighten your space with beautiful home decor items. It also houses many shopping malls and traditional Gujarati food stalls where you will get authentic Gujarati snacks like Dhokla, Farsans, Khandvi and vegetable kebabs, etc.
Lal Darwaza Market: If you wish to buy electric gadgets, Lal Darwaza is a perfect place in Law Garden. You will also witness a variety of children’s garments, toys, books and wallets.

Ramakda Market: It’s one of the most popular markets to go with family, especially those who have kids, as there is a variety of toys available at the best rates. You will also find many beautiful accessories for women.

blocks.text: Gujarat has excellent connectivity by air, rail, and road. Here’s a quick guide to reach the western state .
Gujarat has several domestic airports, and among all, Ahmedabad is the primary airways hub. Major airports are:

items: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad: This airport serves both international and domestic airlines. It is well-connected to major Indian cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, etc.
Vadodara Airport: This one primarily handles domestic flights.
Bhuj Airport: It is perfect for travellers going to the Kutch and Rann of Kutch.
Surat Airport: This serves domestic flights from metro cities like Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Delhi.
Rajkot Airport: It is well-connected with big Indian cities.

Gujarat Travel Tips for a Memorable Trip
Follow these tips to maximize your spending power and get the best travel experience in Gujarat with family and friends-

items: Enjoy the Festivals: Plan your Gujarat trip in late September and early October as the month's festivities will make your day unforgettable. During Thai time, people celebrate Navratri with Garba and Dandiya Raas, community gathering, folk music and traditional costumes. It is one of the major festivals in Gujarat .

Plan in Advance: Planning must be perfect to explore- Gujarat is an amazing place, but it is also very vast in terms of tourist places. You need to plan your itinerary to avoid last-minute hassle. You can book your Gujarat trip with us, and we will take care of your complete travel arrangements.

Art and Crafts: Do not forget to explore the art heritage and textile craft of Gujarat . Gujarat is very famous for its art and textile industry. There is a variety of textiles like Patola, Bandhani, Lehariya, Dhamadka, Ajrakh, Mushroo, etc. Also explore Sadeli Art, which is a technique used by craftsmen to carve floral and geometrical patterns on teak or other wood available locally.

Book Hotels in Advance: Hotels and Resorts in Gujarat range from Budget, mid-range, to luxury. You will also get budget guesthouses and Dharamshalas, and tents if you are planning to enjoy Rann Utsav. The quality of hotels will depend on your budget. So, choose wisely and book your hotels in advance. Sometimes, your selected hotels may not be available due to the peak tourism season.
Free to Nominal Entry Spots: You should also explore the best free/nominal entry spots like Sabarmati Ashram, Kankaria Lake, Sun Temple Modhera, Rani Ki Vav Patan, and local markets.
Check for discounts: Sometimes, travel agents run festivals or off-season discounts; always check them.

blocks.text: Q1: What Is the Best Time to Visit Gujarat?

Ans: Gujarat is a dry state and hence winter months are considered best for your Gujarat trip as in this season you find pleasing and favourable weather to complete all the outdoor activities. Participating in outdoor activities in summer and monsoon months is very hectic and troublesome.
Q2: What Is Famous Food in Gujarat?
Ans: Dhokla, Khandvi, Methi Ka Thepla, Khakhra, Jalebi, Gujarati Samosa, Bardoli Ki Khichdi, etc. are some of the most famous foods in Gujarat.
Q3: What Is the Capital of Gujarat?
Ans: Gandhinagar is the capital city of Gujarat that attracts a huge number of tourists with its beauty.
Q4: What Is Gujarat Famous For?
Ans: Gujarat is famous for several things like Dwarkadhish Temple, Somnath Temple, Beyt Dwarka Beach, shopping in Ahmedabad, Rann of Kutch, and many more things.
Q5: What Is Famous in Gujarat For Shopping?
Ans: Khadi, Patola Silk Sarees, dress materials, bangles, handlooms and handicrafts, jewelry, traditional Ghaghra Choli, embroidered and appliquéd quilts are few of the must buy stuffs in Gujarat.
Q6: Which Is the Biggest Mall in Gujarat?
Ans: Ahmedabad One mall happens to be the biggest mall in Gujarat where shopaholics love visiting.
Q7: How Can I Go to Gujarat By Flight?
Ans: There are three major airports in Gujarat- Vadodara Airport, Surat Airport, and Ahmedabad Airport where flights from different cities land.
Q8: How many days are sufficient for my Gujarat trip?

Ans: For a short trip, 4-5 days are sufficient to cover important destinations like Ahmedabad, Somnath, Gir National Park, and Dwarka. However, if your Gujarat tour package has more days to spare, you can extend it to 7-10 days, covering spots like Vadodara, Bhuj, and Rann of Kutch as well.
Q9: Is Gujarat safe for solo travellers?
Ans: Gujarat is generally considered safe, even for women. However, all tourists must exercise caution. Keep your luggage and wallets secure at all times and avoid secluded places at night.
Q10: What are some wildlife experiences that I can enjoy on my Gujarat holiday package?
Ans: Gujarat offers some of the most thrilling wildlife experiences. You can visit places like:

items: Gir National Park: Meet the majestic lions and watch them being their regal self.
Blackbuck National Park: This is an excellent place to spot the blackbucks soaking in the sun or sauntering around in the grass.
Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary: Thinking of watching those rare colorful birds? Come here and watch their sky show for yourself.
Marine National Park: When you’re done with land animals, head here and enjoy the coral reefs and vast marine biodiversity.

blocks.text: Q11: Do people speak Hindi in Gujarat?

Ans: Gujarati is the main language that is spoken all over Gujarat. However, both Hindi and English are widely understood, especially if you’re in tourist hot spots like Ahmedabad, Vadodara, and Bhuj.
Q12: What should I wear on the Gujarat trip?
Ans: Different seasons call for different attires. For example:

items: In winter (October to March), light woolens are recommended.
In summer (April to June), pack cotton clothes along with hats, sunscreen, and sunglasses.
In Monsoon (July to September), make sure you have umbrellas/raincoats and waterproof footwear.

Ans: You will get accommodations in Gujarat according to your budget. For budget travellers there are guesthouses, hostels, Dharamshalas and 3-star hotels will all the basic facilities and amenities. In mid-range category you will find boutique hotels, 3-4-star hotels. For Luxury travellers heritage hotels, boutique hotels and 5-star resorts etc are available at your convenience.

blocks.text: Tirupati Balaji, also known as Lord Venkateswara, is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Devotees from all over India visit Tirupati Balaji Temple (Tirumala Temple) to get his divine blessings. Tirupati Balaji temple is the Bhuloka Vaikuntam (earthly abode of Lord Vishnu). Visiting here is equivalent to visiting the real Vaikuntam (the original heavenly abode of Lord Vishnu).

items: According to Hindu Mythology, Rishi Bhrigu, the sage of Fortune, once wanted to know who is supreme among Lord Shiva, Lord Brahma, and Lord Vishnu.

He asked Lord Shiva and Lord Brahma but was unsatisfied with their answer. So, he visited Lord Vishnu for his answer, but when he didn't get any answer, he kicked in the chest of Vishnu, where Goddess Lakshmi resides.
Goddess Lakshmi felt insulted and left Vaikuntha to stay on earth.
To bring Lakshmi back, Lord Vishnu reincarnated as Sri Venkateswara and appeared on Tirumala hill. There he met Padmavati, who is an incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi, and married her.

The marriage was funded by Lord Kuber, the god of fortune. It is said that Lord Venkateswara took a loan for his marriage with Padmavati from Lord Kuber. The donations made by devotees today symbolically help him repay his loan.

blocks.text: Best Time for Tirupati Balaji Darshan 2026

Post-monsoon (July to September) and winter months (October to February) are the best times of the year to plan your Tirupati Balaji Darshan. The temperature during this time ranges from 15°C to 30°C, which is ideal to take the divine blessings of Lord Venkateswara.

items: The weather during post-monsoon and winters is cool and misty, making the divine Darshan possible and bearable.

December and January are the most preferred months for pilgrims to book tickets for Tirupati Balaji Darshan. Tickets during this time booked very fast and completely sold out. So, it is better to book your tickets for Tirumala Venkateshwara Temple Darshan in advance.
Brahmotsavam (September/October) -a 9-day festival at Tirupati Balaji where the processions of deities are carried on different vehicles.
Vaikuntha Ekadashi (December/January) -This festival marks the beginning of Uttarayana.

blocks.text: Months to Avoid for Tirupati Balaji Darshan
Summer (March to June) is not a favorable time for Tirupati Balaji Darshan. The temperature can range up to 40-45°C, which makes Darshan unbearable due to heat and humidity.
Best Things to Do in Tirupati Balaji
Within the temple premises of Lord Venkateshwara (Tirupati Balaji) and near its surroundings, there are many things to do to elevate your spiritual and cultural experiences. Let's know in detail.

items: Take a holy dip at Swami Pushkarini, Papavinasanam, and Akshaya Ganga Theerthams before visiting Swamy Venkateshwara Temple.
The main activity of any pilgrim at Tirupati Balaji is to get the divine blessings of Lord Venkateshwara at Shri Venkateshwara Swamy Temple.
You can stand in a Vaikuntam Queue complex II to get a glimpse of Lord Venkateshwara. It's a free Darshan scheme for the general public.
If you want a quick Darshan of Lord Venkateshwara, then you can book the Special Darshan scheme in advance through TTD portal.
Take part in a daily seva program at the temple, which starts at 2:30 am with Suprabhatam (awakening of the lord) and ends at 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm after Shuddhi (night rituals).
Take Darshan of other sub-shrines in the temple like Padmavati Amma, Varaha Swamy, and Anjaneya.

Explore S.V. Museum, which displays ancient and historical artifacts of the medieval period. It has around 6000 historical items from different periods in history. Witness Srivari Vahanas used during the festival of Brahmotsavam, original copper plates of Annamayya's compositions, and the Varahaswamy copper inscription.
There is a meditation hall on the roof of the museum to indulge in meditation and embrace mindfulness.

Places to Visit Around Tirupati Balaji
Apart from visiting Swamy Venkateswara Temple, you must visit these places to completely dive deep into the spiritual, natural, cultural, and historical whirlwind of Tirumala.

items: If you are interested in exploring historical places, then you must visit Chandragiri Fort, which is located 15 km from Tirupathi.
Yadava rulers built the fort in the 11th century.
It houses a museum that displays amazing artifacts from the time of the Vijayanagara Empire.
TTD Garden is also known as Balaji Garden. It is located near Tirupati Balaji Temple. It's a scenic garden spread over 460 acres, which offers refreshing vibes to solace seekers.
The flowers of these gardens are used for temple rituals of Tirumala Temple.
Located 3 km from Sri Venkateshwara Temple, visit this naturally occurring rock formation.
It is a perfect spot to hang out for nature lovers. Capture blissful views of nature and nourish your soul with enchanting views.
This place is more than 1000 years old, which also makes it one of the most popular historical spots around Tirupati.
Talakona waterfall is one of the best scenic spots in Andhra Pradesh. It is also the tallest waterfall here. Seek solace in the lap of nature. The height of the waterfall is approximately 270 ft.
It is surrounded by the dense forests of Sri Venkateshwara National Park, which is teeming with rich wildlife and flora. You can also enjoy scenic hikes and birdwatching at this spot.

One of Asia's largest zoos, Sri Venkateshwara Zoological Park is a wonderful destination for wildlife enthusiasts. If you are looking for adventure apart from spiritual bliss, then you must come here with your family and friends.
There are around 31 mammal species and 7 reptile species in the zoo. Spot some amazing animals like Royal Bengal tigers, white tigers, leopards, crocodiles, exotic birds, etc.
Located in Tirupati, it is a must-visit sacred place to fine-tune your spirit with divine wisdom. The temple is dedicated to Sri Govindaraja Swamy.

There are many other temples located within the main temple complex. Some of the most notable temples are Shri Kurath Alwar Temple, Shri Parthasarathy Swamy Temple, Shri Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Shri Anjaneya Swamy Temple, and many others.

You will get decent stay options like guesthouses, Dharamshalas, religious lodges, and rest houses, which are managed by the temple administration of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

blocks.text: The route to Tirupati Balaji Temple is not complex, as it has good air, rail, and road connectivity. Let's know in detail how to reach Tirupati Balaji-

items: The best way to reach Tirupati Balaji is by taking a flight. You will get direct flights from New Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Bangalore, and Indore to reach Tirupati Airport, which is also known as Renigunta Airport.
From the airport, you will get taxis or buses, or you can also hire private AC vehicles to reach Tirumala.
If you prefer to go to Tirupati by rail, then the closest railway station is Tirupati Junction, which is located 10 km away from Tirupati.
From the railway station you will get private buses or buses run by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams to reach the foot of the hills of ALIPIRI and SRIVERIMETU.
There are two well-carved stone footpaths to reach Tirumala. From the ALIPIRI footpath, you will reach Tirumala in 3 hours, and from SRIVERIMETU, you will reach Tirumala in 1 hour 30 minutes.

blocks.text: If you prefer a road route, then take NH44. You will get regular buses run by APSRTC or private buses to reach Tirumala. If you are coming by your own vehicle, then you have to take the ghat road route, which has time restrictions. There is a Ghat road that is laid between Tirupati and Tirumala.

items: The distance from Ghat Road to reach Tirumala is 17.80 km.
The distance from Ghat Road to reach Tirupati is 18.00 km.
The timings of the opening of Ghat Road: 3:00am to 00:00 hours (21 hours).

blocks.text: Useful and Safety Tips for a Memorable Tirupati Balaji Darshan
Some useful Tips for safe and memorable Tirupati Darshan are as follows-

items: Before starting your Tirupati Darshan, take a holy dip in Swami Pushkarini and worship Sri Bhu Varaha Swamy.
If you are in Tirumala, then bathe in Papavinasanam and Akasha Ganga Theerthams, as these are the most sacred Theerthams to nourish your mind and spiritual purification.
Please deposit your offerings at Hundi.

If you are a senior citizen and want to get the divine blessings of Tirupati Balaji, then you have to submit your Aadhaar card and a valid medical certificate issued by the concerned surgeon/specialist if there is any health issue.
Consuming liquor or any non-vegetarian food is highly prohibited in and around temple premises.

You have to wait politely for your turn to get a glimpse of Lord Venkateshwara Swamy, as devotees wait long in the queue if they are opting for General free Darshan. For special Darshan, you don't have to wait that long.
Do not wear flowers at Tirumala Temple; the flowers are reserved for the presiding deity only.
In case of any emergency or accident while coming from Ghat Road, call 0877-2263636/9000503089 and 108 to get the help of an auto clinic/crane and ambulance.
Dress modestly in the temple. Women need to wear covered clothes like Sarees, Chudidars, and Pajamas, and men should wear Dhotis, Kurtas, or Pajamas with upper cloth.

blocks.text: Q1. How many days are enough for Tirupati Darshan?

Ans. If you only want to get the divine Darshan of the Tirupati Tirumala Temple, then 2 days and 1 night is sufficient, but if you also want to offer Seva and explore other temples, the zoological park, and waterfalls, then take 4-5 days.
Q2. How to book Darshan tickets for Tirupati Balaji?
Ans. You can book Darshan tickets for Tirupati Balaji through the official site, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).
Q3. How can you buy Seva tickets for Tirupati Balaji?

Ans. To buy Seva tickets, you need to register yourself at the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam online portal and then book seva tickets. You have to book 120 days in advance for Sevas, as slots fill quickly in peak pilgrimage season.
Q4. How can you book accommodation for Tirupati Balaji?

Ans. After registering at the TTD portal, you have to choose an accommodation location-Tirupati or Tirumala-and then select your stay date and room category. Fill in all the pilgrim details and make payment. You must have valid ID proof to book accommodation for Tirupati Balaji Darshan.
Q5. What are the best months for planning Tirupati Balaji Darshan?
Ans. July to February are the best months to plan your Tirupati pilgrimage tour, as the weather will be pleasant at Tirumala Hill for sightseeing and Darshan.
Q6. What is Kalyanakatta in the Tirupati Balaji Temple?

Ans. If a devotee has a wish and he/she wants to get it fulfilled, then they have to do Kalyanakatta in Tirupati Balaji. Kalyanakatta is a ritual where a devotee is tonsured to fulfill their vows. It is done free of cost.
Q7. What are the sacred offerings devotees give to Lord Balaji as a part of the Fulfilment of the vow?

Ans. When the vow is fulfilled, the devotee's Tulabharam (offering of sugar candy, sugar, rice, jaggery, etc.) is equal to his/her weight. They also offer Niluvu Dopidi (ornaments or other jewels worn by the devotee) at Srivari Hundi.
Q8. What are the most popular temples to visit in Tirupati apart from Swamy Venkateswara Temple?
Ans. Apart from Swamy Venkateswara Temple, devotees can visit Sri Govindaraja Swamy Temple, Kapila Theertham, Kalyana Venkateswara Temple, Kodandarama Temple, and Padmavathi Temple.
Q9. What is the nearest airport for Tirupati Balaji?
Ans. Renigunta Airport (Tirupati Airport) is the nearest airport to reach Tirupati. It is located 14-16 kilometers away from Tirupati.
Q10. What are the main rituals of Tirupati Balaji?

Ans. Tirupati holds numerous rituals on a daily, weekly, and periodic basis. Some of the most prominent rituals in the Tirupati Balaji temple on a daily basis are Suprabhata Seva, Thomala Seva, Ekanta Seva, and Archana, etc.

You'll begin this special tour in the bustling city of Delhi . Admire the iconic landmarks like the Red Fort and India Gate. Now, move to the old city of Agra , where you will witness the timeless beauty of the Taj Mahal pretty closely. Get impressed with the grandeur of the Mughal-era monuments! Conclude the tour in the Pink City, Jaipur. Be in awe of the City Palace and the intricate Hawa Mahal . Our Golden Triangle Group Tour Package will also take you to the bustling bazaars and spice-filled markets. Call us now to know more about this tour plan!

The best time to go on the Golden Triangle Tour is, hands down, in the months of October to March . The weather in this window is quite pleasant and therefore makes for a perfect time to come here and enjoy sightseeing. The low temperature and the clear skies are a great plus of this season.

rows: Peak tourist season — book early; fog risk in Jan

blocks.text: Another great time to go on this tour is in the monsoon season, from July–September. You can experience cool weather and the crowds are less compared to the peak season. This would allow you to complete the trip at your own pace.
We recommend that you avoid booking your Delhi Agra Jaipur travel package in the summers (April–June). The temperature can rise beyond scorching 40°C, especially in Rajasthan.

Important January note: Dense fog frequently affects morning flights and road visibility in Delhi and Agra in December–January. Early morning Taj Mahal visits can be obscured. Our itineraries build in flexibility for this.

By Air: The Golden Triangle Tour starts from Delhi, and the national capital has a very well-maintained Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI — code DEL). By Train: All three cities of the trip have railway stations. With frequent trains like the Shatabdi Express and Rajdhani Express, you can easily access these cities. Book train tickets online at the official IRCTC website. Book 45–60 days in advance during October–March peak season.

By Road: If you wish to go on the tour by road, use the national highways — NH-44 (Delhi to Agra via Yamuna Expressway, ~230 km, 3–3.5 hrs) and NH-48 (Jaipur to Delhi, ~280 km, 4–5 hrs). These are in good condition and make a smooth link between Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur.

blocks.text: Q1. What is the price of Golden Triangle tour packages in 2026?

Ans: Budget 3N/4D packages start from ₹12,500 per person. Standard 5N/6D: ₹22,000–₹32,000. Luxury: ₹85,000–₹1,50,000. Extensions with Ranthambore or Varanasi add ₹8,000–₹20,000. Contact us for an exact quote.
Q2. How many days is the Golden Triangle tour?
Ans: Minimum 3 nights / 4 days for core highlights. Recommended: 5 nights / 6 days. Extended versions with Ranthambore, Varanasi, or Udaipur run 8–12 days.
Q3. What is the best time for Golden Triangle tour?
Ans: October to March — ideal temperature range (8°C–30°C). November and February are peak months. Avoid April–June (extreme heat, up to 45°C).
Q4. Is Taj Mahal closed on any day?
Ans: Yes — Taj Mahal is closed every Friday for Muslim prayers. This is critical planning information. All My Quick Trippers itineraries are built around this.
Q5. How many UNESCO sites are on the Golden Triangle?
Ans: Eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites — Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb (Delhi), Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri (Agra), Jantar Mantar, and Walled City of Jaipur.
Q6. Is the Golden Triangle suitable for senior citizens?
Ans: Fully suitable — no trekking, no altitude. All travel by private AC vehicle. Wheelchair assistance at monuments on request. We pre-book ground-floor rooms.
Q7. What is the Taj Mahal entry fee in 2026?
Ans: Indian citizens: ₹50. Foreign nationals: ₹1,300. Paid directly at monument — carry cash.
Q8. Can I add Ranthambore tiger safari?
Ans: Yes — add 2 nights between Agra and Jaipur for two jeep safaris. Ranthambore has 70+ tigers. Adds approximately ₹8,000–₹15,000 per person.
Q9. What is Fatehpur Sikri and should I visit?
Ans: Emperor Akbar's 16th-century ghost capital — UNESCO-listed. Sits on Agra–Jaipur highway. Add 90 minutes. All Standard+ packages include it. Do not skip.
Q10. Is the Golden Triangle tour private or group?
Ans: My Quick Trippers tours are 100% private — your vehicle, your guide, your schedule. No shared coaches or group schedules.
Q11. Can I customise the itinerary?
Ans: Yes — duration, hotel tier, guide language, dietary requirements, extension destinations — all customisable.
Q12. Is the Golden Triangle good for international tourists?
Ans: India's most popular international circuit — English-speaking specialist guides, international-standard hotels, direct Delhi flight connectivity from all major hubs.
Q13. What is the Sheesh Mahal at Amber Fort?
Ans: Hall of Mirrors — ceiling and walls entirely covered in intricate mirror mosaic. A single candle reportedly illuminates the entire room. Go at 8 AM sharp before crowds arrive.
Q14. Are tripods and drones allowed at Taj Mahal?
Ans: No — tripods and drones are strictly banned inside the Taj Mahal complex. Mobile phones and personal cameras are permitted.
Q15. What is the best hotel in Agra for Taj Mahal view?

Ans: Oberoi Amarvilas offers a direct Taj Mahal view from every room — considered the most spectacular hotel position in India. ITC Mughal and Trident Agra are excellent alternatives at lower price points.

blocks.text: Reaching Mathura is fairly easy due to its good connectivity with major cities through trains, flights and highways.

items: By Air- The nearest airport to Mathura is Agra (47 km), but Delhi's Indira Gandhi Airport (147 km) is a better option for tourists. You will easily get a bus or a cab to Mathura from the airport.

By Road- Mathura has good road connectivity to the major towns and cities in Uttar Pradesh. If you are travelling by car, NH 19/44 is the best road route. From Delhi, My Quick Trippers suggests the path of the Yamuna Expressway. You will also get direct buses from Agra, Delhi, Indore, Lucknow, etc.

Kanyakumari, the southernmost tip of India , attracts travelers from all over the world. Why not? It's a place where the world begins to end. Here you see the magical views of the most unique geographical phenomena-the meeting of three water bodies: the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

The place gets its name from the virgin goddess Kanyakumari, who is an incarnation of Goddess Parvati and sister of Lord Krishna. Britishers during their rule changed the name Kanyakumari to Cape Comorin, but later it was again renamed by the Indian government to Kanniyakumari.

blocks.text: Every corner of Kanyakumari is a thing of beauty and joy forever. Its beauty will be etched onto your soul and mind even after you leave its delightful shores. Here are some special highlights of Kanyakumari from our Kanyakumari holiday packages, which are a must-not-miss.

items: The Statue of Saint Thiruvalluvar is a must visit. The grace of sage Thiruvalluvar glows when the first rays of the sun touch the statue. Visiting here in the early morning will give you the chance to capture the best views.

Visit Thanumalayan Temple, as it holds a very significant place for Hindu devotees. You will be amazed to know that it's the only place where the holy trinity-Lord Brahma, Lord Vishnu, and Lord Shiva-are worshipped in a single idol.

Visiting the Triveni Sangam will nourish your mind, body, and soul with positive vibes. It's the only place in India to witness the unique phenomenon of the meeting of three water bodies-the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

Get the divine blessings of Goddess Kanyakumari at Kumari Amman Temple. Kanyakumari was named after the virgin goddess Kanyakumari, who is an incarnation of Goddess Parvati. It is also one of the 52 Shakti Peeths of Devi Sati in India.

blocks.text: Once upon a time, there lived a demon called Banasura who got a boon from Lord Brahma that he cannot be killed by any god or demon but only a woman. When he got the boon Lord Shukra intervened and advised him to modify the boon to be more specific. So, Banasura modified the boon- only a virgin girl could kill him.

Taking the advantage of this boon, Banasura felt invincible so he started to destroy the peace of devas and the earth. Devi Kanyakumari was incarnated to kill demon Banasura. She meditated at this southernmost tip which later came to be known as Kanyakumari. Lord Shiva, when he saw Kanyakumari, intended to marry her.

On the day of the wedding Sage Narada intervened by making a rooster crow on the auspicious timing of the wedding to make the wedding auspicious. It was done for a bigger purpose- to make Kanyakumari realize that she has to kill Banasura. She is fulfilling the condition of the boon that only a virgin girl could kill him.

After the disrupted wedding, Kanyakumari felt sad. So, she started destroying everything around and scattered colorful sands which are believed to be the origin of Kanyakumari unique and colorful beach sands. She killed demon Banasura and restored the balance of the universe. Later she revealed herself as Parvati, the divine consort of Lord Shiva.

blocks.text: Festivals and Rituals Unique to Kanyakumari

Kanyakumari is a land of festivals and unique rituals. If you are planning to book Kanyakumari holiday packages, ensure that you are visiting here at peak festive season to get a chance to witness some of the most unique festivals of Kanyakumari.

This festival is celebrated in Kollemcode Temple in Kanyakumari. It is one of the most popular festivals of Kanyakumari. The festival is dedicated to goddess Bhadrakali. In this festival, devotees are suspended in the air by hooks pierced through the skin on their back. They are suspended as an offering to goddess Bhadrakali. This act is significant as it bestows blessings for good health, prosperity and protection from the goddess.

This festival is celebrated in Bhagavathy Temple. The festival starts with a flag hosting ceremony which is witnessed by devotees from all over the region. The main Prasad of the temple is Appam which is made up of rice, Payar and Jaggery.

This festival is celebrated in Suchindram Temple in Kanyakumari. It's a 10-day festival. The festival is dedicated to Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. During this festival the idol is taken in procession on the street. Devotees from all over India witness the cultural expressions (music and religious dance), processions and rituals.

Chaitra Poornima Festival, Cape Festival is a very popular festival celebrated in Kanyakumari. It celebrates the culture and heritage of Kanyakumari by displaying traditional dance, music and folk performances in the backdrop of Kanyakumari sunset.
Best Places to Explore in Kanyakumari on Your Trip

Kanyakumari, as an integral part of Tamil Nadu Tourism, has seen significant tourist footfall in 2024. Tamil Nadu has welcomed around 286 million tourists in the year 2024, with Kanyakumari being one of the most visited tourist destinations for relaxing holidays. Source: Trade Brains. Witness some of the notable attractions covered in our Kanyakumari itineraries-

items: Kumari Amman Temple in Kanyakumari is one of the oldest shrines (approx. 3000 years old) dedicated to the goddess Kanyakumari. Goddess Kanyakumari is an incarnation of Goddess Parvati, or Devi Kumari, who is a symbol of purity and penance.

The temple's Dravidian-style architecture is a sight to behold. The idol of the goddess faces east of the ocean, but the eastern door of the temple is kept closed and opened only for special events. It's a landmark destination in Kanyakumari you must not miss.

It is the only place where you can view both sunrise and sunset over the ocean, which is a great sight to capture for photographers and travelers. In fact, if you are on a honeymoon trip to Kanyakumari, then the views of Kanyakumari Beach would be a perfect backdrop for romantic poses.
You will also witness Sangam on the Beach, as the beach is the official meeting point of three oceans-the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

Don't miss Kanyakumari's most popular landmark-the Thiruvalluvar Statue. It stands on a rocky islet next to Vivekananda Rock Memorial. This 133 ft statue is of a legendary Tamil poet and philosopher-Thiruvalluvar.

He is famous for composing Tirukkuṟaḷ, which is considered holy scripture and a guide for many Tamilians. The statue symbolizes 133 chapters of Tirukkural. The 38-foot pedestal represents the chapters on virtue, and a 95-foot figure symbolizes the wealth and love chapters.

Vivekananda Rock Memorial is one of the most famous attractions to explore in Kanyakumari. It was constructed in 1970 in honor of Swami Vivekananda. It is said that he meditated at this spot in 1892 and got some inspiration, which shaped his work in India and the West.
Also behold the sacred Shripada Mandapam as it holds footprints of the goddess Kanyakumari, making it a place of worship for devotees.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Kanyakumari on Your Trip
Indulge in these fun-filled activities to enjoy the best of Kanyakumari Tourism; it's a scenic land of spiritual solace and many thrilling adventures.
Enjoy Leisure Time at Baywatch Theme Park.

items: Baywatch Theme Park is the best place to visit in Kanyakumari. It's a popular water-based amusement park spread over 25 acres inspired by Kanyakumari Beach. It's a perfect spot to enjoy with family and friends.

Some notable rides and attractions in this park are giant wheels, hot teacups, crazy chairs, bumping cars, sky cabs, wave pools, and multiple splash zones. You can also savor delicious cuisines at food stalls in the park.

Located on the scenic shorelines of Kanyakumari town, Kanyakumari Lighthouse is a must-visit for awe-inspiring views of the ocean, Vivekananda Rock Memorial, and Thiruvalluvar Statue. From here you will also witness the scene where the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean meet.
It's a beautiful spot for photography and views of the mesmerizing sunrise and sunset.

You must visit Thirparappu waterfalls for a rejuvenating experience. It's a perfect place to enjoy walking around the rocky riverbed and lush greenery extended around the waterfall. The views of the waterfall will blow your heart away. You can also take a refreshing dip in the natural pool formed at the base of the waterfall.
Also visit Thirparappu Mahadevar Temple, which is a historic rock-cut temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
Enjoy a pedal boat on the Kodayar River near the waterfalls for a serene ride surrounded by lush greenery. Spot amazing wildlife such as birds and monkeys.
Enjoy unique flavor, which reflects traditional Tamil Nadu and Kerala's culinary heritage. Try staple dishes like Appam and fish curry.
Also try Nandu Varuval, a local crab dish; Kothu Parotta, minced with chicken; Pazham Sarbath; Rasa Vadai; and Maravalli Kizhangu served with Kadala curry or fish curry.

Whether you are planning a honeymoon or you are desperately looking for a well-planned family escape, ensure you know everything before you book a Vietnam trip from Bangalore .
Why You Must Add Vietnam to Your Travel Wishlist?
There is no shortage of amazing places on Earth. But Vietnam has the charisma that encourages travelers to keep it on their travel bucket list. Let’s dive into why you must choose Vietnam:

items: Stunning Landscapes: Explore terraced rice fields to pristine beaches, and you’ll experience everything your heart may desire.
Food Paradise: Vietnam is a paradise for foodies on Earth . From relish pho and spring rolls to Banh Mi, and Vietnamese iced coffee, you’ll get everything you want to slake your taste buds.
Shopping & Nightlife: Whether chic rooftop bars fascinate you or it’s bustling market, you’ll get a mix of local and cosmopolitan experiences here.
Rich Culture & Heritage: Experience the soul of Vietnam through its French colonial architecture, Buddhist Temple, and UNESCO World Heritage towns like Hoi An.
Budget-Friendly Luxury: Indulge yourself in the luxury and enjoy world-class amenities without breaking the banks.

blocks.text: The overall experience of your trip depends on the time you visit the destination. If you want to make the most out of your escape, ensure you choose the best time to visit Vietnam . Since it stretches from north to south, the weather varies across regions.

items: Spring (March–April): This time is considered pleasant and great for sightseeing.
Autumn (September–November): The weather is cool with less rainfall during this time. Thus, it is the best time to visit.
Winter (Dec–Feb): During this time, you’ll experience cold in the north and mild in the south.
Summer (May–Aug): Expect this time to be hot, humid, and rainy, and good for beach hopping.

Popular Places Not to Miss in Vietnam

Now, you know why Vietnam is the ideal destination for your next escape, what the visa requirements are, and when you should visit. My Quick Trippers ensures you never miss out on the popular places in Vietnam. Let’s have a look at some popular places you should cover during your escape:

items: Hanoi: Vietnam’s capital, full of historical charm, renowned for its buzzing street food culture and French architecture.
Hoi An: Ancient town with lantern-lit streets will amaze you with tailor shops and riverside cafes.
Da Nang & Ba Na Hills: This place is famous for beaches and the Instagram-worthy Golden Bridge.
Halong Bay: UNESCO-listed wonder with emerald waters and limestone islands will delight your soul when you hop on an overnight cruise.

blocks.text: FAQs on Vietnam Tour Packages from Bangalore

When you are investing your hard-earned money, efforts, and soul in planning your international trip to Vietnam, it’s always better to clear all your doubts and gather as much information as possible. Below are the most common questions travelers ask:
Q-1: Is a direct flight available from Bangalore to Vietnam?
Ans: No, currently, no direct flights are available. All flights have one stop layover in the hubs like Singapore, Bangkok, or Kuala Lumpur.
Q-2: How long does it take to reach Vietnam from Bangalore?
Ans: The journey usually takes 7–9 hours, including layovers.
Q-3: Do Indians need a visa for Vietnam?
Ans: Yes, a visa is required for Indians visiting Vietnam. Ensure you apply for an e-visa online for a hassle-free process.
Q-4: How many days are enough for a Vietnam trip?
Ans: This depends on what you are expecting from your trip. But, a 6 to 8-day trip is ideal to cover North, Central, and South Vietnam highlights.
Q-5: Which is better—North or South Vietnam?
Ans: Both regions offer unique experiences. You can choose one or cover both based on your preferences. North has Hanoi and Halong Bay, while South has Ho Chi Minh City and the Mekong Delta.
Q-6: What is the best time to travel from Bangalore to Vietnam?
Ans: March–April and September–November are the best months for pleasant weather.
Q-7: Is Vietnam an ideal destination for couples?
Ans: Yes, Vietnam is ideal for couples as it offers romantic cruises, beaches, and heritage towns.
Q-8: Is Vietnam safe for Indian travelers?
Ans: Yes, Vietnam is generally safe for tourists. Usual precautions should be taken as a traveler in an unknown country.
Q-9: What currency should I carry to Vietnam?
Ans: You must carry Vietnamese Dong. However, USD is widely accepted for exchange. Make sure you get rupees exchanged with USD in India to spend hassle-freely in Vietnam.
Q-10: Are vegetarian and Indian food options available in Vietnam?
Ans: Yes, though the options are limited. However, you can find restaurants serving Indian and vegetarian food easily.
Q-11: Can I use Indian debit/credit cards in Vietnam?
Ans: Yes, but make sure you inform your bank in advance. Don’t forget to carry some cash as cards may not work in small shops.
Q-12: Is travel insurance mandatory for Vietnam?
Ans: It’s not mandatory, but strongly recommended for medical emergencies or trip delays.
Q-13: How is the nightlife in Vietnam?
Ans: Nightlife is vibrant and you can expect rooftop bars, beach clubs, night markets, and karaoke spots.
Q-14: What kind of hotels are included in Vietnam packages?
Ans: Packages include accommodations that range from 3-star budget hotels to luxury 5-star resorts and boutique stays.
Q-15: Can Vietnam be combined with other destinations?
Ans: Yes, My Quick Trippers helps you get the most out of your escape and offers you choices to combine Vietnam with Cambodia, Thailand, or Singapore for a multi-country experience.

blocks.text: Saraswati Pushkaram is a holy festival of the River Saraswati that takes place once every 12 years. Devotees celebrate this because they believe taking a bath in the river cleanses their soul and gives them moksha (salvation). According to Purana, during Pushkaralu, Guru Brihaspati (Jupiter) increases the river’s holiness and importance. Many devotees visit here to perform puja and rituals for blessings.

This is the best time to go for Darshan and receive spiritual blessings. Saraswati Pushkaram 2025 will take place from May 15 to 26 in Mana village near Badrinath. People believe that the Saraswati River flows underground and appears at Mana. Visitors should never miss this holy Yatra. Our Saraswati Pushkar Yatra package includes the best hotels, transportation and a guide to make your journey easy. We welcome visitors from Delhi or Haridwar. Book this holy journey now, where you will experience the divine energy with the natural beauty of Badrinath.

blocks.text: Best Places to Explore in Maharashtra on Your Trip

If you want to experience a vibrant urban energy, you must visit Maharashtra once in a lifetime. In 2024, Maharashtra welcomed over 3.7 million tourists, the highest among Indian states ( Times of India ). It is one of the most visited travel destinations in India. Here are some of the most popular places to explore in Maharashtra, covered in our travel itineraries-

items: The charm of Mumbai is unbeatable. Known as City of Dreams, Mumbai comes first in the list of top travel destinations in Maharashtra. It is a perfect place for family holidays, romantic getaway, spiritual and adventure trips.

Explore some of the best places like Gateway of India, Marine Drive, Elephanta Caves, markets like Chor bazar, Colaba Causeway. Don't forget to visit Bollywood studios and film sets, these places will amaze your curious mind.

Known as the "City of Gates" Aurangabad stands still with pride by keeping Mughal and medieval history remnants intact. You must have heard about Ajanta Ellora Caves, Bibi Ka Maqbara, Daulatabad Fort and Grishneshwar Temple. These places are the crowning jewels of Aurangabad Tourism.

It is also one of the best places to enjoy a honeymoon in Maharashtra. Explore places like Jayakwadi Dam, Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary, and Goga Baba Hill and enjoy trekking, bird watching, and scenic views with your loved ones.

Nashik is very famous for its sacred sites and cultural experiences. It houses two most famous pilgrimage sites- Trimbakeshwar Temple (one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva) and a revered Shaktipeeth- Saptashrungi Devi Temple.
You will also witness Panchavati, a sacred site associated with Lord Rama's exile. For capturing scenic views, witness Anjaneri Hills, Vihigaon Waterfall and Dudhsagar falls.

Pune's liveliness and rich culture and heritage attract diverse travellers. It has many amazing places to explore like Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati temple, Aga khan Palace, Sinhagad Fort and hill stations like Lonavala and Khandala.
To experience the authentic culture and traditions, you can also plan your Pune sightseeing tour during festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi or Pune Festival.

Kolhapur has a rich heritage and natural beauty. The city boasts of many historical places like Panhala Fort, New Palace, and the revered pilgrimage sites of Shri Mahalaxmi Temple, Jyotiba and Kopeshwar.
You can also enjoy adventure trekking in forts of Vishalgad and Panhala etc. These multifaceted offerings in terms of tourism makes it a must visit travel destination in Maharashtra.

Lonavala is the best place to explore in Maharashtra for family-friendly outings. The beauty of Lonavala will take your breath away. This scenic hill station offers a perfect blend of history, adventure and relaxation in the lap of nature.
It is located in the beautiful Sahyadri Range which is very famous for misty hills, cascading waterfalls, majestic forts and caves etc.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Maharashtra on Your Trip
Not a single day is dull in Maharashtra as there are many things to do here for all types of travellers. Here is the list of best activities to do in Maharashtra, covered in our itineraries-

items: Paragliding is one of the most fun-filled and thrilling adventure activities to do in Maharashtra. You must not miss it.

Through paragliding, you will get a chance to get aerial views of the beautiful Sahyadri Range, Western Ghats, hills and valleys. Some of the best areas to try paragliding in Maharashtra are Kamshet, Panchgani, Saputara, Talegaon etc.

Landscapes of Western Ghats and Scenic Sahyadri mountains offer the best trekking trails to explore in Maharashtra. You must not miss the most popular Kalsubai Peak Trek which is the highest peak in Maharashtra.
You can also try a heritage trekking trail of Rajmachi Fort which passes through scenic dense forests and waterfalls.
Enjoy a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation at the scenic Arabian Sea coastline in Maharashtra.

Enjoy thrilling activities like jet skiing, banana boat rides, parasailing, snorkeling, and kayaking etc. with beachside relaxation with your family. Explore heritage forts like Kolaba Fort near Alibaug.

Don't forget to explore Maharashtra's rich biodiversity spots and enjoy exotic wildlife of the region. Spot Bengal tigers, Indian leopards, sloth bears, Indian bison, deer species and a variety of bird species.
Some of the most popular National Parks in Maharashtra are -Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve, Pench National Park, and Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary.

blocks.text: Top Travel Tips for Memorable Holidays in Maharashtra
Here are some best travel tips to explore Maharashtra for memorable holidays

items: Plan your Visit- Plan your Maharashtra visit during peak tourism season to enjoy culture, festivities, heritage sightseeing and adventure activities. The best time to visit in Maharashtra is from October to March.

What to Pack -Align your packing list with season and planned activities in Maharashtra. Pack versatile clothing perfect for warm days and cool nights. Wear comfortable walking shoes as you may have to walk a lot during sightseeing. Carry sun protection (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen), modest clothes for temple visits, basic toiletries, personal medications, and travel essentials like ID, cash, and chargers to enjoy hassle free trips.
Be Safe- Don't visit less frequented areas in Maharashtra after dark. If you wish to explore offbeat destinations then hire a local guide for a comprehensive Maharashtra Tour.
Maharashtra is culturally diverse. So, to experience the best Maharashtra tour, include a mix of all types of attractions like famous UNESCO sites, beaches, Hill stations, adventure parks etc.
Dress Modestly -Dress modestly in religious places. Cover your head, shoulder and knees. Wearing revealing clothes in religious sites in India is considered disrespectful.
Licensed Guides- Always hire licensed guides to enjoy Maharashtra tourism. They possess local insights on history, culture, heritage, offbeat locations and festivals.

Ans: October to February, winter is the best time to explore Maharashtra with family and friends for sightseeing and planning adventure. The weather will be pleasant for sightseeing, trekking, and enjoying festivals.
Q-2: How to plan a Maharashtra Tour?

Ans: Planning a Maharashtra Tour on your own for the first time will be too time consuming. You have to plan carefully about the budget (day to day) according to the duration of your stay, transportation, hotel booking and hiring guides etc. If you don't want to take stress on travel logistics then you can book our Maharashtra Tour Packages and enjoy Maharashtra holidays.
Q-3: What is the easiest and the most convenient way to reach Maharashtra?

Ans: Air mode of travel is the easiest and the most convenient way to travel to Maharashtra. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM) has amazing domestic and international connectivity. The duration of your travel will be less compared to train and road journeys.
Q-4: How many days are enough for the Maharashtra Tour?

Ans: Maharashtra is culturally very versatile. There are many historical, nature and adventure places to explore in Maharashtra. You have to select your duration of travel according to your interest. It is not possible to have a comprehensive trip in 2-3 days; you will only be able to cover one or two places in Maharashtra in 2-3 Days in a rush. To enjoy a comprehensive tour of Maharashtra, at least 7-8 days are needed. Yes, you can explore a part of Maharashtra in 2-3 days but to have a comprehensive tour 7-8 days are needed.

Ans: In 2024, Maharashtra welcomed over 3.7 million tourists, the highest among Indian states. This shows that Maharashtra is one of the most visited places in India. It offers an incredible diversity of experiences. You can see ancient UNESCO sites, pristine beaches to bustling metropolitan cities and serene hill stations which makes it a worth visiting place for every type of traveller.

blocks.text: If you are searching for a Badrinath tour package in 2026, the two questions most pilgrims ask first are the same: how much will it cost, and will someone handle everything so I do not have to figure it out myself?

Getting to Badrinath from any Indian city involves long-distance travel, a 10–12 hour mountain road drive, accommodation at 3,133 metres altitude, Yatra Registration , and temple logistics — all of which need advance coordination. Most pilgrims who try to plan this independently spend weeks on it and still arrive uncertain about what comes next.

My Quick Trippers is a Ministry of Tourism, Government of India approved operator with 17 years of Himalayan pilgrimage experience. We offer Badrinath Yatra packages starting from ₹18,500 per person — budget group options, standard private packages, deluxe tours, and helicopter packages — all fully managed from your departure city to your safe return.
What Is a Badrinath Tour Package?

A Badrinath tour package is an all-inclusive Badrinath pilgrimage tour covering travel to the temple and back. It includes hotel accommodation, pure vegetarian meals, private transport, VIP Darshan assistance, and a dedicated tour manager. Standard packages start from ₹18,500 per person (3N/4D Ex Haridwar) and go up to ₹75,000+ for helicopter packages. Duration ranges from 3 nights to 8 nights depending on departure city and package tier.

Badrinath Dham is one of the four sacred Char Dhams and one of the most essential pilgrimages for Hindu devotees across India. Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, the temple sits at 3,133 metres in the Garhwal Himalayas of Uttarakhand, on the banks of the Alaknanda River.

Badrinath is one of the 108 Divya Desams - the most sacred Vishnu shrines in the Vaishnava tradition and a realm of Moksha (liberation from the cycle of birth and death). Open to devotees for approximately six months each year, pilgrims from across India and the world visit the Badrinath temple to seek the blessings of Badri Vishal.

The temple was established and systematised by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century CE. He instituted the tradition of the Rawal - the head priest - being from Kerala's Namboodiri Brahmin community, a practice that continues today. This connection makes the Badrinath Dham Yatra especially significant for South Indian Vaishnava families.
On the 2026 opening day (23rd April) , over 16,000 devotees attended as the Kapat opened amid Vedic chants.

Key Attractions Covered in Our Badrinath Packages

The main sanctum houses the idol of Lord Badrinarayan — a black Shaligram stone idol in Padmasana posture, approximately 1 metre tall. The Abhishek Puja at 4:30 AM and Sandhya Aarti at 7:30 PM are the most auspicious daily rituals. VIP Darshan is included in all our packages.

Natural sulphur hot spring at 45°C , directly adjacent to the temple. Pilgrims traditionally bathe here before Darshan — believed to purify before entering the sanctum. Our tour manager guides you on timing to avoid the mid-morning rush.

A sacred ghat on the Alaknanda River where pitru tarpan (ancestral prayers) are performed. For families wishing to offer prayers for departed relatives, Brahma Kapal is the most significant spot near Badrinath. Priest fees are paid directly (approximately ₹500–₹2,000). Our packages include dedicated time here.

Located 3 km from Badrinath by road — one of the last inhabited villages near the Indo-Tibet border. Contains Vyas Gufa (where sage Vyasa composed the Mahabharata), Ganesh Gufa , and Bhim Pul — a natural rock bridge over the Saraswati River. Our itinerary schedules Mana Village at 8 AM — before tourist crowds arrive.
A 145-metre waterfall located 9 km from Badrinath (3 km by road to Mana, then 6 km trek). Included as an optional add-on for fit pilgrims with adequate time.

Five sacred river confluences on the Haridwar–Badrinath highway: Devprayag, Rudraprayag, Karnaprayag, Nandaprayag, and Vishnuprayag. Our standard and deluxe packages include short stops at key confluences — adding spiritual depth to the journey.
Peak season general queue: 3–6 hours . Our VIP Darshan arrangement reduces wait time to 20–40 minutes . Booking VIP Darshan well in advance is essential for May–June visits.
