Mandatory Yatra Registration — Do This First
Every Char Dham pilgrim must register before travel. This is compulsory — not optional.

items: Visit registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in on your phone or computer
Enter personal details — name, age, address, Aadhaar number
Select your pilgrimage destinations and travel dates
Submit and download your Yatra Registration Number (YRN)

blocks.text: Each group member registers individually — one YRN per person. Carry printed + digital copy. YRN is checked at checkpoints throughout the route. Pilgrims without YRN are turned back at the first checkpoint and must register on-site — causing significant delay during peak season.
When you book with us, our team verifies your YRN before departure and assists anyone facing difficulties with the portal.
Health and Safety for Badrinath Yatra
At 3,133 metres , oxygen levels are approximately 30% lower than at sea level.

items: Consult your doctor before booking — essential for anyone above 60 or with cardiovascular, BP, or respiratory conditions
Drink 3–4 litres of water daily on mountain days
Eat light, warm meals at altitude — your body is already managing adjustment
AMS symptoms: headache, nausea, dizziness, breathlessness — stop ascending and rest immediately
Our itineraries include an acclimatisation night at Joshimath — this is non-negotiable

blocks.text: What to Pack for Badrinath Yatra

items: Thermal inner wear (top and bottom) — 2 sets minimum. Even June nights reach 2–6°C at Badrinath.
Ankle-support walking shoes with grip sole — not sandals or flat-soled shoes
One extra pair of warm socks in waterproof bag
Personal daily medicines — carry 3 extra days' supply
ORS sachets, pain relief, antiseptic cream
Pulse oximeter (₹800–₹1,200) — monitors blood oxygen at altitude
Sunscreen SPF 50+ — UV intensity significantly higher at 3,133m
Yatra Registration Number — printed copy + saved offline on phone
₹3,000–₹5,000 cash from Haridwar — ATMs at Badrinath fail frequently during peak season due to network issues
Skipping Joshimath acclimatisation. Direct Haridwar-to-Badrinath in one day is the leading cause of AMS on this route. Our itinerary builds this rest day in — it is not removable.

Booking without checking inclusions. A ₹10,000 "Badrinath package" excluding accommodation and transport is not cheaper than our ₹12,500 all-inclusive option. Always get a written line-by-line breakdown before paying.
Travelling in July–August without buffer days. Landslides close the Haridwar–Badrinath highway for 12–48 hours multiple times per season. No buffer days means no Yatra.
Not registering online before leaving home. Registration at registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in takes 10 minutes. On-site registration at checkpoints during peak season causes 2–4 hour delays.
Underpacking warm clothing. Badrinath is at 3,133 metres. Even June nights reach 2–4°C. One light jacket is not enough.
Booking helicopter without lead time. Helicopter slots for May–June fill 60–90 days in advance. Walking in and expecting same-day availability is not realistic.
Schedule Mana Village at 8 AM, not 11 AM. Tourist crowd at Mana peaks between 10 AM and 2 PM. An 8 AM visit gives you Vyas Gufa and Bhim Pul with almost no crowd — a completely different experience.

Attend both the 4:30 AM Abhishek Puja and the 7:30 PM Sandhya Aarti. Most pilgrims attend one. The Abhishek Puja at dawn with snow peaks in the background, and the Sandhya Aarti at dusk with the temple lit — these are two distinctly different and equally powerful experiences.
Carry cash from Haridwar — not just Joshimath. ATMs along the entire Haridwar–Badrinath route have limited cash availability during peak season. Withdrawing from Haridwar eliminates any risk.

Book ground-floor rooms if travelling with parents above 65. Mountain hotels at Joshimath and Badrinath do not have lifts. After a long mountain drive, climbing 3 flights of stairs at altitude is genuinely exhausting.

Start your Day 1 mountain drive by 6:00–6:30 AM from Haridwar. The 10–12 hour Haridwar–Joshimath drive is long. Starting early means arriving before dark — mountain roads at night are not advisable even with experienced drivers.

blocks.text: Some Surprising Truths on Dubai- World's most Ambitious City

Dubai has tall, towering buildings, a glimmering skyline, a place where numerous movies are shot each year, where people come together as one and create a vibe of immense adoration to this unbelievable man-made feat that makes us realize that anything is possible in the world. Here are some amazing facts to know about Dubai-
Dubai was once a Fishing Hub

Dubai's development started through oil exports after the 1960s. Before it, Dubai was only a simple fishing village. Today it is one of the fastest growing cities in the world which attracts travelers from all across the globe.

You will be compelled to think about whether Dubai is a city or a collection of world records. It has over 300 extraordinary achievements. It has the world's tallest building- Burj Khalifa, one of the world's largest shopping malls by total area — Dubai Mall, and the iconic luxury Burj Al Arab hotel, widely considered the world's most luxurious hotel.
Islands in Shape of Palm Tree

Have you ever seen the world's largest artificial archipelago? No? then see Palm Jumeirah. It is best seen from above from a helicopter ride or skydiving adventure. You will also see the iconic Burj Khalifa, Burj Al Arab, Atlantis, the Palm and Jumeirah beach shoreline.

Dubai receives sunshine throughout the year, and it has a very hot desert climate. Sometimes, the summer temperature can exceed 100 degrees. It receives very little rainfall (average of 25 days per year).

Can you believe that in Dubai you will enjoy snowfall? Well, Dubai is a city with endless possibilities. So, snowfall is also possible. At Ski Dubai, you will be able to enjoy snow adventures in summer. Enjoy indoor skiing and other snow adventure activities. The temperature will be around -2°C.
Experience Dubai like Never Before- Best Places to Visit in Dubai

Rising from a desert land creating an aura of ultimate thrill, adventure, and vibrancy it is a place for people of all age groups to have fun. Let's know about some of the best places to explore in Dubai -
In Burj Khalifa you will not only see a new tower but a new horizon. It is the tallest building in the World. Scale the new heights on the world's fastest glass elevator to the 124th floor.

In Dubai's Global Village, every culture finds home. You will be amazed to see various countries setting up pavilions to introduce you to their culture. There will be many shops, dining stalls where you will get to taste cuisine from all over the world.

Expect world's most delightful and exciting underwater adventure at Dubai's Aquarium and underwater Zoo. This underwater universe is home to thousands of marine species you have never seen before. Spot endangered tiger sharks, King Croc crocodile, Ray, giant Pacific octopus, giant grouper, blacktip reef sharks, etc.

Shaped like a Palm tree, Palm Jumeirah is one of the most visited tourist attractions in Dubai. It is the world's most exclusive shoreline. Enjoy world class luxury dining at places like Maiden Shanghai and Grand ZOR - Fairmount the Palm, adventure activities at water parks and exciting desert safari in the Dubai desert. Also, do you enjoy arcade games? If yes, visit GAME OVER Escape Rooms at Palm Jumeirah to enjoy family friendly escape rooms and arcade games.

Don't miss one of the world's largest shopping malls by total area. It is indeed one of the best places to hang out with your family and friends in Dubai. It's the beating heart of Dubai. There are around 1200 stores here and 120 restaurants and cafes. Shopping here means shopping around the world. There are also tons of leisure and entertainment options like Ekart Zabeel, VR Park, KidZania, China Town, Ice Rink and Dubai fountain show.

Mesmerized by Dubai's waterfront view at Dubai Marina. The views here will enchant your soul. There are also many eateries and cafes to savor delicious cuisines with your loved ones. Also enjoy skydiving over Palm Jumeirah yacht cruises and boat rides, and shop and dine at Marina Mall.
Dubai Bucket List- Things to Do
Dubai will leave you amazed right from the moment you step in. Let's check out some of the best activities to do in Dubai-
Dubai Miracle Garden - Blooming Miracles in the Desert

items: Explore Dubai Miracle Garden as it offers a variety of amazing botanical and artistic expressions.
Here you will witness a life- sized A38 aircraft which is not made of metal but of million petals. Don't miss the flower parade which features vibrant costumes, dance and music.
Pose for a selfie at one of the most scenic locations- Sunflower field here. It's a perfect place for a honeymoon couples' trip in Dubai.
Enjoy a thrilling desert safari adventure in Dubai deserts. Capture the beautiful views of dunes and sunset. Try exciting adventures like camelback riding and sandboarding.
Later, relax at a traditional desert campsite, savor delicious cuisines and enjoy cultural folk dance performances such as Tanoura Dance.
Dubai Fountain lake boat ride is one of the best things to do in Dubai. Leave all the chaos of the city on the shore and enjoy stunning views of Burj Khalifa.
Also view the most scenic and largest choreographed fountain from Burj Lake.

blocks.text: Rides at IMG Worlds of Adventure

items: IMG World adventure is one of the best places to explore in Dubai if you love adventures and want to spend quality time with your family.
Enjoy thrilling rides like The Last Valley and savor delicious food and buy amazing toys, merchandise and clothes as souvenirs from various stalls.
Sky Dubai's charm is unparalleled. It is the Middle East's first indoor Ski resort which is located in the Mall of Emirates.

If you want to try something unique then you must visit here. Enjoy snow adventure activities in summer like snowboarding, skiing and interacting with penguins. The resort is accessible throughout the year.

blocks.text: Standing 150 metres tall and shaped like a giant picture frame, Dubai Frame is one of the top 5 most-visited attractions in Dubai. The glass-floored sky bridge between the two towers gives you stunning views of old Dubai on one side and modern Dubai on the other. Located in Zabeel Park, it is an easy half-day visit. Price of Ticket: AED 50 | Timings: 9 AM — 9 PM daily
Expo City Dubai — Now a Permanent Destination

Originally built for Expo 2020, Expo City Dubai is now a permanent attraction. It houses the Terra — The Sustainability Pavilion, Al Wasl Plaza (the world's largest 360° projection dome), and the Women's Pavilion. Great for families and those interested in innovation and sustainability. Entry to the main grounds is free; individual pavilions have separate ticket prices.
Dubai on Plate- What to Eat
Dubai offers multicultural dining experiences to the tourists. Arabic and Indian food are the most preferred food loved by the people of Dubai. Let's know in Detail where should you eat in Dubai-

items: Ravi- Cheap Indian Restaurant with sidewalk seating
Al Ustad Special Kebab - Try here delicious Iranian Kebab
Al Tawasol- One of the best places to try Yemeni food.
Logma- Try Emeriti breakfast and Dessert
Aseelah - Try Traditional and Contemporary Emeriti Food
Al Fanar- Lovely joint for traditional Emeriti Food
Qwaider Al Nabulsi- Try delicious and fluffy Falafel and Kunafa.
Zaroob - Place to try delicious Lebanese street food
Kinara by Vikas Khanna- A fine dining restaurant to try the best Indian food by Michelin Star Chef Vikas Khanna.
Indego by Vineet - Visit here if you want to try contemporary versions of classical Indian dishes. It is a restaurant by Michelin star chef Vineet Bhatia.
Kashkan by Ranveer Brar - It's a fine dining restaurant by an Indian chef Ranveer Brar to try the best regional dishes from Kashmir to Kanyakumari.
Govinda's - Try Sattvic Food without onion, garlic and oil. They offer simple and delicious vegetarian dishes.
Saravana Bhavan - It is a very famous Indian joint to try popular South and North Indian dishes.

blocks.text: Currency & Budget Guide — Dubai for Indian Tourists

items: Currency: UAE Dirham (AED). As of 2026, approximately 1 AED = INR 23–24 (check live rates before travel).
Daily Budget (per person): Budget traveller — AED 150-200/day (approx. INR 3,500-4,800). Mid-range — AED 350-500/day. Luxury — AED 1,000+/day.
Free Attractions: Dubai Fountain show (free, viewable from outside), The Creek waterfront, Gold Souk and Spice Souk, JBR Beach, La Mer Beach.
Nol Card: Purchase a Nol Card (available at metro stations) to use public transport — metro, trams, buses, water taxis. Minimum recharge: AED 20.

blocks.text: Ramadan Travel in Dubai — What to Know

items: Eating, drinking and smoking in public during daylight hours is prohibited during Ramadan. Tourists must follow this rule outside of hotels and designated areas.
Many restaurants open only after iftar (sunset). Hotel restaurants remain open during the day for guests.
Dubai is still very much open to tourism during Ramadan — shopping malls, attractions operate (sometimes with adjusted hours). Nightlife after iftar can be lively.
Dress modestly when visiting public places during Ramadan.

blocks.text: Dubai International Airport is the main airport where most international flights land. From India, by air is the fastest way to reach Dubai.

items: Cities- Some of the main Indian cities to get direct flights for Dubai - New Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Pune, Surat, Jaipur, Bhubaneswar and Amritsar.
Major Airlines- Emirates, Air India, Indigo, Spice Jet, Oman Air, Etihad Airways.
Nol Card - It's a travel pass which must be purchased to use public transport and other relevant services in Dubai like paying for rides on metro, trams, taxis and buses.

blocks.text: Gujarat, the westernmost state of India is worldwide for its white sandy deserts, holy destinations, historical and cultural places, and glimmering beaches. Browsing our Best of Gujarat Tour Package offers you an opportunity to explore various other tourist destinations dotted in the state. As you are on a family tour and the taste of each family member is different so we have compiled all such destinations that could match with the taste of each member of your group.
Best of Gujarat Tour Itinerary Package

Once you get down at the Ahmedabad airport or the railway station, you will find our representative waiting for you and then take you to one of your pre-decided hotels through a private transfer. Once you are ok with all the formalities required to do the check-in at the hotel get yourself ready to explore the destinations scheduled for today. The day visit commences with the exploration of Gandhi Ashram, Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, a perfect example of architecture grandeurs, enjoy visiting boat ride in Kankaria Lake, Akshardham Temple, and Adalaj Temple. After completing the day visitation, retire to the hotel for gorging upon the night cuisine and staying overnight.
Day 2 : Drive to Dwarka via Jamnagar

Post goring upon your morning meal, get yourself done with the formalities needed to check-out from the hotel and get ready to explore the leftover destinations that are covered under the Gujarat tour package. From Ahmedabad, you will be taken to Jamnagar en-route which you can visit Lakhota Museum and Lakhota Lake. After visiting these spots you will drive straight towards Dwarka by the road where you can seek the blessings of Bala Hanuman Temple. After covering a long distance from Ahmedabad to Dwarka and on reaching Dwarka, drive towards the hotel where you can accommodate yourself with your family and can relax for the next day trip. If time allows you then visit the Dwarkadhish Temple in the evening where you can participate in the evening Aarti ceremony.

Give a perfect start to your third day of the trip with a relishing breakfast at the hotel and after treating your taste buds with the morning meal, take a holy dip into the River Gomati and then start your temple-hopping tour in Dwarka. Nageshwar Jyotirlinga Temple, Gopi Talav, and Bet Talav are some of the best destinations and after completing these destinations when you drive back to Dwarka via the boat ride visit the popular Rukmini Devi Temple. Spend your afternoon in exploring the coastal attractions including the lighthouse standing tall at the beach. If you are left with some energy after the daily schedule then attend the evening Aarti at the Dwarkadhish Temple. Conclude your third day of the tour with a scrumptious Gujarati meal served at the night.
Day 4 : Transfer to Somnath via Porbandar

This is your last day in Dwarka from where you will drive straight to Somnath via Porbandar. On the way to Somnath, make your visit to the destinations falling en-route especially Kirti Mandir which is considered to be the place where Mahatma Gandhi was born and also visit the Sudama Temple. This is the time to start exploring the destinations established in Somnath. On reaching the destination town, complete the check-in formalities at the hotel where you are going to stay in Somnath. Bhalka Tirth, Geeta Mandir, and Triveni Sangam are some of the destinations you are exploring today. Later in the evening, visit the Somnath Temple again for attending the evening Aarti ceremony and to participate in the light and sound show at the temple. This is all for the day so conclude your day with a relaxing overnight stay.
Day 5 : Drive to Diu and Sightseeing

According to the schedule of the Gujarat tour package, check-out from your stay in Somnath drive towards Diu with your family members. On reaching the destination city, enter your room after completing the check-in formalities and then unwind yourself. Here you will be visiting Nagaon Beach, Diu Fort, and Diu Museum, Gangeshwar Temple, Naida Caves, and Chakratirth Beach. By the time it gets dark, drive back to the hotel for a night of sound sleep.

Early morning after completing the check-out formalities at the hotel and continue your drive towards Gir where on arrival you will be dropped at the hotel to get freshen up and unwind yourself followed by a trip to Gir National Park. Board the bus to spot Asiatic lions where you can enjoy the incredible wildlife of Gujarat. On the 6th day of the tour you will be treating your taste buds with the traditional Gujarati cuisines in dinner which is then followed by a relaxing night stay.

On the very last day of your Gujarat Trip, kick start your day with a relishing morning meal. Finally, the day has come where you will be returning to Ahmedabad and on the way to Junagarh including Navlakha Palace, Gondal, and Uparkot Fort. After covering such destinations, you will be escorted back to the Ahmedabad Airport or the railway station from where you board the flight or train for your onward journey towards home. Kumbh Mela is famous for its historical and mythological stories that attract a lot of devotees:

items: In the 7th century, a Chinese traveler Xuanzang wrote about Prayagraj. He described its temples and rituals, indicating that the Kumbh Mela began during that time.

Kumbh Mela is also popular for it’s another story, because it is believed that Lord Vishnu was carrying a pot of Amrit (nectar), which fell in specific places like Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain. People who drink the nectar become immortal. After this event, these spots are important in Hinduism.
Prayagraj is mentioned in the Rigveda and Buddhist writings. These writings describe that being good is more important than taking baths for cleanliness.

Another interesting part of Prayagraj’s history is found in the Mahabharata. It is said that the Pandavas came to Prayagraj to perform rituals for their ancestors. This place is holy because performing rituals here strengthens the bond between living people and their family members who have already passed away.

blocks.text: What Tourists Can Expect at Kumbh Mela 2025
In 2025, there will be a huge crowd of people. Pilgrims, sadhus, and visitors from all over the world will come to Prayagraj for this spiritual event. The main events at the Kumbh Mela are:

Sadhus and Akharas - A big highlight of the Kumbh Mela is the sadhus, or holy men. They are respected for their discipline and spiritual knowledge. Sadhus are a part of different groups called Akharas. Some sadhus focus on their spiritual goals, while others offer blessings to visitors.

Shahi Snan- During the Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj, sadhus take a holy dip in the river before other people, this ritual is known as the Shahi Snan. Visitors can enjoy the energy of the chanting and music during the royal bath at the Kumbh Mela.

Spiritual discussions and cultural activities- At the Kumbh Mela, spiritual leaders talk about Hindu philosophy like rituals, moral values, and life lessons. Tourists can also go for cultural shows, including dance performances, folk art displays, and music events.

items: You can fly to Prayagraj Airport (Bamrauli Airport), located just 15 kilometers from the Kumbh Mela.
Taxis or auto-rickshaws are easily available at the airport to reach Mela.
The nearest main railway station is Prayagraj junction, which is connected to many cities.
When you reach, local transport options, like auto-rickshaws or taxis are available for the Mela.
You can reach Prayagraj by bus or vehicle. Convenient bus services are available, including many private buses from nearby areas.

blocks.text: While in Prayagraj, tourists should explore city’s popular historical and cultural attractions:

items: Triveni Sangam - This is the meeting point of three holy rivers - the Ganges, Yamuna, and Saraswati Rivers.
Allahabad Fort - This fort was built by Emperor Akbar. Tourists can enjoy great views of the rivers, and it is a perfect place to explore history.
Anand Bhawan - It was the home of Jawaharlal Nehru (Gandhi family). Now there is a museum inside, visitors can see personal belongings, photographs, and documents of the Nehru family.
Swaraj Bhawan - It is a special place where you can learn about India's struggle for freedom.

blocks.text: Travel Tips for the Kumbh Mela

items: Choose a meeting point - When you are traveling with family or friends, make sure to decide a specific area to meet, if you get lost in the crowd.
Phone network : Purchase a local SIM card for a better connection because SIM cards from other states cannot work well.
Book accommodation in advance : Make sure to book your hotel in advance and choose a location a bit away from the event area to avoid crowds.
Keep yourself hydrated : Drink enough water, especially during rituals and carry a water bottle with you.
Use apps to manage crowds : Some apps can track crowded places and suggest less busy paths.
Have emergency contacts : Keep local emergency numbers and find out where the nearest hospitals or clinics are.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth going to the Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the Golden Triangle is worth visiting because it includes 3 popular cities like Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur, where you will explore amazing sights and it's a great way to experience India’s rich culture and history in a short trip.

mainEntity.name: What adventure activities visitors should try on a Delhi tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Delhi, visitors can try many adventure activities, like hot air balloon rides for a unique view of the city. In Gurgaon, rock climbing in the Aravalli hills is also a perfect option. Apart from this, bungee Jumping at Adventure Island in Rohini is also the best part to enjoy.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to visit the Golden Triangle Tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The perfect time is between October to March when the climate is cooler and more pleasant.

mainEntity.name: What are the other best places to explore in Jaipur?

acceptedAnswer.text: Travelers must explore Panna Meena Ka Kund due to its beautiful well with unique architecture and a peaceful atmosphere. Moti Dungri Fort is also nice and a small fort with lovely views of Jaipur which is rarely crowded.

mainEntity.name: What Is The Golden Triangle’s Significance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The national capital, New Delhi, and the cities of Agra and Jaipur are connected by a tourist route known as the “golden triangle” of India. The three states of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan make a triangular shape on a map, hence the moniker “Golden Triangle.”

mainEntity.name: When Is The Ideal Time Of Year To Visit The Golden Triangle In India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Since there will be a lot of walking involved, the best time to visit the Golden Triangle is from October to mid-April, when temperatures vary from 22 to 32 °C. Delhi may endure frigid spells in January and February and hot 45°C temperatures in May and June as a result of the Himalayan influence.

mainEntity.name: Why Is The Golden Triangle In India Called That?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Golden Triangle got its name because gold was originally stored here. Gold was used for more than only transporting goods to Delhi and Agra; it was also used to make ornaments and coins, among other things.

mainEntity.name: .Is A Trip To The Golden Triangle Worthwhile?

acceptedAnswer.text: This area of history-rich jungle and foggy mountains is well-known for its history of opium cultivation. Even though the Golden Triangle is a well-known tourist site nowadays, it is still highly recommended.

mainEntity.name: .How Many Days Would You Need In India’s Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: When Can You See the Golden Triangle? Most visitors decide to travel the entire Golden Triangle in three to seven days, but I strongly advise at least a week.

blocks.text: There are countless temples in India. However, Jyotirlingas hold a place of their own! Deemed as the ultimate pilgrimage, See More

the trip to these holy temples is considered highly sacred for it promises Moksha – liberation from the cycle of birth and death! The Jyotirlingas are distributed across the country – from Somnath in Gujarat to Rameshwaram in Tamil Nadu! Although this is a challenging journey, our 12 Jyotirlinga Tour Package takes you to all these special shrines of Lord Shiva across the entire nation.

So think no more! Book this package now, and be the recipient of the abundant blessings that will fall your way once you complete this trip. To get a quote and know more, simply give us a call and we’ll get back to you shortly!

The 12 Jyotirlingas are considered highly sacred, and visiting them is a must for every Lord Shiva devotee. It’s believed that these temples manifest from the very energy of him when he was in the form of an infinite cosmic light pillar.

As per the Shiva Purana, once Lord Shiva appeared in the form of this bright light in order to exert his supremacy over Lord Vishnu and Lord Brahma. And now, each Jyotirlinga is a representation of his divine energy, and is considered to be a self-manifested lingam! Also, it’s believed that taking this sacred spiritual tour of Lord Shiva temples cleanses one’s sins and grants them Moksha, in turn.

Moreover, if you go to these holy temples, you can enjoy the culture and traditions of different places that you get to visit while being on this holy journey. Also, many devotees combine this trip with other tours such as Char Dham Yatra or Shaktipeeth visits, to make this a truly mega pilgrimage!
Book My Quick Trippers’s Jyotirlinga Darshan package and take an easy-peasy comfortable trip to India's most sacred shrines!
Here’s a quick guide to all twelve shrines covered in the 12 Jyotirlinga Tour Package:

items: Somnath: This was one of the very first Jyotirlingas! This sea-facing temple symbolizes eternal faith. Devotes simply love the evening light and sound show here.
Mallikarjuna: Also known as the “Kailash of the South”, this temple is associated with Parvati as Mallika and Shiva as Arjuna.
Mahakaleshwar: This is the only south-facing Jyotirlinga you’ll find. It’s famous for its holy Bhasma Aarti, where Lord Shiva is offered the sacred ash.
Omkareshwar: The specialty of this Jyotirlinga is that it is located on an island that is shaped like the OM symbol. It’s believed that coming here fulfills your wishes.
Kedarnath: This temple has a huge significance associated with it. Not only is it a Jyotirlinga, it’s also a part of the Chhota Dham circuit. It’s also the highest Jyotirlinga in altitude.
Bhimashankar: Surrounded by dense forests, this temple is linked to the mythology about the demon Tripurasura being defeated by Lord Shiva.
Kashi Vishwanath: Located in the ‘spiritual capital of India’, Varanasi, this temple promises Moksha if someone dies here of natural causes.
Trimbakeshwar: This is a unique Jyotirlinga that has 3 lingams, representing Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. This temple is popular for its Narayan Nagbali Puja rituals.
Vaidyanath: This temple sees a load of pilgrim traffic in the Shravan month, that is, when Kanwariyas visit this temple. Lord Shiva is worshipped here as the supreme healer, a Vaidya that is.
Nageshwar: This Jyotirlinga houses a tall Shiva statue, and it’s associated with the demon Daruka.

Ramanathaswamy: This temple has a very old Ramayana link. It’s believed that Lord Rama worshipped Lord Shiva here before he went to the Lanka war. There are also 22 sacred wells inside the temple where one can take a ritual bath.
Grishneshwar: This is the smallest Jyotirlinga, located very close to the Ajanta-Ellora caves. You can enjoy the rich carvings on temple walls here and the ever-present peaceful atmosphere.

blocks.text: To enjoy a smooth trip, simply opt for our Jyotirlinga Yatra booking and travel in comfort!
12 Jyotirlinga Tour Package by Train and Flight

My Quick Trippers also offers you combo 12 Jyotirlinga Tour Packages by Train and Flight , where you get to travel by both railways and plane. This combined trip makes the journey easier and far smoother. With the comfort & high speed of air travel, along with the traditional experience of the train journey, you get to enjoy the best of both worlds.

On this hybrid route, we would cover segments like Mumbai to Madurai and Hyderabad to Deoghar by flight. This is the most suitable way, as these are located far from each other and flying there considerably reduces the travel time. And for the shorter segments like Omkareshwar to Ujjain or Nashik to Bhimashankar, we can go for the scenic train journey.

With this train and flight Jyotirlinga Yatra package , devotees reach the Jyotirlingas in the most optimal time and also reduce fatigue. In general, this fight and train to Jyotirlingas tour is the best way to complete Darshan of all 12 Jyotirlingas (takes about 12-18 days). Book now or call us to know more about this combo package!
Best Time for the 12 Jyotirlinga Tour

The best time to go on this sacred Jyotirlinga tour differs from region to region, as the sacred shrines are distributed all across India. However, for most shrines, you can consider the season of autumn (September – November) for taking this sacred tour. The weather in this window is pleasant for the most part, and therefore can be considered for the holy trip.

Moreover, this is also ideal for the tour to Kedarnath , which gets closed in November, and stays so until April. Also, this window is great for visiting the temple in the south ( Rameswaram and Srisailam ) as well.
Here is some travel advice that you might find useful on this Jyotirlinga Yatra Package:

items: Even before you step out for this sacred tour, make a Sankalp in front of Lord Shiva’s idol in your home or a nearby temple, asking for the success of this tour.

Book your 12 Jyotirlinga Travel Package in advance – at least 3-6 months. The slots get quickly filled up, especially if you’re planning to travel during special occasions, such as Shravan, Navratri, and Maha Shivaratri.
If you’re a senior citizen, then consider going by train or plane, as this will help you reduce the physical strain and exhaustion caused by road travel.
If you plan to take the helicopter services, then make sure you have your ID proof and medical certificate ready.

Try to make your trip even more fulfilling by combining your Jyotirlinga tour with nearby major sightseeing attractions, like Dwarkadhish Temple (in Dwarka), Ellora Caves (in Aurangabad), and Rameswaram beaches (in Rameswaram).

Try to group your Jyotirlinga tour in a region-wise cluster. For example, combine your temple trips in West India, South India, Central India, and North India. This organised tour will help you save time and reduce your fatigue significantly.
There’s always a chance of delays. This could be due to weather and other unforeseeable factors. Therefore, always keep 1-2 days spare in your Jyotirlinga Yatra itinerary.
Throughout your trip, stay hydrated. Always carry a water bottle with you. Also, eat easily digestible, light food to aid digestion.
Always follow the temple etiquette. Some common practices include removing your shoes before entering the temple, wearing modest clothes, and not carrying leather items inside the shrine.

blocks.text: Day 1: : Arrival in Mumbai and Journey to Rajkot

items: Once you reach Mumbai, our travel representatives will greet you with a warm welcome.
Now, it’s time to catch the overnight train to Rajkot, Gujarat. You’ll get full assistance in boarding from our side.
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train. We recommend packing some light snacks and water for this train journey.

blocks.text: Day 2: Trip to Dwarkadhish and Nageshwar Jyotirlinga

items: By early morning, you’ll arrive in Rajkot.
Deboard the train, and now you’ll be driven to Dwarka. This holy city is one of the Char Dhams and also a Sapta Puri.
Now, check into your pre-booked hotel and freshen up!
Later, you’ll be taken to the Dwarkadhish Temple first. It is dedicated to Lord Krishna, where he’s worshipped in his royal form as the King of Dwarka!
Next, you’ll be driven to the very first Jyotirlinga of this tour, that is, Nageshwar Jyotirlinga. Lord Shiva is worshipped here as the protector against poison.
After your Darshan and Poojan, return to your hotel for dinner in the evening.
Get a restful night of sleep at your hotel.
Have breakfast and then check out of your hotel.
Now, you’ll be transferred to Somnath near Veraval. Once you arrive in this city, check into your hotel and take rest for a while.

Afterwards, you'll be taken to Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple, a shrine that enjoys a glorious history. According to the Hindu mythology, it’s believed that the temple was originally built by Chandra Dev in order to please Lord Shiva. Over centuries, this temple has been destroyed and rebuilt 17 times, and now stands as a metaphorical symbol of faith and resilience!
Also, attend the evening Aarti at the temple.
Then, come back to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 4 – Somnath to Ujjain transfer (Overnight Train Journey)

items: Wake up early and attend the morning Aarti at Somnath temple.
Now, check out of your hotel and head to the railway station and catch a train to Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh.
This will be an overnight journey by train. We recommend carrying a light shawl or blanket with you as the nights can get a little chilly.

blocks.text: Day 5 – Arrival in Ujjain and Visit to Omkareshwar Temple

items: You’ll arrive in Ujjain early in the morning. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and take a little rest for a while.

Now, you’ll be taken to the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga, which is situated on an island surrounded by the Narmada River. There’s another specialty of this island, which is that it is shaped like an ‘OM’ symbol. You can also choose to circumambulate the island, as many devotees do.
Afterwards, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 6 – Ujjain (Mahakaleshwar Darshan) and Train to Haridwar

items: Get up early in the morning and proceed for the Darshan and Poojan at the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga. This is one of the most revered shrines of Lord Shiv, where he’s worshiped as the destroyer of time itself.
If you reach there early, you can also witness the Bhasma Aarti, which takes place from 4 AM to 6 AM. In this sacred ritual, Lord Shiva is offered the sacred ash.
Later, enjoy a trip to the popular temples like Harsiddhi Mata Temple and Kal Bhairav Temple. Both of these temples have a strong background in the rich Tantric traditions of India.
In the evening, you’ll be driven to the railway station, where you’ll board the train to Haridwar.
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train.

blocks.text: Day 7 – Arrival in Haridwar (Ganga Aarti Experience)

items: You’ll reach Haridwar in the morning. From the railway station, you'll be transferred to your hotel, where you can check in. Take some time to relax and freshen up. The rest of the day is free!
In the evening, drop by the Har ki Pauri and witness the mesmerizing Ganga Aarti. Watch as the thousands of Diyas float by on the Ganga River.
Return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 8 – Transfer to Guptkashi and Visit to Ardhanarishvara Temple

items: Now, begin a scenic drive towards Guptkashi. Once you get there, check into your pre-booked hotel.
Now, you’ll be taken to the Ardhanarishvara Temple. This temple holds a great deal of significance as it symbolizes Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati’s unity.
Return to the hotel for dinner and overnight stay.
In the morning, we’ll depart from Sonprayag to start the trek to the Kedarnath temple.
Begin your 16 km trek via Gaurikund. You can also hire a pony/Palki service to reach the Kedarnath Dham.
Once you reach the temple, engage in the Darshan and Poojan ritual. The views all around are gorgeous, providing you with a backdrop of snow-capped peaks.
Wait till the sun goes down, when you can attend the evening Aarti, which is a soul-stirring experience, to say the least.
Your dinner and overnight stay will be arranged in Kedarnath only.

blocks.text: Day 10 – Morning Aarti at Kedarnath and Transfer to Rudraprayag

items: Wake up early before sunrise and attend the morning Aarti at Kedarnath temple.
Now trek back to Sonprayag. From there, you’ll be taken to Rudraprayag.
Check into your hotel there and enjoy an overnight stay.
Now, you’ll be driven back to Haridwar.
Once you reach there, board the overnight train for Varanasi. Your lunch and dinner will be served on the train itself.

blocks.text: Day 12 – Evening Ganga Aarti at Varanasi

items: Welcome to Varanasi! This is one of the world’s oldest cities, and is quite dear to Lord Shiva.
Now check into your hotel and rest for a while.
Visit the Dasaswamedh Ghat in the evening, where you can witness the grand Ganga Aarti live. Take in the whole experience of chants, bells, and floating lamps!
Come back to your hotel in the evening for an overnight stay.

blocks.text: Day 13 – Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga and Transfer to Deoghar

items: Wake up early to go for a morning Darshan at the Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga. Perform Poojan to your heart’s content.
Next, we’ll take you to the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple.
After that, board a train to Jasidih. Once you get there, you’ll take a short drive towards Deoghar, Jharkhand.
Enjoy an overnight stay in your hotel at Deoghar.

blocks.text: Day 14 – Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga and Train to Chennai

items: Wake up early in the morning and get ready for Darshan at the Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga. This temple is special since here Lord Shiva is worshipped as a healer (Vaidya).
Perform your Abhishek Puja & Darshan and soak in the calming atmosphere of the shrine. It is believed that Ravana himself worshipped Lord Shiva here by offering his heads as a sacrifice.
Next, board a train to Kolkata from here. Once you reach Howrah station, take a connecting train to Chennai.
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train.

blocks.text: Day 15 – Arrival in Chennai and Train to Rameswaram

items: You’ll arrive in Chennai in the morning.
Take some time to freshen up and relax in the station waiting room.
Later, board the train to Rameswaram, one of the most holy pilgrimage towns in India!
Enjoy an overnight stay on the train.
Once you reach Rameswaram, get to your hotel and check in.

The rest of the day is purposefully made free of any sightseeing. You can take this leisure time to rest or travel on your own around the area. If you go out, do indulge in the local Tamil vegetarian cuisine, which is simply delicious.
At night, enjoy dinner and get a restful night of sleep.

blocks.text: Day 17 – Rameswaram Darshan and Drive to Madurai

items: We’ll visit the Ramanathaswamy Temple early in the morning. This temple houses the very Rameshwaram Jyotirlinga that Lord Rama worshipped after he went to war with Ravana.
Afterwards, you’ll be taken for a drive to Madurai.
In the evening, visit the majestic Meenakshi Amman Temple, which is dedicated to Goddess Parvati. Enjoy the masterpiece of Dravidian architecture that this temple is!
Spend the night in your Madurai hotel.
Treat yourself to a delicious breakfast.
Now, you’ll be transferred to Madurai railway station, where you can board the train to Pune.
Enjoy an overnight journey on the train.
Once you arrive in Pune, check into your hotel.
The rest of the day is free. You can utilize it by either resting or going sightseeing/shopping on your own.
Enjoy the overnight stay at your hotel in Pune.

blocks.text: Day 20 – Visit to Bhimashankar and Trimbakeshwar

items: Have breakfast and then get ready for the Jyotirlinga tour.
Today, you’ll be taken to the Bhimashankar Temple, which is located in the lush Sahyadri Hills. It's also considered to be the source of the river Bhima.
In the latter part of the day, we’ll visit yet another Jyotirlinga, that is Trimbakeshwar Temple, which is located in Nashik.
At night, return to the hotel and get a restful night of sleep.

blocks.text: Day 21 – Trimbakeshwar Darshan, Nashik Sightseeing, and Trip to Shirdi

items: In the morning, set out again for the Darshan at the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga.

Afterwards, you’ll indulge in a sightseeing tour of Nashik, where you’ll be visiting: Sita Gufa (This is where Sita stayed during exile) Kapileshwar Temple Kala Ram Temple Panchavati and Godavari River
Later in the day, drive towards Shirdi and check into your hotel for an overnight stay.
After breakfast, get ready for Darshan of Shri Sai Baba at the famous Shirdi temple.
Spend ample time here to perform Pooja, Aarti, and pay homage to Baba.
Enjoy lunch and some free time for shopping at the local market for Sai Baba souvenirs.
Return to your hotel for overnight stay.
After breakfast, check out of the hotel and proceed towards Aurangabad.
Check into your Aurangabad hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening. Overnight stay at Aurangabad.
After breakfast, proceed for sightseeing of Ajanta and Ellora Caves. Ajanta caves are famous for their ancient Buddhist rock-cut architecture and murals.
Ellora caves are known for their Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain rock-cut temples, representing India’s religious harmony.
Return to Aurangabad hotel in the evening and enjoy dinner and overnight stay.

blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More

Ans. The 12 Jyotirlingas are special shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva. These are spread all across India, and it’s said that whoever completes a visit to all the temples gets his special blessings. The 12 Jyotirlingas are Somnath, Mallikarjuna, Mahakaleshwar, Omkareshwar, Kedarnath, Bhimashankar, Kashi Vishwanath, Trimbakeshwar, Baidyanath, Nageshwar, Ramanathaswamy, and Grishneshwar.
Q2. Why are the Jyotirlingas considered special?

Ans. According to the Hindu mythology, it’s believed that each Jyotirlinga is a manifestation of Lord Shiva. In the beginning of the universe, he took the form of a light pillar, symbolizing his infinite form, which is now manifested as the Jyotirlinga temples.
Q3. How many days are needed to cover all 12 Jyotirlingas?

Ans. For a comfortable trip to all the Jyotirlingas, it’s suggested that you take 25-30 days for this sacred tour. In this plan, you can comfortably cover the tour by giving sufficient time to each of the temples in this trip.
Q4. What is the cost of a 12 Jyotirlinga tour package?

Ans. We offer our 12 Jyotirlinga tour package at INR 95,000 per person. In this plan, all your meals, accommodation, and transfers will be covered completely by us. All you have to do is book our package and relax as we take you to the twelve most sacred shrines in the country.
Q5. Which Jyotirlinga is the hardest to visit?

Ans. The hardest Jyotirlinga to visit is the Kedarnath, which is located in the Himalayan region. The toughest thing about this shrine is that devotees have to undertake a full 16 km trek to reach the temple. Although you can book a helicopter or pony/Palki service, there’s still harsh weather and high altitude conditions that pilgrims have to brave.
Q6. Can senior citizens do the 12 Jyotirlinga Yatra?

Ans. Yes, senior citizens can also undertake this holy tour. My Quick Trippers offers special care towards senior citizens with Darshan assistance, flight arrangements, medical supplies, and 24x7 call support.
Q7. Is there a government package for the 12 Jyotirlinga Yatra?

Ans. Yes, you can also avail of government Jyotirlinga circuit tours (via IRCTC), which offer you a train and bus journey to cover this trip. The best thing about these packages is that they are very affordable and usually well-organised.
Q8. What is the best time to do the Jyotirlinga Yatra?
Ans. The best time to visit the Jyotirlinga is in the autumn season – September – November. During the window, the weather remains quite pleasant to cover them in your trip.
Q9. What is the spiritual benefit of visiting all 12 Jyotirlingas?

Ans. There are lots of spiritual benefits to covering the 12 Jyotirlingas. It’s believed that whoever visits all of them is granted moksha and has their sins cleansed. In addition, it’s said that the devotee is blessed with peace, prosperity, and spiritual fulfilment.
Q10. Which Jyotirlinga is closest to Varanasi?
Ans. The Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga is closest to Varanasi. In fact, it is itself located in Varanasi.
Q11. Which Jyotirlinga is near Dwarka?
Ans. The Nageshwar Jyotirlinga is closest to Dwarka. It is located just 16 km from there. Also, it’s also situated very near the famous Dwarkadhish Temple.
Q12. What is special about Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga?

Ans. This Jyotirlinga is quite special as only here Lord Shiva is worshipped with sacred ash. You won’t find this ritual of Bhasma Aarti anywhere else in India. Also, this is the only Jyotirlinga that faces south.
Q13. Which Jyotirlinga is located in the Himalayas?
Ans. The Kedarnath Jyotirlinga is situated in the Himalayas. In fact, it’s the Jyotirlinga with the highest elevation – 11,755 feet above the sea level.
Q14. What should I pack for the Jyotirlinga Yatra?

Ans. For most of the Jyotirlingas shrines, you can be safe with packing comfortable cotton clothes. However, for the Kedarnath shrine, which is located in the Himalayas, pack warm woollen clothes. In addition, we advise packing comfortable walking shoes, in addition to medicines, a water bottle, and an ID proof.
Q15. Which Jyotirlinga is also one of the Char Dhams?
Ans. Kedarnath Jyotirlinga is also one of the Char Dhams, in addition to Badrinath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri. Being part of the Chhota Dham circuit increases its spiritual significance even more.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit during Uttar Pradesh Trip

India’s most populous state in Uttar Pradesh today is a rich religious, natural, and historical tourist destination. Come let’s know some of the best tourist destinations in Uttar Pradesh to visit during this trip:

Varanasi is one of the oldest living cities in the world. It is believed that Lord Shiva himself created this holy city with the essence of all his sacred energies. Varanasi has many ancient temples and Ghats. In puranas, Varanasi was named as Avimukth as Lord Shiva never expressed or left it. In every corner the sacred vibes will nourish the soul. It is one of the must visit places in Uttar Pradesh.

items: Dashashwamedha Ghat - It is one of the most famous sacred ghats to visit in Varanasi. This place was named Dashashwamedha after Lord Brahma performed Ashvamedha Yagya. The final construction of the ghat was done by Bajirao Peshwa in 1735 AD.

The Kashi Vishwanatha Temple - Close your eyes and imagine Varanasi. What do you see? The first image which pops in our mind is the sacred Kashi Vishwanath Temple. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is the landmark destination of Varanasi. It is the first place where the sacred light of Lord Shiva in the form of Jyotirlinga manifested.

Goddess Annapurna Temple - Located near Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Goddess Annapurna Temple is dedicated to the mother of the universe (Devi Parvati) who blesses devotees with abundance and nourishment.

Sankat Mochan Temple - In 16th century, a saint named Tulsi Das established the idol of Lord Hanuman under a fig tree which later became known as Sankat Mochan Temple. It is believed that he created some parts of his epic Ramcharitmanas. You must visit Sankat Mochan Temple, if you are in Varanasi.

Chausath Yogini Temple - Situated above the Chausath Yogini Ghat, the temple is dedicated to goddess Kali. It is also a 64 Yogini temple. You will see 64 female deities attending to the goddess. In ancient Varanasi, it is said that there used to be many more Yogini temples but today this temple remains containing all their spiritual energies.

Tulsi Manas Temple - Tulsi Manas Temple is dedicated to Lord Ram. It is said that at this place saint Tulsi das used to live and wrote his epic Ramcharitmanas. You will see many sacred verses of Ramcharitmanas inscribed on the walls of the temple.

Assi Ghat - Here the sacred confluence of Asi River and Ganga River takes place, it is also one of the most popular ghats to visit in Varanasi. The sunrise here starts with enchanting Vedic chants and Kriya Yoga.

blocks.text: Don’t forget to visit these two most sacred cities- Mathura and Vrindavan in Uttar Pradesh. Mathura is a birthplace of Lord Krishna and Vrindavan is that sacred place where he spent his childhood. Together these places are considered as major pilgrimage circuits for Krishna Devotees. Here are some of the most popular places to visit in Mathura and Vrindavan:

items: Shri Krishna Janma Bhoomi - Believed to be the birthplace of Lord Krishna, Shri Krishna Janma Bhoomi temple is a landmark destination of Mathura. Devotees from all over India visit here to take divine blessings from Lord Krishna.

Dwarkadhish Temple - Dwarkadhish Temple in Mathura worships Lord Krishna in his kingly avatar as Lord Dwarkadhish. It was built in 1814 by Seth Gokul das Parikh who was a treasurer in the court of Gwalior. The idol of Lord Dwarkadhish is made up of black marble and you will witness the beautiful white marble idol of Radha Rani.

Jain Siddha Kshetra Chaurasi - It’s a major Jain pilgrimage site in Mathura. It’s a sacred place where Jambu Swami, the last Jain saint attained nirvana at the age of 84 (Chaurasi in Hindi). Hence this place is named as Jain Siddha Kshetra Chaurasi.
Gurudwara Holigate - It is a prominent Sikh religious site in Mathura. It is located near the Tilak Dwar area. Attend Kirtanas, prayers and community service- Langar.

Prem Mandir - Located in Raman Reti Road in Vrindavan, Prem Mandir celebrates and worships the divine love of lord Krishna and Radha Rani. There are beautiful carvings in the walls of the temple depicting the scenes from the divine life and pastimes of Lord Krishna, Radha Rani, Lord Rama and Devi Sita.

Rangji Temple - Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, Rangji Temple is one of the most popular temples to visit in Vrindavan. The temple follows Shri Vaishnava Agama tradition and holds daily prayers, music and rituals to worship Lord Vishnu as Lord Ranganatha.

Bankey Bihari Temple - It is one of the most famous temples of lord Krishna. This temple was built by the guru of Tansen (great musician) Swami Haridas, who was a great devotee of Lord Krishna. The Lord is named as Bankey because of his posture which is bent at three places- neck, wrist and knee.

blocks.text: Ayodhya is a place in Uttar Pradesh where the spiritual heart of India resides gracefully in the epic tales of Ramayana. It is the birth place of Lord Rama. Devotees from all across India come to Ayodhya to seek divine grace from Lord Rama. Recently the construction of Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in 2024 has made Ayodhya a global spiritual destination. Here are some of the most famous tourist places to visit in Ayodhya :

items: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple : Lifeline of Ayodhya, Ram Janmabhoomi Temple is a sacred place where Lord Rama was born. It is a prominent pilgrimage place in Ayodhya for Hindu devotees.

Hanuman Garhi Temple : Dedicated to Lord Rama, Hanuman Garhi Temple is a massive fortress-like temple. It is said that Lord Hanuman is the protector and presiding deity of Ayodhya. The temple offers scenic views of the entire city of Ayodhya.
Ram Ki Paidi : Witness Ram Ki Paidi- a serene series of iconic ghats (river steps) on the banks of the Sarayu River. Take a holy dip here to get rid of all the karmic backlogs and embrace solace.

Kanak Bhavan : It’s a marvellous temple worth capturing for Instagram. The exquisite beauty of Kanak Bhawan will take your breath away. The Kanak Bhawan is a gift to Lord Rama and Devi Sita after their marriage by Devi Kaikeyi.
Nageshwarnath Temple : Built by the son of Lord Rama- Kush, Nageshwar Nath Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Maha Shivratri is celebrated here with great pomp and show.
Saryu River : Flows along Ayodhya, Saryu River is a sacred river in which taking a dip is considered auspicious. Witness the ethereal Saryu River aarti in the evening.
Treta Ke Thakur : It’s a place where Lord Rama performed Ashvamedha Yagya. The temple houses idols of lord Rama, Devi Sita and Laxman.

blocks.text: Formerly known as Allahabad, Prayagraj is one of the most popular travel destinations to visit in Uttar Pradesh. It is a major religious site for Hindu devotees. It houses the most sacred site for the world’s largest gathering called Kumbh Mela which is held every 12 years. Beyond spiritual significance, it also has many beautiful colonial era monuments. In essence, Prayagraj has a perfect vibe for history, spiritual and cultural enthusiasts. Here are some of the most popular places to visit in Prayagraj :

items: Sangam : Don’t miss the sacred confluence of Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers. It’s the same sacred place where one of the world’s largest religious gatherings takes place every 12 years. Take a holy dip to get rid of all karmic backlogs.

Allahabad Fort : Allahabad Fort is one of the most popular and massive forts which showcase Mughal era’s craftsmanship. The fort was built by emperor Akbar in 1583. It is located near the serene banks of Sangam.

Anand Bhavan : Witness the ancestral home of Nehru- Gandhi family in Uttar Pradesh. It houses a museum which displays artefacts related to the freedom struggle. There are rooms which have still kept the essence of India’s independence movement intact.

Khusro Bagh : It’s a beautiful large walled garden showcasing intricate Mughal era tombs of Prince Khusro and other family members. Prince Khusro was the eldest son of emperor Jahangir and Sultan Begum.

Allahabad Museum : A historical museum located within Chandrashekhar Azad Park is very famous for its unique displays of ancient sculptures, paintings, rare documents and historical artifacts, known for its collection of ancient sculptures from Maurya, Gupta period.

Nagvasuki Temple : Dedicated to Nag Devta, Nagvasuki Temple is one of the most famous religious sites to visit in Prayagraj. It is located in Daraganj. The Nag Vasuki idol is a five hooded idol installed by sage Kashyapa.

blocks.text: Agra is a crowning jewel of Uttar Pradesh’s tourism landscape. It is one of the most visited tourist destinations for Indians as well as foreigners. It houses the iconic Taj Mahal, one of the new seven wonders of the world. Beyond Taj, it also has many Mughal era heritage monuments which today offers unique insights on India’s majestic past. Here are some of the most popular places to visit in Agra:

items: Taj Mahal : The lifeline of Agra- The Taj Mahal is an iconic white marble monument built by emperor Shah Jahan in the memory of his beloved wife Mumtaj Mahal. Tourists from all over the world come to Agra to witness this beautiful symbol of Love.

Agra Fort : Agra Fort is one of the most famous red sandstone forts of the Mughal era in India. It’s a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Within Agra Fort, there are many beautiful structures like Diwan-i-Khas, Diwan-i-Am, Nagina Masjid, Sheesh Mahal etc.

Fatehpur Sikri : Once, Fatehpur Sikri was an abundant town built by emperor Akbar to honor a saint Salim Chishti. In fact, it served as a Mughal capital for a decade but due to water scarcity, the town was abandoned. It has many beautiful Mughal eras like Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai’s Palace etc.

Mehtab Bagh : Don’t miss the beautiful Moonlight Garden called Mehtab Bagh. It is one of the most popular attractions in Agra. It is perfectly aligned with the iconic Taj Mahal. The Bagh is quite peaceful which offers refreshing vibes.

Itimad-ud-Daulah's Tomb : Also known as ‘Baby Taj’ Itimud-ud-Daulah’s Tomb is a beautiful marble tomb carved with semi-precious stones. It is said that the structure of this tomb was considered as a draft for the Taj Mahal design.
Kinari Bazaar : Located near Taj, Kinari Bazaar is a hub in Agra to experience its local life, shops, food handicrafts, leather goods and culture.

blocks.text: You will be mesmerized to witness the beauty of one of the most famous Buddhist pilgrimage sites of India . It is a revered place where Prince Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under a Bodhi Tree and became Buddha. The iconic Mahabodhi temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is one of the major centres for Buddhist culture and learning. Here are some of the most popular places to see in Bodhgaya:

items: Mahabodhi Temple - This tall pyramid shaped temple is a sacred place where Lord Buddha attained enlightenment. It’s a major centre for Buddhist learning. It’s a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Bodhi Tree - Witness the most sacred fig tree which still carries the divine essence of lord Buddha as he used to meditate here.

Great Buddha Statue - Embrace the inner peace by viewing the 80 ft tall outdoor statue of Lord Buddha in meditation pose. The statue is surrounded by other disciple statues and serene landscaped gardens.
Thai Monastery - It’s golden tiled sloping roofs and colossal bronze Buddha Statue will amaze your curious mind. Indulge in a peaceful meditation session for self-introspection.
Sujata Temple & Stupa - The temple and the Stupa was built in the honor of Sujata who offered food to Buddha. The temple is the symbol of her compassion and divine grace.

Bodhgaya Archaeological Museum - Don’t miss this stunning archaeological museum. You will learn about many things related to Buddhism. It houses many artefacts, sculptures, antiques related to Buddhist traditions.

items: You will be delighted to attend the morning Subah-e-Banaras on a wooden boat. It’s best thing to do is to enjoy the slow-paced Varanasi Tour to watch sacred rituals and how life unfolds at the sacred ghats.
The ancient ghats of Varanasi and Prayagraj show the spiritual wealth of Uttar Pradesh. Make sure you visit some of the most popular ghats and offer your prayers.

blocks.text: Visit Some of the Most Famous Heritage Monuments
Monuments of Uttar Pradesh showcase the history, culture and heritage of erstwhile rulers and offer great insights on India’s golden past.

items: Captivate your senses with the beautiful views of Taj Mahal and Agra Fort.
Explore the architectural wonders of Lucknow. The city of Nawabs has many mesmerizing structures like Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Dilkusha Kothi, Chota Imambara and Hazaratganj etc.
Explore the historical sites of Bodhgaya. Dive deep into the history of Mahabodhi Temple, archaeological museum and other sites.

blocks.text: Try Delicious Cuisines of Uttar Pradesh

Food of Uttar Pradesh is an invitation to know the poetry of flavours, stories behind ancient traditions, rituals and sacred philosophies. Let’s know about some of the best street food to try in Uttar Pradesh :

items: Try Delicious Biryani, Korma and Nihari. In Uttar Pradesh, at many top-rated food joints you will find these food items. Don’t miss this cuisine. These cuisines follow the tradition of Dum (slow cooking technique). The food is cooked slowly in a pot over a low flame. The pot is sealed with wheat dough to capture every flavor and aroma.

Try Temple Food. Though it is not a street food, food in Uttar Pradesh is a medium of service and devotion. In temples you will find Bhandara Prasad. The prasad is prepared without garlic or onions. Try Mathura’s Peda, Varindavan’s Makhan Mishri or Kashi’s Launglata.
Visit Varanasi’s Ram Bhandar to try Kachodi sabzi. It is one of the most popular street foods of Uttar Pradesh.
Try Kebabs, Sweet dishes like Malaiyo, Paan, Sheermal, shahi Tukda, Phirni, etc to tickle your taste buds with the richness of Uttar Pradesh.

blocks.text: Shop for the Famous Handicrafts & Souvenirs

Uttar Pradesh is very famous for its rich handicrafts and souvenir items. Through their craftsmanship Uttar Pradesh tells centuries old stories behind each craft and artistic traditions associated with it. Here are some of the best things for shopping at Uttar Pradesh :

items: Look for Banarasi Saree and Brocades . Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its high quality Banarasi Sari with gold and silver Zari work.
Lucknow Chikankari - It is a must not miss in Uttar Pradesh. You will get finest hand embroidered designs crafted on cotton, muslin kurtas and dupattas.
Your trip to Uttar Pradesh will be incomplete without trying Kannauj Attar . The perfumes are crafted with regional flowers and herbs.
Look for the best Meenakari jewelleries . The ornate enamel and gemstones will take your breath away.

blocks.text: Sikkim, nestled in the lap of the Himalayas, is a small yet captivating state in northeastern India. Sikkim tour packages offer a unique opportunity to explore this hidden gem, known for its breathtaking landscapes, vibrant Buddhist culture, and adventure activities.

One of the major attractions in Sikkim is its stunning natural beauty. The state is adorned with snow-capped mountains, lush green valleys, cascading waterfalls, and serene lakes. The mighty Kanchenjunga, the third highest peak in the world, dominates the skyline and offers a mesmerizing backdrop for travellers. Popular destinations like Gangtok, Pelling, and Lachung provide access to these picturesque landscapes and serve as gateways to explore the beauty of the region.

Sikkim is also renowned for its Buddhist monasteries and spiritual sites. The Rumtek Monastery, one of the largest and most significant monasteries in Sikkim, attracts visitors with its intricate architecture and serene atmosphere. The Enchey Monastery, Pemayangtse Monastery, and Tashiding Monastery are other notable places of religious and cultural importance.

Adventure enthusiasts will find plenty of opportunities in Sikkim. Trekking in the Himalayas is a popular activity, with options ranging from the famous Kanchenjunga Base Camp Trek to the shorter Dzongri Trek. River rafting, paragliding, and mountain biking are also available for those seeking an adrenaline rush.

Sikkim’s rich cultural heritage is deeply rooted in its Buddhist traditions. The state celebrates several festivals, including Losar, Saga Dawa, and Bumchu, which offer a glimpse into the vibrant local culture. Travellers can witness traditional dance performances, participate in rituals, and savour authentic Sikkimese cuisine during these festivals.

Sikkim tour packages provide an unforgettable experience of exploring pristine natural landscapes, immersing in Buddhist spirituality, and enjoying thrilling adventure activities. Whether you seek tranquillity amidst the mountains, cultural immersion, or adrenaline-pumping adventures, Sikkim has something to offer for every traveller.

blocks.text: Best Time to Visit Madhya Pradesh

The best time to visit Madhya Pradesh is during the winter season - October to March , as the weather is mostly cool (8°C to 25°C) and pleasant during this time - ideal for sightseeing, pilgrimage, and spotting wildlife. Moreover, if you come during this period, you can enjoy the live celebrations of festivals like the Khajuraho Dance Festival (February) and the Tansen Music Festival (December).

Another great time for the Madhya Pradesh trip is during the monsoon - July to September. Tourists come here to take in the views of lush green landscapes and hill stations (like Pachmarhi) whose beauty grows exponentially at this time. Also, don't miss out on nature gems like waterfalls (especially Dhuandhar Falls) which are in their full flow then!
Best Places to See on the Madhya Pradesh Tour

Madhya Pradesh is a unique mix of culture, architecture, wildlife, and spirituality. In a nutshell, you won't go back home disappointed, as the heart of India has something for everyone! Here are some of the best tourist places in Madhya Pradesh :
Khajuraho Group of Monuments (UNESCO World Heritage Site)

Khajuraho must be added to your Madhya Pradesh trip packages for it's a stunning collection of 22 temples! Tourists especially admire the exotic erotic art here which is one of its kind in the world. Moreover, it is a vibrant setting for an annual dance festival , cultural performance s, Light and sound show , and much more! It's the perfect place to get to know India's rich heritage and culture.

Close to Katni, Bandhavgarh is another nature park and Tiger Reserve to visit. If you are lucky you might spot a tiger which is likely as the tiger density is quite high here . And Madhya Pradesh is rightly called the 'land of tigers' due to this reason! Also, there are plenty of other animals to look for (Indian Wild Dog, Sloth Bear, Striped Hyena, Sambar Deer, Hanuman Langur, and more!). Many tourists add ju ngle safaris to their Madhya Pradesh tour plan, which are available through both jeep and canter.

Sanchi in Raisen is the go-to place for Buddhists! From attending Buddhist festivals and guided tours to Buddhist monasteries to marvelling at the Ashoka Pillar and exquisite art, Sanchi is simply a hub for Buddhist architecture and culture. Moreover, the place attracts history enthusiasts as well for it's one of the oldest structures in the entire country!

Gwalior is yet another city one must visit on their Madhya Pradesh trip. The seat of power of Scindias was once home to the Rajput Rulers. Immersed deep in history, you'll frequently find here majestic palaces and forts which are truly mindblowing! Gwalior Fort, the tomb of Tansen, Jai Vilas Palace, Scindia Museum, and Man Singh Palace visits give you a glimpse into the royal and glorious past of Madhya Pradesh. If you happen to come here during the Tansen Music Festival (December), you get to enjoy the ethereal classical music.

Orchha is a picturesque town situated on the banks of the Betwa. The Fort and palace here are just astounding! Boating on the river is something you'll find tourists actively engaging in. Also, do add Jahangir Mahal, Ram Raja Temple, Orchha Fort, and Chaturbhuj Temple to your Madhya Pradesh holiday packages.

Welcome to the city of temples! Ujjain is a stronghold of Lord Shiva and most of the temples here are dedicated to him! It also houses the Mahakaleshwar temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas . In addition, Ujjain is the place where the Kumbh Mela takes place, and no wonder it's one of the seven sacred cities for Hindus! You'll see people enjoying evening Aarti at the Ghats, Darshan at Kal Bhairav Temple, and soaking in serenity at Ram Ghat! Book our Madhya Pradesh Jyotirlinga tour and enjoy a spiritual trip to this holy city!

This is the capital city and you'll find here an amazing combination of modernity and historical charm. Bhopal also gives a glimpse into Muslim culture which is evident in the Taj-ul-Masajid, Moti Masjid, Jama Masjid, and Shaukat Mahal. Explore museums, go boating, and savour that delicious Mughlai cuisine - you're in for a treat in Bhopal.
Top Things to Do on the Madhya Pradesh Trip

Madhya Pradesh has a lot in store for you once you step on its soil. From nature lovers and adventure seekers to spiritual tourists and history buffs, there's something for everyone here! To make the most out of your experience, make sure to add the following activities to your Madhya Pradesh holiday packages:

rows: Here, you can see beautifully carved gateways that will transport you right back to ancient times. Moreover, it's the perfect place where you can learn about Emperor Ashoka's contribution to Buddhism.

Come and marvel at the architectural brilliance of the intricately carved temples and erotic sculptures here. Witness the bygone era's glory depicted through carved scenes of love, life, and spirituality. It's one of the most popular Madhya Pradesh tourist spot.
End your heritage tour by witnessing prehistoric cave paintings that are over 30,000 years old! Get up and close with marvels of the Stone Age, witnessing some very early-stage human creativity.

This is one of the best Madhya Pradesh wildlife sanctuaries. Hop on jeeps and go for an adventure-filled safari - spotting Bengal tigers, swamp deer (barasinghas), and a variety of bird species. One fun fact about this park is that it served as the inspiration for Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book !
This is a must-visit on your Madhya Pradesh wildlife & heritage tours if you are a wildlife enthusiast as this park has a very high density of tigers. So spotting one isn't too hard here!
Explore this lush forest for its variety of fauna and witness leopards, wild boars, and bison up close.
One among the 12 Jyotirlingas, this temple hosts a grand Aarti which is a must-watch.
Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Temple is another Jyotirlinga and therefore warrants a visit! Moreover, tourists also enjoy a serene boat ride on the Narmada around here.
You have to visit the location which is known as "Teerthraj"! You can explore various locations here, like Narmada Kund, an ancient temple, and even the origins of the holy river Narmada herself!
Whether it's the mighty Gwalior Fort, the fancy Sas-Bahu Temples, or the classic Jai Vilas Palace Museum, every spot here is immersed deep in royal heritage.

Steeped in Mughal and Rajput architecture, Orchha was once a stronghold of Rajput kings. You haven't seen Madhya Pradesh until you have seen the gems like Orchha Fort complex, Chaturbhuj Temple, and Cenotaphs!

Come watch Mandu for its romantic ruins and architectural spectacle! Get enchanted by Rani Roopmati Pavilion, bowled over by Jahaz Mahal, or just be proud to be on the same land as Baz Bahadur's Palace, the choice is yours!

Q1: How to plan Madhya Pradesh tour?
Ans. Planning for Madhya Pradesh gets easier once you decide your preferences, time to spend on destinations, and the best season. Here's a quick guide:

items: Determine which locations you want to travel to, whether historic, wildlife hotspots, adventurous spots, places with cultural importance, or a mix of them all!
Decide the time you want to visit here. Typically, tourists come here during the winter months as the weather is nice and sightseeing is pleasant.
Pick a duration for your trip. Most tourists cover all major attractions within 3-7 days.
Plan transportation - whether you can come via air, rail, or road.
Book accommodation in advance to avoid hassles.
Set a budget - low-cost options to luxury travel!

blocks.text: Q2: How many days are required for the Madhya Pradesh trip?
Ans. Usually, 7-10 days are sufficient to cover key attractions of the state such as Bhopal, Sanchi, Pachmarhi, Khajuraho, Bandhavgarh, and Ujjain.
Q3: What should I pack for the Madhya Pradesh tour?

Ans. If you're visiting in winter, pack cotton clothes for summer. Having comfortable walking shoes is a must as they come in handy during safaris and heritage site exploration. Also, add sunscreens, hats, and insect repellent.
Q4: When is the best time for a wildlife safari on Madhya Pradesh trip?

Ans. The best safari time is from October to March. However, April to June is when the tigers become highly frequent. So plan your travel as per your preferences and what you want most out of this trip.
Q5: What are some hidden gems in Madhya Pradesh?

items: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters (popular for prehistoric rock art)
Tamia: (a nice scenic, secluded hill station)
Chitrakoot (a historical town closely linked to Ramayana)

blocks.text: Q6. What are the best tourist places in Madhya Pradesh?

Ans. If you're a tourist to Madhya Pradesh, make sure you add the following to your itinerary to make the most out of your trip: Khajuraho, Ujjain, Bhopal, Indore, Gwalior, Pachmarhi, Kanha National Park, Bandhavgarh National Park, and Sanchi.
Q7. What is included in the Madhya Pradesh tour package?
Ans. With our MP tour packages, you get accommodation, meals, local transfers, and sightseeing.
Q8. Can the Madhya Pradesh tour package be customised?
Ans. Yes, our packages are fully customizable. You can change the trip duration, add sightseeing stopovers, and pick the vehicle of your choice.
Q9. Is Madhya Pradesh safe for tourists?
Ans. Yes, Madhya Pradesh is quite safe for travellers. However, tourists must exercise precaution. Be wary of pickpockets, especially in the crowded markets. Also, avoid going out late at night.
Q10. What kind of accommodation is available in Madhya Pradesh?

Ans. The state of Madhya Pradesh offers a range of hotels, ranging from budget hotels to luxury resorts. You can also get heritage hotels and guesthouses here. If you're near national parks, you can also stay in jungle lodges
Q11. How much does a Madhya Pradesh tour package cost?
Ans. Our MP tour packages start from INR 6,500 and go up to INR 34,500. These plans vary in sightseeing inclusions, duration, and budget. Pick what suits you best.
Q12. What local foods should I try in Madhya Pradesh?
Ans. While in MP, don't miss finger-licking good Poha-Jalebi, Dal Bafla, Bhutte ka Kees, and Kebabs. Street food is equally good, with options like Indore's famous Sarafa Bazaar.
Q13. What are some of the best hill stations in Madhya Pradesh?

Ans. You can visit Pachmarhi, which is quite a popular hill station in the entire state. There are also other options like Tamia and Amarkantak, which are famous for their scenic and peaceful environments.
Q14. Is Madhya Pradesh a good destination for a honeymoon?
Ans. Yes, MP is quite a nice place for going on a honeymoon. You can indulge in romantic stays at heritage hotels, enjoy the Pachmarhi hill station, and stay in luxe wildlife resorts.
Q15. What adventure activities can I try in Madhya Pradesh?
Ans. You can go for a wildlife safari in national parks. There is a good opportunity for trekking in Pachmarhi. You can also try boating and camping in Bhedaghat and Satpura respectively.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth going to the Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the Golden Triangle is worth visiting because it includes 3 popular cities like Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur, where you will explore amazing sights and it's a great way to experience India’s rich culture and history in a short trip.

mainEntity.name: What adventure activities visitors should try on a Delhi tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Delhi, visitors can try many adventure activities, like hot air balloon rides for a unique view of the city. In Gurgaon, rock climbing in the Aravalli hills is also a perfect option. Apart from this, bungee Jumping at Adventure Island in Rohini is also the best part to enjoy.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to visit the Golden Triangle Tour?

acceptedAnswer.text: The perfect time is between October to March when the climate is cooler and more pleasant.

mainEntity.name: What are the other best places to explore in Jaipur?

acceptedAnswer.text: Travelers must explore Panna Meena Ka Kund due to its beautiful well with unique architecture and a peaceful atmosphere. Moti Dungri Fort is also nice and a small fort with lovely views of Jaipur which is rarely crowded.

mainEntity.name: What Is The Golden Triangle’s Significance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The national capital, New Delhi, and the cities of Agra and Jaipur are connected by a tourist route known as the “golden triangle” of India. The three states of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan make a triangular shape on a map, hence the moniker “Golden Triangle.”

mainEntity.name: When Is The Ideal Time Of Year To Visit The Golden Triangle In India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Since there will be a lot of walking involved, the best time to visit the Golden Triangle is from October to mid-April, when temperatures vary from 22 to 32 °C. Delhi may endure frigid spells in January and February and hot 45°C temperatures in May and June as a result of the Himalayan influence.

mainEntity.name: Why Is The Golden Triangle In India Called That?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Golden Triangle got its name because gold was originally stored here. Gold was used for more than only transporting goods to Delhi and Agra; it was also used to make ornaments and coins, among other things.

mainEntity.name: .Is A Trip To The Golden Triangle Worthwhile?

acceptedAnswer.text: This area of history-rich jungle and foggy mountains is well-known for its history of opium cultivation. Even though the Golden Triangle is a well-known tourist site nowadays, it is still highly recommended.

mainEntity.name: .How Many Days Would You Need In India’s Golden Triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: When Can You See the Golden Triangle? Most visitors decide to travel the entire Golden Triangle in three to seven days, but I strongly advise at least a week.

And just when you think your trip can’t get any better, we’ll take you to the best wildlife adventure. Enter Kaziranga National Park , a place that boasts of a high density of tigers and the endangered one-horned rhinoceros! Enjoy elephant safaris, jeep safaris, or both – you’re in for the time of your life. Moreover, the stunning Orchid Park here will give you enough photo ops to flaunt the pictures on your stories! By the way, our well-crafted itineraries are ideal for a trip down here and see the best of the best that this place has to offer. Wait no more, call us now and set out on this one-of-a-kind trip!
