blocks.text: FAQs - Frequently Asked Questions See More
Q1. Which month is Kaziranga closed?

Ans. Kaziranga National Park is closed during the monsoon season, which is from May to October. This is primarily due to the heavy rainfall (and consequently floods) that the region receives in this time frame. The park resumes operation in November.
Q2. Which month is better to visit Assam?

Ans. The best time to visit the state of Assam is in winter. The months of November to February mark the best time to come here, as they offer the most pleasant atmosphere with clear skies. The wintery charm is just a cherry on top! You can comfortably go on safaris and other sightseeing at this time.
Q3. What is Majuli famous for?

Ans. Majuli is famous for preserving Assamese art & culture in its monasteries, Vaishnavite Satras, and tribal culture. Moreover, its serene environment is another popular thing about the island that draws tourists in.
Q4. What is the time of the Ferry from Majuli to Jorhat?
Ans. Ferries between Majuli and Jorhat start running in the morning at 7:00 AM and continue until 4 in the evening.
Q5. How long is the Majuli ferry ride?
Ans. The ferry ride from Jorhat to Majuli takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. The duration can change depending on the season and the water levels.
Q6. Is This a Private Tour?
Ans. Yes, this tour is private. No other travelers will join your group, ensuring a personalized experience just for you group.
Q7. Can the Driver speak Hindi or English?

Ans. The Drivers can speak in Hindi and Regional Language. Our drivers understand basic English phrases, which should be sufficient for regular communication during the tour. We also provide complimentary city guides in major cities. However, if you prefer a fluent English-speaking driver, we recommend booking a professional guide to ensure smooth communication. Additionally, we offer guides fluent in languages such as French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Russian, and German, available at an extra cost. Please inform us in advance or mention it in the special remarks section while booking the tour online
Q8. How can I get help with my booking?
Ans. You can message one of our live chat teams using the chat with us’ button on the right of the screen, when available.
Q9. Does the Driver Know All the Attractions and Places for Sightseeing?
Ans. Yes, all our drivers are well-versed in the entire region and are knowledgeable about all the attractions and places of interest.
Q10. Will the Taxi and Driver be with us always?
Ans. Yes, the Taxi and Driver will be at your Service from the Start till the End of the Tour.
Q11. Can I Use the Car After 8 PM?

Ans. It depends on the specific tour, but generally, we do not allow the taxi and driver to be on duty after 8 PM. This is to ensure that the driver gets adequate rest and is ready for the next day's activities.
Q12. Does the Taxi Have Roof Carriers for Luggage?

Ans. Only the Ertiga and Innova Crysta vehicles are equipped with roof carriers for luggage. Sedans and Tempo Travelers do not have roof carriers. If you require a vehicle with a roof carrier, please make a special remark during your booking.
Q13. How Can I Rely on Your Company?

Ans. Our company, has been in operation for 15 years and is recognized by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, as well as other state tourism departments. We are an approved travel company with accreditations from IATA, IATO, ABTO, and more. We have built a strong reputation and have successfully served over 100,000 tourists, ensuring reliability and quality service.
Q14. Will Someone Be Available for Assistance While I Am on Tour with You?

Ans. Yes, we will be available to answer any questions or address any concerns you may have during your tour. You can reach out to us at any time. We are committed to providing the best possible service and ensuring our guests have memorable vacations they will cherish forever.
Q15. Why Should I Book with You Instead of Other Travel Companies in the Market?

Ans. We differentiate ourselves from other travel companies through our commitment to personalized service, local expertise, and customer satisfaction. Our team goes above and beyond to understand your travel preferences and provide tailored recommendations. With years of experience and numerous industry accreditations, we ensure that you receive the best possible experience at competitive rates. We are dedicated to making your journey memorable and stress-free.
Q16. Can I Modify or Cancel My Booking?

Ans. Yes, you can modify or cancel your booking. However, it depends on how many days in advance you notify us. Cancellation charges may apply, so please contact us as soon as possible to discuss your options.
Q17. How Do I Make a Booking on Your Website?

Ans. There is no specified time duration for stops at each landmark. Since this is a private tour, you have the freedom to spend as much time as you wish at each location. You can also shorten the tour by skipping certain places or making quick visits.
Q19. Can I Make Customizations on the Tour?

Ans. Yes, since this is a private tour, customizations are possible based on your arrival/departure times, duration of stay, and personal interests. Feel free to reach out to your travel expert to discuss your specific needs.

blocks.text: Best Time To Visit Himachal Pradesh

Himachal Pradesh is a best travel destination for all seasons. Your visit depends on the choice of activities you want to enjoy and places you want to cover. Ideally, March to June is the best time to travel to Himachal Pradesh . Here is a detailed overview of the best time to visit Himachal Pradesh

items: It is the best time to enjoy sightseeing of all the popular places of Himachal Pradesh. The weather is pleasant to enjoy the best Hill station tours as well as honeymoon tours in the mountains.
You can enjoy trekking, camping, paragliding, mountain biking in famous hill stations like Shimla, Manali and Dharamshala etc.
Festivals - Shimla Summer Festival, Sipi Fair, Minjar Festival, Shoolini Fair

It is the best time to enjoy a romantic honeymoon in Himachal Pradesh. Those who love winter will get mesmerized by the beauty of snow in various places of Himachal Pradesh. You can also enjoy trekking, snow related adventures in Manali, Kufri and Solan Valley.
During this time, you can also enjoy Bonfires & village stays. Many homestays and resorts in Himachal offer soothing bonfires, local food tasting, music nights and village walks etc.
Festivals - Halda Festival (Lahaul and Spiti), Losar Festival, Winter Carnival (Manali), Christmas, New Year.
It is also the best time to enjoy a sightseeing tour with family in Himachal Pradesh. You can also enjoy wildlife safari at Great Himalayan National Park and Renuka Wildlife Sanctuary.
Enjoy trekking to Pin Parvati, Triund, Hampta Pass, and the Great Himalayan National Park routes.
Try adventure activities like paragliding in Bir Billing and river rafting in Beas River.
Festival- Sazo Fair, Mandi Shivratri Fair, Kullu Dussehra, Hemis Festival, Diwali
If you want to enjoy lush greenery, cascading waterfalls and less crowd than Visit Himachal Pradesh in Monsoon.
Heavy rains and landslides may disturb your travel schedule but if you are tolerant of minor disruptions then you can enjoy the best monsoon views of Himachal Pradesh.
You can explore Jibhi, Tirthan Valley, McLeod Ganj, Kanatal and Chakrata and Chamba in Monsoon.
Festivals -Suketi Fair, Kanwar Yatra, Baisakhi Festival.

blocks.text: Best Places To Visit in Himachal Pradesh

In 2025, Himachal Pradesh welcomed around 9.99 million domestic tourists from all over India and 55,000 foreign tourists by September 2025, which shows it is one of the most visited tourist destinations in India. It is showing potential for growth for foreign tourists' arrivals. (Source- Amar Ujala ) Here are some of the best places covered in our Himachal Pradesh Travel Packages -

items: Explore the beauty of Shimla . It is one of the most visited tourist destinations in Himachal Pradesh.
Enjoy the colonial charm, scenic Mall Road, iconic ridge area. Explore some famous places in Shimla like Jakhu Temple, Kufri and Christ Church.
It is also the best place to try skiing and snowboarding, trekking, paragliding and camping etc.
Manali is best known for thrilling mountain adventures and fairytale-like setting. You must try skiing, river rafting, paragliding and trekking.
Explore famous tourist hotspots in Manali like Hadimba Devi Temple, old Manali village and hot springs at Vashisht.

Located near Manali, the beauty of this high- altitude mountain pass will take your breath away. It is also one of the best places for photography of the stunning snow-capped mountains and icy glaciers.
Enjoy adventure activities like trekking, skiing, mountain biking and snow scooter rides here. Rohtang Pass remains open from June to October. It is closed every Tuesday for maintenance.
Rich cultural heritage, natural beauty and spiritual vibes, Kangra Valley is a perfect blend of all and it is a must visit destination in Himachal Pradesh.
It is a perfect destination for travellers with varied interests. You can enjoy paragliding in Bir Billing and witness the beauty of Dhauladhar ranges.
Explore all the heritage places like Kangra Fort, Masroor Rock Cut Temples, Baijnath Temple and Kareri Lake.
Dharamshala and Mcleodganj are must not miss scenic hill stations in Himachal Pradesh. It is renowned for its Tibetan culture and spiritual significance for Buddhists and Hindus.
Dharamshala, winter capital of Himachal is famous for its lush greenery, pristine tea gardens and HPCA stadium which hosts IPL matches.
Mcleodganj is also known as 'Little Lhasa'. It is a residence of the 14th Dalai Lama and a center for Tibetan Buddhism.
Explore Kalachakra Temple, Bhagsunath Temple and Waterfall, Triund Trek base, Naddi View Point, and the serene Dal Lake.
Renowned as 'Valley of Gods' Kullu is a serene escape for travellers who want to enrich their mind by exploring the culturally rich region of Himachal Pradesh.
Explore the beautiful lush green valleys, scenic apple orchards, flowing Beas River and enjoy thrilling river rafting, trekking, hiking, mountain climbing, paragliding, and camping.
Explore Raghunath Temple, Bijli Mahadev Temple, Basheshwar Mahadev Temple, Manikaran, Naggar Castle and Parvati Valley.

blocks.text: Try River Rafting In Beas And Satluj Rivers

items: In Himachal, river rafting is one of the best adventure activities to do. The beauty of white water can be found nowhere else. Imagine doing river rafting in white water with waves which travel through the Himalayan Mountain terrains. Isn't it scenic and thrilling at the same time.
April to June is the best time to enjoy white water rafting. If you want exciting rapids then try it in September to early October.

blocks.text: Scenic Trekking Trails of Himachal Pradesh

items: If you are planning your vacation in Himachal Pradesh then trekking is an activity you must not miss. Himachal has some of the most beautiful trekking trails which are perfect for beginners as well as seasoned trekkers.
Try Triund, Hampta Pass, Pin Parvati, Kheerganga Trek and the Great Himalayan National Park trails for the best thrilling experience.
Himachal has India's only open- air natural ice-skating rink near Ridge area in Shimla. The charming rink is a beautiful place to try ice- skating.
Skate rentals and coaching for skating is available on site for assistance. December to February is the best time to enjoy this activity in Shimla.

Himachal Pradesh is accessible by road. There is 8 National highways and 19 State highways. You will get government or private buses from Delhi, Pathankot or Chandigarh. You will enjoy scenic views if you prefer traveling by road.
Kalka, Shimla (via Kalka-Shimla Toy Train), Pathankot-Joginder Nagar, Una

items: Every travel mode for Himachal Pradesh is reliable and offers a comfortable journey. There are mainly three domestic airports (Shimla, Kullu, Kangra) but the access is limited only to major regions. Chandigarh Airport is the nearest airport to Shimla.

It is not difficult to travel by road in Himachal Pradesh. We offer best transportation services which include transfer, pick up and drop services through our Himachal Pradesh tour packages. You will get frequent bus service from Delhi, Chandigarh, Pathankot. HRTC also operates Volvos and deluxe buses to travel for tourists.

If you are choosing train mode for Himachal Pradesh then most of your trip will involve a short bus or taxi ride from nearest railheads. The train connectivity is limited. blocks.text: Useful Travel Tips For A Memorable Trip In Himachal Pradesh

items: Best Time to Visit - Every season in Himachal Pradesh has its own charm. So, choose the best time according to your preferred activities. Choose March to June if you want to enjoy family holidays in Himachal Pradesh and October-February for cozy stays, snow and adventure activities.

What to Pack- Pack weather specific items for a comfortable journey in Himachal. For summers- pack light clothes and light jackets. For winters- layered woolens, thermals and heavy jackets are very important to pack.
Keep Documents Safe- Carry comfortable footwear and an anti-theft bag to keep important documents and cash.
Licensed Operators - You should hire only licensed guides and adventure operators for safety for enjoying trekking, rafting or paragliding etc.
Enough Cash- Carry enough cash with you as in most places ATM might not work or due to weak internet digital payments options might not be accessible.
Dress Code- Respect the local customs of the temples and places. Wear covered clothes while exploring any sacred site.
Responsible Tourists -Avoid plastic items, don't litter anywhere. Be a responsible tourist. It's our responsibility to keep the beauty of Himachal Pradesh intact.

Ujjain has a lot to offer visitors. Whether it's the delicious local cuisine, important Jyotirlingas, or magnificent monuments, you're sure to see and experience a lot here. With this Mumbai to Ujjain trip, you can enjoy culture, spirituality, and history in one go. So wait no more, pack your bags, and get ready for a one-of-a-kind adventure!
Best Time to Visit Ujjain from Mumbai

The best time to visit Ujjain is hands down in the winter months of October to March. The weather is pleasant for the most part and therefore makes for an excellent time for sightseeing and temple tours. If you come here in February/March, you can also witness the Mahashivratri festival that is celebrated with great grandeur at the Mahakaleshwar Temple.
We also advise against booking your Ujjain Omkareshwar Maheshwar Tour from Mumbai in the monsoon period, as too much rainfall can mar your experience.
The Mumbai to Ujjain path takes the following route map:
Mumbai → Thane → Nashik → Dhule → Indore → Ujjain
The distance between Mumbai and Ujjain is about 650 km, and you can reach here via NH 48 and NH 52. Moreover, the highways are in good condition and make for a scenic drive.
How to Reach Ujjain from Mumbai?
There are a variety of ways via which you can reach Ujjain from Mumbai:
By Air : The nearest airport to Ujjain is Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, located in Indore. It's about 55 km away from the city, from where you can easily hire a cab or taxi to reach Ujjain.

By Train : Luckily, there are several direct trains that run between the two cities. You can hop on any of the following: Avantika Express, Mumbai -- Indore Express, and Mumbai -- Ujjain Express to comfortably reach Ujjain. The journey takes around 10 hours and is ideal for travelling with family or when you're going on a group tour.

By Road : The road journey is quite long and easily takes 10-11 hours of your time. You can use the NH 48 and NH 52, and reach there via Nashik. You can also book our Mumbai to Ujjain road package to easily and comfortably reach the holy city.

blocks.text: Places To Visit On Your Trip To Tamil Nadu
Our signature Tamil Nadu Trip Packages cover some of the most popular as well as hidden gems in Tamil Nadu. Let dive into details-
Kodumbalur Moovar Koil- Offbeat and Sacred Gem

items: It is an ancient temple complex of three Shiva Temples which dates back to the 9th century.

If you are interested in Chola architecture then it is a must visit temple as it is one of the oldest surviving temples of that period. The temple was built by Boodhi Vikrama Kesari of Irukkuvel Clan.
Located in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, The Meenakshi Amman Temple is a place where stories come to life. It has 14 spectacular Gopurams covered in thousands of colorful stucco figures.
The temple is dedicated to goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar. The temple was built by the Pandya dynasty.
In the 14th century, Meenakshi Amman Temple was invaded and looted by Malik Kafur but later the temple was renovated by Nayak rulers in the 17th century.
Mahabalipuram has exquisite ancient temples to captivate tourists from all over the world. Its rock cut temple architecture is so sublime as if it is breathed into being by gods.
Witness the beautiful monolithic bas reliefs, legendary Shore Temple, the iconic Pancha Rathas and Arjuna’s Penance.
It is also the best place to learn about ancient sculpting techniques and stone carving.

The Pamban Island of Tamil Nadu is sacred as it is nourished by a sacred pilgrimage place called Rameswaram. It is in the top list of the best places included in our Tamil Nadu Spiritual Package Tours.

It is also a famous Chardham pilgrimage site. Devotees from all across the globe come to Rameswaram to visit Ramanathaswamy Temple and offer their prayers to Lord Shiva. It is believed that the Shivling in the temple was constructed by Devi Sita to help him offer his prayers to atone for his sin of killing Ravana.
It also houses 22 holy water Theerthams (sacred water bodies) which have healing properties. A holy dip is believed to dissolve the sins and karmic backlog of devotees.

blocks.text: Kodaikanal - Scenic Hill Station in Tamil Nadu

items: Don’t forget to explore the “Princess of hill Stations”. It is one of the best hill stations to enjoy peaceful vacations with your family in Tamil Nadu. Nature lovers and solace seekers often pick this place for recreation.
It’s a perfect place for a relaxing family vacation in Tamil Nadu. Here, enjoys boating, cycling, photography of breathtaking plains and valleys, birdwatching and soothing nature walks.
Pondicherry is also known as Puducherry. It is a scenic coastal town which offers relaxing beach getaways in Tamil Nadu.
It is also a French colonial heritage town. There are many well- maintained colonial heritage buildings and French style cafes to explore.
Visit Auroville for peace, Promenade beach for leisure strolls, Puducherry Museum to witness traditional crafts.
Explore French bakeries such as Baker Street, Zuka and Bouche Sucree and try various French pastries and delicacies.

The vibrant Metropolis Chennai will captivate your heart and mind. It offers a perfect blend of history, culture and nature. Chennai is renowned for its traditional arts, music and dance forms. If you are here, you must watch Bharatnatyam Dance performances.
Chennai also houses many serene eco-parks like Semmozhi Poonga which houses around 500 exotic plants. Here you can enjoy fun-filled picnics, nature walks with your family.
You can also explore Snow Kingdom which is one of the largest indoor snow centers to enjoy snow and snow related fun activities in any season.

blocks.text: Top Things to Do on Your Trip in Tamil Nadu

Tamil Nadu is a place where no tourist can feel bored. There is something to do for every kind of traveller. Because it has so much to offer tourists often get confused as to what to do here to have an authentic Tamil Nadu tourism experience. So here is a short list of our top picks of things to do in Tamil Nadu-
Wander at the UNESCO Sites of Mahabalipuram

items: The archeological genius of Mahabalipuram is Mind-boggling. Capture the exquisite shore temple and other exquisite rock cut temple architecture.
Learn about the ancient technique of stone carving from local artisans.

blocks.text: Offer Prayers at the ancient temples of Madurai and Thanjavur

items: Don’t just visit Meenakshi Amman Temple but also stay for a night ceremony where the deities are put to sleep. Witness the sacred rituals like Abhishekam, Alankaram and Deepa Aaradhanai etc.

Offer your prayers to the sacred Brihadeeswarar Temple. The temple houses a famous Bronze Nataraja Statue, displaying Lord Shiva as a cosmic dancer. Here you will also learn a detailed history about the Chola Empire through inscriptions and murals in the temple complex.

blocks.text: Recreation at the Hill Stations in Tamil Nadu

items: The cool climate and scenic views of the soothing hill stations of Tamil Nadu such as Yercaud, Kodaikanal, Ooty will delight your soul. Visit any of the scenic hill stations in Tamil Nadu and capture beautiful natural views.

Enjoy trekking in lush green forests, boating at Ooty lake or Kodaikanal Lake or spend quality time with your family at lakeside points. Honeymooners and families often visit Tamil Nadu Hill station Tour Packages to enjoy an unforgettable holiday.
Enjoy Birdwatching at Mudumalai and Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuaries. These popular bird Sanctuaries in Tamil Nadu offer wild escape to nature lovers and bird watchers.
Bring Binoculars and capture unique birds like Darters, Painted Storks and Spot Billed Pelicans etc.

blocks.text: Spiritual Shores of Rameswaram and Kanyakumari

items: Indulge in ritual baths at Rameswaram. It houses 22 sacred Teerthams (holy water bodies) which are believed to dissolve the karmic backlog of devotees.
Explore the beauty of Dhanushkodi beach and ruins. Capture the scenic sunrise and sunset views.

Witness the confluence of Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal and Indian Ocean at Kanyakumari. Visit Kumari Amman Temple dedicated to goddess Parvati. Also visit Adikesava Perumal Temple which is one of the 108 Divya Desams dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

blocks.text: Enjoy a thrilling Wildlife Safari in Tamil Nadu

items: Adventure lovers must try a thrilling wildlife safari in Tamil Nadu. You can book Annamalai Tiger Reserve Safari or visit Kalakad-Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve and Guindy National Park (Chennai).
Spot various animals like Tigers, Nilgiri Langur, Chital, Jackal, blackbucks, Lions, Gaur, Elephants and endemic lion-tailed macaques.

blocks.text: Tamil Nadu Travel Tips for Memorable Holidays with Family

Tamil Nadu is a travel destination which will offer you a perfect blend of cultural, spiritual heritage, scenic hill stations, vibrant cities and beautiful beaches. Here are some useful tips for you to follow for a memorable holiday with your loved ones-

items: If you want to enjoy the best of Tamil Nadu hospitality in general then you should plan your trip in winters - November to February. It is ideal for enjoying outdoor adventures and sightseeing of all the famous destinations.
While planning for temple visits, dress conservatively. You need to wear covered clothes. Carry shawls, stoles and Dupattas to cover your head and shoulders.
Respect the customs and traditions of a place. There is a local custom of folding the banana leaf after eating.
While we offer multilingual guides, it is still better to learn important phrases in Tamil to understand the communication better with locals.
Try to avoid beaches and remote areas after dark and keep your belongings safe. Use anti-theft luggage and bags to keep your belongings and documents safe.
Always carry enough cash for small purchases and temple visits. You may not get online payment facilities at some places.
Carry weather specific clothes for a comfortable Tamil Nadu sightseeing tour.

blocks.text: Q-1: What are some of the must visit places in Tamil Nadu?
Ans: Out of many places in Tamil Nadu, you must see Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai, Sore Temple in Mahabalipuram, Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, Rameswaram, Ooty and Kodaikanal.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit During Odisha Trip

Odisha is one of the best travel destinations in India. We usually hype about the beauty of northern states of India but come to Odisha and you will realize what you are missing. Here is a list of must visit places in Odisha to know its true essence-

Puri, a serene coastal city in Odisha is a soul pleasing tourist destination to fine tune your senses with inner peace, recreation activities and sacred wisdom. This place is a perfect blend of spiritual solace with heritage, culture and nature. Here are some of the most popular places to see in Puri -

items: Lord Jagannath Temple - It’s not wrong to say that Jagannath Puri Dham is the soul of Odisha. Millions of devotees visit Odisha’s Rath yatra just to get one glimpse of the sacred Jagannath Idol. The temple of Lord Jagannath’s divine grace is something which is very difficult to explain in words.

Kuruma Buddhist Site - This site is still under excavation which makes it more beautiful as it takes us back in time. It’s a beautiful place to learn about Buddhist heritage. Locally it is also known as Yama Dharma Pitha. It is one of the most popular heritage places to see in Puri.

Chandrabhaga Sea Beach - Located at the eastern side of the majestic Sun temple of Konark, Chandrabhagha Sea beach is a scenic spot to relax with your loved ones. The endless blue of the ocean is everywhere as far as your eyes can see. Nourish your soul with the pleasing views of the ocean, golden sands and sunrise and sunset.

Sakhigopal Temple, Satyabadi, Puri - Sakigopal Temple is a sanctuary of inner peace. The temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna. The idol of Shri Radha Rani is also present in the temple. During the occasion of Anla Navami, the temple allows devotees to embrace Radha Rani’s feet.

Raghurajpur Handicrafts - Witness the beautiful Pattachitra art which is a very popular art form practiced in this village for decades. Here, every family is engaged in some kind of art form or crafts. You will also see paper Mache products, stone carving art, palm leaf etching, tusser paintings and cow dung toys etc.

Sun Temple Konark - Faith, art and astronomical genius, The Konark Sun Temple is the most beautiful architectural marvel built in the 13th century. The temple is in the shape of a grand chariot with 24 intricately carved stone wheels. Each wheel has precise sundials with eye pleasing carvings on the spokes.

blocks.text: Deogarh is very popular for its natural beauty and cultural richness. It was earlier an integral part of Sambalpur but got its distinct identity in 1994, making it one of the youngest administrative divisions in Odisha. You will be mesmerized to see its beautiful hilly, forested areas and scenic waterfalls. It's nature's bliss.

items: Jagannath Temple Deogarh - It is one of the most popular temples in Deoghar. Here Lord Jagannath, Lord Balarama and Devi Subhadra are the main presiding deities. Like Puri, Jagannath Rath yatra is the main festival of this temple.

Gohira Dam Deogarh - Enjoy the scenic view, listen to the serene silence of nature and spend some fun-filled moments with your family as it’s a great picnic spot. Also get divine blessings from Lord Shiva at the temple situated near the Dam.

Kailash Palace Deogarh - It was built by Raja Dibya Sankar Dev in 1919. It has many scenic natural sights to capture as this place is surrounded by hills and mountains from all sides. It is also one of the top ecotourism spots in Odisha.

Olata Bata, Deogarh - Located 2 km away from Deogarh Bus Stand, Olata Bata is a giant fiscus tree which holds immense religious significance for the people. Its leaves grow in the opposite direction from normal trees which makes it a very unique sight to see.

Jhadeswar Temple - The temple was constructed during the reign of Raja Brajasundar Deb in 1854. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The lingam of Lord Shiva here is not implanted, it’s a Swayambhu (self-manifested form of Lord Shiva).

blocks.text: Lying at the serene confluence of Koel and Sankha rivers, Rourkela sits amidst the hilly terrains, laterite rich red soils bordering scenic forests. It proudly showcases one of India’s largest steel plants which also gave it a nickname- Ispat Nagar (Steel city of India).

items: Ved Vyas - Visit this serene secluded spot at Rourkela for peaceful vibes. It’s a place where Ved Vyas wrote Mahabharata. You will witness the scenic confluence of Koel, Sankha and Saraswati River. It also houses Vedic ashram which is a center of traditional Vedic education, healing practices, Sanskrit studies and religious activities etc.

Hanuman Vatika - It houses the beautiful 75ft tall statue of Lord Hanuman which makes it a must visit place in Odisha. The Vatika was designed by Shri Laxman Swami of Hyderabad in 1994. It is a very popular spot for spiritually inclined people, leisure lovers and solace seekers.

Vaishno Devi Temple - Vaishno Devi Temple in Rourkela is the replica of the original Vaishno Devi Temple of Jammu& Kashmir. It is situated atop the Durgapur Hill. The temple offers scenic views as it is surrounded by dense forests. Also visit Bhairavnath Temple located near Vaishno Devi Temple.

Khandadhar - This stunning waterfall will blow your heart away with its pleasing views. It’s a great spot for nature photography. Khandadhar is also known as Sword waterfall because of its sword-like shape of falling water.

Pitamahal Dam - Don’t miss this scenic recreational spot across Pitamahal river. The river is a tributary of Sankha River which merges with Koel River to form Brahmani River. Enjoy the scenic sunset and boating with your family.

blocks.text: 4- Sambalpur - Where Mahanadi Flows with Culture

Jewel of western Odisha, Sambhalpur is very famous for its natural beauty and handloom crafts especially Sambhalpuri sarees. It is one of the most famous tourist destinations to visit in Odisha. It is also known as the cultural capital of Odisha.

items: Hirakud Dam - It is one of the largest dams in the world built on the scenic Mahanadi River. It is 200ft in height. There is a lake behind the dam which is Hirakud reservoir. It spreads across 746 sq km.

Samaleswari Temple - Samaleswari Temple is located on the serene banks of Mahanadi River. It’s a soul pleasing sight. The presiding deity of the temple is goddess Samaleswari. It is a shakti Pitha which got its mention in the Odia Mahabharata by Adikabi Sarala Das.

Pataneswari Kali Temple - Pataneswari Kali Temple is dedicated to goddess Kali who is considered as the sister of Smaleswari Devi. The temple is also located near the iconic Samaleswari Temple. It was built by Balram Dev, the first Chauhan ruler of Sambhalpur in the 16th century.

Gudguda Waterfall - surrounded by Sal, Pia Sal, Mahul forests and hills Gudguda waterfall is a scenic nature paradise for peace lovers. It is also very famous for Mountain trekking opportunities and weekend picnics.
Huma Temple - You will be stunned to see the famous leaning Shiva Temple. It was built in the reign of the fifth ruler Balilar Singh of Sambhalpur. You can also enjoy boating here at Mahanadi River.

Ramsagar Park - It is one of the best places for nature lovers to visit in Odisha. There are many native trees and plants in this park which makes it the greenest place in Sambhalpur. Enjoy boating and leisure walks at this stunning nature paradise.

blocks.text: 5- Balasore- Sandy Shores and Timeless Stories

Natural wonder and deep history, Balasore captivates the heart of every traveller in Odisha. It’s a scenic place to witness how ancient temples, colonial remnants have shaped Odisha’s glorious past. History buffs and science enthusiasts will surely love Balasore.

items: Bhimkund - Take a deep plunge into mythology at Bhimkund. It’s a scenic spot of freshwater decked with a dramatic gorge. It is believed that this place was created by Bhima of Mahabharata. The waters of Bhimkund are considered holy, devotees who take a holy dip in it get relief from their sins.

Khairachora Gopinatha - The temple is dedicated to Lord Krishna. It is believed that the idol of Lord Krishna was carved by the arrow of Lord Rama for the worship of Devi Sita. It was brought by Langula Narasingha Dev to Balasore from Chitrakut in the 13th century.

Chandaneswar Temple -The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. You will also witness here a black statue of Nandi which is a center of prime attraction. Chadak Mela is one of the main festivals celebrated here. In this festival devotees observe a strict fast by not even swallowing saliva.

Saisura Waterfall - It’s a peaceful nature retreat to visit in Odisha. Perfect for weekend getaways, photography and nature lovers, its beauty never fades. Very few travellers visit Saisura Waterfall which makes it a hidden gem of Odisha.

Chandipur Sea Beach - It is also known as Odisha’s Hide and Seek beach due to the occurrence of a unique phenomenon where the sea water recedes up to 5km during low tide. It happens twice a day. It houses too many marine species like red crabs, sea urchins, starfish etc. You can spend your night at small and large eco camps located near the beach to spend the night with your family and friends.

blocks.text: Capital city of Odisha, Bhuvaneshwar is a must not miss place to make your Odisha Tour memorable. It is a hub of beautiful ancient temples and heritage sites older than 6th century AD. Bhuvaneshwar gives eternal and spiritual vibes as its name is also derived from Tribhuvaneshwari- Lord of the three World (Lord Shiva).

items: Lingraj Temple - It is one of the most famous temples to visit in Bhuvaneshwar. It was built in 11th century AD in Kalinga style of architecture which is a marvelous sight to behold. The presiding deity of this temple is Lord Shiva in his Harihar form.

Udyagiri and Khandagiri Caves - These are beautiful pairs of rock cut cave complexes near Bhuvaneshwar. The complex dates back to 1st and 2nd century BCE. It was built for the meditation and stay purpose of Buddhist monks in the reign of King Kharavela of Kaling.

Nandan Kanan Zoological Park - It’s one of the most famous places for wildlife lovers in Odisha. It is located inside Chandaka Forest in 400 hectares. The most marvelous creature White Tigers are a must not miss here. It is also the first zoo in India to breed white tigers from colored parents.

Odisha State Museum - Founded in 1938, it is a must visit place in Odisha if you are interested in knowing about the heritage and culture of Bhubaneswar and Odisha. This museum houses many artefacts, tools, manuscripts, amours and weapons of the erstwhile rulers of Bhuvanaeshwar. You will also learn about the ruling dynasties of Odisha and Bhuvaneshwar here.

Parsurameswara Temple - It is one of the oldest temples in Bhuvaneshwar dedicated to Lord Shiva who is worshipped as Lord Mukteswara. It was built in Kalinga style of architecture in the reign of Somavanshi dynasty who were great devotees of Lord Shiva.

blocks.text: Top Things to Do on Your Odisha Trip

Odisha is still a hidden gem; it is less explored in terms of other states in India. To truly feel its pulse, we have included some of the very unique experiences in your Odisha itinerary for an unforgettable trip with your family. Here is a list of top things to do in Odisha Tour-
Seek Solace at Puri’s Sacred Sanctuary

items: Embrace the beauty of Sun Temple in Konark Puri
Enjoy the annual Konark Festival. See the magical dance performance at the illuminated temple of Konark.
Feel the sacred bliss at Jagannath Puri Dham and enjoy your day at Puri Beach. Click awesome pictures of scenic views.

blocks.text: Witness the Wild Mangroves of Bhitarkanika

items: Bhitarkanika mangroves is the second largest mangrove ecosystem, famous for its rich biodiversity and natural beauty.
Enjoy scenic boat rides through narrow creeks and canals from the famous route of Khola to Dangmal.
Spot different species of Kingfishers, eagles and migratory birds.
Embrace some of the hidden gems of Odisha. The raw beauty of Odisha’s coastlines will take your breath away.
Explore the scenic Chandrabhagha Beach and see the unique phenomena of receding water during the low tides.
See Olive Ridley Turtles residing peacefully at Rushikulya or Gahimatha Beaches.

blocks.text: Try different traditional cuisines in Odisha and treat your soul with wholesomeness. Here are some of the famous dishes to try in Odisha-

items: Pakhala Bhata - It’s one of the most famous dishes to taste in Odisha. It’s a comfort food of Odisha made with love in every household. It is a fermented rice served with curries, fried fish, or green chilies etc.

Chenna Poda - It’s a sweet gift of Odisha to the world. Try this tasty caramelized cheesecake called Chenna Poda in Odisha. It has a caramelized crust on the outside and from inside it is soft and chewy.
Dalma - Try Dalma, a wholesome dish of lentils and vegetables cooked with seasonal spices. It’s a comfort dish in every Odia household.
Kanika Bhat - If you are in Odisha, you must not miss Kanika Bhat. It is a sweet rice made of resins, ghee, and cashews. It is served in temples or on special occasions.
Chenna Jhili - You must try these sweet deep fried cheese balls dipped in sugar syrup. It’s a local favorite sweet dish in Odisha.

blocks.text: Himachal is the land of Gods and a beautiful paradise for touring and for adventure activities in India. It is not that India lacks in attractions. From the sandy stretches of Rajasthan to lush green rainforests of the Northeast and the cold Himalayan ranges to the warm backwaters of Kerala, there is everything one could wish for. Passionate adventure seekers have plenty to explore in India. Adventure tour packages India are specially designed to give one the much sought-after thrill.

Manali is a perfect resort for relaxing and for spending a weekend. It is also perfect for adventure sports such as white water rafting, paragliding, skiing, trekking along mountain trails and fishing. The entire valley is scenic and Kullu is especially beautiful. If trekking is what you like then the Malana village trek is one you should undertake. Just 21 km from Manali, this is a picture postcard destination with mountains, trees, and clouds to make your day. You can just as well go on the Bara Banghal and Bir Trek, the Hampta Herbal Trek or the Hampta pass trek. However, the Jogini waterfall trek is one you should not miss.

Leh and Spiti are altogether different. These destinations are for the hardy who can withstand rigors and challenges of this inhospitable region of wild beauty. Located in the north-east of Himachal, Spiti is slightly easier than Leh, a place where you can go mountain biking or hike leisurely without worrying about crowds.

However, if mountains and steep trails are not your things and you love warm and breezy coastal areas then Goa in the West, Kovalam in Kerala, Diu on the West Coast in Kutch and Orissa have lovely beaches where you can relax, go snorkeling or riding on a boat and enjoy yourself. You could take it a step higher by going on to Andaman and Nicobar Island where adventure sports like snorkeling and scuba diving will thrill you. Of course, these activities are also available on the lovely beaches of Goa. You can easily find adventure tour packages India based taking you to these places.

Trekking in nature parks is enjoyable. There are well-beaten trails one can follow and luxuriate in the diversity of nature. Jim Corbett National park in the North and the Periyar sanctuary in Kerala offer a relaxed experience. The North-east abounds in National Parks where you can trek amid lush greenery. The Kaziranga National Park in Assam, Manas National Park in Assam, Balpakram National Park in Meghalaya and Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh offer an entirely different trekking experience.
You could go to the heart of India, central India, for trekking and to know more about the land and the people. Join the Bandhavgarh-Kanha experience in Madhya Pradesh or head to Mandu.

If you love water sports and have a penchant for white water rafting then head for the North. The petulant and turbulent rivers in Uttarakhand and Himachal are perfect to enjoy a thrilling experience. Head to Rishikesh and upwards and you have great opportunities for white water rafting. Go farther up to Sikkim and the Teesta River challenges you to take on its might. Zanskar is another place where you can experience the thrill of bobbing along on turbulent waters of the Indus while the Brahmaputra rafting is more sedate experience in the North East of India. It is not that the south lacks in rafting opportunities. Head to Coorg and navigate the Barapole River. Just pick the right adventure tour organizer in India for a customized experience.

If golfing is what you like India has quite a few golf courses to help you indulge your passion. Arrive in Delhi and head to the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurgaon or the Qutab Golf Course in South Delhi. You could join a golfing holiday package tour and sample golf courses from Kolkata to Kerala.

If you love desert sands and vast open skies then you have two choices. One is Rajasthan, a colorful land where you can have your fill of trekking outside places like Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, and Bikaner while getting to know about its royal past by visiting the innumerable palaces and forts. For an out and our experience in the desert head to Kutch and walk along the coast or trek farther inland in the Marine National Park, an all-encompassing experience where you get to see aquatic marine life and birds as well as animals.

Adventure tour packages India is available to suit your taste, be it trekking mountain biking, rafting, paragliding or sailing. India is a spicy mix that changes flavor as you travel from one region to another.

blocks.text: East or West, North or South, India does not lack wildlife sanctuaries and wildlife parks where you can indulge your wish to be at one with nature. India is vast; so you can pick a specific region and go off on a wonderful tour into the reserves to get a firsthand view and experience of the flora and fauna. India Wildlife Tour Packages come with an enticing repertoire of wildlife tours that will make you go into the hearts of forests and explore the exotic wildlife. Kashmir is better known for its breathtaking scenic beauty and you should visit the Dal Lake, Sonmarg, and Gulmarg at least once in your life. While here do not overlook the Dachigam Wildlife Sanctuary. Established in 1910 it has a unique topology comprising meadows, rocky cliffs, and grasslands as well as forests that are home to the Himalayan Black Bear, the brown bear, otters, leopards, deer, and innumerable birds.

Uttarakhand, on the other hand, is the land of gods and pilgrimages but it is also home to the Jim Corbett National Park, one of the largest parks with a wonderful of trees, hills, water bodies, and of course, animals ranging from elephants to deer and leopards to jackals not to speak of birds. There are facilities for accommodation outside the park and plenty of trekking trails inside. So, India Wildlife tour packages can let you explore the most endangered wildlife of the high Himalayas too. Travel eastwards and you will come across several nature parks but Kaziranga is a must-visit national park. Spread over 430 square kilometers, it is home to tigers, elephants, water buffalos, deer, and birds but the main attraction is the rhino. The Northeast also has Manas in Assam.

Go west and you have the choice of Sariska and Ranthambore National Park, home to the tiger and a far different experience from the lush forests of the North-east. Travel a bit south and west and you come to Sasan Gir, home to the last of the Asiatic Lion. From here you can go on to the arid regions of Kutch where the Marine National Park is located, one of the biggest of its kind encompassing drylands, swampy lands, seas, and islands. Go south and you have so many choices that it can be confusing. In Karnataka, you have the Dandeli and BR Hills wildlife sanctuaries, Mudumalai in Tamil Nadu and Periyar as well as Neyyar in Kerala. Whatever direction you choose, each wildlife park presents a different environment and experience. There are custom as well as standard India wildlife tour packages available here, a back-to-nature experience you will cherish.

blocks.text: Best Places to Visit in Rajasthan on Your Trip

Rajasthan has a splendid past of ancient Rajasthan rulers. The ceremonial lifestyle and bravery of royal Rajput families are being reproduced from its heritage and historical destination. In 2025 Rajasthan saw a massive surge in tourist footfall. The state welcomed 37.8 million domestic tourists in just the first two months (January and February) of 2025 which shows that it is one of the most visited tourist destinations in India. ( Source : Rajasthan Tourism. Online ). Mentioned here are the list of the best places to visit in Rajasthan, covered in our Rajasthan tour itinerary.

items: Known as Pink city, Jaipur is one of the top tourist destinations to visit in Rajasthan. Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh, It was one of the earliest planned cities of India. Domestic as well as international travellers cannot resist the charm of Jaipur. It boasts of majestic forts, palaces, and colorful markets which display royal extravagance.
Some of the best places to visit here are Hawa Mahal, Amber Fort, City Palace, Jal Mahal, Johri Bazaar, Bapu Bazaar and Chokhi Dhani.
Dominated by the imposing Fort of Mehrangarh, the blue city of Jodhpur attracts the traveler from far and wide.

Forts, palaces, temples and havelies, its attractions reflect royal splendour. Explore Jaswant Thada, the scenic white marble cenotaph, the majestic Umaid Bhawan Palace, beautiful alleys of Navchowkiya, Turji Ka Jhalra, Mehrangarh Fort, Chamunda Mata Ji Temple etc.

Located at the heart of Thar Desert, Jaisalmer, the golden city will mesmerize you with its awe inspiring forts and Palaces. See the most beautiful Jaisalmer Fort, famed for yellow sandstone architecture.
Also visit the scenic havelies like Patwon Ki Haveli and Nathmal Ki Haveli, known for intricate carvings.
One must not miss the city's Jain temple heritage. There are 7 Jain temples located inside the fort, highlighting the artistic and religious heritage of India.
Bliss of Southern Rajasthan, Udaipur, the city of Lakes which will take your breath away with its scenic beauty.
Explore Saheliyon ki Bari, famed for its scenic fountains and lotus pool, beautiful Fateh Sagar Lake and Lake Pichola which offers stunning views and recreation opportunities with family and friends.
Also explore Jag Mandir, the stunning lake garden palace and Taj Lake Palace, the white marble beauty.
Renowned for the tranquil Pushkar Lake and is home to one of the world's few Brahma temples, Pushkar offers solace to Peace seekers. It is also known as Tirthraj.
The lively fairs and spiritual vibe of Pushkar makes it one of the most sought after stops for travellers.
Pushkar's lively fairs and spiritual ambience make it a captivating stop for pilgrims and travelers

Located in the Southwest direction of Jaipur, Ajmer is a popular religious attraction for both Hindu and Muslims. It is a final resting place of a renowned Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti. Hindu and Muslims devotees from all across the globe visit Ajmer Sharif Dargah to honor the shrine of the Sufi saint and get his divine blessings.
It is also a very popular Jain pilgrimage spot. Visit Jain Golden temple which is also known as Soni Ji Ki Nasiya which Honours Lord Rishabhdev (Adinath).
The land of Chittorgarh has kept the stories of bravery, passion and pride intact through its rich culture and heritage. The city is named after the magnificent structure of Chittorgarh Fort.
There are many places to explore in Chittorgarh which you must not miss such as Chittorgarh Fort, Vijay Stambh, Kirti Stambh, Fateh Prakash Palace, Kalika Mata Temple and Tulja Bhavani temple etc.

blocks.text: Best Things to Do in Rajasthan on your Trip

Rajasthan has so much to offer to the travellers that might get confused what to do here. What you want to do will depend on your interest and energy. There is something to enjoy for everyone. We have picked the best activities to do in Rajasthan. Based on your interests, you can customize your Rajasthan tour packages and add the best things as per your preferences.

items: Zip-Lining in Rajasthan is a must try adventure activity if you are a thrill seeker. It is available at many locations which combine thrill with heritage views.

You can try Zip-lining in Mehrangarh Fort. The six thrilling Ziplines here will cover the entire fort, battlements and the desert lake. It will take 90 minutes to get the best views of Mehrangarh fort and Jodhpur.
You can also try Zip lining at Neemrana Fort Palace. It is India's first heritage Zip line. Through zip-lining you will get the stunning views of Aravalli hills and the entire Neemrana Fort.

Rajasthan boasts of some of the best wildlife and bird Sanctuaries in India. You can enjoy wildlife safari at Ranthambore National Park, Sariska National Park, Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary or Keoladeo National Park.
You can also go for camel safari and stay in a luxury desert camp in Thar Desert near Jaisalmer or Bikaner.
Enjoy the beauty of star-lit sky, cultural folk music performances and dances, delicious traditional meals, puppet shows and cozy beddings while camping in Rajasthan.
Don't miss the village themed resort- Chokhi Dhani in Jaipur while enjoying your sightseeing here. If you want to truly experience Rajasthan's culture and heritage then Chokhi Dhani is a must visit.
Here you will enjoy many cultural shows and performances like Kalbeliya, Ghoomar and Chari dance and other most popular shows like Puppet shows, traditional fire act, and bamboo acrobatics.
Also enjoy the drama enactment of the famous battle of Haldighati which displays the courage of Maharana Pratap and other Rajputs.
There are many rides to enjoy here like Camel rides, elephant rides, horseback rides, bullock cart rides and boat rides in a village lake called Tal Talaiya.
Trekking in Rajasthan is a perfect blend of adventure, heritage fort routes and scenic views. October to March are the best months to enjoy trekking here.

Alwar and Mount Abu have the best trekking trails for adventure lovers. You can also enjoy trekking in Jaipur at Nahargarh Fort. It's a 1-2 hours moderate trek which starts from the city to Aravalli hills and ends at the Historical Nahargarh Fort.
Jawai Hills are also perfect for trekking in Rajasthan. It boasts of dramatic granite domes, natural caves and volcanic trails.
Enjoy a fun-filled day with Elephants at Dera Amer. Here you can enjoy exciting elephant rides and join them on long walks through the desert scrub.
The tranquil desert views, organically local grown food, dining near elephants in a natural setting and spacious tents will make your camping at Dera Amer memorable forever.

Rural Tourism in Rajasthan offers rich experiences of traditional village life, eco-tourism, cultural and heritage of the region. You must visit some of the most beautiful villages like Bishnoi Village near Jodhpur which offers tourists a chance to see the village lifestyle, animal conservation practices, pottery and cow milking techniques.
Also visit, Mandwa, Khimar, and Khuri, Samode to experience village culture, festivals , learn organic farming, enjoy traditional music, dances and savor most authentic Rajasthan cuisines.

blocks.text: Useful Travel Tips to for Memorable Rajasthan Holidays
Here are some most useful travel tips for safe and fun-filled holidays in Rajasthan with your family and friends-

items: Best time to Visit- Plan your Rajasthan tour in peak tourism months (October- March). During this time the weather will be fantastic for sightseeing and outdoor adventure activities. Though, you will have to book your tickets and hotels in advance due to the peak tourism season. You will also witness crowds at famous tourist spots in Rajasthan.

Duration- At least spend 7-12 days to enjoy a comprehensive Rajasthan Tour. Rajasthan has many opulent places, and forts, temples, bustling bazaars, and many adventure opportunities. It is not possible to cover the best of Rajasthan in just 2-3 days. In a short duration you will only be able to see only one or two places. It is not enough for the best Rajasthan trip experience. So, plan your duration to cover most of Rajasthan.

Advance Booking- Advance booking is important if you are trying zip lining and other adventure activities in Rajasthan in peak tourism season. If you wish to enjoy camping at desert camps then also you need to book your luxury tent in advance.
Comfort over Budget- If comfort is your priority then we recommend you to hire a private car or taxi for Rajasthan sightseeing. If you are travelling with kids or elders then, it is the best option.
Cultural Experiences- Don't miss places where you will get a chance to listen to folk music and see dance performances for authentic cultural immersion.

What to Pack- In winters, carry jackets, woolen clothes as the temperature during this time will be 10-27°C.In summer, carry light breathable fabric, stoles and comfortable footwear. During Monsoon, carry a raincoat, rain gear, light jackets and sturdy shoes.
Cash- Carry enough cash to buy souvenirs from small vendors and shopkeepers. If you are visiting rural areas, you may not find digital payment options.
Anti-Theft Bag- Take special care of your belongings. Carry Anti-theft bags to keep your important documents like passport, ID, license and cash etc. safe.
Emergency Contact- Keep emergency numbers of relevant persons whom you can approach anytime for help during unforeseen circumstances apart from tour operators.
Safety- Always hire licensed operators for adventure activities who provide safety gears. Check their ID and expiry date of the license.
Modest Clothing- Wear covered clothes at sacred sites. Respect the culture and customs of the spiritual places.

Q1. What Distinguishes Karnataka From Other States?

Ans. The state is well known for its ancient culture, traditions, and heritage and is one of the oldest places in all of India. Some of the most powerful nations, philosophers, saints, ancient monuments, renowned pilgrimage sites, and innumerable natural wonders have all called it home. It has been a popular destination for travellers of all stripes.
Q2. Which Deity Is Well-Known In Karnataka?

Ans. The majority of the populace of Karnataka worships Shiva (Linga). Along with other well-known temples in Karnataka, the Dharmasthala Manjunatha temple contains an idol of Shiva on its property. It is the main draw of each temple.
Q3. Which Temple In Karnataka Is The Biggest?

Ans. Near Nanjundeshwara Temple lies the Parasurama Temple. Devarajammanni, the queen of the Mysore monarch Krishnaraja Wadiyar III, constructed the nine-story, 120-foot-tall temple Gopuram and its expansive façade.
Q4. Which River In Karnataka Is The Largest?
Ans. The largest river in Karnataka, the Kaveri (or Cauvery), rises in the Coorg district.
Q5. Which Temple In Karnataka Is The Oldest?

Ans. One of the earliest Hindu temples, the Chalukya Shiva Temple (formerly known as Lad Khan Temple), honours Shiva. It is one of a series of monuments at Aihole in the Indian state of Karnataka. It is currently estimated to be from the fifth or sixth century, as opposed to the seventh or eighth.

blocks.text: Ayodhya tour packages offer one-of-a-kind spiritual, cultural and historical experiences. Not only is it the most popular sacred destination for Hindu devotees, it is also a historical city and a cultural hub of living traditions. Devotees are mostly drawn to its sacred significance as the birthplace of Lord Rama, and Ayodhya is strongly linked to spirituality and Hindu mythology. Situated along the sacred Sarayu River's banks, the holy city is deeply linked with the Ramayana — referred to as the ancient Kosala Kingdom's capital in the epic. The city enjoys a special place in the hearts of all Hindus, and many devotees choose the Ayodhya pilgrimage trip to seek spiritual solace and closeness to God.

In 2024, Ayodhya recorded over 203 million visitors, strengthening its position as one of the leading spiritual destinations in India. Ayodhya's significance has grown further after the consecration of the Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir on 22 January 2024 — a moment millions of devotees had awaited for decades.
Why Choose My Quick Trippers for Your Ayodhya Tour Package?

The sacred city of Ayodhya has a lot to offer - whether it's the pious Ghats, unique architecture, stunning temples, or vibrant local markets. At My Quick Trippers, we understand travellers' mindsets and curate Ayodhya itineraries that help you explore in a carefree and comfortable way. Our Ayodhya travel packages cover:

items: Guided tours by licensed, experienced local guides

blocks.text: Don't wait - book your Ayodhya Yatra today!
Other Reasons to Visit Ayodhya in 2026

items: Ayodhya has numerous places which will transport you back to the Treta Yuga. You can relive the tales of the Ramayana.
Witness festivals related to Lord Rama - Ram Navami, Dussehra, and Deepotsav - celebrated here with unmatched devotion as this is the birthplace of Lord Rama.
Visit the original birthplace of Lord Rama - Ram Janmabhoomi. This is the most iconic landmark in Ayodhya which you must not miss.
Maharishi Valmiki International Airport now connects Ayodhya directly to Delhi, Mumbai, and other major cities - 2026 is the most connected year to visit.
Ayodhya is one of the seven Sapta Moksha Puris - sacred cities believed to grant moksha. A visit here holds the highest spiritual merit for Hindu pilgrims.
The new Ram Path corridor, upgraded Ghats, and modern amenities make sightseeing more comfortable than ever before.

blocks.text: Best Time to Go for an Ayodhya Trip

Standard Ayodhya tours start from INR 18,900 (hotels, meals, transfers, Darshan assistance, guide). Luxury package go up to INR 38,500 with luxury hotels, private car, VIP Darshan assistance, and a tour guide. We have packages for every budget.

October to March are the best months to travel to Ayodhya. During this time you can explore Ayodhya's famous temples and sacred places comfortably. The weather stays pleasant for sightseeing and strolling the Ghats for hours. Outdoor activities like boating on the Sarayu are also fully enjoyable.

Summer is not a favourable season to explore Ayodhya. The day's heat can be exhausting, especially for senior citizens and children. If you do visit in April, plan all temple visits before 9 AM and after 5 PM.

Heavy rains from July to September will disrupt sightseeing plans and boat rides on the Sarayu River. Ghat steps become slippery and unsafe. You may miss out on key activities and not be able to enjoy the full potential of your Ayodhya travel package. Avoid this season unless you are visiting specifically for Sawan (Shravan) religious observances.
Festival Special — Plan Around These 2026 Dates
Note: During Ram Navami and Deepotsav, Ayodhya attracts lakhs of additional visitors. Hotel prices rise and availability drops quickly. Book well in advance for festival travel.
Places to Visit on Your Ayodhya Trip

Ayodhya holds a special place in the hearts of Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Rama. Beyond its spiritual significance, the city also offers deep historical and cultural experiences. Here are the best places to include in your Ayodhya holiday package:
Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir (Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra)

items: This is the most iconic place in Ayodhya and the single most important reason millions visit every year. The grand temple was consecrated on 22 January 2024 after decades of anticipation.

As the name suggests, this is the place where Lord Rama was born as per Hindu scripture. The temple is built in the Nagara style using pink Rajasthani sandstone and houses the idol of Ram Lalla (infant Rama) in the main sanctum.
For a peaceful Darshan, visit on weekday mornings. VIP Darshan passes are available at the temple counter for priority access.

Resting atop a hill with 76 steps leading to the entrance, Hanuman Garhi is a prominent Lord Hanuman temple. It is customary in Ayodhya to seek Hanuman ji's blessings here before visiting Ram Janmabhoomi.
Devotees commonly offer Ladoo Prasad — easily available from vendors outside. The panoramic views of Ayodhya from the top are stunning, and the temple architecture is a sight to behold.
This stunning temple, also known locally as 'Sone Ka Ghar' (House of Gold), is believed to have been gifted to Goddess Sita by Queen Kaikeyi as a wedding present.
Devotees love the exquisitely adorned golden-crowned idols of Lord Rama and Sita, and the intricate carvings on the temple walls. It is one of the most photographed temples in Ayodhya.

blocks.text: Located a few kilometres from Ayodhya, Bharat Kund is the sacred spot where Bharat — Lord Rama's devoted brother — performed penance for 14 years during Rama's exile, awaiting his return. The Kund (sacred tank) here is considered holy.

items: This temple is famous as the site where Lord Rama performed the Ashwamedha Yagna. Visiting during Diwali, when the temple is decorated beautifully, is an experience like no other.
Unique to this temple: the idols of Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, and Hanuman are carved from black sandstone, giving them a rare look not found in other Ayodhya temples.

blocks.text: This memorial is dedicated to the poet-saint Tulsidas, the author of Ramcharitmanas. Regular recitals of the Ramayana are performed here, along with other spiritual and cultural events.

items: This popular museum houses manuscripts, artefacts, and paintings related to the Ramayana and Lord Rama.
The museum takes about 1–2 hours to explore fully, offering a deep understanding of the city's cultural heritage.
Gulab Bari is a beautiful 18th-century mausoleum and garden complex of Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula — a fascinating piece of Mughal-era history within a Hindu pilgrimage city.
Capture the stunning rose gardens and Mughal-era architecture. Open from 4 AM to 7 PM.
Mani Parvat is a sacred hillock in Ayodhya. It is believed to be a part of the Sanjeevani hill that Lord Hanuman carried from the Himalayas to revive Lakshmana.
As Hanuman flew with the Sanjeevani Hill, a part of it fell here at Ayodhya — forming Mani Parvat. The view from the top offers a good perspective of the city.

blocks.text: Located in the northwest corner of the Ram Janmabhoomi complex, Sita Ki Rasoi is believed to be the kitchen where Goddess Sita cooked after her marriage with Lord Rama. The site houses idols of Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Bharat, and Shatrughan, and carries a calm, intimate atmosphere.

One of Ayodhya's oldest temples, Nageshwarnath is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is believed to have been established by Kush, the son of Lord Rama. Significant during the Shivratri festival, it is the only temple that was maintained during Ayodhya's long period of obscurity.

Believed to be the palace of King Dashrath, father of Lord Rama, Dashrath Mahal features a colourful entrance, beautiful idols of Ram, Sita, and Lakshmana, and hosts daily Aarti and Bhajans. Located close to Ram Janmabhoomi, it fits into any Ayodhya Darshan plan.

Guptar Ghat is where Lord Rama is believed to have taken Jal Samadhi — leaving his earthly form and ascending to Vaikuntha through the sacred Sarayu waters. Beautiful temples surround the Ghat and the serene atmosphere makes it deeply moving, especially at sunrise.

Ram Ki Paidi is the main Ghat complex on the Sarayu riverfront and the heart of Ayodhya's spiritual evenings. The nightly Sarayu Aarti here — with lamps, conch shells, and devotional chanting — is one of Ayodhya's most beautiful experiences. During Deepotsav, this Ghat glows with hundreds of thousands of Diyas in a world-record setting.
Things to Do on Your Ayodhya Trip
Ayodhya is a sacred city centred on Lord Rama. While you are enjoying your Ayodhya travel package, make sure you do the following to get the most out of your experience:

items: All festivals related to Lord Rama take on a different meaning in Ayodhya. Ram Navami — celebrating Lord Rama's birth — is marked with grand processions and cultural events across the city.
Deepotsav and Diwali are where Ayodhya glows with millions of lamps to commemorate the return of Lord Rama. The riverfront during Deepotsav is truly unforgettable.
Guptar Ghat holds a special place among devotees as the site where Lord Rama left his earthly body. The site is surrounded by beautiful temples and tourists enjoy the calm ambiance.

blocks.text: Take a Boat Ride on the Sarayu River

items: A boat ride on the Sarayu River is a relaxing and beautiful way to see the ghats and temples from the water. The surrounding views are breathtaking. The best time is early morning or evening.

blocks.text: Ayodhya, being a spiritual centre, offers a variety of vegetarian dishes you must try:
Attend Sarayu Aarti at Ram Ki Paidi

Experience the divine atmosphere at the banks of the Sarayu River during the evening Aarti — with recitation of hymns, lamps, and chanting. Also attend the Mangala Aarti at Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in the early morning for the most spiritually powerful start to your day (free Aarti pass required, collected from trust office 30 minutes before the Aarti).

items: Local bazaars near the Ghats and temples have a wide variety of souvenirs and spiritual goods.

From handmade artefacts to traditional sweets, there is much to explore. Ayodhya, being a religious hub, also offers temple bells, brass items, Rudraksha beads, religious books, and Ramayana scriptures.
Best shopping areas: Ram Ki Paidi market, Chowk Bazaar, Kanak Bhawan Temple shops, Faizabad Main Market, and the Tulsi Smarak Bhawan market.

blocks.text: Take a Holy Dip at the Sarayu River

A holy dip in the Sarayu River — particularly at Ram Ki Paidi or Guptar Ghat — is considered deeply auspicious. Pilgrims believe it cleanses sins and brings spiritual merit. The most sacred time is at sunrise.
Watch the Light and Sound Show

Ayodhya's Light and Sound Show (typically starting at 7:30 PM) narrates the story of the Ramayana through visual storytelling and light effects. It is a highly recommended evening activity, especially for families visiting with children.

Ayodhya now has its own airport: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport (AYJ), approximately 10 km from the city. Direct flights connect Ayodhya to Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, and Bengaluru. Lucknow Airport (LKO), 135 km away, is an alternative with wider connectivity. Our packages include airport pickup.

Ayodhya Dham Junction is the main railway station — recently upgraded and located about 1.5 km from Ram Janmabhoomi. Direct trains from Delhi (Vande Bharat, Ayodhya Express), Mumbai, Lucknow, Varanasi , Kolkata, and Prayagraj. Electric auto-rickshaws and e-cabs are available outside the station.

Ayodhya is connected via NH-27 and the Purvanchal Expressway. Regular buses and cabs are available from Lucknow (135 km, ~2.5 hrs), Varanasi (200 km, ~3.5 hrs), and Prayagraj (170 km, ~3 hrs). Note: private vehicles are not permitted near the Ram Janmabhoomi complex — e-rickshaws and walking are the only options within the temple zone.

blocks.text: Yamunotri Yatra is a holy trip that is highly revered in Hinduism. On this sacred pilgrimage, you visit the Yamunotri Temple , located in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. The shrine is dedicated to Goddess Yamuna .
It is also one of the Dhams in the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit , and is visited first in the Yatra.
Why Yamunotri Is First Dham in Char Dham Circuit?

As per the Hindu customs, the Char Dham Yatra should be done in a clockwise direction , starting from the west. And Yamunotri falls on the westernmost side of the Char Dham circuit, and hence it's visited first.

Another reason is that Char Dham Yatra follows the origin of the sacred rivers : from west to east. And Yamuna (originating at Yamunotri) lies west of River Ganga (originating at Gangotri). Hence, the order:

Also, from the travel perspective, it is practical to start your Yatra from Yamunotri. This Dham is located at the lowest altitude among all the Dhams, and therefore helps the pilgrims acclimatise better and helps them only gradually move towards the other higher altitudes sites.

blocks.text: Here is the detailed route map, starting from Haridwar:
Haridwar → Rishikesh → Chamba → Mussoorie → Kempty Falls → Barkot → Nainbagh → Purola → Janki Chatti → Yamunotri Temple (6 km trek)
The total distance from Haridwar to Yamunotri is about 311 km (including the trek). The total time is about 14-16 hours by road , in addition to 3-4 hours of trekking .
If you start from Delhi, then the total distance up to Yamunotri is about 450 km (including trek). It will take about 14–16 hours by road + 3–4 hours trek.
The history of Yamunotri goes back to the ancient ages . This is another reason the place where the temple is located is considered to be extremely pious in nature.

Yamunotri is also the place where the prominent Hindu Sage Asit Muni used to stay and take his bath in both the rivers of Ganga and Yamuna, which in those times used to flow next to each other. So the sage set up his hermitage here.
Later on Adi Shankaracharya, the propagator of Advaita Vedanta, re-established this temple as a part of the Char Dham Yatra circuit , which further increased its spiritual significance in Hinduism.

Yamunotri Temple is dedicated to the goddess Yamuna. It also honours the Yamuna River , as the river is considered to be the manifestation of the Goddess herself. This makes the Yamunotri temple a unique and one of the rarest temples in India.
The Goddess is also the sister of Yama, the God of death, in Hindu mythology. It's said that whoever visit the temple does not suffer from untimely or painful death .

People from all over the globe flock here to offer their prayer to the goddess at her place of birth. Devotees make their way to the shrine after covering a gruelling trek from Janki Chatti to worship the glistening black pyramidal stone . The stone is said to be the form of the goddess herself, making it her holy abode.

blocks.text: The registration for the Yatra is mandatory . The Uttarakhand government has made it compulsory in order to better track the pilgrim movement.
You can register in two ways: online and offline.
For online registration , simply visit the official portal of the Uttarakhand Tourism . You must have a valid government ID (Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, etc.) and a phone number for OTP verification.
For offline registration , there are counters available at Haridwar, Rishikesh, and other base towns. You must also produce your government ID.

Pilgrims also sometimes choose the summer window (April to June) to come here. Be wary of the hot weather that you'll have to brave here in this season, when the temperature easily crosses 35 °C during the daytime.

Also, we advise against buying your Hyderabad to Ujjain tour package in the monsoon season (July to September). Although it blesses you with lush greenery, traveling is quite a difficult task because of road blockage and slipper paths owing to the heavy rain during this time.
How to Reach Ujjain from Hyderabad?
There are several ways by which you can reach the city of Ujjain from the state of Hyderabad:

By Air: Take a direct flight from the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad to Indore's Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport. From here, you can hire a taxi to get to Ujjain, which will take less than 2 hours for this 55 km road journey.

By Train: Ujjain is also connected with Hyderabad with direct trains. Opt for either the Ujjaini Express or Indore Express, the tickets for which you can buy from the official website of the IRCTC. The trip is long, taking about 19 hours, so be mentally prepared for it.

By Road: The distance between Ujjain and Hyderabad is approximately 860 km and takes about 16 hours. You can also book our Ujjain to Hyderabad road package to get to the holy city with comfort and ease. Also, many government and private buses run on this route.
